The cool façade paradox: Balancing urban climate regulation and outdoor thermal stress – A systematized review
abstract: Cool façades — building walls with high solar reflectance and high thermal emittance — are promoted as a passive urban cooling strategy. However, their effects on outdoor thermal strain remain insufficiently understood. This systematized review synthesizes evidence from 77 studies to quantify the effects of increased façade solar reflectance on air temperature and outdoor thermal stress in urban environments. Based on façade-only interventions, each 0.1 increase in solar reflectance was associated with an air temperature reduction of 0.04 °C and a mean radiant temperature (MRT) increase of 1.63 °C, as derived from origin-constrained linear regression slopes ( β ). Studies that isolate façade-only interventions remain comparatively scarce, underscoring the need for further research to refine these estimates. The air-temperature response was highly context-dependent, whereas MRT increased in every study in the dataset. This asymmetry reveals what this review terms the cool façade paradox: during daytime hours, the MRT increase outweighs the air-temperature benefit, worsening pedestrian heat exposure despite cooler air. Air temperature reductions were consistently larger when façade modification was combined with complementary strategies, such as cool roofs, cool roads, and urban greening, than when applied alone. These findings indicate that cool façades should be assessed for their pedestrian-level radiative effects, not only for their air temperature benefits, before being adopted as a heat mitigation strategy.

title: MIST-Net: A Heterogeneous Spatiotemporal Network for Regional Ozone Forecasting Robust to Sparse Data
A robust optimization method for integrating on-site medical waste treatment in rural areas with centralized treatment in urban areas
abstract: Rural healthcare facilities generate medical waste (MW) and current practice routes this waste to centralized treatment plants in urban areas. Advances in on-site equipment have made local treatment of rural MW feasible, but no systematic framework exists for coordinating on-site and centralized treatment in an integrated urban–rural system. This study is the first to formulate on-site treatment as a mode-choice decision jointly optimized with centralized treatment across urban and rural areas under transportation cost uncertainty. A multi-objective robust optimization model is developed to minimize cost, risk, and carbon emissions, evaluating three centralized technologies and two on-site treatment options. Results show that on-site treatment reduces system risk and carbon emissions. The robust model yields more conservative cost estimates than its deterministic counterpart while achieving lower risk and emissions by retaining more on-site treatment selections. Combining centralized and on-site treatment withstands larger surges in MW generation than centralized treatment alone, offering resilience for public health emergencies. Incineration is the most cost-effective centralized technology despite the highest emissions, while microwave sterilization is the cheapest on-site option and high-temperature steam sterilization yields the lowest emissions. This study offers a practical decision-making tool for the integrated management of urban–rural MW systems with centralized and on-site treatment under uncertainty.

title: Informing pharmaceutical regulation in China: Risk-based priority ranking across nine river basins
abstract: Pharmaceuticals are widely detected in surface waters, posing significant ecological and human-health risks. China is a major producer and consumer of pharmaceuticals, and widespread contamination has been reported in its surface waters. Regional differences in topography, hydrology, land use, and socioeconomic conditions can shape patterns of pharmaceutical exposure and risk, calling for priority lists tailored to individual river basins. However, previous studies mainly focused on national-scale assessments, selected river basins, or specific pharmaceutical classes. In this study, we systematically reviewed 226 peer-reviewed articles and compiled 8628 occurrence records for 158 pharmaceutical compounds. A multi-criteria prioritization framework that integrated both hazard and exposure potential was used to identify priority pharmaceuticals across nine river basins. Antibiotics were the most frequently detected class of pharmaceuticals, although most had low or moderate priority scores. Erythromycin, roxithromycin, and azithromycin were notable exceptions and ranked highly. Among nonantibiotic pharmaceuticals, estrone and ibuprofen ranked highly in all nine basins. Beyond these shared priorities, several pharmaceuticals showed distinct basin-specific priority pattern. Psychotropic medicines, including diazepam, fluoxetine, sertraline, and citalopram, were identified as priorities in highly urbanized basins, particularly the Haihe and Yangtze River basins. In the Yellow River Basin, the lipid modulator gemfibrozil was prioritized, while in the Pearl River Basin, the veterinary antibiotic salinomycin was prioritized. Combining the rankings with uncertainty estimates showed that high-priority compounds with low uncertainty should be considered for stringent monitoring and control, whereas compounds with high uncertainty require additional occurrence and toxicity data. These findings underscore the importance of basin-scale prioritization in capturing regional differences and provide a basis for tiered monitoring and management in China.

title: Sowing vegetation islets enhance plant diversity and habitat heterogeneity in Mediterranean long-established road verges
abstract: Halting biodiversity loss requires innovative conservation approaches, and road verges offer opportunities for biodiversity-friendly measures. Although native seed mixes are increasingly used in post-disturbance revegetation, long-established road verges outside urban areas are often overlooked for proactive conservation. To promote species-rich and heterogeneous vegetation, we established vegetation islets by sowing a specifically designed seed mix of native herbaceous species along long-established road verges in a semi-arid Mediterranean agricultural landscape across two experimental blocks with different sowing years. Over four years, we conducted an integrated assessment of seed mix performance and plant diversity, composition, and structure, comparing vegetation islets and control plots and exploring the influence of local edaphoclimatic conditions. The establishment of vegetation islets had the strongest observed effect on plant composition and diversity, locally adding sown and spontaneous species absent from controls, and increasing species richness and compositional heterogeneity. Although seed mix persistence and relative cover declined over time, composition remained distinct from controls, shifting from annual to perennial dominance. Vegetation islets supported denser, shorter vegetation, enhancing local structural heterogeneity without compromising road safety. Higher rainfall, lower temperatures, and lower soil nutrient levels were associated with higher seed mix persistence and species richness. Experimental block affected only species composition and seed mix relative cover. An appropriate bespoke native seed mix, applied to stable long-established plant communities, helped support reliable conservation outcomes under semi-arid Mediterranean conditions. Vegetation islets may offer a resource-efficient approach to promote plant diversity and habitat heterogeneity in long-established road verges, highlighting their potential for proactive conservation.

title: The composite acidifier of superphosphate and sulfuric acid for swine slurry storage treatment: Assessment of gases emission reduction and stabilization
Maternal PM2.5 exposure induces preeclampsia-like phenotypes in mice through placental angiogenic dysfunction and lncRNA–RUNX1 dysregulation
abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) is an idiopathic gestational disorder defined by placental structural abnormalities, systemic inflammatory activation, angiogenic factor imbalance, and endothelial dysfunction. While existing epidemiological studies have established a correlational association between maternal fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) exposure and elevated PE risk, the specific underlying molecular mechanisms driving this association have not been fully elucidated. Using a C57BL/6J mouse model of maternal PM 2.5 exposure via intranasal instillation (3 mg/kg body weight, every other days from gestational day 0.5 to 17.5), we investigated the mechanisms underlying PE-like phenotypes induced by heating-season PM 2.5 from northern China. Exposed pregnant mice exhibited significantly elevated blood pressure at E13.5 and E17.5, accompanied by reduced vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and placental growth factor (PLGF) levels, increased urinary protein, and elevated serum levels of the tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α), interleukin-6 (IL-6), and soluble fms-like tyrosine kinase-1 ( sFLT-1). Conversely, the endothelial markers endothelin 1 (ET-1) and nitric oxide (NO) remained unchanged. Placentas from PM 2.5 -exposed mice exhibited abnormal architecture and impaired angiogenesis in the labyrinth region. These phenotypes were consistent with key features of PE. Through transcriptomic profiling, bioinformatics analyses, immunofluorescence, quantitative reverse transcription PCR ( RT-qPCR), and chromatin/RNA immunoprecipitation assays, we identified the long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) NONMMUT087808.1 and NONMMUT044449.2 as potential regulators of placental development and function that are associated with runt-related transcription factor 1 (RUNX1) dysregulation, suggesting a possible contribution to PE-like phenotypes. Taken together, our findings provide experimental evidence linking exposure to heating-season PM 2.5 from northern China with adverse gestational outcomes and highlight the critical need for targeted air pollution mitigation strategies and population-specific health interventions for vulnerable subgroups, including pregnant women.

title: Integrating structural and functional connectivity to optimize ecological security patterns at multiple levels in the Yellow River Delta, China
Stocking density shapes phytoplankton community stability in rice-crayfish integrated systems
abstract: The rice-crayfish integrated system (RCIS) has expanded rapidly across China, yet its ecological impacts on phytoplankton remain inadequately understood. To fill this gap, we conducted a 40-d field experiment with five crayfish ( Procambarus clarkii ) stocking densities (0, 1, 2, 3, and 4 ind./m 2 ; CK, T1–T4) in replicated paddy plots. Water samples were collected weekly, and phytoplankton were identified and enumerated under light microscopy. Community structure, diversity indices (Margalef, Pielou, and Shannon–Wiener), co-occurrence networks, neutral community model (NCM), and Spearman correlations were analyzed. One-way ANOVA with Tukey tests was used for treatment comparisons, and network stability was assessed by robustness and vulnerability. Our results showed that crayfish stocking significantly reduced species richness and total biomass relative to CK ( P < 0.05) and shifted dominant taxa. Diversity indices declined to their lowest values at T2 and then recovered: Margalef decreased from 2.67 ± 0.05 in CK to 1.40 ± 0.10 in T2 ( P < 0.001), Pielou from 0.88 ± 0.01 to 0.80 ± 0.02 ( P < 0.05), and Shannon–Wiener from 2.91 ± 1.03 to 2.11 ± 0.10 ( P < 0.001), corresponding to reductions of 47.57%, 9.09%, and 27.49%, respectively. Co-occurrence networks were simplest and least stable at T2, with the highest vulnerability, whereas T3 had the lowest vulnerability among stocked treatments. NCM fitting showed higher stochasticity in stocked treatments (Rsqr = 0.683–0.806) and lower migration rates (Nm = 3–4) than CK (Nm = 11). Spearman correlations (significance at P < 0.05) identified dissolved oxygen, water temperature, and total nitrogen as key drivers in CK, whereas stocked treatments showed more complex nutrient-phytoplankton relationships. From a phytoplankton-based perspective, a stocking density of 3 ind./m 2 appears ecologically favorable, but this recommendation requires integrated testing with production, water quality, and multi-trophic indicators.

title: Status hope: the conceptualisation of the status game
abstract: Purpose This study develops a sociological conceptualisation of status hope to explain how the status game is produced and sustained across international marketplaces. It addresses the tension between status pursuit as joyful and autonomous and status as a field-structured struggle over symbolic power and uncertain recognition. Design/methodology/approach The research is conceptual and theory-building. It synthesises Bourdieusian theory, consumer culture theory research on status consumption and the conception of hope. It develops a tri-construct framework comprising belief in status, desire for status and perceived potential for status attainment. Findings Status hope is an illusive yet compelling pursuit of status under field constraints. Belief in status operates at the field level, where sociocultural ideologies generate tensions between ideals and realities. Desire for status operates at the habitus level through reference group selection and discrepancy management. Perceived potential for status attainment functions at the meso level through legitimation and enactment infrastructures. Research limitations/implications As a conceptual research, the framework requires empirical testing across international markets. It encourages research beyond national-culture typologies towards ideological field configurations explaining cross-market convergence and local variation. Practical implications The framework helps status brands refine segmentation beyond country-level cultural traits by identifying consumers according to ideologies they embody and internalise, and habitus-shaped changing referents as life unfolds. Originality/value The study reframes the status game as status hope: a field-structured, market-mediated and socioculturally sustained pursuit of uncertain recognition. It organises fragmented status consumption research across field/macro, meso and habitus/micro levels. Counterfeit consumption is treated as one illustrative application of our framework within the status consumption literature.

title: Predicting leadership emergence in global virtual teams: machine learning applications in algorithmic HRM
abstract: Identifying leadership talent early remains a persistent challenge for organizations, particularly in distributed and multicultural settings. Responding to calls for predictive approaches in algorithmic HRM, this study evaluates the relative performance and interpretability of supervised machine learning models for predicting leadership emergence in non-hierarchical global virtual teams (GVTs). Using data from 8,112 individuals nested in 2,371 GVTs, we benchmark five supervised algorithms (Artificial Neural Networks, Naïve Bayes, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Logistic Regression) on out-of-sample classification performance using demographic, psychological, motivational, behavioral, and team climate features collected across multiple time points. All models demonstrate strong predictive validity, with XGBoost achieving modestly superior overall performance (79% accuracy; AUROC = 0.87), consistent with its ability to capture nonlinear relationships in complex, high-dimensional data. Explainable AI analyses using SHAP identify the features that contribute most strongly to leadership emergence predictions (help with coordination, effort, friendliness (inverse), English language proficiency, and perceived team efficacy (inverse)) and reveal nonlinear predictive patterns that are difficult to detect with traditional statistical approaches. By framing leadership identification as a predictive talent analytics problem, this study advances algorithmic HRM research while illustrating how interpretable machine learning models can generate theoretically informative insights for leadership research in global and virtual contexts.
journal_name: The International Journal of Human Resource Management

title: Dual pathways from adversity: CEO childhood famine experience, motivational orientations, and organizational resilience
abstract: Organizational resilience is critical for sustained development in turbulent contexts; however, the mechanisms linking chief executive officers’ (CEOs) early-life adversity to organizational resilience and their boundary conditions remain underexplored. Drawing on imprinting and upper echelons theories, we argue that childhood famine experiences shape CEOs’ motivational orientations and thereby influence organizational resilience. Two pathways were identified: achievement and differentiation orientations. The empirical results show that childhood famine experiences increased achievement orientation but decreased differentiation orientation. However, only differentiation orientation served as a robust mediating mechanism, whereas the indirect effect of achievement orientation was not significant in the full sample. Further analyses showed that the achievement pathway became significant only under low organizational slack and was not significantly moderated by ownership, whereas the differentiation pathway was stronger under high slack and nonstate ownership. Taken together, these findings suggest that the two motivational mechanisms rely on distinct organizational conditions.

title: Harvesting trade partners online with AI: A joint learning method for predicting the business role of massive web pages
abstract: In small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), users often perform tedious and complex human–computer interactions between search engine data ( S D ) and webpage data ( W D ) when seeking potential business partners online via search engines (SEs). While artificial intelligence (AI) has been shown to improve search efficiency, conventional machine learning methods still face challenges in retrieval accuracy and efficiency, particularly in complex big-data environments. To address these limitations, this study proposes an AI module termed the Multi-source Data Joint Learning (MDJL) model, designed to assist SME users in efficiently retrieving online business partners. The MDJL model employs a multimodal information fusion approach to separately represent unstructured data elements in S D and W D as vectors. An encoder-decoder architecture then jointly learns the associations between S D and W D . Based on these learned joint representations, MDJL incorporates a multi-label attention mechanism to train a classifier that accurately predicts the business roles of companies associated with webpages. The model’s effectiveness is validated using real business datasets annotated by domain experts. Experimental results show that MDJL can effectively learn joint information from any two cross-correlated datasets. The resulting classifier exhibits high efficiency and robustness, especially when data from certain sources are partially missing or unknown. From a managerial standpoint, a trained MDJL model can further help SMEs digitize and consolidate the business knowledge of highly skilled employees, supporting more informed and efficient decision-making in partner search activities.

title: Improvements to pharmaceutical manufacturing capacity; Ethiopia
abstract: Abstract Problem Ethiopia's heavy dependence on imported pharmaceuticals created public health vulnerabilities, foreign exchange pressures and recurrent medicine stock-outs. Approach In 2015, Ethiopia launched a 10-year National Strategy and Plan of Action for Pharmaceutical Manufacturing Development to improve access to quality-assured medicines. The strategy, overseen by a Joint Steering Committee co-chaired by the Ministries of Health and Industry with technical assistance from the World Health Organization (WHO), combined industrial incentives, preferential centralized procurement and regulatory strengthening. Local setting Before strategy implementation, Ethiopia had limited manufacturing capacity. Local manufacturers supplied approximately 20% of national generic medicine demand, while supply chain fragmentation and foreign exchange constraints compromised access to imported medicines. Relevant changes By 2025, six facilities had achieved national good manufacturing practice compliance, 11 manufacturers were operational and the Ethiopian Food and Drug Authority reached WHO Maturity Level 3. Locally produced coverage of the National Essential Medicines List increased from 90 to 140 chemical entities, across 167 dosage forms, and a vaccine manufacturing initiative was launched. However, domestic supply only increased to 23% against a 60% public procurement target; active pharmaceutical ingredient production and WHO prequalification remained unachieved, and export and workforce targets were missed. Lessons learnt Combined, the strategy’s cross-sectoral governance, regulatory strengthening, preferential centralized procurement and industrial incentives advanced local production. However, foreign exchange constraints, dependence on imported raw materials and financing and capacity gaps limited progress. Future efforts should prioritize WHO prequalification, upstream manufacturing, skilled workforce development, export competitiveness and sustainable financing while maintaining patient-centred objectives.
journal_name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: Accountability for large language models in health care
abstract: Abstract Large language models are entering clinical workflows faster than health-care institutions can assign responsibility for their failures. This situation is creating governance gaps with consequences that extend beyond individual patients to public health systems. The result is an accountability vacuum in which responsibility for harm mediated by large language models can be spread across clinicians, institutions and vendors. This responsibility gap distributes harm inequitably, particularly in low- and middle-income countries where regulatory infrastructure for digital health is still developing. We propose earned delegation as a predeployment standard: authority should be delegated only when evidence is proportionate to clinical risk, substantive human oversight is integrated and resourced, and responsibility for foreseeable failure modes is assigned in advance. To operationalize this standard, health systems should adopt a predeployment accountability charter specifying intended use, excluded use, validation evidence, oversight design, escalation pathways, auditability, subgroup performance review and named accountable parties. The charter should be integrated into existing institutional review, accreditation and procurement structures. Earned delegation provides a governance framework that health ministries, regulators and institutional leaders can adopt to ensure that use of large language models serves public health goals without outpacing them.
journal_name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: An oral health module for use in noncommunicable disease risk factor surveys
abstract: Abstract The World Health Organization (WHO) Global strategy and action plan on oral health 2023–2030 emphasizes the need to strengthen oral health information systems, including surveillance, to support public health action. Objective 5 of the Global strategy and action plan on oral health 2023–2030 calls for reliable, timely and policy-relevant data to inform decision-making, promote accountability and monitor progress, in other words, surveillance of oral diseases. However, most countries face challenges in identifying and applying practical tools to generate such population-level data. Until recently, the WHO STEPwise approach to noncommunicable disease risk factor surveillance (STEPS) included an oral health module that relied on self-reported data on perceived oral health and oral health-seeking behaviour. However, this module is outdated. In response to growing global demand and policy needs, the new STEPS oral health module updated the self-reported questionnaire and added a clinical assessment component that can be done by oral or non-oral care workers after a short training. This paper presents the rationale, development process, structure and policy implications of the updated module. The paper provides an outline of the updated module and evidence to support this new approach as a practical, scalable and aligned solution to one of the most persistent gaps in noncommunicable disease surveillance. As countries move towards universal health coverage and integration of oral health into broader noncommunicable disease strategies, the updated WHO STEPS oral health module is a timely and necessary improvement in surveillance of noncommunicable diseases and their risk factors.
journal_name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: Capacity for national health policy modelling; Bahrain; Kuwait; Oman; Qatar; Saudi Arabia; United Arab Emirates
abstract: Abstract Gulf Cooperation Council countries (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and United Arab Emirates) have similar governance structures, economic profiles and health system organization, creating an opportunity for collective action on health. Similarly, these countries have the same challenges including ageing populations, climate and heat risks, immigration, service delivery and disease profiles. We argue for the need to shift from opinion-driven policy discourse to computer-based, decision-focused policy analysis that is participatory, aware of inherent uncertainties surrounding decisions and context-specific. Despite areas of excellence, modelling capacity in these countries is fragmented and underresourced and models are rarely used to guide decision-making. The coronavirus disease 2019 pandemic saw very few decision-oriented models tied to local data from Gulf Cooperation Council countries. Gulf Cooperation Council models rely on outside modellers, which limits both the relevance and ownership of the findings. The coming decade will bring challenges that demand a change in how evidence is generated and applied. A structured, regionally anchored policy-modelling system can help governments test reforms, prioritize investments and engage in scenario planning before crises force reactive measures. Our paper outlines pragmatic steps towards effective health policy modelling based on four supporting pillars: (i) a regional co-produced modelling and knowledge translation strategy tied to priority decisions; (ii) embedded capacity-building across ministries, public health institutes and universities; (iii) a viable modelling stack that allows transparency, speed and reproducibility; and (iv) explicit communication and evaluation of the uncertainty of models to reduce risks within the choices made.
journal_name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: How a 10-minute bout requirement for physical activity affects guideline adherence estimates; Germany
abstract: Abstract Objective To examine how adherence to the World Health Organization’s (WHO) physical activity guidelines changes with and without the application of a 10-minute bout requirement. Methods We analysed accelerometry data from the baseline assessment of the German National Cohort, NAKO. Using predefined acceleration thresholds, we classified each participant’s volumes of moderate and vigorous intensity physical activity and compared these values with WHO guidelines. We analysed data with and without the 10-minute bout requirement. We used Welch’s analysis of variance and equal proportions tests to compare demographic and health characteristics between participants who met the activity guidelines and those who did not. Findings Of 63 134 participants, 22 226 (35.2%) met the guidelines with the bout requirement, while 62 532 (99.0%) met the guidelines without it. Participants who met the guidelines under each condition differed in demographic and health-related characteristics. For example, mean age was 48.6 years (SD: 13.0) among participants meeting the guidelines with the bout, 50.8 years (SD: 12.2) among those meeting only the guidelines without the bout and 60.8 years (SD: 10.4) among those meeting neither guidelines. Participants meeting the guidelines with the bout had a lower body mass index (25.2 kg/m2; SD: 4.0) than those meeting only the guidelines without the bout (27.0 kg/m2; SD: 5.1) and those meeting neither guidelines (30.6 kg/m2; SD: 7.1) Conclusion Removing the 10-minute bout requirement for accelerometry-measured activity volumes substantially increased estimated guideline adherence. The change has implications for interpreting time trends in guideline adherence and alters conclusions about which population subgroups meet the guidelines.
journal_name: Bulletin of the World Health Organization

title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention effectiveness and drug resistance in Plasmodium falciparum: a matched parallel cohort study; Kenya
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate seasonal malaria chemoprevention with sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine and amodiaquine in a semi-nomadic community in north-western Kenya, and to examine the relationship between parasite resistance and breakthrough infections. Methods A parallel cohort study conducted during the peak malaria season in 2024 involved 10 randomly selected villages in Turkana Central subcounty, where children younger than 5 years received seasonal malaria chemoprevention, and 10 matched villages in Turkana North subcounty (non-intervention cohort). We conducted surveillance of malaria symptoms weekly. The primary outcome was malaria-like symptoms plus a positive rapid diagnostic test result. We analysed Plasmodium falciparum genomic DNA in dried blood spot samples from children with symptomatic infections to identify pfdhfr and pfdhps gene substitutions associated with sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine resistance. Findings Children (198 in the intervention cohort and 200 in the non-intervention cohort) were followed until four weeks after the last chemoprevention cycle. In the intervention cohort, 72% (143/198) completed all five cycles. The incidence of malaria was significantly lower in the intervention than non-intervention cohort (adjusted incidence rate ratio 0.29; 95% confidence interval: 0.13–0.67). Plasmodium falciparum genomic DNA analysis of samples from 68 infected children showed that pfdhps gene mutations were more common in the intervention than non-intervention cohort and became more frequent as the number of treatment cycles increased. Conclusion Seasonal malaria chemoprevention with sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine and amodiaquine was associated with substantial protection against malaria in children in an area where sulfadoxine–pyrimethamine resistance was common. Treated children were more likely to harbour resistant parasites.

title: Enhanced online detection of lithium plating via a dynamic threshold generation strategy with aging effect compensation
abstract: Lithium plating (LP) is an abnormal side reaction during lithium-battery cycling that accelerates capacity loss and introduces safety risks. Existing online detection methods often suffer from LP-feature masking caused by gradual aging, baseline drift, and cell-to-cell inconsistency, which can delay warning and reduce adaptability. This study proposes a physically informed and experimentally validated cell-level online LP detection framework under controlled continuous charging conditions. The framework estimates a time-domain equivalent ohmic resistance using a second-order equivalent circuit model and an aging-aware OCV-SOC compensation strategy based on an iterative multi-objective Gaussian process. With the OCV-SOC tracking error controlled below 3.0% over the investigated aging stages, the compensated resistance sequence shows improved linear consistency with the EIS-based reference resistance. Based on this stabilized resistance sequence, sequential SOC-relative resistance (SRR) features are constructed to enhance localized high-SOC LP-associated mutations against macroscopic baseline offsets caused by condition variation, cell inconsistency, and residual polarization coupling. A semi-supervised dynamic K-means threshold strategy is further introduced to update battery-specific LP warning boundaries from historical and current high-SOC SRR features. Under the tested cell-level conditions, the proposed method advances the warning cycle by more than 15.0% relative to the selected baselines, while post-mortem SEM images show surface morphology consistent with the corresponding LP-associated warning states. The framework uses ordinary voltage-current cycling data and requires no specialized rest or pulse protocols under the tested continuous charging conditions. It therefore provides an experimentally validated cell-level algorithmic basis for future BMS-oriented validation.

title: Scalable and Interpretable Chemical Neurotoxicity Prediction via Multi-Modal Gated Fusion and ChemBERTa
abstract: Abstract Chemical exposure causes adverse neurological outcomes, highlighting the need for high-throughput screening of chemical neurotoxicity. However, existing computational methods rely on single-modality inputs and lack complementary molecular information to sufficiently enhance the accuracy and efficiency of neurotoxicity risk assessment. Here, we present NeuroToxPredictor, a scalable and interpretable multimodal framework built on a curated chemical neurotoxicity dataset for accurate and efficient chemical neurotoxicity prediction. It integrates graph attention networks and molecular fingerprints with ChemBERTa, a pretrained chemical language model that provides contextual encoding of SMILES. A gated fusion module adaptively weights these complementary representations according to their predictive relevance to enhance modality-specific weight allocation through a gating fusion mechanism. NeuroToxPredictor achieved competitive performance across five independent training seeds (AUC = 0.919 ± 0.004; accuracy = 0.845 ± 0.014; F1-score = 0.861 ± 0.011; recall = 0.884 ± 0.013; precision = 0.839 ± 0.024; MCC = 0.688 ± 0.028), outperforming both single-modality and reduced-modality baselines. It demonstrates strong generalizability with an AUC of 0.861, as externally validated on an independent set of 279 compounds. NeuroToxPredictor is deployed on a publicly platform (https://www.ai4environ.cn/NeuroToxPredictor), enabling an end-to-end intelligent workflow from chemical retrieval, neurotoxicity prediction, applicability-domain assessment, and large language model-assisted result interpretation.

title: How to ensure sustained investment in distributed photovoltaics in a market environment? – A multi-agent game based capacity planning model under the DLMP

Does Digital Transformation Drive the Adjustment of Bank Loan Structure? Evidence From China
abstract: ABSTRACT This article examines the impact of digital transformation on bank loan structure. We employ text mining and the entropy weight method to measure the five‐dimensional digital transformation index of banks and conduct an empirical analysis based on the panel data of 132 commercial banks in China from 2013 to 2022. The results indicate that digital transformation significantly drives the adjustment of various types of bank loan structures, increasing the proportion of unsecured loans, personal loans, medium‐ and long‐term loans, manufacturing loans, and green loans. In terms of the impact mechanism, improving information screening capability and enhancing risk control capability are two key channels through which digital transformation exerts its impact. Furthermore, the heterogeneity analysis reveals that the impact of digital transformation on loan structures varies among banks with different asset size, profitability, and management efficiency. Finally, we propose targeted suggestions for commercial banks and regulatory authorities.

title: How Brokers Enable Collective Identity Formation in Fragmented Industry Groups: The Case of Franciacorta Wineries
abstract: Abstract This study illuminates the role of brokers, that is, actors spanning inter‐organizational boundaries, in the process of collective identity formation in fragmented industry groups. Through an in‐depth longitudinal analysis of the Franciacorta wineries from the 1960s to the 1990s, we uncover how technical consultants acting as brokers facilitated collective identity formation by interacting with wineries through three mechanisms: translation, cross‐pollination, and integration. Our grounded model of collective identity formation reveals a distributed and co‐creative pathway to cohesive identity understandings built from the interstices of fragmented industry groups, through the co‐creation of practices, the weaving of social connections, and the facilitation of an optimally distinctive collective identity via inward adaptation and outward alignment between broader industry domains and local contexts. Our study advances theory by foregrounding the more inconspicuous practice‐level and social work that precedes, and ultimately determines the success of, the more visible identity‐defining moments that happen via symbolic representation or institutional codification.

title: Signaling uniqueness: The psycholinguistic effect of language precision on product perceptions
abstract: Abstract This research reveals a psycholinguistic effect whereby more precise words in product communications increase consumer perceptions of product uniqueness. Drawing on Categorization Theory ( Cognitive Psychology , 7, 1975, 573; Foundations of cognitive psychology: Core readings , 2002, MIT Press, 251), the authors propose that more precise words in product descriptions are situated deeper within their semantic categories and denote narrower subsets of referents, thereby eliciting perceptions of product uniqueness. Four experiments provide robust evidence supporting the “precise‐unique effect” and its underlying psycholinguistic mechanism driven by categorical depth. The findings further suggest that consumers' need for product uniqueness moderates the downstream effects of language precision on perceived attractiveness and behavioral intention via perceived uniqueness. This research contributes to the growing literature on language effects in consumer psychology and provides practical implications for making strategic lexical choices that enhance product positioning and differentiation.

title: Technology export controls and persistent firm innovation: evidence from cross-border technology transfer governance in China
A longitudinal and thematic analysis of entrepreneurial university research (1969–2024)
abstract: Abstract This study presents the evolution of the ‘Entrepreneurial University’ concept with the literature dating back to sub-concepts published on in 1969, pre-dating the Bayh-Dole Act in 1980 or Etzkowitz’ (1983) coining of the term. Studying this evolutionary path offers suggestions for future directions of research, considering how universities navigate increasingly diverse, yet complementary, expectations from society, industry, government and their own disciplines. This study identifies 5857 articles via Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar and uses keyword co-occurrence analysis to identify 240 topics and their interrelationships relating to the entrepreneurial university literature. The dataset also reveals journals and topics beyond the realm of R&D management journals, including entrepreneurship education, regional development, public policy and public administration. Longitudinal analysis of the topics indicates how the literature has engaged in perspectives that are increasingly based on complex systems views, including technological, social and environmental systems, accompanied by measurement of associated variables (notably in entrepreneurial self-efficacy, orientation and intentions). Despite the exponential growth of the literature, the growth of topics is plateauing, indicating a maturation of the concept. The literature can be considered to span five approximate eras that organically layer onto each other: (i) technology transfer, (ii) clustering, (iii) innovation systems, (iv) social systems, and (v) human-centered systems. The methodology allows for the 240 topics to be categorized and visualized as a hierarchically topic map, with topics clustering around seven core themes, providing a highly nuanced overview of the core and peripheral concepts relating to the Entrepreneurial University. Overall, this study contributes to a more comprehensive and nuanced understanding of the Entrepreneurial University concept and the evolution of the underlying literature. These contributions open doors to discuss future directions and extensions, and more critical analysis of which topics are more or less peripheral. For instance, we argue that sustainability and wellbeing are beyond scope of the original definitions, and that there is room for more research to on university administration, leadership and strategy. In the appendices, this study identifies top journals and seminal articles that epitomize each of the seven core themes, thus providing a starting point for scholars or policy makers interested in each of the themes.

title: Certified inside directors and tax planning: international evidence
Theorizing Cross‐Boundary Strategizing as Situated in Multilayered Supply Chains: A Strategy‐as‐Practice Approach to Supply Chain Management
abstract: ABSTRACT Supply chain strategy is increasingly recognized as a multilayered phenomenon, with firms strategizing not only within their own boundaries but across supply chain tiers, jurisdictions, and wider regulatory and ecological systems. Yet most existing supply chain management research tends to treat these tiers, jurisdictions, and systems as contexts for strategizing rather than as something strategizing helps to constitute, leaving the cross‐boundary character undertheorized. This article introduces the strategy‐as‐practice (SAP) lens as an epistemic tool for theorizing cross‐boundary strategizing in multilayered supply chains. Drawing on SAP's tripartite framework of practices, practitioners, and praxis (three Ps), we show that strategizing is inherently cross‐boundary, both implicitly through the knowledge practitioners draw on beyond their organization and explicitly through direct interaction with counterparts in other firms and institutions. We introduce three approaches SAP scholars use to conceptualize the complex systems within which strategizing is situated: a “tall” ontology separating intraorganizational from extraorganizational practice, a “flat” ontology treating strategizing as a web of practices stretching sideways, and a zoom‐in/zoom‐out approach tracing connectivity and identifying consequentiality across layers. Using a heuristic case of a European solar company and its Chinese supplier network, we show how each approach can shape the research orientation and theoretical payoff. We close with a research agenda for cross‐boundary strategizing in supply chains and argue that supply chains have the potential to extend SAP's own theoretical apparatus.

Accelerating construction decarbonization: biochar-Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC3) synergy for carbon mitigation and performance enhancement
abstract: The integration of biochar into cementitious materials has emerged as a groundbreaking approach to carbon sequestration, yet its high-dosage utilization and synergistic effects with sustainable cement formulations remain largely unexplored. This study proposes a novel design for low-carbon cement composites by incorporating high levels of biochar up to 30 wt% into both ordinary Portland cement (OPC) and Limestone Calcined Clay Cement (LC 3 ) systems, fundamentally altering their hydration kinetics, microstructural evolution, and mechanical performance. The findings reveal that biochar enhances the flowability of OPC pastes but slightly reduces that of LC 3 due to its high surface area and interparticle friction. It promotes the hydration process of OPC through internal curing and intensifies the early-stage reaction of LC 3 via nucleation effects. Additionally, biochar's well-developed pore network may facilitate the redistribution of calcium species and the diffusion of CO 2 , dramatically promoting carbonation and inducing the crystallization of vaterite and calcite, while simultaneously increasing the polymerization degree of C-(A)-S-H and reducing unhydrated clinker content for both OPC and LC 3 pastes. Despite porosity-induced reductions in the compressive strength of biochar-modified cement, plain LC 3 and LC 3 with 15% biochar achieved an 18% and 4% enhancement in flexural strength over plain OPC pastes, attributed to the formation of nanostructured rod-like ettringite. Critically, the LC 3 mix with 30% biochar exhibited remarkable carbon reduction efficiency, achieving a mitigation potential of up to 88.2 kg CO 2 eq./m 3 /MPa for flexural strength and 1.1 kg CO 2 eq./m 3 /MPa for compressive strength, indicating its potential to contribute to the cement industry's decarbonization efforts. Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of incorporating high biochar contents into LC 3 composites, highlighting their carbon mitigation potential for sustainable construction.

title: Effects of public space recreational service configurations on psychophysiological restoration: A virtual experiment
abstract: Urban public spaces are increasingly recognized as important settings for psychophysiological restoration, which refers to recovery from stress as reflected in changes in psychological states and physiological responses. However, existing research has focused mainly on individual dimensions of recreational environment, recreational facilities, or management services, whereas multidimensional configurations of public space recreational service (PSRS) remain insufficiently examined. Using a typical community park recreational zone in Shanghai as the prototype, 28 PSRS configuration scenarios were constructed. A total of 210 participants were included, and physiological measures of cardiac activity, skin conductance, and brain activity were collected, together with self-reported positive and negative affect and ratings of how restorative each scenario was. Linear mixed models showed that psychophysiological restoration responses differed across PSRS configuration scenarios. Within the tested range, greater water coverage was consistently associated with brain activity indicative of greater relaxation, greater improvement in positive affect, and higher ratings of how restorative the scenarios were. The proportion of greenery visible at eye level and the proportion of activity space showed different directions of association across restoration outcomes. Correlation analysis identified weak but statistically significant correlations between greater improvements in positive affect and more favorable heart rate variability responses, and between greater reductions in negative affect and greater reductions in skin conductance. These findings indicate that PSRS configurations are associated with different psychophysiological restoration outcomes, providing preliminary empirical evidence to inform restoration-oriented design and management of community park recreational zones.

title: Toward low-carbon management of Spartina alterniflora ecological restoration project in China: A multi-objective spatial optimization balancing carbon footprint and economic cost
Valorization of pumpkin-derived residues and waste: An analysis
abstract: The global agricultural sector faces increasing pressure to manage the substantial volumes of waste generated throughout pumpkin production, processing, and utilization, which traditionally represents both an economic burden and an environmental liability. This paper explores the valorization of pumpkin waste within a circular bioeconomy framework, evaluating the conversion of heterogeneous pumpkin-derived biomass into value-added food, nutraceutical, environmental, material, and energy products. Through a comprehensive synthesis of contemporary research, this paper demonstrates that pumpkin residues contain diverse recoverable compounds and structural fractions that can serve as feedstock for multiple valorization pathways, including nutraceuticals, advanced environmental remediation media, and industrial composite materials. Quantitative evidence from recent studies reveals a range of reported performance metrics, including polysaccharide extraction yields, improvements in protein solubility, and recovery or enrichment of phenolic compounds. In the realm of environmental engineering, pumpkin-derived adsorbents have been reported to achieve substantial contaminant removal efficiencies and adsorption capacities, while the incorporation of pumpkin-based fillers has been shown to modify and, in some formulations, improve the mechanical properties of composite and construction materials. Furthermore, energy conversion pathways for biogas and biodiesel production have demonstrated variable reported conversion and yield values depending on feedstock characteristics and process conditions. Despite these reported technical advances, the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to technically, economically, and environmentally viable larger-scale implementation remains a primary hurdle. Key future research imperatives include the standardization of feedstock characterization, harmonization of performance metrics and experimental protocols, rigorous long-term ecological safety assessments, and the adoption of predictive digital frameworks to address the challenges posed by inherent biomass heterogeneity. The integration of hierarchical and cascaded biorefinery architectures could facilitate the sequential recovery and utilization of multiple pumpkin waste fractions, thereby providing opportunities to improve overall resource utilization relative to isolated valorization routes, where supported by integrated technical, economic, and environmental assessments. This systemic approach provides a basis for advancing pumpkin waste valorization from individual laboratory-scale applications toward integrated and scalable biorefinery systems, with potential contributions to resource efficiency, reduced reliance on fossil-derived materials, and the development of more sustainable agro-industrial value chains.

title: Forest Conversion Reduces Soil Water Retention in Tropical Rainforest
abstract: ABSTRACT Extensive primary forests are being converted to secondary forests and plantations owing to human activities in recent decades, which have substantial effects on soil hydrological processes. However, the potential impact of forest conversion on soil water retention remains poorly understood. In this study, tropical primary forests (PF), secondary forests (SF), and rubber monocultures (RM) converted from tropical primary forests were selected on Hainan Island to examine the variation in soil water retention across three forest types and their controlling factors. We found that the primary forests exhibited significantly greater water retention capacity than secondary forests and rubber monocultures. However, secondary forests showed higher water retention than rubber monocultures in shallow soils but lower in deep soils. Similarly, primary forests demonstrated significantly greater soil water storage capacity than secondary forests and rubber monocultures, but secondary forests and rubber monocultures had obvious seasonal variations, which showed that secondary forests had a higher water storage capacity than rubber monocultures in the rainy season and displayed an opposite pattern in the dry season. The saturated hydraulic conductivity in primary forests was higher than that in secondary forests and rubber monocultures. Furthermore, forest types influenced soil properties, with secondary forests and rubber monocultures showing higher bulk density but lower soil capillary porosity compared with primary forests. Among all factors, soil porosity emerged as the dominant controller of water retention, where total porosity and capillary porosity accounted for 31.49% and 30.61% of variation respectively, while soil bulk density contributed relatively less (12.46%). These findings indicate that the conversion of tropical primary forests to secondary forests and rubber monocultures is detrimental to soil water retention and storage. Our results can provide scientific insights for forest development and management in the tropical rainforest.

abstract: Using new consumer-panel data across multiple grocery retailers, I estimate that an additional SNAP dollar raises food-at-home spending by 48 cents (s.e. 6 cents). This multi-retailer estimate is broadly in line with the 59-cent estimate in Hastings and Shapiro (2018), reinforcing evidence that SNAP benefits are non-fungible. Linking food-at-home and food-away-from-home purchases to nutritional data, I find that SNAP substantially increases calorie purchases but has little effect on nutritional composition per calorie. A behavioral welfare calibration implies an efficiency cost of in-kind provision of 12–14 cents per SNAP dollar; because this calculation is highly sensitive to the MPC, pinning down the parameter is quantitatively important.

Information, goal setting and performance: Experimental evidence
abstract: We investigate how information about relative performance shapes goal setting and subsequent performance. Combining a field experiment in a university course with a complementary laboratory experiment, we exogenously vary whether individuals receive baseline relative-performance feedback before or after setting non-binding goals. We document that uninformed individuals anchor goals primarily on subjective, often inaccurate beliefs. Providing information systematically corrects these distortions: individuals who underestimate their relative ability revise their goals upward, whereas overestimators adjust their targets downward. However, the effect of information on performance is limited – it only improves performance for underestimators in the field experiment. To explore the underlying mechanism, we leverage laboratory evidence to examine voluntary goal resetting. We find that delayed feedback affects final goals only when individuals reset them. Accordingly, treatment differences in final goals are substantially attenuated for underestimators but remain sizable for overestimators. Once this goal-adjustment process is accounted for, upward revisions among underestimators improve performance, whereas downward revisions among overestimators reduce challenge and impair ultimate performance.
