The effect of the mandatory disclosure of corporate tax returns on reporting bias
abstract: ABSTRACT How do investor reactions to the mandatory disclosure of firm tax information influence managers' reporting choices? To answer this question, we build a structural model of reporting bias, which we test with a unique data set of Turkish firms that have been mandated to publicly disclose their tax returns since 2009. We find that both book and tax income numbers are informative to investors. Structural estimates are consistent with disclosure of the tax report reducing both market incentives to manage book earnings and investor uncertainty about underlying firm value. Tax disclosure is associated with higher reported tax income, though the increase is not statistically significant. Counterfactual estimates suggest that book‐tax‐conformity could change financial and tax reporting biases, but lead to a lower quality information environment relative to the separate disclosure of book and tax reports.

title: The Effect of Small Quasi-Cash Rewards on Prosocial Behavior: The Case of Voluntary Plasma Donations
abstract: To better understand how prosocial behavior can be effectively encouraged, we study four unresolved issues: whether small rewards also motivate prosocial behavior, how short-term effects differ from longer-run behavioral adjustments, whether incentives induce substitution away from other prosocial activities, and whether reminders about existing rewards meaningfully influence behavior. We examine these issues in a long-run randomized field experiment across 12 donation centers of the Belgian Red Cross-Flanders. Donors normally receive one thank-you-coupon (worth €1.5) for a blood donation and two coupons for a plasma donation. Informing donors about the existing rewards increases plasma donations by 4.6% during the nine-month information period, although this effect fades with repeated reminders. Rewarding plasma donors with an extra coupon raises plasma donations by an additional 7.1% during the six-month reward period; this effect grows during the reward period but disappears immediately afterward. We also document a substitution effect; the plasma reward reduces blood donations by 3.3%. Survey evidence suggests that small rewards act as signals of increased need or as gifts eliciting reciprocity and that our findings may extend to volunteering decisions more broadly. This paper was accepted by Marie Claire Villeval, Behavioral Economics and Decision Analysis. Funding: This paper is based on research funded by the Belgian Red Cross-Flanders; the content reflects solely the views of the authors and not those of the Red Cross. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.08081 .

title: Diversity and/or Inclusion? Evidence from Disability Quota and Inclusion Laws in Brazil
abstract: This paper studies a fundamental trade-off created by quota laws and similar policies that seek to increase workplace diversity by mandating the hiring of disadvantaged populations. We show that firm-level responses to these policies can benefit members of the targeted population seeking entry into employment while imposing unintended costs on those already employed. Failure to account for this trade-off may lead firms and policymakers, when focused exclusively on the promotion of diversity, to pursue initiatives that may undermine the inclusion of incumbent underrepresented workers. To study this trade-off, we develop a conceptual framework and empirically examine employment outcomes for people with disabilities (PwD) in Brazil. Specifically, we study firms’ heterogeneous responses to an evolving institutional landscape: a 2012 reform that strengthened enforcement of Brazil’s pre-existing but largely ineffective disability quota law, and the subsequent 2015 Inclusion Law, a broader nondiscrimination statute that expanded societal protections for PwD. Using matched employer-employee data, we find that stricter quota enforcement significantly increased hiring of PwD, particularly among noncompliant firms that began recruiting from previously underutilized labor pools. Yet these gains in representation came with uneven consequences for inclusion: although job stability improved, wage gaps widened and career progression slowed for incumbent PwD relative to non-PwD, especially within firms that had failed to meet their quota targets. These adverse consequences persisted despite the enactment of the Inclusion Law, underscoring that nondiscrimination frameworks may be insufficient to offset the unintended consequences of quota laws.

title: Can Facebook Ads Prevent Malaria? Two Field Experiments in India
abstract: Two field experiments evaluate a nationwide Facebook malaria prevention campaign in India, finding effects concentrated in urban, more advantaged populations.

title: From Data to Decisions: Marketing Analytics, Mental Performance, and Firm Growth in an Emerging Market
abstract: Using a field experiment with 550 Rwandan firms, we show marketing analytics causally enhances entrepreneurs’ cognition and raises firm sales and profits.

title: Intersubjective resilience: Sustaining collective life under persistent life-and-death risk
abstract: How do organizations sustain collective life when exposure to life-and-death risk becomes a persistent condition of work? Based on an ethnographic study of two elite police units operating under continuous life-and-death risk, we find that organizations sustain coordinated collective life not by eliminating fear, resolving contradictions, or restoring stability, but by continually reorganizing these pressures into shared forms of action. We identify three interrelated organizing mechanisms. First, aspirational discipline transforms vulnerability into collective moral obligation by aligning individual striving with shared purpose. Second, paradoxical knotting enables members to act through enduring tensions, such as aggression and restraint or autonomy and obedience, without having to resolve them. Third, routine enactment restores coordinated action through recurring practices of training, reflection, and operational work. Together, these mechanisms explain how organizations maintain coherent and coordinated action when danger is an everyday condition of work. We conceptualize this capacity as intersubjective resilience : the collective accomplishment through which members repeatedly transform fear, contradiction, and disruption into coordinated action under persistent life-and-death risk.

title: ‘Don’t forget to post it on LinkedIn’: Identity regulation and the assetization of employees’ online selves
abstract: What happens to employees’ sense of who they are online when their organization tells them how to present themselves on LinkedIn? Companies increasingly intervene in employees’ professional social media presence through training programs and internal policies, encouraging them to treat their profile as an asset to be cultivated for future return. Drawing on a 2-year digital ethnography of an in-company LinkedIn training program in a French state-owned enterprise, this article shows how the training regulates participants’ sense of their online selves by first denying that their profile has anything to do with who they are, and only then inviting them to reinvest it with personal meaning within the frame this denial has established. Regulation here operates on the identity stakes of the profile itself: on how much of themselves participants take it to carry. The uneven ways participants took up this invitation point to the entanglement of identity regulation and assetization, and to the capacity of an online self, once assetized, to keep generating value for the organization long after the person behind it has disengaged.

title: The moderating role of tough love on relations between servant leadership and follower outcomes
abstract: Is servant leadership really a Disneyland-inspired fantasy of sunshine, lollipops, and hand-holding that makes followers complacent and lowers the bottom line of organizations, as critics claim? This criticism overlooks that servant leaders, striving to bring out the full potential in followers, do not only give positive strokes but may also provide followers with critical feedback. To assess the role of critical feedback in mitigating the flaws of servant leadership raised by critics, this study introduces tough love, the delivery of criticism with a positive tone and clear intent to help recipients overcome their deficiencies. We hypothesize that the relationship between servant leadership and key outcomes, such as follower performance, is strengthened the more servant leaders provide followers with tough love. We contend that tough love is appreciated by followers, solidifies relationships with their leaders, and helps them to grow through self-expansion. We reason that this growth benefits their work behaviors and attitudes. With multi-source field data covering three points in time, controlling for positive and negative feedback and prior levels of dependent variables, tough love is shown to moderate relations between servant leadership and both in-role performance and organizational citizenship behaviors, with mixed results for creativity and turnover intentions.

title: Ownership, Diversity and the Effectiveness of Government‐backed Financial Support during a Systemic Crisis: Evidence from One Million UK SMEs
abstract: Abstract Using proprietary data on over one million UK Small and Medium‐Sized Enterprises (SMEs) from 2017 to 2024, we examine how ownership composition and director diversity condition the impact of government‐backed Covid‐19 loan programmes on normal (non‐Covid) loan default outcomes. Building on the Behavioural Theory of the Firm and the Attention‐Based View, we develop Attention‐Based Governance (ABG) as a conceptual lens for explaining how SMEs deploy government‐backed slack during systemic crises. Our results show that SMEs with multiple owners from the same family are more effective than single‐owner SMEs in managing Covid support, indicating stronger internal collective oversight and discipline. Furthermore, SMEs with domestic institutional owners and female directors exhibit stronger capability and discipline, while those with foreign institutional owners or foreign directors display higher default risk on normal loans. Additional analysis reveals that foreign‐owned firms are least likely to default on the government‐backed Covid loans themselves. This finding reflects the selective allocation of managerial attention towards highly visible, publicly guaranteed debt to protect reputational capital with global stakeholders. Overall, our study shows how ownership composition and director diversity direct managerial attention and determine whether public funding leads to stronger financial resilience or heightened default risk at the firm level.

title: How followers evaluate social media influencers’ communication: A persuasion‐based perspective and research agenda
abstract: Abstract Scholarly research on social media influencers is expanding. Although the field has grown substantially, its research base remains fragmented. This is largely due to the multitude of disciplines upon which influencer research draws and to the diverse perspectives applied to the subject. While some studies highlight the benefits of social media influencers’ endorsements for brands, others stress the potentially adverse impact of influencer persuasion‐based content on the receivers. The persuasive nature of influencer communication on social media is implicitly acknowledged in past literature, across domains. However, there is a lack of comprehensive understanding of how receivers evaluate and respond to influencers’ persuasive communication and the conditions that promote, or inhibit compliance with their message. Such understanding is pivotal for reconciling existing fragmentation and advancing the field. This paper systematically reviews the influencer literature, integrating knowledge from psychological theories of persuasion. Theoretically, it offers an integrative perspective on how influencers’ attempts at persuasion are evaluated by receivers, while proposing an extensive agenda for further research in this rapidly burgeoning domain. The paper also highlights applications for business practice and implications for policymakers.

title: How Siemens Evolved Its AI Lab for Impact
abstract: Corporate innovation hubs (CIHs) are established to help large firms explore emerging technologies, yet most fail to create a lasting impact. Siemens’s AI Lab is a rare exception. In a longitudinal study (2017–2025), we show how Siemens avoided “innovation theater” by operating its AI Lab as a dynamic platform that continuously recalibrated its goals, value proposition, and operating model. A three-phase evolution model—from exploring AI use cases, to establishing itself as an AI pioneer, to facilitating AI-driven transformation—illustrates how CIHs can remain relevant over time. Above all, the Lab created value by enabling others to innovate, not by owning innovation.

title: Club research: A review and research agenda
Building antifragile humanitarian supply chains: the role of transactive memory systems and big data analytics culture
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how big data analytics culture (BDAC) contributes to the development of antifragile humanitarian supply chains. Specifically, this study examines the mediating role of transactive memory systems (TMSs) and the moderating role of the frequency of natural disasters in the relationship between TMS and antifragility. Design/methodology/approach The authors collected 290 survey responses from key humanitarian professionals involved in disaster response operations. To test the proposed relationships among BDAC, TMS, antifragility and disaster frequency, the authors used Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). Findings The results of this study reveal that BDAC enhances antifragility only when fact-based decision-making improves information credibility, member specialization and coordination, core manifestations of TMS. TMS fully mediates the relationship between BDAC and antifragility, while the positive effect of TMS on antifragility is stronger in contexts with frequent natural disasters. Originality/value This paper advances the literature by empirically demonstrating TMS as the underlying mechanism linking BDAC to antifragility in humanitarian supply chains, showing how TMS operate as microfoundations of dynamic capabilities that enable collective sensing, coordinated decision-making and the reconfiguration of practices.
journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

title: Two sides of the aisle: exploring coping, stress and behavioral avoidance among travelers and airline staff after aviation crisis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how coping strategies influence posttraumatic stress symptoms and subsequent behavioral outcomes among airline employees and travelers following aviation crises. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the transactional model of stress and coping, survey data were collected from 598 respondents, including airline employees and travelers. The study integrates structural modeling with configurational analysis (fsQCA) of qualitative interview data to examine both net relationships and configurations of conditions associated with behavioral outcomes. Findings Problem-focused and emotion-focused coping enhances employees’ readiness for return-to-work and reduces travelers’ flight avoidance, whereas avoidance coping increases avoidance behavior but shows no impact on work readiness. Social support seeking strengthens employee recovery but has limited influence on traveler behavior. Posttraumatic stress symptoms mediate the relationships between coping strategies and behavioral outcomes. Media exposure weakens adaptive coping effects and amplifies avoidance, while perceived organizational support enhances recovery. Configurational findings reveal asymmetric pathways, showing that flight avoidance may arise even under low stress when avoidance coping and media exposure combine, whereas return-to-work readiness can occur despite high stress when institutional support is present. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of strengthening organizational support systems and managing media communication to facilitate workforce recovery and restore traveler confidence after aviation crises. Originality/value This study integrates employee and traveler perspectives within a unified coping framework and demonstrates how both individual relationships and stakeholder-specific configurations are associated with post-crisis behavioral responses.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Status and Stretch: The Effect of Network Status on Collaboration with ‘Distant’ Partners
abstract: Although ‘distant’ partners provide diverse information and resources, firms tend to form ‘local’ ties, favoring partners who are more similar, familiar, or spatially proximate. This underscores the need to investigate how distant ties originate—specifically, identifying the conditions under which firms are more likely to establish distant ties, and when they are not. In this study, we emphasize network status as a key determinant in the formation of interfirm distant ties. Analyzing syndication networks of U.S. venture capital (VC) firms, we establish two sets of key findings. First, we emphasize a balancing imperative in partner selection, whereby firms tend to choose partners that are ‘local’ in one dimension but ‘distant’ in another. Second, and more importantly, our results demonstrate that network status significantly shapes the balancing imperative: high-status firms exhibit a stronger propensity to bridge multiple tie distances simultaneously, unless social distance is involved. These findings extend our knowledge on status and network dynamics.

title: Looking Back, Moving Forward: A Guiding Framework for Future Research in Supply Chain Management
Beyond Compliance: The Impact of Sustainable Water Management Performance on Firm Value amid Global Water Challenges
What, how, and where: the effects of multidimensional CSR communication strategies focusing on content, framing, and target
Ownership structure and the international expansion of German firms
abstract: Despite decades of falling trade barriers and advancing globalization, most multinational enterprises (MNEs) never venture beyond their home region. We argue that part of the explanation lies in ownership structure: who ultimately controls the firm determines how broadly it operates and how freely its geographic scope can be adjusted. Drawing on the attention-based view, we derive eight hypotheses about how ownership origin, international experience, and concentration shape the breadth of geographic scope and the direction of its adjustment over time. Using a large panel of German MNEs, we show that domestic ownership is associated with broader scope and greater propensity for upward adjustment, with the advantage strongest for internationally experienced owners. Ownership concentration constrains the level of geographic scope but not whether it expands or contracts. These findings provide the first evidence on ownership and geographic scope for developed-country MNEs and reorient theoretical debate from resource transfer to organizational authorization.

title: The Pursuit of Security: How Loneliness Shapes Consumers' Preference for Simple Versus Complex Packaging Designs
abstract: ABSTRACT This research examines how loneliness influences consumers' preferences for the design (simple vs. complex) of product packaging and uncovers the underlying mechanisms across 7 studies, including 1 survey and 6 experimental designs ( N = 1636). The results show that loneliness increases consumers' preference for complex packaging designs, which is driven by the desire for symbolic security. Moreover, consumers' security trait negatively moderates the relationship between loneliness and desire for symbolic security, such that the positive effect of loneliness on the desire for symbolic security is stronger among consumers with lower levels of security trait and weaker among those with higher levels of security trait. These findings advance the research fields of sensory marketing and offer actionable insights for marketers, suggesting that consumers' loneliness should be considered when developing packaging strategies involving simple or complex designs.

title: Can AI-generated images match human-generated images in inspiring travel? A visual feature analysis of audience perceptions and visit intention
Organizational Zemblanity: How Organizational Learning Can Reinforce Rigidity, Error, and Misalignment
abstract: Organizational learning can help organizations improve and adapt, but it can also reinforce error and misalignment. These negative outcomes are often interpreted as implementation problems or as signs of incomplete learning. We instead examine the possibility that dysfunction can arise from learning processes themselves, even when those processes operate as intended. We review 290 articles to identify recurring assumptions in the literature and the conditions under which they do not hold. We then identify three mechanisms that can turn learning systems into sources of rigidity and misalignment, and conceptualize the self-reinforcing trajectory produced by their interaction as learning-based organizational zemblanity. Our review shows how organizational learning can generate both adaptive and dysfunctional trajectories and outlines a research agenda on identifying and interrupting negative learning trajectories.

title: Imagining the Invisible: Judicial Epistemology, Carceral Regulation, and the Liberal State
abstract: ABSTRACT In many systems judges exercise judicial review over prison officials' decisions. However, judges are often symbolically, institutionally, and practically distant from prison realities. In the current paper, we explore how judges negotiate their limited epistemological awareness of prison through the lens of epistemic injustice. Drawing on interviews with 17 (retired) Israeli Supreme Court justices regarding their prison administrative review decisions, we identify three epistemic gaps: first, the prison's heterotopic nature; second, the tension between commitment to liberty and authorizing the “pains of imprisonment” at sentencing; and third, the division of labor between sentencing and prison phases. The findings suggest that judges bridge these epistemological gaps through three imaginaries: (a) “ epistemic distancing ”; (b) “ epistemic assimilation ”; and (c) “ parallel epistemology ”. These epistemic imaginaries allow judges to compensate for their experiential absence but also structure their judicial oversight, shaping how courts administratively regulate imprisonment without fully confronting its lived realities. The findings show how judicial imaginaries of prison are shaped through top‐down narrative constructions rather than bottom‐up experiential encounters and include self‐produced “epistemic estrangement” from the prison world. We further examine the implications of these epistemic blind spots, demonstrating how they enable the legitimization of carceral power while obscuring and marginalizing the lived experiences of incarcerated individuals.

title: Policy Agendas in Coalition Agreements: The Enduring Influence of Policy Inheritance
abstract: ABSTRACT New governments frequently inherit issues from their predecessors, and as a result, various policy problems tend to remain on the agenda for many years. Previous research examining the role of policy inheritance has focused mainly on the agenda during a government's term in office. These studies find that because governments must first contend with the problems they inherit, there is considerably less room for new issues to emerge on the agenda. This study seeks to examine the idea of policy inheritance through the lens of coalition agreements. Coalition agreements, a feature of multiparty governments, are drafted shortly after elections and reflect the outcome of the political struggle. For this reason, one can expect that coalition agreements contain mostly issues that parties regard as important. By implication, changes in the coalition agreements' issue agenda would be a function of the political change produced by the electoral cycle, rather than of inheritance. Analyzing coalition agreements in three countries—Israel, the Netherlands, and Norway—across 42 elections, we find no evidence for this assumption. Agendas in coalition agreements do not vary with changes in the party composition of the coalition, changes in the ideological distance between parties, or changes in the party holding the office of Prime Minister. This indicates that even when new coalition governments are preparing for their term in office, inheritance remains the primary driver of agenda‐setting.

title: Organizational Trustworthiness: A Commitment Account
abstract: This paper proposes a commitment account of organizational trustworthiness and describes its application to healthcare organizations. On this account, a trustworthy organization makes commitments it is competent to keep and it has a track record of keeping them. We argue that, unlike other conceptions of trustworthiness, the commitment account best fits the impersonal, diffuse nature of healthcare organizations.

title: Ambient Digital Scribes as Educational Mirrors: Closing the Feedback Gap in Physician Communication
abstract: Healthcare systems are rapidly adopting ambient digital scribe (ADS) technologies to reduce documentation burden and improve efficiency in clinical care. Although these systems are typically framed as technical tools that listen to patient dialogue, they also capture physician speech, creating an underexplored opportunity for ethical and pedagogical innovation. At present, everyday patient-physician interactions largely occur without systematic reflection, producing a persistent 'feedback gap' in which deleterious communication often goes unnoticed. This paper argues for a reframing of ADS as 'educational mirrors', using AI-generated annotations and transcripts to provide physicians with formative feedback on communicative patterns and language that shape patient experience. We theorize the benefits of this reframing on a stakeholder-specific basis, analyze central ethical concerns, and propose governance safeguards and careful implementation to minimize potential harms. With appropriate consent, validation, and equity-centered design, reframing ADS technologies could help close the feedback gap and promote more ethical clinical care.

title: Provision of Appropriate Care as a Source of Clinician Distress
abstract: Clinicians are dedicated to helping others, healing the sick, and protecting the healthy from becoming sick. Obviously, clinicians would prefer to help others without causing them any distress. But, appropriate care includes procedures and interventions that can cause pain, distress, and sometimes even suffering. Clinicians must therefore accept that they frequently have to cause their patients to experience pain and distress. Because patients' distress tends to be short-lived, the resulting distress on the treating clinicians is typically minimal. However, when provision of appropriate care requires clinicians to cause their patients to suffer, the clinicians themselves can experience significant distress. This distress can reduce team cohesion, increase clinician burnout, and undermine clinicians' confidence in the care they provide. In this essay, we describe this source of clinician distress, assess its implications for clinical practice, and begin to consider ways to address it.

title: Non-Anthropocentric Research Ethics? A Reply to the Commentaries
abstract: Which are the normative foundations of our moral interaction with non-human fellows in the planetary ecosystem? The commentaries published on my recent Target Article (Salloch 2026) reach a remarka...

abstract: Our target article argued that federated learning (FL) generates a distinctive variety of opacity—federation opacity, in which no party can access, analyze, or curate the model’s full training data...

title: (In)congruent synergies? Discursive boundary-spanning between the Italian anti-gender galaxy and anti-trans groups
abstract: This article investigates increasing alignment between the anti-gender galaxy and anti-trans groups by looking at the symbolic synergies that these two collective endeavors create in and through social media discourse. Building on social movement theory, we examine processes of discursive boundary spanning through which ecclesial and right-wing actors, dedicated anti-gender organizations, and anti-trans groups converge when discussing gender-related issues at large on social media, aligning around similar agendas, objects of interest, priorities, and frames, while setting aside differences that might hinder their collaboration. Empirically, the study relies on a mixed-method analysis of Facebook and Instagram posts published between 2021 and 2023 by twenty-two prominent actors mobilizing around anti-gender and anti-trans claims in Italy. Combining topic modeling with a computational adaptation of frame semantic grammar and qualitative frame analysis, we examine patterns of discursive convergence across the four sectors as well as the ideological differences that are bracketed to sustain it. Our findings reveal the existence of a transversal and yet fragile cross-sectoral discursive convergence. While all four sectors align around a limited set of shared interests and priorities, stronger discursive commonalities are found between anti-trans actors, dedicated anti-gender organizations and right-wing actors. Moreover, although common diagnostic frames emphasize the protection of women and children from gender ideology, divergent prognostic frames and long-term horizons persist within and across sectors.

title: Similar predicted fatal-crash risk, different contribution architectures: A temporally validated analysis of vehicle–pedestrian crashes in Japan
From coordination to selective intervention: an on-demand coordination method for adaptive traffic signal control, dynamic speed regulation, and route guidance
abstract: Coordinating multiple traffic interventions does not necessarily lead to safer or more efficient traffic operations, because redundant or poorly timed interventions may introduce additional disturbances. This study moves beyond the conventional focus on how multiple interventions should cooperate by formulating coordination as a hybrid decision-making problem that determines whether additional interventions are needed, which interventions to activate, and how to implement them. Accordingly, an on-demand coordination method is proposed to selectively coordinate adaptive traffic signal control, dynamic speed regulation, and route guidance in emerging mixed traffic comprising human-driven vehicles and connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). The method employs two functionally differentiated deep reinforcement learning agents to decouple primary signal control from auxiliary intervention selection while jointly optimizing safety and efficiency. To support risk-aware decision-making, extreme value theory (EVT) is integrated into the control framework to characterize approach-specific tail crash risk. Specifically, a non-stationary generalized extreme value model is developed to capture extreme traffic conflicts and derive value-at-risk estimates, enabling the controller to identify and prioritize severe risk states that may be overlooked by average or instantaneous safety measures. The proposed method is evaluated at two signalized intersections through simulations across various CAV market penetration rates. Compared with non-coordinated and coordinated benchmarks, the proposed method consistently reduces average waiting time and generally reduces upper-tail crash risk. These safety and efficiency benefits are accompanied by a moderate increase in fuel consumption, with the trade-off becoming less pronounced as CAV penetration increases. The findings of this study support a shift from indiscriminate multi-intervention control toward selective coordination and highlight the potential to extend EVT-based safety analysis from post hoc risk assessment to active control decision-making.

title: Global progress in preventing violence against children through data and evidence for action
Child sexual abuse in Canada: Prevalence, perpetrators, and characteristics
abstract: Background Detailed information about the epidemiology of child sexual abuse (CSA) in Canada is lacking. Objective To estimate the prevalence of CSA; determine if CSA prevalence differs by gender and age group; and describe CSA characteristics, including perpetrators, age of onset, age of cessation, duration, and chronicity. Participants and setting Adults aged 18–49 years provided retrospective accounts of CSA in a cross-sectional survey (Childhood Adversity and Resilience-Youth and Early Adulthood Research Study [CARe-YEARS]; N = 3767; May 2024). Methods CSA included non-contact CSA (looking at or exposing private parts) and three types of contact CSA (touching private parts, attempted forced sex, and completed forced sex). Descriptive statistics were conducted. Gender and age-group differences in prevalence were tested with logistic regression. Results The prevalence of CSA was 25.8% overall, including 21.0% any contact CSA and 14.7% non-contact CSA. Women and gender-diverse individuals disproportionately experienced CSA compared to men. The overall prevalence of CSA by perpetrator type included 9.1% friend/schoolmate; 8.4% boyfriend/girlfriend; 4.8% unknown adolescent; 4.3% known adult (non-family); 4.2% unknown adult; 3.6% cousin; 2.1% parent/stepparent/parent's boyfriend or girlfriend; 2.0% grandparent, uncle, or aunt; and 1.4% sibling. Between 22 and 33% of survivors did not recall additional characteristics of the abuse. Of those who reported, the mean age of onset was 11.0 years and one in four reported that CSA occurred six or more times. Age group trends (18 to 29 years and 30 to 49 years) indicated declines in some CSA subtypes. Conclusions Findings from the current study provide detailed evidence of survivors' CSA experiences, addressing important knowledge gaps to inform policy and CSA prevention.

title: In Harm’s Way: How the 2024 U.S. Election Might Affect Sexual- and Gender-Minority Health
abstract: Immediately after taking office in 2025, the current U.S. presidential administration established an unprecedented number of policies hostile to sexual- and gender-minority (SGM) populations: restricting the rights and social legitimacy of transgender individuals, curtailing youth access to gender-affirming medical care, terminating federal research and data collection on sexual and gender diversity, and restricting open discussion of sexual and gender diversity in educational settings. These events pose a greater threat to SGM health than previous state-level hostile policies, because of their scope, speed, and scale, and because they serve to institutionalize animus toward gender-minority populations into U.S. law and policy. We use extant research on structural stigma to predict the most likely mental and physical health consequences of these events, and we also forecast health consequences for the family members of SGM individuals and individuals whose paid employment involves SGM populations. We review evidence for the mechanisms through which these effects may unfold (institutional changes, increased minority stress, decreased social safety, and behavioral changes) and identify subpopulations at disproportionate risk (gender-minority populations, youth, those facing intersectional stigma, and those with existing health vulnerabilities). We conclude with a call for targeted efforts to ameliorate these negative health consequences, and we review research indicating that increasing social support and safety is the most effective and feasible strategy for doing so. We call for urgent, community-based efforts to increase the number and quality of nurturant social connections among all individuals who have been placed in harm’s way by the changed U.S. political climate.

title: Introduction to Rural Child Maltreatment and Child Welfare Practice
More Attractive, More Heterosexual, Less Sexual? Perceptions of People with Physical Disabilities Across Observer Sex and Sexual Orientation
Who Is Using Pornography Generated by Artificial Intelligence? Correlates of AI-Porn Use and Familiarity in an Australian Adult Sample
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are rapidly transforming how people create and experience sexual content, including the emergence of AI-generated pornography (AI-porn). Yet little is known about who is engaging with this evolving medium. This study presents findings from a cross-sectional survey (data collected in 2025) of 367 heterosexual Australian adults (age range = 19–87 years, M = 39.07, SD = 13.43; 52.5% men, 44.8% women [and 2.2% non-binary, excluded from inferential analyses due to small cell sizes]) examining demographic, ideological, and relational correlates of AI-porn familiarity and use. Overall, 26.0% of participants reported having used AI-porn and were moderately familiar with it. Regression analyses showed that men and younger participants were significantly more likely to be familiar with and to have used AI-porn. Ideological factors (religiosity, political orientation) and relational factors (relationship status, relationship and sexual satisfaction) were not associated with use. These findings suggest that engagement with AI-porn is emerging most prominently among digitally curious younger men, yet appears ideologically broad and not linked (in this data set) to relationship dissatisfaction. As AI tools enable new forms of personalized, creative sexual expression, understanding who is exploring these technologies can help researchers and clinicians track evolving norms around intimacy, fantasy, and sexual media in the digital age.

title: The Shock‐Buffering Role of School District Savings
abstract: Abstract School districts operate in an unstable revenue environment, with changes in state transfers being a source of uncertainty. District savings, in the form of unrestricted general fund balance, could provide a tool for maintaining budget stability. This study provides the first cross‐state examination of school fund balance. First, descriptive statistics illustrate variations in state laws regarding district fund balance and in the average balance levels. Second, districts adjust savings based on revenue risk exposure, but the capacity to save also matters. Lastly, districts starting a year with a higher fund balance experience smaller spending gaps when state aid declines.

title: Introduction
Optimal control strategy for compressed air energy storage under off-design conditions
A physics-informed causal learning framework for power consumption of logistics drones
TinyBatteryNet: A compact neural architecture for embedded battery remaining useful life prediction across battery domains
Optimal design and thermodynamic performance analysis of a novel isothermal reservoir supercritical compressed CO2 energy storage system
AC OPF learning via modular decomposition and adaptation to topology changes
abstract: We propose a novel framework for efficiently solving the AC optimal power flow (OPF) problem under varying grid topologies. Traditional learning-based approaches to OPF often retrain entire models when the network topology changes, leading to high computational cost and limited generalization. The proposed approach exploits the fact that different components of the OPF problem respond to topology changes to varying degrees: device-level operating limits remain largely unaffected, the network equations are modified locally around a tripped line, whereas the resulting optimal operating point may change throughout the network. It consists of two complementary training phases. In Phase I (modular pretraining), the OPF learning task under the intact grid topology is decomposed into three sequential subtasks (voltage setpoint prediction, power generation estimation, and generation cost computation) representing distinct functional mappings. In Phase II (adaptive learning), these pretrained modules are jointly fine-tuned for new topologies using a composite loss that combines supervised objectives with physics-informed regularization for branch-flow accuracy, nodal power balance, and operational constraint satisfaction. Extensive evaluations on benchmark grids demonstrate accurate predictions for the intact grid as well as for grids with seen and unseen contingencies. In our numerical experiments, at most 60 N − 1 contingency topologies are used for adaptation, and the largest mean prediction error among the reported variables under unseen topologies is approximately 3.1%.

title: Tokenizing battery degradation: a physics-informed and uncertainty-aware framework for state-of-health estimation
abstract: Accurate and trustworthy estimation of State of Health (SOH) is essential for the safe and efficient operation of modern battery management systems. While data-driven methods have achieved high accuracy, they often lack physical grounding and fail to provide reliable confidence metrics for their predictions, posing risks in safety-critical applications. In this work, we introduce TBD-SOH, an SOH estimation framework that combines physics-informed feature construction with uncertainty-aware regression. Specifically, each charging cycle is represented as a fused cycle-level token constructed from two complementary sources: statistical descriptors of charging behavior and a hardware-free pseudo-impedance representation derived from routine voltage and current measurements in the frequency domain. The pseudo-impedance branch is introduced as a degradation-sensitive proxy rather than a direct electrochemical impedance spectroscopy measurement. In addition, an MC dropout-based regression head is adopted to provide confidence intervals together with point estimates. Comprehensive experiments on the public MIT and HUST battery datasets demonstrate that TBD-SOH achieves high accuracy, outperforming conventional deep learning models. More importantly, its uncertainty estimates are shown to be dynamically responsive to prediction difficulty, and provide a new reference point for developing trustworthy and reliable battery health monitoring systems.

title: Using cross-regional grid interconnection to relieve growing energy storage demand in renewable energy integration: A case study from China
abstract: With the rapid growth of wind and solar generation, power systems face increasing balancing and energy storage needs. Cross-regional interconnection provides spatial flexibility through tie-line power exchange, yet the implications of tie-line scheduling flexibility for capacity planning remain insufficiently understood. This paper uses the Gansu–Shandong–Zhejiang interconnected system in China to quantify how tie-line scheduling timescales affect storage requirements for bulk energy shifting and system balancing. Within a common capacity planning and dispatch optimization framework, three stylized tie-line scheduling strategies are compared: Daily Fixed, Monthly Fixed, and Annual Fixed, representing decreasing levels of scheduling flexibility. Results show that greater tie-line scheduling flexibility changes the optimal capacity configuration, particularly the required battery energy storage (BES) capacity. Compared with Annual Fixed, Daily Fixed reduces BES capacity additions by 59.2% and total system cost by 22.8%. Sensitivity analyses further show that this advantage remains robust to variations in storage parameters and tie-line capacity. These findings indicate that the planning value of cross-regional interconnection depends substantially on its operational flexibility.

title: Life cycle and techno-economic analysis of hydrogen-based ship propulsion concepts in light of future regulatory environments
abstract: The shipping sector faces ongoing challenges in developing pathways to net-zero emission concepts. Hydrogen as an energy carrier offers the opportunity to provide a low- to zero-emission solution, depending on the fuel production pathway. However, high production costs as well as logistical challenges in transporting the fuel globally hinder the economic competitiveness compared to current fossil fuel alternatives. To enable a faster adoption of zero-emission concepts, regulators such as the European Union and the International Maritime Organization have developed mechanisms that provide financial incentives and regulatory specifications. This paper investigates hydrogen-based propulsion concepts for the use case of a short-sea RoPax ferry and a deep-sea liquid hydrogen carrier. System models of different propulsion concepts are used to model their techno-economic performance under different well-to-tank hydrogen production and supply pathways. The proposed IMO GHG Fuel Intensity standards and corresponding penalties/incentives are included in the techno-economic comparison. Results are compared to a fossil-fueled baseline case and a battery-electric benchmark.

title: Risk-aware and network-compatible bidding of aggregated DER under energy-as-a-service model
Frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid renewable P2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers
abstract: Renewable power-to-hydrogen (ReP2H) enables large-scale renewable energy utilization and supports the decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors, such as chemicals and maritime transport, via hydrogen-based renewable ammonia and methanol fuels. As a result, utility-scale ReP2H projects are expanding worldwide. However, off-grid ReP2H systems exhibit low inertia due to their converter-dominated nature, making frequency security a critical concern. Although recent studies show that electrolyzers can contribute to frequency regulation (FR), their support capability depends on operating states and loading levels, creating a trade-off between hydrogen output and frequency security. To address this challenge, this work develops a unified co-optimization framework for frequency security-aware production scheduling of utility-scale off-grid ReP2H systems coordinating heterogeneous electrolyzers. A system-level frequency response model is established to capture multi-stage FR from alkaline water electrolyzers (AWEs), proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs), and other resources, including ammonia-fueled generators retrofitted in co-located chemical plants, battery energy storage, and wind turbines (WTs). Stage-wise transient frequency security constraints are derived, reformulated into tractable forms, and embedded into production scheduling, enabling coordinated on/off switching and load allocation across electrolyzers to maximize hydrogen output under uncertain renewable power input while enforcing frequency security constraints. Case studies based on real-world systems demonstrate that the proposed approach allows hydrogen plants to replace 55.52% and 96.85% of FR reserves from WTs and AFGs, respectively, while improving the system-level net hydrogen yield by substantially reducing ammonia-fuel consumption. Year-long simulations show an average 28.96% increase in annual net profit resulting from reduced reliance on conventional reserves.

title: Assessing industrial land-use efficiency at parcel scale: Actual vs. expected economic outputs across diverse parcel types and spatial conditions
abstract: As urban development shifts toward the optimization of existing built-up areas, identifying inefficient industrial land is increasingly important for targeted land renewal and stock-oriented land governance. Although industrial land-use efficiency (ILUE) has been widely assessed at industrial-park and administrative scales, large-area parcel-scale evaluation remains constrained by limited fine-grained land use information and parcel-scale economic data. To address these limitations, this study develops a parcel-scale ILUE evaluation method by comparing actual economic output (AEO) with expected economic output (EEO), which refers to the reasonably expected output of a parcel given its functional type and spatial conditions. Firstly, using multisource spatiotemporal data, 13,510 industrial parcels in Beijing are classified into four functional types, i.e., technology office, commercial service, manufacturing, and warehouse & logistics, and characterized by built, socio-economic, and ecological conditions. Then, parcel-scale AEO is estimated by integrating gridded economic information with administrative industrial statistics, while EEO is estimated using cyclic random forest regression (CRF-R) to capture nonlinear spatial condition–output relationships. Our results reveal 3684 inefficient parcels, primarily concentrated in southern and eastern peri-urban districts. Compared with observed business revenue and documented renewal projects, the downscaled AEO better captures parcel-scale economic variation, while the inefficient parcels identified using CRF-R achieved a 76.7% project-level spatial correspondence rate. Based on feature importance analysis, the study gives type-specific governance recommendations, including improving transit accessibility for office and commercial land, supplementing residential and public service for manufacturing land, and increasing development intensity and road accessibility for logistics-oriented parcels, thereby providing a practical diagnostic tool for differentiated industrial land renewal.

title: Dual-path clean cooking sustainability in Uganda: Multi-criteria analysis and policy insights (2024 – 2050)
Innovativeness and social acceptance of wind energy: Behavioural heterogeneity and policy implications from a choice experiment
Geopolitical energy shocks and consumer protection under fiscal constraints
abstract: How can energy-importing governments protect fuel-dependent households during geopolitical crises without suppressing conservation incentives or making unaffordable fiscal promises? We develop conditional insurance based on pre-crisis reference fuel consumption, with transfers independent of current purchases. Under stated assumptions, fixed payments preserve the marginal pump-price signal; a strictly concave allocation problem determines how to distribute scarce assistance. A dated liquidity rule prioritizes binding infrastructure guarantees and committed low-carbon investment before discretionary relief, and identifies the conditions under which protection must be rationed or financing fails. Guarantees require verified project-specific external losses and contractual caps. French monthly fuel-price analyses for 2020–2026, a longer exploratory global VAR, and a European synthetic-control comparison of France’s September 2022 intervention illustrate implementation. The latter captures a combined public–private discount and has low-powered donor placebos; it does not isolate the causal effect of the state rebate. Externally released geopolitical energy and macro surprises provide additional exploratory transmission diagnostics; their underlying structural model is not re-estimated and French event samples remain sparse. The framework offers conditional, auditable policy rules rather than a demonstrated universal welfare ranking or unconditional sovereign solvency.

title: Modeling tensions and tradeoffs in community responses to large scale solar development in rural Georgia
Evaluation of waste agricultural residue for sustainable Africa biofuel production: SWOT and SMART outlooks
Ground-source heat pumps for smart building applications: a review
Equal tonnes of CO2, different climate effects: an attribution framework for integrated CCU, CCS, and CDR projects
From pollution control to system governance: five decades of environmental policy evolution in China
abstract: China's environmental governance has undergone a profound transformation since the late 1970s, with implications that extend far beyond its borders. Existing accounts of this evolution rely largely on qualitative periodisation and expert interpretation, offering limited capacity to trace long-term changes in policy priorities and governance logics. This study analyses 3460 central-level environmental policy documents from 1978 to 2025 through an integrated computational framework that combines large language model-based semantic enhancement, dynamic topic modelling, and multi-layer validation, measuring discursive intensity in both absolute and normalised terms across nearly five decades of policy development. The analysis traces five interlinked stages of environmental governance, marking a transition from problem-driven pollution control and energy conservation towards concept-led, system-oriented governance anchored in ecological civilisation and the dual-carbon agenda. Change across these stages is cumulative, not substitutive. Normalised measurement reveals a pattern of institutional persistence with declining relative dominance: foundational regulatory instruments grew in absolute frequency even as their share of policy attention fell, a signature of institutional layering in which new governance paradigms accumulate upon established foundations rather than replacing them. The trajectory of circular economy discourse, from peripheral mention in the 1980s to structural integration with carbon mitigation objectives, shows how resource conservation themes achieve institutional embedding within this evolving architecture. The study provides systematic, corpus-based quantitative evidence that confirms, refines, and extends established qualitative narratives, demonstrates a replicable framework for large-scale policy text analysis, and offers new insight into how state attention and governance paradigms evolve in rapidly transforming economies.

title: Is sustainable design effective? An empirical life cycle assessment of environmental impacts in basketball footwear production
abstract: The footwear industry is characterized by labor-intensive and resource-consuming production. Sustainable design provides a pathway for reducing the environmental burdens of footwear manufacturing, yet its benefits may vary across production processes and impact categories. This study conducts a high-resolution cradle-to-gate life cycle assessment of basketball footwear by linking upstream material acquisition with seven manufacturing processes and compares eight prospective sustainable design scenarios. Environmental hotspots are evaluated using ReCiPe 2016 at midpoint and endpoint levels. Results indicate that raw material acquisition dominates impacts related to toxicity, land use, and resource consumption, while manufacturing dominates global warming potential (GWP) and water consumption potential. At the process level, blanking of upper materials and sole manufacturing are major contributors to endpoint damage, mainly due to textile inputs, petroleum-based polymers, and manufacturing energy demand. Scenario analysis reveals that the reduction scenario (S7), which combines a 3D-printed TPU upper, adhesive-free sole joining, and packaging reduction, provides a relatively balanced environmental response, reducing GWP from 6.44 to 5.90 kg CO₂-eq without the pronounced cross category burden increases observed in the combined scenario (S8). Although S8 achieves the greatest GWP reduction (5.41 kg CO₂-eq), it increases freshwater eutrophication and ecotoxicity burdens. Monte Carlo simulation confirms the robustness of these carbon reductions and the persistence of several trade-offs. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating sustainable design across multiple environmental impact categories rather than carbon reduction alone. High-resolution modeling can support process optimization and sustainable design decisions through precise identification of environmental hotspots.

title: Rethinking eco-efficiency in agri-food system: A bibliometric synthesis of eco-efficiency metrics and frameworks to integrate nutritional indicators
Fusion-DeepRSM for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation and Precursor Sensitivity Prediction
abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and characterization of precursor-response relationships are crucial for human health protection and air quality management. However, current approaches remain limited by the high computational cost and uncertainties of chemical transport models (CTMs), as well as the sample imbalance and limited interpretability of observation-based machine learning methods. Here, we developed Fusion-DeepRSM, an observation-constrained extension of the Deep Learning Response Surface Model (DeepRSM) framework that integrates CTM simulations, multisource satellite observations, and ground-based measurements to derive spatially continuous PM2.5 concentrations and characterize precursor-PM2.5 response relationships. Results from ground-based observations and CTM-based testbed experiments show that Fusion-DeepRSM effectively alleviates the sample imbalance in conventional models and mitigates PM2.5 overestimation in rural regions, with an average reduction of 4.13 μg/m3 while maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.872 and RMSE = 11.82 μg/m3). In addition, Fusion-DeepRSM successfully quantifies precursor-PM2.5 response relationships, revealing pronounced seasonal and regional heterogeneity consistent with established atmospheric chemistry understanding. With high computational efficiency, Fusion-DeepRSM further quantifies the effects of meteorological conditions and pollutant concentrations on PM2.5 variability. During the nationwide PM2.5 decline from 2020 to 2023, unfavorable meteorology partially offset pollutant-related improvements (+1.2 versus −1.8 μg/m3), while changes in precursor pollutant conditions played an important role in the February 2023 PM2.5 rebound in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of Fusion-DeepRSM for air quality modeling and region-specific pollution mitigation.

title: Greenhouse Gas and Ammonia Emission Factors from Raw and Digested Cattle Slurry: A Field-Based Synthesis for Cattle Systems
abstract: Abstract Anaerobic digestion (AD) of cattle slurry is widely promoted as a manure-management strategy, yet its effects on greenhouse gas (GHG) and ammonia (NH3) emissions remain uncertain. This review provides the first field-based synthesis of paired methane (CH4), nitrous oxide (N2O), and NH3 emission factors (EFs) from raw and digested cattle slurry during storage and land application. A total of 98 paired observations from 16 studies were analyzed using paired bootstrap geometric mean ratios. AD reduced dry matter, volatile solids, and carbon content while increasing total ammoniacal nitrogen (TAN) and pH. Consequently, digestate CH4 EFs during storage were 51% lower than those of raw slurry (p = 0.001). In contrast, NH3–N EFs increased by 63% during storage (p = 0.071) and by 40% following land application (p = 0.003). However, TAN-normalized NH3 EFs did not differ between manure types, suggesting similar volatilization potential. AD had no significant effect on N2O EFs. A system-level analysis showed that AD reduced total GHG emissions across the storage-to-land-application continuum by 49%, although this benefit was partially offset by increased NH3 losses. These findings identify AD as an effective CH4 mitigation strategy for cattle slurry when combined with targeted NH3 abatement measures to maximize environmental benefits.

title: Microbial Degradation of Lignin Generates Iron-Binding Organic Ligands
abstract: Abstract The association of organic carbon (OC) with iron (Fe) minerals is a primary mechanism governing soil OC persistence, yet the molecular agents mediating Fe–OC binding remain poorly defined. In this study, we demonstrated that microbial degradation of lignin, one of the major contributors to soil OC, generates organic compounds with the potential to bind to Fe, with implications for mineral-associated carbon stabilization. Lignin samples were microbially degraded by Pseudomonas putida KT2440 for 30 days and subsequently reacted with FeCl3. Ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography–high-resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UHPLC–HRMS/MS)-based analysis identified 494 distinct molecular features with MS/MS data, of which 21 were identified as lignin-derived Fe-binding ligands using Fe isotopologue-enabled metabolomics. Structural annotation of 15 identified ligands further elucidated the chemical nature of the lignin-derived compounds. Systematic meta-analysis of more than 20,000 public HRMS datasets revealed that related compounds occur in soil and aquatic organic matter across diverse ecosystems, ranging from grassland to Arctic tundra. Ion identity molecular networking (IIMN) further revealed additional putative ligands and structurally related transformation products. Altogether, our findings provide a molecular framework for investigating how microbially generated Fe-binding ligands may contribute to Fe–OC interactions and potentially, soil carbon stabilization under changing climate conditions.

title: Data-Driven Accelerated Design-Synthesis of Heterogeneous Fenton-like Catalysts for Water Decontamination
abstract: Abstract Heterogeneous Fenton-like catalysis offers an effective approach for organic pollutant removal, yet catalyst development remains largely empirical and lacks a closed-loop design-synthesis-validation framework. Here, we report a synthesis-oriented inverse-design framework for Fe-based catalysts. We first developed ML_Removal to predict pollutant removal, achieving a test-set R2 of 0.970, while SHAP analysis identified specific surface area (SSA) and Fe loading (Fe wt %) as actionable catalyst descriptors. We then built two synthesis-to-property models to predict SSA and Fe wt %, with SMOTER augmentation enhancing model performance and yielding test-set R2 of 0.782 and 0.856, respectively. Coupling these models with NSGA-II enabled the identification of candidate synthesis recipes targeting the SSA and Fe wt % windows. Two catalysts synthesized according to the NSGA-II-derived recipes exhibited measured SSA of 538.40 and 468.63 m2/g and Fe wt % of 8.19 and 7.01 wt %, aligning with the design targets. The catalysts achieved broad pollutant removal, retained activity in real waters matrices, and maintained >71% naproxen removal after five cycles. External validation of ML_Removal using the experimental data sets yielded an R2 of 0.784, demonstrating transferability to pollutants absent from the training set. Overall, this work establishes a closed-loop design–synthesis–validation framework for data-driven catalyst development and experimental realization.

title: Associations of Early Pregnancy Contaminant Exposure with Gestational Diabetes Mellitus and Mediation by Metabolic Pathway Perturbations
abstract: Abstract Early pregnancy exposure to environmental contaminants is a known risk factor for gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), yet the metabolic pathways linking specific chemical categories to disease pathogenesis remain largely unknown. To address this gap, we conducted a meet-in-the-middle mediation analysis within a prospective birth cohort, leveraging a nested case–control study (116 GDM cases, 232 controls) with 182 contaminants across 11 chemical categories and 702 metabolites measured in early pregnancy serum samples. Seven individual contaminants showed significant associations with GDM risk, with BHT-COOH exhibiting the strongest effect (OR = 2.34, 95% CI: 1.59–3.45). Weighted quantile sum (WQS) regression indicated a positive mixture association with GDM, with Bayesian kernel machine regression (BKMR) providing a complementary assessment of mixture effects. Notably, we identified 506 exposure–metabolite pairs with significant mediation and consistent directionality, providing a comprehensive profile of candidate metabolic intermediates in the associations between contaminant exposure and GDM. Pathway-level analysis identified six candidate metabolic pathways with significant mediation effects, among which the phenylalanine, tyrosine and tryptophan biosynthesis pathway showed the largest mediation estimate, accounting for 75.5% of the DEHP/DNOP–GDM association. Similar pathway-level mediation effects were observed for both individual contaminants and the mixture exposure index. Collectively, these findings identify potential metabolic intermediates linking early pregnancy contaminant exposure to GDM and provide hypotheses for further epidemiological and experimental validation.

title: Perturbation of the Reproductive Endocrine System by Halogenated Nitrophenols via Thyroid Receptor Signaling: Implications for Developmental, Fertility, and Intergenerational Risks in Japanese Medaka
abstract: Abstract Disinfection byproducts (DBPs) are ubiquitously formed in disinfected drinking water and wastewater effluents, with emerging aromatic DBPs constituting a large fraction and generally exhibiting higher toxicity than regulated species. However, their ecological risks remain poorly understood. Here, we focused on two typical halogenated nitrophenols, 2,6-dibromo-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DB-4-NP) and 2,6-dichloro-4-nitrophenol (2,6-DC-4-NP), and systematically evaluated their developmental and reproductive toxicity in Japanese medaka at environmentally relevant ng/L concentrations. Early-life exposure significantly delayed hatching and increased larval mortality, while a 110-day chronic exposure inhibited further gonadal development. These effects were linked to disruption of thyroid hormone homeostasis, reflected by an altered triiodothyronine/thyroxine (T3/T4) ratio and dysfunction of the hypothalamic–pituitary–thyroid (HPT) axis, which subsequently led to sex-specific dysregulation of the hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal (HPG) axis. Males displayed elevated estrogen levels, enhanced estrogen receptor signaling, and hepatic vitellogenin synthesis, whereas females showed the opposite pattern, indicating a feminization risk and diminished estrogenic responses, respectively. Furthermore, parental exposure caused developmental impairments in the offspring, suggesting potential intergenerational toxicity. In silico docking further revealed that 14 other aromatic DBPs exhibited high-affinity binding to thyroid hormone receptors (TRα and TRβ), similar to the two halogenated nitrophenols, supporting their potential to disrupt TR-mediated signaling. Collectively, this study adds to the limited in vivo evidence of thyroid and reproductive endocrine disruption by halogenated nitrophenols under environmentally realistic conditions, underscoring their ecological significance and implicating TR signaling as a mechanistic node for future study.

title: Covering and Flaring Manure Storage Units as a Methane Mitigation Strategy for Small- to Midsize Dairy Operations in the United States
abstract: Abstract Covering manure storages and flaring the captured methane (cap-and-flare) offers a technically feasible mitigation pathway for small- and midsize dairies that has received limited attention relative to anaerobic digestion (AD). While AD systems are more economically feasible for large operations, the dairy segment with fewer than 1,000 cows still produces approximately 34% of U.S. milk and remains largely unaddressed. We estimated technical CH4 mitigation potential under full cap-and-flare adoption using the IPCC Tier 2 model for 8,675 dairy farms across 38 US states. Under 100% adoption, liquid storage CH4 mitigation potential (GWP100 = 27) ranged from 5.53 MMT CO2e yr–1 (central 90% interval: 3.70–6.63) to 10.36 (central 90% interval: 6.93–12.42) depending on the Arrhenius activation energy and reference temperature constants applied, representing 16–30% of the CO2e attributed to dairy manure CH4 in the 2022 EPA Greenhouse Gas Inventory. These values represent an upper-bound technical potential rather than a projected deployment level. Average national Levelized Costs of Mitigation (LCOM) ranged from $55 t–1 CO2e (conservative parametrization) to $29 t–1 CO2e (upper-bound parametrization), positioning cap-and-flare as a cost-efficient CH4 mitigation option. Existing USDA-NRCS Conservation Practice Standard 367 provides an available incentive mechanism, although meaningful scale-up will likely require dedicated funding for infrastructure and technical assistance. These results suggest that cap-and-flare could complement AD as a mitigation pathway for U.S. dairy operations where AD is not economically viable.

Exploring the impact of heat pump integration on the electrification of existing industrial utility systems
abstract: Power-to-heat technologies can substantially reduce industrial CO2 emissions, yet their adoption is hindered by uncertain economics and complex integration choices. This study examines how different levels of heat pump integration influence the design and cost-effectiveness of electrified heating utility systems under varying energy price scenarios and a complete phase-out of natural gas. An optimisation model was applied to a biodiesel plant process to explore the optimal portfolio of heat pumps, mechanical vapour compressors, electric boilers, hydrogen boilers, and thermal storage. Results show that low to medium heat pump integration offers the most economical value by leveraging existing infrastructure and process heat, while high integration levels fail to deliver additional economic benefits due to substantial installation costs. Price volatility primarily drives the deployment of electric boilers and thermal storage for load shifting, whereas heat pumps remain sized to constant process demand and are never coupled with storage. Overall, findings indicate that (a) moderate integration results in the best economic performance, (b) utilising existing infrastructure is critical, and (c) the optimal integration of heat pumps is mainly defined by the average electricity price.

title: Stepped phase change material cavities for enhanced thermal management of photovoltaic panels
abstract: The stepped phase change material (PCM) cavity was investigated as a geometry-based passive thermal-management strategy for concentrated photovoltaic (CPV) modules. A two dimensional transient CPV-PCM conjugate heat transfer model was developed using the enthalpy-porosity method and the Boussinesq approximation. Four cavity orientations, obtained by combining the step-facing direction with upwardly expanding or upwardly narrowing cavity profiles, and three step widths of 4, 6, and 8 mm were compared with a flat cavity under an identical PCM cross-sectional area. Grid and time-step independence tests were examined, and the numerical framework was validated against published CPV temperature and PCM melting data. The obtained results indicate that the illumination side stepped cavity with an upwardly expanding profile shows the strongest heat transfer enhancement. At a step width of 8 mm, the peak value of the maximum PCM velocity increases by 41.4%, the complete melting time decreases by 14.0%, the maximum reduction in average cell temperature reaches 12.83 °C, the heat storage power increases by 8.9%, and the electrical efficiency increases by up to 7.4% relative to the flat cavity. In contrast, the upwardly expanding cavity with steps facing away from the illuminated side provides better temperature uniformity and extends the temperature control duration by up to 36.1%. These results reveal a geometry-induced trade-off between intensified natural convection and cell temperature control performance and provide a numerical basis for the structural screening of compact CPV-PCM thermal-management systems.

title: Hydraulic variability as the governing parameter in hidden hydropower assessment: A standardised framework for water infrastructures
abstract: Water infrastructures host a largely unexploited hidden hydropower potential that could power distributed monitoring systems without external supply. However, its assessment remains challenging due to the lack of standardised, transferable evaluation procedures. This work develops a unified framework for hidden hydropower assessment, integrating multi-year operational velocity data with a physics-informed, neural-network-accelerated reduced-order model and an energy-based optimisation procedure that maximises annual harvested energy under realistic flow variability. The framework is validated across eighteen pilot sites spanning pressurised pipe networks, small open-channel systems and large open-channel environments. The cross-site analysis reveals two novel scientific findings. First, a statistically robust inverse relationship exists between the coefficient of variation of flow velocity (CV) and the capacity factor across all infrastructure categories ( R 2 = 0.8408 ), establishing CV as one of the dominant drivers of long-term energy utilisation that cannot be inferred from device-level, steady-flow studies. Second, the optimal design velocity may deviate from both the mean and the most frequent velocity, owing to the cubic scaling of extractable power with flow speed, confirming that variability-aware optimisation is physically necessary, not merely preferable. Together, these findings support a quantitative site suitability map classifying candidate locations as Suitable, Marginal or Unsuitable based solely on operational flow data, without requiring preliminary harvester sizing. Sites with CV < 0.1 and medium-to-high velocities achieve capacity factors above 80%, suitable for direct sensor powering, whereas sites with CV > 0.2 show severely limited utilisation regardless of instantaneous velocity.

title: Techno-economic and environmental assessment of a Renewable Energy Community based on PV canopies for electric vehicle charging hubs
abstract: Urban EV charging hubs can support transport decarbonization, but their growing electricity demand may be harmful for grid operation if not coordinated with local renewable generation. PV canopies offer a land-efficient way to produce solar electricity in existing parking areas; however, their high structural costs and the limited evidence on their integration in Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) restrain their real-world applicability. To overcome these issues, this study presents an enviro-economic analysis of the integration of PV canopies in EV charging hubs operated within a REC. A simulation framework is developed for eleven parking lots in Milan, Italy, combining PV generation, probabilistic EV charging profiles from an Italian BEV/PHEV fleet database, annual CO 2 emissions, REC incentives, and selected economic indicators. Different PV sizes, charging power levels, and operating configurations with and without the establishment of a REC are compared, including a sensitivity analysis based on future EV demand growth. The results show that PV canopies improve profitability and reduce the environmental impact of EV charging hubs, while REC operation further increases value. Quantitatively, PV deployment increases NPV from a range of 4.54–5.00 M€ baseline to 7.20–14.50 M€ and reduces annual emissions from a range of 845–954 to 485–762 tCO 2 eq; with REC operation, NPV ranges from 7.47 to 15.60 M€ and emissions decrease to a range of 317–718 tCO 2 eq. Payback remains within 4–7 years without REC and 4–6 years with REC. Overall, the study provides design-oriented evidence for integrating PV canopies, EV charging hubs, and RECs in dense urban contexts.

Thermoresponsive Building Envelope with Optical Modulation and Latent Heat Storage: Energy Savings and Thermal Comfort Evaluation Under Diverse Climatic Conditions
abstract: Thermal comfort is essential for occupant well-being, yet maintaining it consumes a substantial portion of building energy. To address this, this study proposes and fabricates an innovative thermoresponsive building envelope integrating a thermoresponsive hydrogel (TH) layer with a phase change material (PCM) layer. The TH enables optical modulation, adjusting solar absorption and reflection with temperature to reduce solar radiation during hot seasons while capturing solar heat during cold seasons. Simultaneously, the PCM provides latent heat storage, reducing daily temperature fluctuations and maintaining nighttime indoor temperatures during cold seasons, thereby lowering heating demand and improving thermal comfort. Sensitivity analysis indicated that the optimal transition temperature of the TH layer is higher in the colder regions due to greater heating demand and lower ambient temperatures, whereas the optimal phase change temperature of the PCM layer lies below the heating setpoint to compensate for the heating reduction. Based on typical meteorological year weather data, simulations across 34 provincial-level capital cities of China demonstrated that the proposed envelope can reduce annual energy consumption by 4.0-18.2% (7.8-17.1 MJ m -2 ) and increase comfort hours by 0.2-9.7% compared to a bare envelope in residential buildings with heating and cooling setpoints of 20 °C and 26 °C, respectively, depending on the region and the optimal transition temperatures of both the TH and PCM layers. These results highlight the feasibility of passive building envelope designs as an effective energy-saving and thermal comfort strategy across different climates.
