Solar–driven simultaneous degradation of dimethyl and diethyl phthalate using NH2–UiO66(Ce/Zr)–derived ZrO2/TiO2 photocatalysts: Mechanistic insight and detoxification
abstract: Phthalate esters (PAEs), including dimethyl phthalate (DMP) and diethyl phthalate (DEP), are priority emerging contaminants that commonly coexist in aquatic environments and pose significant ecological and human health risks. Herein, a series of NH 2 –UiO66(Ce/Zr)–derived ZrO 2 /TiO 2 heterostructured photocatalysts were synthesized via a solvothermal–calcination route using NH 2 –UiO66(Ce/Zr) as the precursor and evaluated for the simultaneous solar–driven degradation of DMP and DEP. Structural characterization revealed that the incorporation of MOF–derived Ce/Zr into TiO 2 reduced crystallite size, increased surface area, promoted interfacial charge transfer, and suppressed electron–hole recombination. Among the prepared materials, NU–Ce/Zr–T10 exhibited the highest photocatalytic activity, achieving 89.6% DMP removal, 96.9% DEP removal, and 56.7% total organic carbon (TOC) reduction after 5 h of simulated solar irradiation. Compared with the Ce–free counterpart (NU–Zr–T10), the enhanced performance was attributed to cerium's role in controlling crystal growth, facilitating charge separation, and improving interfacial redox processes. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Mott–Schottky analyses confirmed the superior charge–transfer characteristics of the heterostructure. Reactive species trapping experiments showed that ● O 2 − , ● OH, and h + participated synergistically in the degradation process, with superoxide radicals playing the predominant role. GC–MS analysis revealed degradation pathways involving hydroxylation, de–esterification, aromatic ring opening, and the formation of low–molecular–weight carboxylic acids. Importantly, ECOSAR predictions and Vibrio fischeri bioassays confirmed progressive detoxification of the treated effluent, while the photocatalyst maintained high activity and structural stability after three reuse cycles. These findings demonstrate that NH 2 –UiO66(Ce/Zr)–derived ZrO 2 /TiO 2 heterostructures constitute an effective and environmentally safe platform for the simultaneous degradation, mineralization, and detoxification of phthalate–contaminated waters under solar irradiation.

title: Drought induces oak growth synchrony at stand level but amplifies individual variability across the Romanian Carpathians
abstract: Heightened drought stress affects growth synchrony among trees in broadleaf oak forests. These effects differ by region and species but remain poorly understood and are not well connected to drought stress. This study compared synchrony that captures high-frequency variation among coexisting trees with drought-induced tree growth synchrony while controlling for age, diameter, and species. The analysis was conducted on an extensive database comprising annually resolved tree rings from 5815 individuals across 132 sites, representing two principal European oak species, Quercus robur and Quercus petraea , which were sampled across the Eastern, Southern, and Western Romanian Carpathians. Different climatic characteristics across regions are reflected by varying breakpoints in temperature trends, buffering intervals, and steeper heating gradients. The Western region experienced the highest number of months characterized by extreme drought conditions per site during the 1960s and 2000s. Throughout these decades, the growth synchrony among coexisting trees, particularly Q. petraea , rose in the West and remained comparatively low in the East. Q. robur highlighted the lowest synchrony amplitude and trend variability, with nearly uniform values across all regions. Climatic aridity increases stand synchrony while promoting tree-level growth asynchrony. This pattern is more evident in the West, where spring drought limited Q. petraea growth, while summer droughts negatively impacted Q. robur , with no statistical influence of tree age or diameter. In the South, both spring and summer droughts limited growth, but older Q. robur trees showed slow post-drought growth recovery. In the Eastern region, summer drought constrained oak growth, particularly in Q. robur . Growth gradually increased in trees with larger diameters, masking site synchrony, while individual trees remained decoupled. The impacts of increasing drought stress on tree growth synchrony partly explain the overall common heteroscedastic patterns observed across regions, species and populations.

title: Soil microbial traits shift on contrasting timescales following restoration of former grazing lands
abstract: Native vegetation restoration is a key strategy for restoring degraded lands globally. While this process can reshape belowground microbial communities, the extent to which such changes restore soil ecosystem functions, and whether different microbial traits recover synchronously or on distinct timescales remains less clear. Understanding the sequence of functional recovery is essential for evaluating restoration success, as distinct microbial traits drive different ecosystem services, from carbon storage to plant growth promotion, and serve as meaningful indicators of long-term ecological recovery. To address this, we applied deep metagenomic sequencing to characterise soil microbial responses following native vegetation restoration (spanning 1-31 years prior to sampling) on grazing agricultural lands. We found that microbial functional changes occurred in distinct phases: an early, rapid restructuring of core soil health processes, detectable as early as three years, including enrichment of nutrient retention and carbon fixation pathways, followed by a more gradual development of plant growth-promoting traits as the plant community matures. Genome-resolved analyses of nearly 500 metagenome-assembled genomes revealed a fundamental shift in dominant microbial life history strategies. Specifically, communities transitioned from a resource-scavenging and stress tolerance profile in grazing soils to strategies that prioritise biosynthesis and growth yields in restored soils. These lifestyle shifts have important implications for enhancing the microbial biomass and carbon sink potential of soils. Together, these findings show that microbial functional shifts following restoration are temporally structured – informing expectations for when key restoration targets may be achieved, and providing a practical framework for monitoring ecosystem recovery.

title: Public willingness to pay for hybrid blue-green infrastructure: Evidence from the Clyde and Forth Estuaries, Scotland
abstract: Nature-based solutions are increasingly recognised as climate-resilient strategies for coastal climate adaptation. This study estimates public willingness to pay (WTP) for the creation of hybrid blue–green infrastructure in place of vacant and derelict land in the Clyde and Forth estuaries, using a contingent valuation method with a payment card format. Tobit and interval regression models were used to evaluate the effects of socioeconomic, attitudinal, and consequentiality variables on WTP. Modelled mean annual household WTP was £84.95 (95% CI:£78.82–£91.13) for the Clyde and £86.01 (95% CI: £80.51–£91.58) for the Forth, with corresponding conservative lower-bound estimates of £38.91 (95% CI: £34.25–£43.57) and £41.22 (95% CI: £36.95–£45.50), respectively. No statistically significant difference in WTP was observed between regions ( p = 0.473 ), indicating no evidence of systematic regional differences in stated WTP within the study sample. A split-sample methodology was used to assess alternative status quo framings, vacant and derelict land versus residential mixed-use development. No statistically significant difference in WTP was detected between the two framings ( p = 0.084 ), although this result does not establish that preferences are invariant to baseline conditions. Key predictors included income, environmental awareness, and membership of an environmental body or organisation. Sensitivity analysis showed that WTP estimates remained positive when protest responses were retained as zero-WTP observations, although the estimated magnitude declined. When aggregated to the Central Belt of Scotland, the results indicate substantial support for hybrid blue–green infrastructure, while population-level extrapolation should be interpreted in light of sample representativeness and protest-response classification. These findings provide supporting evidence that estuarine restoration delivers valued public benefits and can play an important role in long-term coastal resilience strategies. The methodology is applicable at the national scale, incorporating relevant coastal features, and could be applied elsewhere to assess public preferences and support climate-resilient policy.

title: Uncertainties in adaptation pathways planning: Insights from diverse international case studies
Placemaking under circumstances of forced displacement: The case of a community centre in the Syrian neighbourhood in Tarsus
abstract: This article examines refugee placemaking as a relational and politically embedded process through an ethnographic study of a community centre established in a Syrian tented neighbourhood in Tarsus, Turkey. Drawing on participant observation and interviews with Syrian refugees, local residents, and public actors, the paper analyses how placemaking emerges through everyday practices, religious brokerage, and negotiations with local authorities under conditions of legal precarity and spatial informality. Rather than approaching placemaking solely as a phenomenological experience, the article conceptualises it as a power-laden and uneven process through which refugees establish contingent claims to presence while forming attachments and social relations over time. The findings show that placemaking can be politically enabling without being politically transformative: it facilitates social relations and forms of attachment while simultaneously reproducing gendered exclusions, moral hierarchies, and delegated modes of refugee governance. This article demonstrates how placemaking is organised in a semi-permanent tent settlement that develops outside of formal camp management, shaped by informal land use, agricultural labour relations, local mediation, and delegation of authority. It contributes to human-geographical debates by showing how place is made in an informal tented settlement—through religious brokerage and delegated governance rather than humanitarian design—moving beyond the conventional camp–city binary.

title: Speaking with authority
Gate-tunable chiral spin mode in WSe 2 /WS 2 moiré superlattices
abstract: The interplay between many-body and spin-orbit coupling (SOC) effects can lead to previously unobserved phenomena in solids. Chiral spin modes (CSMs) are collective spin excitations that arise from such interplay and connect states with opposite chirality. Here, we report a gate-tunable CSM that occurs between conduction SOC-split minibands in near-0°-twisted WSe 2 /WS 2 bilayers. This mode manifests as a sharp resonance with giant Raman efficiency in the pseudovector-symmetry channel of the Raman spectra. By varying the filling, the CSM transitions from a chiral spin exciton to an excitonic polaron. The spin-flip nature is directly confirmed by the Zeeman effect, and the filling dependence indicates a charge-transfer insulator at unity filling. Our results demonstrate that transition metal–dichalcogenide moiré superlattices are a fertile platform for exploring exotic low-lying collective excitations.

title: Dendritic computation for abstract rule-based flexible decision-making
abstract: Intelligent behavior involves flexible integration of sensory input and abstract rule knowledge. Dendritic computation has been shown to contribute to top-down modulation of sensory processing; however, whether and how it is involved in flexible cognitive processing remains to be elucidated. Combining a rule-based flexible decision-making task with in vivo two-photon imaging and optogenetics in mice, we found that within single layer 5 extratelencephalic neurons in the auditory cortex, apical dendrites preferentially encoded the inferred abstract rule and somata preferentially represented sensory stimuli, whereas choice signals were present in both compartments. Optogenetic dendritic inhibition impaired rule-dependent somatic choice coding, supporting a task-relevant integration across the dendritic and somatic compartments. These results indicate that dendritic computation in cortical neurons mediates flexible behavior.

title: Electrically driven chiral emission from plasmonic tunnel junctions
abstract: Chirality plays a crucial role in a broad range of processes, including light-matter interactions in physics, chemistry, and biology, while quantum tunneling provides a promising mechanism for light generation at the nanoscale. By integrating tunnel junctions with chiral plasmonic nanohelicoids, we achieved electrically induced nanoscale generation of chiral light at the single-particle level. The tunneling-driven resonant excitation of chiral dipolar modes of the nanohelicoids results in emission of a vortex light beam possessing both spin angular momentum with handedness selectivity of more than 0.8 and orbital angular momentum equal in magnitude and opposite in sign. Our electrically driven approach offers a means for engineering photon spin generation at the nanoscale, highlighting its potential for next-generation optical components in display applications, as well as quantum information processing and photochemistry.

title: A pair of chitosan receptors confer broad-spectrum fungal resistance
abstract: Chitosan, a major fungal cell wall component, activates plant immunity, yet the underlying perception mechanism remains unknown. In this study, we identified OsFID1, an apoplast-localized DUF26 domain protein, as a chitosan-binding receptor essential for chitosan-triggered immunity. OsFID1 forms a receptor complex with OsFID2, a plasma membrane–localized DUF26 receptor-like kinase, to mediate chitosan sensing and immune activation, requiring OsFID2 phosphorylation for function. The OsFID1-OsFID2 complex confers broad-spectrum resistance to fungal pathogens. OsFID1 homologs are conserved in land plants, which show chitosan-binding activity in both monocots and dicots. Ectopic expression of OsFID1 in wheat and maize enhanced fungal resistance without growth penalty. These findings uncover a conserved receptor complex for direct chitosan sensing, advancing our understanding of plant-fungus interactions and providing a potential strategy for engineering durable fungal resistance crops.

title: Modular van der Waals MOSFETs through layer-by-layer chalcogen substitutions
abstract: In two-dimensional transition-metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), the local electrostatic field of the chalcogen p -orbitals dictates the crystal field splitting of the transition metal d -orbitals, stabilizing diverse electronic states from semiconducting and semimetallic to exotic topological phases. On-demand substitution of the lattice chalcogens is therefore an efficient route to tuning TMDC electronic phases. Here, we custom-molded van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures by layer-by-layer vapor-phase chalcogen substitution starting from p -type WSe 2 multilayers into which we locally inscribed insulating WO x , n -type WS 2 , and semimetallic WTe 2 . This spatially precise conversion seamlessly integrated distinct electronic phases, both vertically and laterally, into modular vdW semiconductor heterostructures that are otherwise inaccessible. As a demonstration, we integrated WO x /WSe 2 local gate stacks to build ultrascaled metal oxide–semiconductor field effect transistors (MOSFETs), achieving an unprecedented subthreshold swing at subnanometer equivalent oxide thickness.

title: Regulation of target gene expression by chromatin-associated protein-coding transcripts in plants
abstract: Protein-coding transcripts are regarded as intermediates that mediate DNA-to-protein information flow, leaving their noncoding regulatory potential largely underappreciated. Genome-wide profiling of RNA–chromatin interactions in Arabidopsis has uncovered widespread associations between protein-coding transcripts and distinct genomic loci, implying that they possess regulatory functions. Here, we found that BT2 and GSL8 transcripts modulate target gene transcription independently of their protein products through distinct mechanisms. The BT2 transcript represses transcription of its targets CEP2 and MRF4 by forming RNA–DNA triplexes, thereby restricting root growth and promoting flowering, whereas GSL8 acts through a triplex-independent pathway. Our findings unveil intrinsic regulatory activities of protein-coding transcripts, challenging the canonical definition of mRNA function and blurring the functional distinction between coding and noncoding RNAs in the context of genome evolution.

title: To reverse nature loss, change what drives it
abstract: This week, at the 17th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP17), delegates from 195 countries and the European Union are gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, for a global review of progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, an international set of goals and targets adopted in 2022 to tackle the biodiversity crisis. The urgent question before them is clear: What must change now to halt and reverse nature’s decline and put it on a path to recovery by 2030? COP-17 comes as international cooperation is under increasing strain. Extreme weather is intensifying, ecosystem deterioration is creating new security risks, and geopolitical tensions are rising. Yet nature’s decline does not pause for geopolitical instability—it deepens it. That makes effective multilateralism, with North and South as equal partners, more important, not less.

title: Structural basis for size-selective perception of chitin in plants
abstract: Plants detect microbes through pattern recognition receptors that perceive conserved microbial surface motifs known as microbe-associated molecular patterns (MAMPs). Lysin motif (LysM) receptors recognize and mediate downstream responses to chitinous MAMPs. In this study, we elucidated the mechanism for the specific recognition of long-chain chitin oligomers and identified a hallmark bridge domain characteristic of the CHITIN PERCEPTION (CHIP) receptor class. Structural analysis of receptor-ligand complexes, biochemistry, and in planta functional studies of inhibitory nanobodies revealed the mechanism of size-selective, high-affinity chitin perception in Lotus japonicus and Medicago truncatula . Additionally, we identified the CHITIN ELICITOR RECEPTOR KINASE (CERK) class as low-affinity, yet essential, co-receptors and propose a mechanistic model for a ligand-induced core signaling heterocomplex. Our findings establish the structural and mechanistic basis of differential chitin perception and receptor complex assembly in chitin-elicited plant immune signaling.

title: Frequency encoding regulates cell type composition in the small intestine
abstract: Intestinal homeostasis requires tight regulation of stem cell maintenance and differentiation to absorptive and secretory cell types, two major intestinal lineages. Key signaling pathways have been identified, but how they balance cell type composition remains unclear. We uncovered oscillatory expression of the Notch-target protein Hes1 (hairy and enhancer of split 1) that controls cell fate specification in a frequency-dependent manner. An endogenous fluorescent Hes1 reporter revealed distinct, cell type–specific oscillation frequencies forming a gradient along the crypt-villus axis, which was modulated by cell cycle phase as well as Wnt (wingless-related integration site)–signaling and Notch-signaling activity. We developed a microfluidic system to modulate Notch-signaling oscillations in organoids and found the oscillation frequency to regulate the balance of cell type composition. This study provides evidence that information for cell fate specification is encoded in the frequency of an oscillatory signal.

title: Engineering ordered two-dimensional defect phases to strengthen structural alloys
abstract: Defects in crystals are usually considered to be consequences of deformation, but they can also be engineered as strengthening features. Planar defects can strengthen structural alloys but usually form only during deformation or service, limiting control over their density, stability, and chemistry. We show that predeformation followed by aging can convert such defects into a designed architecture of ordered defect phases. In a single-crystal cobalt-nickel–based superalloy and a polycrystalline cobalt-chromium-tungsten alloy, this treatment creates dense networks of coherent, atomically thin, ordered defect–confined phases. These increase room-temperature strength by more than 200 megapascals and reduce the superalloy’s minimum creep rate by more than threefold. Electron microscopy and simulations show that local chemical ordering amplifies strengthening and that the ordered defect phases remain shearable while impeding slip transmission.

title: Airflows redefine the cost of aerial transport in the wild
abstract: Fuel economy matters to both animals and machines, as the cost of transport can determine where, when, and how far locomotion is possible. However, established estimates of these values for animal flight come from laboratories and treat the atmosphere as constant, even though free-flying animals routinely extract energy from atmospheric flows. Using high-resolution movement data, we estimate the cost of transport for 50 bird and bat species flying in the wild. Our results revise the classic ranking of locomotion costs, suggesting that flying can be cheaper than swimming though almost as costly as running, depending on interactions between physical environment, morphology, and behavior. Linking transport costs to atmospheric conditions provides a mechanistic basis for predicting how changing windscapes will reshape the energetics, movements, and distributions of flying animals.

title: Empirical constraints on ice cliff calving
abstract: When calving cliffs at the margins of Earth’s ice sheets exceed a critical height, runaway retreat may be initiated in a process called the marine ice cliff instability. However, sufficiently tall ice cliffs have rarely been observed. To address this gap, we measured the characteristics of 15,330 ice cliffs across Earth’s ice sheet margins using laser altimetry. We show that cliff height is highly correlated with mélange thickness, water depth, and crevassing. We found that tall cliffs calve more rapidly than parameterizations assume, but dynamic thinning and retreat into regions with low ice thickness gradients prevent runaway retreat. These observations suggest that model projections may underestimate subannual rates of cliff calving, but that the potential for instability will depend sensitively on additional quantities, not cliff height alone.

title: Deterministic generation and distribution of genuine multipartite entanglement in macroscopic acoustic resonators
abstract: Generating complex multimode entanglement is a central goal of quantum information science. However, scalable creation of genuine multipartite entanglement is challenging as it requires excellent control and efficient state verification. We report the generation and transfer of genuine multimode entanglement across two multimode acoustic resonators. We prepare genuine multipartite entangled states involving two, four, and six modes across the resonators with respective fidelities of 0.912 ± 0.003, 0.790 ± 0.003, and 0.570 ± 0.001. We further demonstrate the transfer of two- and four-mode genuine entangled states between the resonators with fidelities of 0.785 ± 0.006 and 0.601 ± 0.006. This hardware-efficient and scalable architecture enables deterministic control and generation of complex multimode mechanical states. Our results push the boundary of quantum control in macroscopic mechanical systems, establishing a pathway toward large-scale mechanical quantum networks.

title: Prioritize contaminants of emerging concern in the High Seas Treaty
Magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing requires a universal gate set, but the necessary non-Clifford gates represent a significant resource cost for most quantum error correction architectures. Magic state cultivation offers an efficient alternative to resource-intensive distillation protocols; however, testing the proposal’s assumptions represents a challenging departure from quantum memory experiments. We present an experimental study of magic state cultivation on a superconducting quantum processor. We implement cultivation, including code-switching into a surface code, and develop a fault-tolerant measurement protocol to bound the magic state fidelity. Cultivation reduces the error by a factor of 40, with a state fidelity of at least 0.9999(1) (retaining 8% of attempts). Our results experimentally establish magic state cultivation as a viable solution to one of quantum computing’s most important challenges.

title: Atomic functional site scaffolding in biopolymers with RFdiffusion3
abstract: The catalytic and other sophisticated functions of biomolecules arise from the placement of many atoms in three-dimensional space. Here, we describe a generative artificial intelligence method for biopolymers, RFdiffusion3 (RFD3), which employs free atom diffusion to satisfy complex sets of atomic constraints more rapidly and accurately than previous methods across several challenges from enzyme design to RNA structure design. We demonstrate experimentally the power of the RFD3 pipeline for enzyme design by designing de novo phosphotriesterases with a complex active site architecture incorporating a carbamylated lysine coordinating two metal ions and zinc proteases specific for the transthyretin protein involved in amyloid diseases; in both cases we obtain active catalysts in zero shot 96 construct design campaigns.

Educational intervention can rewire village social networks
abstract: Social networks shape behaviour, affect information dissemination and undergird collective action. And they can be exploited in the design of interventions in these domains1–7. Although social networks obey fundamental principles, such as the degree distribution8,9, they can nevertheless evolve as ties form and break. Here, through a randomized controlled trial involving a total of 8,331 people in 110 remote Honduran villages, we evaluate the secondary effects of a 22-month public-health intervention1 on pre-existing social-network structure. We used a design in which a varying fraction of village households received the intervention, and villages in which no one received the intervention were used as the primary reference group. In ‘low-dosage’ villages (in which 5–30% of households received the intervention), people who received the intervention tended to sever ties with untreated individuals to whom they previously went for health advice. Conversely, in high-dosage villages (50–100%), treated individuals increased their ties. These average changes are explained mainly by tie dynamics; that is, treated–treated pairs persist and form new links, whereas treated–untreated ties dissolve. A mediation analysis indicates that absorption of health information increases the likelihood of tie formation and persistence. The rewiring patterns generally lasted for three years after the intervention ceased. Moreover, although the intervention delivered health information, it reshaped friendship and financial ties, not just health-advice connections. In aggregate, the introduction of a new information regime acted as a kind of social institution, rewiring individuals’ connections even though the overall degree distribution of village-wide networks remained relatively stable. A randomized controlled trial involving a health-education intervention in rural villages in Honduras shows that the intervention changed social network connections, including not only health-related connections but also friendships and financial ties.

title: Early tetrapod neck mobility modelled using an extant analogue
abstract: Abstract Tetrapods arose from lobe-finned fishes with a notochord-dominated axial column 1–3 . During this transition, the skull became separated from the shoulder girdle 4–6 , giving rise to a neck region. This head–shoulder separation has generated hypotheses suggesting that neck mobility increased during the origin of tetrapods, facilitating the ecological transition towards more terrestrial habitats 4,5,7–9 . However, incompletely co-ossified vertebral components 10 have posed a challenge to modelling the mobility of these early tetrapod necks. Here we used material tests on the similarly configured axial columns of sturgeon to predict the capacities of the tetrapod neck region for lateral flexion, extension and rotation across the tetrapod stem. Our model indicates that the soft tissue-dominated axial column was surprisingly rigid, despite lacking co-ossified vertebral components. We estimate that most stem tetrapods could move their heads less than 6° laterally and less than 3° dorsally but could not rotate them. Notably, mobility did not shift in conjunction with the head–shoulder separation that occurred between the origin of tristichopterids (represented by Eusthenopteron ) and that of more crownward stem tetrapods. Therefore, mobility in the tetrapod neck did not serve as a functional driver of head–shoulder separation. Instead, forelimb-driven locomotion, implicated in early tetrapods 11–14 , provides a better functional explanation for the head–shoulder separation.

title: Elp1 is required for myeloid differentiation and brain repopulation
Engineered TYK2 dependence enables myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonism
abstract: Abstract Interleukin-10 (IL-10) is a central anti-inflammatory cytokine that suppresses immune responses in myeloid cells but can also activate T cells, limiting its therapeutic use in chronic inflammatory diseases owing to narrow efficacy windows and dose-limiting toxicities 1–5 . Here we show that myeloid and T cells differ in their dependence on JAK-family kinase pairing for IL-10 signalling and function. We took advantage of this differential kinase dependence to engineer a tetravalent nanobody-based myeloid-selective IL-10 receptor agonist (msIL-10R agonist) that fully recapitulates IL-10’s potent suppression of monocytes, macrophages and dendritic cells while avoiding stimulation of T cells. Cryo-electron microscopy structural analysis reveals a distinct receptor cross-linking geometry of the msIL-10R agonist compared with native IL-10 family cytokines. This tetravalent architecture renders signalling strictly TYK2-dependent and highly sensitive to IL-10Rα and IL-10Rβ receptor abundance, thereby conferring selective activity in myeloid cells. This msIL-10R agonist reduces inflammation in humanized mouse models of lipopolysaccharide challenge, delayed-type hypersensitivity and colitis. A humanized version exhibits IgG-like pharmacokinetics, sustained receptor occupancy and durable myeloid suppression up to 30 days without T cell activation or haematological toxicities in non-human primates. These findings establish a geometry-based strategy for achieving cell-type-selective cytokine signalling and identify the msIL-10R agonist as a therapeutic candidate for myeloid-driven inflammatory diseases, including inflammatory bowel diseases.

Sexual dimorphism in epidermal stem cell dynamics
abstract: Abstract The epidermis is a stratified epithelium comprising proliferative basal cells and differentiated suprabasal cells that are continuously renewed throughout life. Conflicting theories have been proposed regarding the heterogeneity of the basal cell layer, with some studies proposing that all proliferative cells have self-renewal potential during homeostasis 1–5 . Meanwhile, others posit a model in which stem cell differentiation occurs through an intermediate transit-amplifying-like progenitor state with strictly limited proliferative potential 6–10 . Here, to determine the heterogeneity and pattern of cell fate, we performed intravital time-lapse imaging to track the fate of lineage-labelled cells in the skin interfollicular epidermis. Results from quantitative analyses of clonal dynamics support a two-compartment model of epidermal homeostasis, whereby basal cells are organized in a stem cell–transit-amplifying cell hierarchy. Critical to these conclusions was the discovery of sexual dimorphism in epidermal fate, with female mice showing a highly synchronized pattern of cell division, differentiation and delamination that contributes to accelerated wound healing. Single-cell RNA sequencing, transcriptional profiling and clonal analyses of castrated mice revealed that male sex hormones promote stem cell differentiation and delamination. In summary, our study provides insight into the functional identity of the stem cell population and identifies sex-specific differences in the regulation of epidermal stem cells and transit-amplifying cell fate.

title: De novo design of cysteine proteases
Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates
abstract: Conservation areas are critical for tackling the global environmental crisis1. These sites are reported as covering 18.5% of the terrestrial realm2 and governments have committed through Global Biodiversity Framework Target 3 to increase this to at least 30% by 2030 (ref. 3). There are concerns that this potential near-doubling of conservation area coverage will negatively affect vulnerable people and over-stretch conservation resources4. However, nationally available datasets indicate that more conservation areas exist than are reflected in global figures5–7. We evaluated progress towards the area component of Target 3 using a globally representative sample across 25 countries and territories that incorporated these national datasets8. Extrapolating from this sample, we show that conservation areas likely already cover 26.81% of the terrestrial realm. We may be much closer to achieving 30% terrestrial coverage than previously thought. However, we also show that the extra land does not substantially address gaps in ecological representativeness, indicating that solely meeting the area component of Target 3 will do little to solve continuing global biodiversity loss. More focus and resources are needed to achieve the other components of the target, using a more strategic and inclusive approach to fill present gaps and produce equitable and effective conservation area networks. A globally representative sample of 25 countries and territories indicates that conservation areas cover 26.81% of the land, much closer to the 30% by 2030 target than officially reported.

title: Artificial intelligence-enabled clinical phenotyping of human brown fat
abstract: Adipose tissue has a central role in systemic energy balance and the pathogenesis of obesity and its sequelae1,2. In contrast to white adipose tissue, brown adipose tissue (BAT) uses energy to produce heat3. Detectable BAT in humans is associated with decreased prevalence of cardiometabolic diseases4. However, the complete spectrum of health conditions associated with BAT remains unknown, and high-throughput methods to quantify BAT activity in humans are lacking5,6. Here we leveraged big data and artificial intelligence to systematically define the clinical impact of BAT in a cohort of 101,243 patients from a large cancer centre. Our unbiased analyses revealed that, across all diagnoses, cardiovascular and psychiatric diseases were less prevalent in people with BAT. Using a machine learning approach, we semi-automatically quantified BAT activity in approximately 8,700 patients and demonstrated that higher BAT activity, especially in the axillary depot, is associated with lower odds of cardiometabolic diseases and healthier white fat distribution. People with BAT also exhibited more favourable glycaemic parameters, lipid profiles, inflammatory markers and echocardiographic indices. Analysis of medication usage demonstrated that angiotensin receptor blocker use was positively associated with BAT presence. As proof of concept, we showed that the angiotensin receptor blocker losartan increased brown adipocyte activity and whole-body energy expenditure. Altogether, our studies harnessing artificial intelligence and big data identify new clinical phenotypes linked to BAT and serve as a platform for drug repurposing to activate this tissue in humans. Artificial intelligence-enabled quantification and analyses of brown adipose tissue (BAT) activity uncover links between BAT and a healthier metabolic profile along with lower rates of psychiatric disease, and can identify pharmacologic agents that could be repurposed to activate this tissue in humans.

title: Capillary-selective vasodilation through myosin inhibition halts ischaemic cascades

A microexon regulatory code reveals autism-linked genetic variation
abstract: Abstract Neuronal microexons are a highly conserved class of alternative splicing events enriched in genes with critical functions in nervous system biology 1,2 . Microexon splicing is often disrupted in the brains of autistic individuals, and mice with microexon deficiencies display autism-like phenotypes 1,3,4 . However, the full landscape of microexons is not known, and the impact of genetic variation on these exons has not been systematically investigated. Here, through extensive transcriptome profiling, we detect hundreds of new microexons, including many with neuronal subtype-specific splicing patterns, and others that activate nonsense-mediated mRNA decay. Using machine learning, we define a sequence code predictive of neuronally spliced microexons and use this to identify critical regulatory elements surrounding the expanded microexon repertoire. This code further reveals genomic variants predicted to alter microexon splicing in individuals affected by autism, with rare variants having the strongest estimated impact. These variants are mostly detected in idiopathic individuals and are associated with autism status. They also converge on synaptic and other autism-linked genes, as well as genes not previously linked to autism. Our results collectively define an expanded repertoire of microexons, delineate their regulatory code, and pinpoint variants predicted to affect their splicing, with implications for the disruption of functions central to neuronal biology and brain disorders.

title: Advancing subseasonal forecasting with machine learning
abstract: Decision-makers rely on weather forecasts to plant crops, manage wildfires, allocate water and energy and prepare for weather extremes1–3. Today, such forecasts enjoy unprecedented accuracy as far as 2 weeks thanks to steady advances in physics-based dynamical models and data-driven artificial intelligence models4–10. However, model skill drops precipitously at subseasonal timescales (2–6 weeks ahead) due to compounding errors, systemic model biases and the chaotic nature of the atmosphere11–15. To counter this degradation, we introduce probabilistic bias correction, a machine learning framework that substantially reduces systematic error by learning to correct historical probabilistic forecasts. When applied to the leading dynamical and artificial intelligence models from the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF), probabilistic bias correction doubles the modest subseasonal skill of the AI Forecasting System16 and improves the skill of the operationally debiased dynamical model17 for 91% of pressure, 92% of temperature and 98% of precipitation targets. We designed probabilistic bias correction for operational deployment, and, in the 2025 real-time forecasting competition of ECMWF18, its global forecasts were the best for all weather variables and lead times, outperforming the dynamical models from six operational forecasting centres, an international dynamical multimodel ensemble, the AI Forecasting System of ECMWF and the forecasting systems of 34 teams worldwide. These probabilistic skill gains translate into more accurate prediction of extreme events and have the potential to improve agricultural planning, energy management and disaster preparedness in vulnerable communities19. The AI framework probabilistic bias correction is shown to correct weather forecast errors 2 to 6 weeks ahead and boost forecast skill, making it promising for improved extreme-weather prediction.

title: Modelling mouse embryogenesis from chemically induced totipotent stem cells
Divergent genomic evolution in astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas
abstract: Astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas are isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH)-mutant gliomas that most commonly arise in adults under the age of 50 and exhibit variable responses to treatment1–3. To understand the genetic drivers of disease progression, here we used whole-genome and whole-exome sequencing to characterize longitudinally collected tumour specimens from 183 patients with IDH-mutant glioma. Samples were collected through the Glioma Longitudinal Analysis (GLASS) Consortium4. Most primary surgery samples were classified as grade 2 on the basis of histology (73% for astrocytomas and 93% for oligodendrogliomas). We validated known genomic markers of tumour progression, including hypermutation and homozygous deletion of CDKN2A or CDKN2B (hereafter, CDKN2A/B)5, and discovered genetic alterations that distinguish between the evolutionary trajectories of astrocytomas and those of oligodendrogliomas. Mutations in phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K) and NOTCH1 were newly acquired in recurrent oligodendrogliomas, regardless of treatment, and were associated with an increased tumour mutational burden. In recurrent astrocytomas, however, again irrespective of treatment, acquired focal oncogene amplifications and CDKN2A/B homozygous deletions were associated with an increase in chromosomal imbalances, which converged with markers of chromosomal instability such as chromothripsis and whole-genome doubling. In both types of IDH-mutant glioma, we observed a convergence of acquired alterations, genome-wide changes and worse patient outcomes, suggesting that treatment-refractory clones were being selected. Treatment with temozolomide was associated with the mutational signatures SBS11 and SBS119 in both tumour types, whereas the radiotherapy-associated ID8 signature increased in astrocytomas specifically. We show that the genomes of oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas adapt to the selective pressures of tumour progression and treatment in distinct ways, suggesting that oligodendrogliomas and astrocytomas differ in their responses to treatment-induced DNA damage. Longitudinal genomic analyses in patients with astrocytoma or oligodendrioglioma suggest that these two types of tumour differ in the mechanisms by which they become resistant to treatment, with astrocytomas accumulating copy-number alterations and chromosomal instability markers but oligodendrogliomas acquiring new driver mutations.

title: Targeted stimulation of motor cortex ensembles drives learned movements
Interhemispheric monsoon dynamics over the past 450,000 years
Parity-dependent coupling of molecular spin chains to a superconductor
abstract: Collective behaviour in quantum materials can produce excitations carrying only a fraction of the quantum numbers of their constituents. A notable case occurs in chains of spin-1 units1, in which a topological gap protects the interior of the chain, whereas spin-1/2 states, half the spin of the units that form it, emerge at the ends2. In short chains, these fractional edge spins couple to each other and their topological protection makes them attractive for hybrid spin–superconductor devices. Whether such fractionalization survives the proximity of a superconducting condensate, however, remains an open question. Here we grow molecular Haldane chains of antiferromagnetically coupled spin-1 triangulene units on a proximitized Au(111)/Nb(110) surface and resolve a parity-dependent coupling of their spin-1/2 edge states to the superconductor by scanning tunnelling spectroscopy. Odd-length chains host Yu–Shiba–Rusinov (YSR) bound states inside the superconducting gap, originating from a global S = 1 ground state, whereas even-length chains form an S = 0 ground state decoupled from the superconductor. A two-site model attributes this alternation to the sign and strength of inter-edge interactions, independently confirmed by extra-gap spin excitations in tunnelling spectra. Many-body spin excitations of the S = 1 chain are also detected, decoupled from the superconductor by the much larger Haldane gap. The length-tunable coupling of the edge spins to superconductors opens a route towards molecular spin qubits based on π-conjugated carbon architectures. Scanning tunnelling spectroscopy shows that the fractional spin-1/2 end states of molecular Haldane chains couple differently to a superconducting condensate depending on whether the chain contains an even or odd number of spin-1 triangulene units.

title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
abstract: Abstract Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition 1 . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

title: Closing Ranks: Organized Labor and Immigration
A Theory of Economic Coercion and Fragmentation
Gas Flaring, Agricultural Productivity and Labor Reallocation: Evidence from Nigeria
abstract: of the Paper This paper investigates the impact of natural gas flaring—a byproduct of oil production—on agricultural productivity in Nigeria. Using a panel dataset of Nigerian households from the Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS) spanning 2012–2018, combined with geocoded data on monthly gas flaring volumes from oil fields, the study employs variation in the timing of interview surveys to assess effects of gas flaring during harvest and planting seasons. The analysis focuses on southern Nigeria, where oil production is concentrated, and leverages a 2010 policy reform (Local Content Act) that increased local onshore oil activities and thus gas flaring. The empirical strategy includes fixed effects (household, and region-by-month-by-year) to control for unobserved heterogeneity, weather variables (precipitation and temperature), and an instrumental variable approach using global oil price changes interacted with pre-sample flaring intensity to address endogeneity. Key outcomes measured are real crop yield per hectare and labor productivity (real agricultural output divided by worker-days). The findings reveal significant negative effects during the harvest season, particularly in rainy periods, but minimal impacts during planting. Mechanisms are explored through satellite data on air pollutants, showing elevated levels of black carbon, sulfur dioxide, and nitrogen dioxide in flaring areas. Robustness checks confirm the results against various confounders like conflicts, oil spills, and placebo tests. The paper contributes to literature on the impact of air pollution on worker productivity and crop yields and climate change impacts on agriculture, highlighting policy needs to mitigate environmental costs from extractive industries in developing countries.

title: Balancing the Burden: Shared Responsibility in Intergenerational Financial Support in Rural Ghana
Structural transformation towards healthcare
Love-for-variety: with an application to an Armington model of competitive trade
Immigration and the Slope of the Labour Demand Curve: The Role of Firm Heterogeneity in a Model of Regional Labour Markets
abstract: Abstract In this paper, we provide new explanations for the puzzling findings that migrants do not decrease natives’ wages and that skilled immigration can increase them. We develop a model with regional labour markets and heterogeneous firms in which workers of different skill levels are imperfect substitutes, but for a given skill level, natives and migrants are perfect substitutes within a firm. In this setting, a skilled labour supply shock due to immigration induces skill-intensive firms to expand. These across-firm reallocations reduce the within-firm substitution between skilled and unskilled workers, thus limiting relative wage adjustments. When this mechanism is coupled with human capital externalities that are skill-neutral at the firm level but skill-biased on aggregate, the same skilled immigration shock can increase absolute and relative skilled wages. These two mechanisms are quantitatively important: the negative impact of immigration on natives’ wages is reduced by at least one-third when the across-firm reallocation mechanism is at work, and human-capital externalities can revert the sign of this relation.

title: ESTIMATION AND INFERENCE OF NONLINEAR AUTOREGRESSIVE DISTRIBUTED LAG MODELS WITH TIME TREND BY ORDINARY LEAST SQUARES
abstract: This study examines the large-sample behavior of an ordinary least squares (OLS) estimator within a correctly specified nonlinear autoregressive distributed lag (NARDL) model for nonstationary data. Although the OLS estimator suffers from an asymptotically singular matrix problem, it remains consistent for unknown model parameters and asymptotically follows a mixed normal distribution. Additionally, we examine the large-sample behavior of the standard Wald test, as defined by the OLS estimator, for asymmetries in long- and short-run NARDL parameters, and enhance this analysis with a super-consistent long-run parameter estimator. We then confirm the theory on the Wald test using Monte Carlo simulations. Finally, using U.S. GDP and exogenous fiscal shock data, we demonstrate the use of the OLS estimator and show statistical evidence of long- and short-run symmetries between the effects of tax increases and decreases on U.S. GDP.

title: ON THE RELATION BETWEEN DISCRETE- AND CONTINUOUS-TIME AFFINE OPTION PRICING MODELS
abstract: This article studies the weak convergence of discrete-time generalized autoregressive conditional heteroskedasticity (GARCH) and stochastic volatility (SV) option pricing models that allow for fat tails, multi-component volatilities, and non-monotonic pricing kernels. We introduce a general affine framework that enables the simultaneous derivation of new diffusion limits for Gaussian and inverse Gaussian GARCH models based on distributional invariant parametric convergence rates. When restricted to one-component specifications, our limits yield non-degenerate bivariate diffusions, generalizing the existing results in the affine GARCH literature. By using alternative parametric convergence rates, we further provide a comprehensive classification of all possible limits for two classes of affine and non-affine discrete-time SV models. Specifically, we show that the canonical affine classes of models popularized in discrete and continuous time are not analogous to one another. Our theoretical results are supported by a series of numerical experiments that investigate the impact of parametric scaling assumptions and model features on the convergence of European option prices. Overall, we find that the new limiting diffusions produce option prices that are closest to their discrete-time counterparts sampled at daily frequency.

title: Debt Aversion: Theory and Measurement
abstract: ABSTRACT We propose a model of debt aversion and conduct an experiment with real debt and saving contracts to jointly elicit debt aversion and preferences over time, risk, and intertemporal losses. We find that 89% of participants are debt averse, which strongly influences their choices. The estimated “borrowing premium,” the compensation an average person requires to accept debt, is around 16% of the principal. Applying a validated survey module to a representative sample of German households, we find that debt aversion is both statistically and economically significantly associated with actual debt‐taking and financial health.

title: Constrained interactions and the evolution of conventions:An experimental analysis
Critical peak pricing or rebate? An impact analysis in a cold climate market
Reference Points and Affordability Perceptions of Hybrid Maize Seed in Uganda: Evidence on Endowment and Expectations
abstract: ABSTRACT Despite demonstrated yield advantages, adoption of hybrid maize seed in Sub‐Saharan Africa remains low, raising questions about smallholders' perceptions of value and affordability. We examine whether farmers value hybrid maize seed differently depending on whether they already possess it or form expectations about likely prices or ownership, and how this affects willingness to pay (WTP) for a 1‐kg pack of seed in Uganda. We elicit WTP and willingness to accept (WTA) using Becker‐DeGroot‐Marschak auctions and measure ownership expectations with a multiple price list. The experiment tests three mechanisms: an endowment effect, by comparing WTP and WTA; price expectations, by randomly varying price probabilities; and ownership expectations, by varying the probability of keeping the seed for free. We find a strong endowment effect: farmers require substantially more money to give up seed they already possess than they are willing to pay to acquire the same seed, with WTA exceeding WTP by about 60%. The average WTP of UGX 4605 is well below the market price of UGX 8500. Loss aversion is associated with lower WTP and higher WTA, but these effects are small, imprecise, and do not explain the valuation gap. We do not find evidence that price expectations or ownership expectations generate economically meaningful reference points. Overall, our results indicate that current possession of seed is a more salient benchmark for valuation than forward‐looking expectations. These findings suggest that scaling strategies establishing early ownership, such as trial packs or plant‐now/pay‐after‐harvest schemes, may be more effective than attempts to shift price expectations alone.

title: Disease and development: productivity, exchange, and social segregation
Identifying the impact of financial sanctions on innovation of target countries
abstract: Financial sanctions have become an increasingly prevalent tool in international relations, particularly since World War II. However, one critical area that remains underexplored is the impact of financial sanctions on the technological innovation capabilities of target countries. Our main finding is that financial sanctions reduce the overall number of patent and trademark applications in target countries. The channel analysis provides suggestive evidence that this adverse effect is consistent with disruptions to international trade and international capital flows, which may limit access to the external knowledge, technology, and capital needed for innovation. We also discover that the negative association between financial sanctions and innovation is weaker in countries with greater financial openness, deeper financial development, and stronger investment facilitation. These findings highlight policy conditions that may help target countries sustain innovation under financial sanctions.
journal_name: Journal of International Money and Finance

title: A Generalized Framework for Multivariate Predictive Regressions
abstract: ABSTRACT Predictive regressions are subject to small‐sample bias when innovations in persistent predictors are correlated with predictive errors. One approach to bias reduction is the multi‐predictor augmented regression method (mARM), which augments the predictive regression with bias‐corrected proxies for predictor innovations. We extend this framework to allow for first‐order autocorrelation in predictive errors, first‐order autocorrelation in predictor innovations, and contemporaneous correlations between shocks to the two processes. Simulations show that the mARM estimator can exhibit substantial bias, whereas our proposed extended mARM estimator significantly reduces bias relative to both mARM and ordinary least squares. Looking at predictive regressions of stock returns on several widely used financial ratios, we find that the mARM approach yields spurious statistical significance for some predictive coefficients, which is not observed with the proposed extended mARM.

title: The Dynamics of Credit Rating Report Content
Expected investment and stock returns: A machine learning approach
The positive investment premium in China
Consumer support for minority entrepreneur farmers
abstract: This study examines whether beginning farmers’ race and gender influence consumer support, measured through monetary contributions, voluntary effort, and willingness to pay for agricultural products. Using an incentivized online experiment with 1459 U.S. consumers, we exogenously manipulate the farmer’s race (White, Hispanic, and Black) and gender (male and female) on product labels. We do not detect statistically significant effects of race or gender across the three support outcomes. Overall, our findings indicate broadly similar levels of consumer support across the racial and gender groups studied, while not ruling out smaller or context-dependent forms of discrimination. These findings have implications for the economic viability of beginning farmers.

title: A cultural transmission explanation for the Little Divergence: The shock of the Black Death
abstract: Before the Industrial Revolution, Northwestern Europe was characterized by late marriage under the European Marriage Pattern (EMP) and persistently high wages, two central features of the Little Divergence. Yet individuals following the EMP had fewer children, raising the question of how this norm could persist. We develop a cultural-transmission model to address this puzzle. Holding cultural composition fixed, higher wages raise fertility for both cultural types. Over time, however, sustained high wages increase the prevalence of the lower-fertility EMP type. This cultural-composition effect reduces average fertility and population pressure, thereby helping sustain high wages. The resulting feedback generates a weak-EMP/low-wage equilibrium and a strong-EMP/high-wage equilibrium. We further argue that regional differences in the severity of the Black Death shifted European societies between these equilibria. Regions with larger population losses experienced more persistent labor scarcity and high wages, allowing the EMP to spread and persist. The model therefore explains the joint persistence of late marriage and high wages in Northwestern Europe.

title: Economic uncertainty and fertility cycles: baby boom and busts in twentieth century USA
abstract: Abstract Using variation across US counties and states in the volatility of income growth over the course of the twentieth century, we identify a negative effect of economic uncertainty on fertility. Our findings contribute to the unraveling of the determinants of the post-WWII baby boom: the decline in economic uncertainty endured by women born in 1910 compared to that of those born in 1933 can account for an increase in fertility by 0.4 to 0.6 child, which is about 45% to 67.5% of the change across these cohorts.

title: Why identity matters for development
abstract: This paper argues that while development economics has moved beyond income-based metrics toward a broader capabilities framework, it remains insufficiently attentive to the role of social identity in shaping life chances. Identities such as caste, race, gender, and ethnicity structure access to resources, opportunities, and power in ways that conventional and multidimensional indices fail to capture. Drawing on evidence from global gender disparities and caste-based inequalities in India, the paper demonstrates how identity-blind policies risk reinforcing structural hierarchies. It concludes by advocating an identity-conscious development framework that centres historical injustice, targeted interventions, and inclusive governance to advance equitable development.

title: The effect of new housing supply in structural models: A forecasting performance evaluation
Long-lead forecasting of El Niño–Southern Oscillation using score-driven models with many predictors
Asset value and securitization under heterogeneous beliefs
abstract: This paper studies how securitization affects asset prices and realized excess payoffs when investors hold heterogeneous beliefs. I extend the resale-option asset-pricing model of Harrison and Kreps (1978) by allowing the owner of a long-term asset to issue a finite set of asset-backed securities backed by its future cash flow. These securities are organized into tranches with different payment priorities. The no-tranching benchmark has a unique equilibrium price, but tranching can generate multiple equilibrium prices because separately priced tranches feed back into the asset’s resale value. Securitization weakly raises the equilibrium prices of the underlying asset relative to the no-tranching benchmark. Furthermore, there exists a tranching that raises the lowest equilibrium price strictly above its no-tranching level if and only if, at some state, no agent perceives a distribution of the next-period asset price in the no-tranching benchmark that first-order stochastically dominates the distributions perceived by all other agents. Tranching has ambiguous effects on individual realized excess payoffs, but the aggregate realized excess payoff is nonpositive and weakly decreases as the tranching is refined. When one agent has the finest information partition, securitization may lower some agents’ realized excess payoffs without raising anyone else’s. The results characterize how belief disagreement shapes the effect of security design on asset prices and realized payoffs.

title: Economic & Trade Cooperation Zones and Cross-Border Supply Chain Synergy: Evidence from China-ASEAN Integration
Government Accounting Supervision and Local Government Implicit Debt: Empirical Evidence from China
Does the Widespread of Mobile Internet Narrow the Urban–Rural Labor Income Gap? Evidence from China
Corporate Greenwashing, R&D Manipulation, and Corporate Value
Shared leadership and information production: how co-lead arrangements reshape syndicated loan governance
abstract: Using syndicated loan data, we examine how co-lead arrangements are associated with information production and monitoring. Co-lead loans exhibit greater sensitivity of loan spreads to hard-to-observe future borrower risk, consistent with more informative ex ante pricing. Co-lead loans are also associated with fewer covenant violations when lead arrangers are highly reputable. These associations are generally stronger for informationally opaque borrowers. Overall, the evidence is consistent with shared leadership facilitating the incorporation of borrower risk into loan pricing and strengthening monitoring when arrangers have strong reputational incentives.
journal_name: Journal of International Financial Markets, Institutions and Money

title: The Impact of Repealing Certificate‐of‐Need Laws on Healthcare Spending: A Causal Analysis
abstract: Certificate-of-Need laws in 35 US states require healthcare providers to obtain government approval before building new facilities or expanding services. Their stated goal is to ensure a genuine community need and avoid redundant services, with the aim of controlling healthcare costs and distributing resources fairly, although their effectiveness is debated. Our study differs from previous literature as we present the causal effects of repealing Certificate-of-Need laws on various healthcare expenses using modern difference-in-differences techniques and event studies. Our findings suggest that repealing Certificate-of-Need laws can reduce the burden of healthcare spending.

Talent Attraction Policies, Corporate Innovation, and Spillover Effects
The invisible architect: Fiscal incentives and floor area ratio growth in China
The ripple effects of customer orientation: Personal, vicarious, and temporal pathways to frontline employee well-being
