title: Pet-owner synchrony: Operationalization, application, and implications
abstract: Abstract Despite the pet industry’s significant economic and social importance, academic attention to this sector of the economy has been limited. Rather than focusing solely on the household demographics of pet ownership or the attitudinal components of the pet-owner relationship, we explore actual purchase decisions of pet owners. In this study, we examine pet-owner synchrony, a behavioral operationalization of pet-owner relationships that is grounded in attachment theory, anthropomorphism, and the extended self. Utilizing scanner data from 875,853 market baskets including 23 million transactions collected from a regional supermarket chain, we analyze cross-category co-occurrence patterns within shopping baskets. Our analysis reveals affinities, or parallels, in pet owners’ purchases of health and wellness products and hedonic products for both themselves and their pets, which we attribute to pet-owner synchrony. We identify two moderators that influence the strength of pet-owner synchrony: pet type (cat versus dog) and the presence of young children in the household. In addition, we evaluate how basket size, holidays, and price elasticities impact pet-owner synchrony. Our findings deliver useful insights into pet-owner relationships, have direct implications for retail and manufacturing managers, and yield recommendations for public policy.
journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

title: Beyond Greenwashing: Environmental Commitments and Gas Flaring in the African Oil Sector
Shipment Monitoring, Allocation, and the Impact on Food Waste
abstract: Often advocated for the potential to reduce waste in fresh produce supply chains, sensor technologies enable firms to monitor the condition of each product unit and allocate them to markets at different transportation distances, thereby matching units with shorter shelf lives with closer markets. In this paper, we consider a firm purchasing and transporting a fresh produce product for sale in two destination markets. Postharvest processes cause a proportion of the product to be in risky condition, potentially becoming unsalable (“spoiled”) due to shelf-life deterioration during transportation. With monitoring technology, the firm first determines a purchase quantity and then decides how to allocate each unit (in either good or risky condition) between markets. We characterize the optimal allocation policies, which can be used to efficiently determine the optimal purchase quantity. Our analysis shows that such technology may inadvertently increase total waste by inducing larger purchase quantities; this increase is often, but not always, accompanied by a lower waste rate and improved distribution efficiency. As firms increasingly adopt monitoring technology for shipment allocation, additional policy and managerial attention may be required. Improvements in postharvest processes can strengthen the waste-reduction benefits of monitoring technology. Firms seeking to maintain their sustainability goals can capture most of the profit gains from monitoring by carefully moderating increases in purchase quantities. This paper was accepted by Jeannette Song, operations management. Supplemental Material: The online appendices and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2024.07382 .

title: Retail on Wheels: A Time-Sensitive Traveling Salesman Problem
abstract: Rapid advancement in self-driving technology has brought mobile retail into the spotlight. Motivated by its potential, we present a model, theory, and insights into the operations of mobile retail, where a fleet of wheeled stores traverses a service region, selectively seeks locations in which to perch, and fulfills local customer demand. The goal of retailers is to strike a balance between perching and migrating to maximize total revenue. To dispatch such stores, retailers need to consider the following time-sensitive factors: (i) how busy the service is, (ii) how soon customers will arrive, and (iii) how quickly freshness decays. We propose and analyze a model that incorporates these factors into the classical traveling salesman problem (TSP), which we call the “time-sensitive TSP.” Using the continuous approximation approach, we derive the optimal revenue as well as the upper and lower bounds in the asymptotic regime as candidate locations increase to infinity. The tightness of the bounds is validated. Our analysis demonstrates that store mobility creates value by bringing proximity to customers. We further uncover the effects of these time-sensitive features on decision making. Specifically, the scaling relationship between revenue and fleet size is affected by customer tardiness and busyness. Busyness determines stores’ ability to expand their service, whereas tardiness affects how effectively stores can utilize the initial high-freshness period. These findings deepen our understanding of mobile retail operations. This paper was accepted by Karan Girotra, operations management. Funding: J. Cao acknowledges the support from McCombs Research Excellence Grant. W. Qi acknowledges the support from the National Natural Science Foundation of China [Grants 72242106, 72188101, and 72521001]. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2023.04259 .

title: Marketing misinformation in the age of AI
abstract: Abstract We shine a spotlight on marketing misinformation—claims about products and brands that contradict or distort verifiable facts. Misinformation may be created unintentionally or intentionally by companies, competitors, customers, or third parties seeking to harm companies or consumers. We focus on the role of AI in creating, obfuscating, and disseminating misinformation in the form of text, audio, images, and videos generated using large language models. This type of information can pose a substantial risk for brand safety. Consumers may be aware that AI can generate misinformation but may lack the ability to guard against it. We discuss how different stakeholders in the information ecosystem can help in the prevention and correction of misinformation and propose a future research agenda in this critical and fast‐growing area.

title: A window to the brand's soul: eyes express affect and impact consumer attitudes
journal_name: International Journal of Research in Marketing

title: Designing Liminal Spaces for Upstream Performativity: Lessons From The Futures Lab
abstract: Abstract This paper examines how business schools can function as liminal socio‐material infrastructures for upstream performative experimentation. Recent work has advanced management scholarship to foreground the role of imagination in theorizing for desirable futures. However, less is understood about how alternatives might be made sufficiently tangible and credible to acquire performative force in the first place. This is compounded by performativity research that has largely examined how theories acquire effects once they circulate in markets and organizations. To address this, and drawing on a 5‐year qualitative case study of The Futures Lab (TFL), I show how shared visual workspaces, repeated critique, direct engagement with stakeholders, and the making and remaking of maps, models and prototypes enabled participants to (re)‐search alternative futures by making possibilities visible, contestable and open to revision. These practices produced credible fictions: tangible yet provisional representations to which external actors could attach, align with, and sometimes enrol around emerging possibilities. I develop prefigurative theorizing as a materially experimental mode of prospective theorizing, showing how desirable futures gain performative force not through imagination alone, but by being externalized, provisionally enacted, tested and revised in the present. The study thereby specifies conditions through which business schools can cultivate upstream performativity.

title: Sustainability as a Selective Safeguard: ESG, Earnings Management Types, and Financial Distress in an Emerging Market
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance is associated with lower financial distress arising from earnings management in an emerging market and whether this association differs for accrual‐based earnings management (AEM) versus real earnings management (REM). While prior research generally treats ESG as a uniformly effective governance mechanism, it largely overlooks differences in strategies adopted by managers for earnings management and the conditions under which ESG can constrain such actions. Addressing this gap, this study conceptualizes ESG as a selective governance safeguard whose effectiveness depends on the nature of earnings management. Drawing on agency, stakeholder, and signalling theories, we argue that ESG may attenuate the negative risk arising from accounting‐based opacity but not from real operational manipulation. Using a panel of 569 Indian nonfinancial firms from 2019 to 2023 and fixed effects regressions, we examine the interplay between AEM, REM, and financial distress proxied by the emerging‐market Altman Z ‐score. The results show that ESG attenuates the negative association between AEM and financial health but does not moderate the relationship between REM and financial health. Results are robust to winsorization and GMM estimations. These findings identify a key boundary condition in ESG's governance role, suggesting that ESG is not a comprehensive safeguard against all forms of managerial opportunism.

title: The Impact of Strategically Involved Middle Managers on Green Outcomes
abstract: ABSTRACT There has been extensive research on the determinants of green outcomes, particularly from a management perspective. Despite the crucial roles of middle managers (MMs) in management theory, the existing literature emphasizes top managers as the primary managerial drivers of green outcomes. This study addresses this gap by examining whether and how MMs involved in strategy (MMIS) contribute to firms' green outcomes. A total of 107 valid responses were collected through an online cross‐sectional survey with a structured questionnaire. Hierarchical linear regression and bootstrap analyses were used to test the model. The empirical results reveal that MMIS can significantly affect green innovation (GI). Additionally, for MMIS to contribute to environmental performance (EP), green dynamic capabilities (GDCs) act as an effective mediator. The results further indicate that regulatory stakeholder pressures (RSPs) moderate the relationship between MMIS and GI, whereas no moderating effect of RSPs is observed between MMIS and EP. The study suggests that while strategically involved MMs can effectively improve short‐term green outcomes (GI), enabling them to drive long‐term green outcomes (EP) requires cultivating appropriate organizational capabilities. With a unique dataset collected exclusively from MMs, the study extends the green management literature and informs practitioners about MMs as “green champions.”

title: Trust in algorithmic governance: How algorithmic control and fairness shape justice perceptions and employee voice in luxury hotels
A study analyzing factors retarding digital transformation and configuration pathways: Based on the perspective of digital transformation acceptors
abstract: The high-touch service nature of the hospitality industry highlights that the success of digital transformation depends primarily on human factors rather than technology itself. Existing research indicates that approximately 80% of strategic initiatives fail due to employee resistance to change or capability deficits. Furthermore, nearly three-quarters of middle managers and staff exhibit resistance toward such transformations. This alarming trend raises a fundamental question: how can the hospitality industry navigate the inherent tension between high-touch emotional labor and digital depersonalization to transform employee resistance into proactive adoption? While traditional research frequently focuses on hotel management as change promoters, this study shifts the analytical focus to hotel employees as change recipients. Guided by cognitive appraisal and social information processing theories, within the context of hotel service scenarios, this research constructs models of resistance mitigation and antecedent condition linkages across individual, organizational, and managerial levels. Through an empirical analysis of 545 survey responses from various hotel categories and the application of fuzzy set qualitative comparative analysis (fsQCA), this study systematically explores the mechanisms of resistance alleviation and the synergistic effects of the identified influencing factors. Regression results indicate that digital literacy, digital strategy consensus, and perceptions of digital technology warmth and capability are negatively associated with hotel employee resistance to digital transformation. Additionally, organizational strategic flexibility and digital leadership positively moderate the relationships between these individual factors and resistance. The fsQCA results further identify two primary equifinal patterns sufficient for fostering a state of low resistance, demonstrating how strong digital leadership serves as a social cue that effectively compensates for the absence of organizational strategic flexibility. Ultimately, this research deepens the understanding of human-centered digital transformation in the hospitality sector and offers theoretical frameworks for managers to mitigate employee resistance to digital initiatives, thereby facilitating successful strategic implementation.

title: When passion breeds silence: How coworkers’ work passion elicits envy and employee silence in hospitality workplaces
abstract: While work passion is well-studied as an intrapersonal motivational construct, its interpersonal consequences for coworkers remain underexplored. Drawing primarily on the Social Functional Theory of Emotions, we examine how employees' observed work passion functions as a social signal that elicits coworker envy and, in turn, shapes silence behaviors. Across four studies (three experiments and a multi-source dyadic field study with hotel employees), we find a robust asymmetric pattern: harmonious passion primarily elicits benign envy, which is associated with prosocial silence, whereas obsessive passion primarily elicits malicious envy, which is associated with deviant silence. Cross-path effects were weaker and less consistent across studies. An exploratory field-study finding suggests that obsessive passion may occasionally relate to benign envy, although this association did not emerge in the experiments and warrants replication. This research extends passion theory by highlighting its interpersonal signaling effects and reframes silence as a strategic emotion-regulation response.

title: The dark side of disrespect: How workplace incivility breeds service sabotage and turnover
abstract: This study examines how different sources of workplace incivility affect frontline hotel employees. Drawing on Conservation of Resources Theory and Social Identity Theory, Study 1 compares the effects of employee incivility (originating internally) and customer incivility (originating externally) on emotional exhaustion. Based on a scenario-based experiment with 263 participants, the results show that employee incivility causes greater emotional exhaustion than customer incivility. Study 2 further differentiates in-group sources by their hierarchical level—supervisor, same-level colleague, and subordinate—and examines their specific impacts on emotional exhaustion, which, in turn, affects sabotage and turnover intentions. Using survey data from 302 respondents, the findings reveal that same-level colleague incivility has the strongest negative impact, followed by supervisor, subordinate, and customer incivility. Perceived organizational support buffers these effects. The study contributes to workplace incivility research in collectivist and high power-distance cultures and offers practical implications for hotel management.

title: Wellbeing in and through projects: A multilevel view
Heart work for empowerment: how subordinate emotional labor influences leader empowering behavior
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how subordinates’ emotional labor strategies (deep acting versus surface acting) toward supervisors influence leader empowering behavior, with leader–member exchange (LMX) as a mediating mechanism and leader emotional intelligence as a moderating condition. Design/methodology/approach The authors conducted two complementary studies. Study 1 used a scenario-based experiment (n = 222 hotel and restaurant managers) to establish causal relationships. Study 2 used a two-wave, multisource field survey (n = 229 supervisor-subordinate dyads in hotels and restaurants) to examine mediating and moderating mechanisms. Findings Deep acting (genuinely experiencing expected emotions) increases leader empowering behavior, whereas surface acting (feigning emotions) decreases it. LMX partially mediates both relationships, and leader emotional intelligence strengthens both effects. Practical implications Empowerment decisions should be based primarily on employees’ competence, performance and task readiness rather than emotional conformity. Organizations should develop employees’ emotion-regulation resources while training supervisors to distinguish emotional impressions from task-relevant evidence. Originality/value This study challenges the assumption that empowerment flows solely from leaders. The authors demonstrate that subordinates actively shape empowerment through emotional labor, with effects contingent on leader emotional intelligence. This reveals emotional labor as an LMX antecedent and shows that empowerment in hospitality organizations results from interactions between subordinate emotional capabilities and leader perceptual skills, not leader characteristics alone.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Implementing gender-focused DEI initiatives in B2B sales: Navigating cultural forces and organizational resistance
abstract: Diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) has emerged as a strategic imperative in business-to-business markets. Yet, existing DEI implementation frameworks underplay the roles of frontline translation and organizational resistance. This omission is consequential in global sales contexts, where institutional forces amplify structural barriers to gender-focused DEI initiatives. Drawing on institutional theory and interview data from 41 sales and marketing professionals in India, this study examines how gender-focused DEI initiatives are received within a business context characterized by high power distance and entrenched masculine norms. Conceptualizing DEI implementation as a process of frontline translation, the authors develop an empirically grounded 2 × 2 typology of resistance to DEI initiatives. The typology is organized along two dimensions—form (ideological vs. operational) and level (active vs. passive)—and reveals four distinct resistance types, each driven by specific antecedents rooted in cultural norms and sales-specific constraints. The authors also identify contextually adaptive mitigation strategies and theorize the causal mechanisms linking them to specific drivers of resistance, offering actionable pathways for achieving sustained change. Collectively, findings demonstrate that effective DEI implementation requires strategies that are both culturally informed and operationally grounded. Further, the resulting framework provides a foundation for future research on gender-focused DEI across diverse institutional settings.

title: Artificial intelligence is not enough to enhance organizational performance
abstract: This study examines the relationship between Artificial Intelligence (AI), supply chain visibility, supplier integration, and organizational performance through the lens of Organizational Information Processing Theory (OIPT). Drawing on empirical data from UK-based organizations that have adopted AI technologies, we employ structural equation modeling along with mediation and moderation analyses to test our hypotheses. The findings indicate that AI does not have a significant direct effect on performance; instead, its impact is fully mediated through supply chain visibility and supplier integration. This supports the view that AI-driven supply chain visibility acts as an information-processing mechanism that enhances firms' ability to coordinate, collaborate, and integrate with supply chain partners, thereby improving organizational performance. Furthermore, supply uncertainty positively moderates the relationship between supplier integration and performance, amplifying the benefits under conditions of higher uncertainty. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying AI's indirect role in driving performance and highlighting the importance of embedding AI within broader organizational capabilities. It also offers practical insights for managers seeking to leverage AI to enhance supply chain integration and organizational effectiveness. • AI does not directly enhance organizational performance. • AI-enabled supply chain visibility strengthens supplier integration. • Supply chain visibility and supplier integration jointly mediate the AI–performance link. • Supplier integration contributes more strongly to performance under high supply uncertainty. • The findings extend Organizational Information Processing Theory in AI-enabled supply chains.

title: Flying low for greener farms: Configurational pathways linking the low-altitude economy to agricultural green total factor productivity in China
abstract: The low-altitude economy is increasingly viewed as a new technological frontier for agricultural transformation, yet its relationship with agricultural green total factor productivity remains poorly understood. This study examines how low-altitude economy-related conditions are associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity in China. We develop an institutional-technological-scenario framework and apply a sequential mixed-method design that combines qualitative coding, necessary condition analysis and dynamic fuzzy-set qualitative comparative analysis. The empirical analysis uses a balanced panel of 30 Chinese provinces from 2014 to 2022, covering 270 province-year observations. The period is treated as a formative and pre-consolidation stage of the low-altitude economy rather than as a fully mature integrated system. The results show that no single condition constitutes a statistically supported necessary condition for high agricultural green total factor productivity. Exploratory bottleneck analysis nevertheless reveals descriptive threshold patterns at higher outcome levels. The dynamic configurational analysis identifies three pathways associated with high agricultural green total factor productivity, namely technology-application coupling, institution-innovation coupling and scale-application diffusion. The non-high productivity configuration further shows that enterprise development, policy support and market support may fail to translate into green productivity improvement when industrial application is absent. Regional and temporal analyses reveal substantial spatial and temporal heterogeneity. The findings suggest that the low-altitude economy is better understood as an emerging socio-technical enabling system rather than as a single UAV-based technology, and that agricultural green transformation depends on the configuration of institutional support, technological capacity and application scenarios.

title: Can Stress Curb Unethical Employee Behavior? Evidence From Frontline Contexts
abstract: ABSTRACT Unethical employee behavior is widespread in frontline service contexts and can severely damage organizations through theft, service sabotage, and reputational harm. Because such unethical behavior can emerge under conditions of work‐related stress, workplace stressors are typically viewed as risk factors that undermine ethical judgment while promoting misconduct. However, demanding frontline situations can also foster competence, responsibility, and growth, raising the possibility that some stressors can reduce rather than increase unethical behavior. Using the challenge–hindrance stressor framework and transactional stress theory, we examine how different stressor types influence unethical employee behavior. Across three studies with 708 frontline employees, we find that challenge stressors (opportunities for achievement) reduce unethical behavior while hindrance stressors (barriers to growth) increase it. Self‐efficacy emerges as a key mechanism, increasing under challenge stressors to reduce unethical behavior and decreasing under hindrance stressors to increase it. In addition, we explore the moderating roles of two coping strategies: self‐led (internally initiated) and peer‐led (externally initiated) development. Self‐led development moderates both stressor types, while peer‐led development only affects challenge stressors. Our findings offer managers valuable insights into harnessing stressors' positive aspects rather than solely mitigating their negative effects.

title: How Color Differentiation Shapes Luxury Evaluation: Converging Evidence From Neural and Self‐Report Data
abstract: ABSTRACT The present research examines how color differentiation shapes not only consumers' immediate evaluations of products but also their expectations about how long those products will remain appealing. In luxury markets, where value is closely tied to perception of timelessness, subtle visual cues may influence anticipated length of ownership and use. Study 1 combines fMRI and self‐report measures to show that exposure to lower‐differentiation color composition is associated with greater activation in reward‐related brain regions (including bilateral nucleus accumbens and the anterior cingulate cortex) and with higher liking, choice, willingness to pay, and perceived length of product use. Importantly, neural reward responses predict downstream behavioral intentions. Study 2 provides evidence consistent with the proposed role of chromatic timelessness: lower color differentiation increases perceived chromatic timelessness, which is associated with greater liking and, subsequently, with stronger choice and long‐term use intentions. Study 3 establishes a boundary condition, showing that these effects are driven primarily by consumers low in sensation seeking. Together, the findings contribute to research on visual design and consumer inference by linking the degree of color differentiation within the bundled color composition to reward processing, timelessness perceptions, and individual differences, while offering actionable guidance for luxury brands seeking to foster enduring consumer value.

title: Influencer Breaks as Relational Interruptions: The Roles of Attribution, Disappointment, and Emotional Attachment
abstract: ABSTRACT Temporary breaks from content creation have become increasingly common among social media influencers, yet little is known about how such interruptions affect follower retention. Drawing on attribution theory and relationship research, we conceptualize influencer breaks as relational interruptions and examine how followers respond to these events. Across a pilot field study and three experiments, we examine how followers' perceptions of break controllability shape disappointment and unfollow intention, and how emotional attachment conditions these effects. The findings show that breaks perceived as more controllable generate greater disappointment and stronger unfollow intention than breaks perceived as less controllable. Disappointment mediates the relationship between perceived controllability and unfollow intention. Although emotionally attached followers are generally less likely to unfollow, emotional attachment also amplifies emotional responses to controllability cues, strengthening the indirect effect of perceived controllability on unfollow intention. These findings contribute to influencer marketing research by extending the concept of relational interruptions to influencer–follower relationships and demonstrating how attributional interpretations influence follower retention during temporary breaks. More broadly, they apply attribution theory to digitally mediated relationships by identifying disappointment as the mechanism linking perceived controllability to unfollow intention. The findings also offer practical insights for influencers, brands, and agencies seeking to manage breaks while preserving follower relationships.

title: The impact of language formality on review helpfulness across online platforms
abstract: Purpose To date, a broad range of factors have been linked with review helpfulness, such as star rating, rating extremity and review length, as well as linguistic features such as text complexity and readability. A hitherto unstudied linguistic style concept in relation to helpfulness of online reviews is text formality. Formal written text is precise, lucid, eloquent and persuasive, unlike informal text which is written in a style more akin to spoken conversation between friends. This study aims to show that text formality has a major influence on the perceived helpfulness of online reviews, more so than text complexity and readability. Design/methodology/approach A Tobit model is used to assess the relative importance of text formality, complexity and readability, as well as to control for a range of factors known to influence review helpfulness. Findings Text formality has higher relative importance at driving helpfulness votes than either of text complexity or readability. However, too much formality can reduce the number of helpfulness votes, thereby creating a curvilinear effect. Research limitations/implications The context is limited to two experiential products, movies and books. Practical implications Amazon movie and book reviews already have about the right level of text formality, while Google movie reviews and LibraryThing book reviews need to increase their formality. Review platforms can provide review writers with a formality score to enable them to obtain more helpfulness votes. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first study to apply an arithmetic measure of text formality to online reviews. The authors also contrast the effect of text linguistic features for the same movies or books across two platforms, a type of analysis not yet considered in the literature.

title: Subsidizing Consumers to Share: An Economic Analysis of Manufacturers’ Cooperation with Sharing Platforms
Beyond Integration to Validation: The Differential Impact of Physicians’ Knowledge Collaboration Behaviors on Online Medical Team Performance
Inclusive Leadership as a Site of Struggle: Resistance and Mitigation Strategies for Sustaining Inclusion for Historically Marginalized Employees
abstract: ABSTRACT Scholars emphasize inclusive leadership's benefits for leaders and employees, yet existing theory largely overlooks the challenges leaders face when addressing disparities experienced by historically marginalized employees. Drawing on an inductive study of 47 historically marginalized STEM employees and 14 leaders they identified as inclusive, we model inclusive leadership as a three‐part process: (1) leaders’ inclusion efforts (attentive learning, talent amplification, and structural debiasing); (2) resistance to these efforts (skepticism, gatekeeping, fit critiques, and non‐compliance); and (3) leader strategies to mitigate resistance and protect inclusion (explaining value, co‐crafting strategies, evaluating fit critiques, and managing change momentum). We triangulate findings and test our theory's boundary conditions using qualitative data from three additional STEM samples: racial minority men, lower‐ranking women, and White males. The first two samples replicate our model; the third reveals that White men may perceive inclusive leadership differently than historically marginalized employees. By centering the perspectives of those most affected by bias, our study extends inclusive leadership theory. We offer a processual view that moves beyond detailing inclusive behaviors to highlight the challenges leaders face enacting them.

title: Economic Inequality Reduces Sustainable Consumption: Cross-National and Experimental Evidence and Psychological Mechanisms
abstract: Abstract This research investigates the relationship between economic inequality and sustainable consumption, highlighting how socioeconomic disparities shape consumer behavior. Across three studies—using secondary data from 20 countries, a vignette experiment, and UK survey data—we provide empirical evidence that individuals report lower levels of sustainable consumption when inequality levels are objectively high, perceived as high, or experimentally manipulated as high. This effect can be explained through norm activation theory: As inequality rises, consumers feel less responsible for environmental damage and are less aware of the environmental impact of their consumption choices. These dynamics weaken sustainability-oriented personal norms and, in turn, reduce sustainable consumption. Our findings suggest that reducing economic inequality can significantly enhance sustainable consumption.

title: Media-Manager Sentiment Gap and Stock Returns: Evidence from China
External collaboration and local knowledge divergence in regional knowledge spaces
Innovation adoption across regions: psychological openness and the early diffusion of digital platforms
abstract: Early regional adoption is crucial for platform-enabled innovations because their viability depends on enough people within a region adopting them to generate network effects. Existing research on regional innovation diffusion explains early adoption largely through demographic, economic, infrastructural, or institutional conditions, paying limited attention to regional population psychology. We conceptualize regional psychological openness as an invisible social infrastructure that is relevant for understanding early platform adoption. To test this idea, we introduce a newly curated dataset that allows us to trace the initial development of three major platform innovations (i.e., accommodation sharing platforms, ride-sharing platforms, social media platforms) across hundreds of U.S. metropolitan regions. Across all three platform types, regions differ markedly in early adoption. We link these adoption data to large-scale geo-referenced personality information from millions of U.S. residents ( N = 3,234,899). Results show that regional psychological openness consistently predicts earlier uptake even after accounting for demographic, socio-economic, social, infrastructural, geographical, and other psychological characteristics. In sum, the study advances a behavioral perspective on regional innovation adoption by integrating population psychology into explanations of platform diffusion.

title: Steering and Setting Free: Insights From a 20‐Year Retrospective Case Study of a Security and Justice Organization's Digital Transformation
abstract: ABSTRACT Advances in digital technologies are expected to fundamentally change how organizations operate and create value. Empirical studies show that public organizations face difficulties organizing and sustaining this digital transformation. To better understand these challenges, this study examines the organizational mechanisms underlying digital transformation in a public organization over the past 20 years. Our findings show that this transformation was primarily enabled by an emergent change approach, with influential planned changes occurring only occasionally. We identify the organizational mechanisms underlying both types of change and analyze their interdependence. Our findings suggest that both emergent and planned change approaches may be needed to enable digital transformation in public organizations effectively, but that combining them is complex in practice.

title: Staging the invisible: tracing public value co-creation through sub-micro infrastructures configured by information coordination organizations in China’s disaster information services
abstract: In disaster information services, citizen- and volunteer-generated information arrives as dispersed, uncertain reports rather than usable response information. This qualitative case study examines how Organization Z, a Chinese NGO functioning as an Information Coordination Organization (ICO), makes such information usable for response through sub-micro infrastructures. Data comprise 43 volunteer and 11 coordinator interviews, longitudinal participant observation, and multi-source materials. Four mechanisms emerged: emotional activation makes participation visible; epistemic calibration supports report credibility through traceability and comparability; cross-sector translation makes verified information interpretable and acceptable as a basis for response action; and reflexive learning makes response experience partially reusable. We conceptualize staging as a conditional account of public value formation organized around the four thresholds of visibility, credibility, legitimate actionability, and partial reusability. The study contributes to public value co-creation research by explaining how ICO information work conditions whether information-related participation contributes to disaster response and public value formation.

title: When Geography Dilutes Accountability: Managerial Discretion and Fiscal Expansion in Local Government
abstract: Democratic accountability assumes that the citizens who bear the costs of government decisions can sanction the officials who make them. We identify a structural break in this assumption. When a city funds itself through taxes that fall partly on nonresidents (highway travelers, commuters, and regional shoppers who cannot vote in local elections) the electoral link between bearing costs and imposing sanctions weakens. Analyzing two decades of Texas municipal data (2000–2019) with two-way fixed effects and generalized synthetic control methods, we find that cities better positioned to shift costs onto nonvoters raise resident fiscal exposure more, after they adopt dedicated local sales taxes. This pattern is strongest for cities on or near major metropolitan areas and highways, whereas geographically isolated cities, where residents bear nearly all costs, show little change. It reverses the relief that classical tax-exportation theory predicts and reveals an accountability gap that funds discretionary fiscal expansion. The gap proves temporary: fiscal outcomes across contexts converge within six to thirteen years. Geography, we conclude, shapes democratic accountability as powerfully as electoral rules.
journal_name: The American Review of Public Administration

title: Cohort Profile Update: The Adverse Events Questionnaire of Medications and Vaccines (ADE-Q) in the Estonian Biobank
Response to Abnet’s comments on “Alcohol consumption and cancer risk in South Korea and the UK”
Classification Matters: Divergent Estimates of Dementia Risk Factors in the Health and Retirement Study
abstract: Abstract Clinical dementia diagnosis requires substantial expertise and is complex and costly. Therefore, large population-based studies often lack gold-standard longitudinal diagnoses and instead use classification algorithms employing cognitive, functional, and health-related measures to identify dementia. We evaluated whether algorithm choice affects conclusions regarding dementia risk in the nationally representative Health and Retirement Study (HRS; 2010-2020). We constructed four algorithm-specific samples of participants age 70+ without dementia in 2010: Langa-Weir (n=6,498), Hudomiet (n=6,556), Expert (n=5,751), and Wu (n=5,935). Participants were followed until first dementia classification, death, or censoring. We estimated dementia incidence rates (IRs) and used adjusted Cox models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) for known risk factors. Dementia IRs per 1000 person-years meaningfully varied across algorithms, from 26.5 (95% CI 24.5–28.5, Hudomiet) to 62.8 (59.9–65.8, Expert). Sociodemographic risk factor associations also varied substantially. HRs for education (< vs. ≥high school) ranged from 1.36 (1.19–1.54, Hudomiet) to 2.22 (1.98–2.50, Langa-Weir), and HRs non-Hispanic Black vs. non-Hispanic White ranged from 1.86 (1.53–2.27, Expert) to 2.74 (2.40–3.12, Langa-Weir). Differences were less pronounced for health-related risk factors. In the absence of gold standard longitudinal diagnosis in HRS, researchers should examine the robustness of findings across multiple algorithms.

title: Age 70 as a threshold for vulnerable road user case fatality: A population-based study of older drivers in Taiwan
abstract: Age-based licensing renewal policies are implemented in aging societies to protect vulnerable road users (VRUs), yet the rationale for selecting age thresholds remains uncertain. This study examined whether age 70 represents a threshold for VRU case fatality among crash-involved older drivers and whether license status modifies this association. This population-based cross-sectional study analyzed Taiwanese police-reported crash data from 2011 to 2024 involving nonprofessional car drivers aged ≥ 50 years and VRUs. Driver age was modeled categorically and continuously using restricted cubic splines (RCSs). License status was examined as an exploratory effect modifier. A prespecified primary linear-spline analysis directly tested for a change in slope at age 70, while supporting RCS analyses evaluated overall nonlinearity. Multivariable logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors estimated adjusted odds ratios (AORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 602,782 crash-involved VRUs, 2,789 sustained fatal injuries (0.46%). The prespecified analysis did not detect a change in slope at age 70 (change-in-slope AOR per year, 1.001; 95% CI, 0.977–1.025; P = 0.95), and the selected 3-knot RCS specification provided no evidence of overall nonlinearity ( P = 0.24). Compared with drivers aged 50–64 years, odds of VRU case fatality were higher among drivers aged 65–69 years (AOR 1.15; 95% CI, 1.03–1.28) and ≥ 70 years (AOR 1.14; 95% CI, 1.01–1.29). However, among drivers aged 65–99 years, age ≥ 70 years was not independently associated with VRU case fatality (AOR 1.08; 95% CI, 0.93–1.25; P = 0.32). Unlicensed driving was associated with higher odds of VRU case fatality (AOR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.62–2.28). Overall, the prespecified analysis did not detect a change in slope at age 70, while the association with unlicensed driving highlights a potentially important correlate of VRU case fatality among crash-involved older drivers.

title: Dynamic estimation of airport taxiway hotspots using spatio-temporal traffic and kinematic risk modeling
abstract: At busy airports, airfield operations are among the most safety-critical phases of flight because aircraft move through complex taxiway and runway-crossing networks. Despite ground-surveillance advances, taxiway conflicts remain a concern. We develop a traffic-based method for dynamic taxiway hotspot estimation that identifies conflict-prone locations without incident or accident histories. Unlike static FAA-defined hotspots, the method represents airfield infrastructure as a directed graph and uses agglomerative clustering to identify critical intersections. Hotspot scores combine spatial utilization probabilities from Runway–Gate routes with a KDE-based temporal overlap estimated from intersection arrival times. The trajectory-level score incorporates aircraft kinematics, including relative speed and convergence geometry. We validated the model using one full day of surface-surveillance data from Hartsfield–Jackson Atlanta International Airport (1 July 2019) and cross-validated it on an independent post-pandemic day (10 September 2024). The model identified clusters corresponding to all three 2019 FAA-designated hotspots within the northern study area, ranking two of them among its top five (Recall@5 = 0.67 vs. 0.33 for an aircraft-count baseline). Cross-year validation also identified both 2024 FAA hotspots as stable or rising high-risk clusters, and the method flagged conflict-prone locations not shown in FAA airport diagrams. Arrival and departure operations yielded distinct hotspot patterns: arrival risks clustered at runway exits, while departure risks clustered at runway-entry merge points. Sliding windows capture temporal changes, enabling dynamic estimation. By combining traffic-based hotspot detection, kinematic risk integration, operation-specific analysis, and a trajectory-level collision-risk score, the method bridges offline analysis and real-time conflict-risk monitoring.

title: Latent profiles of identified support needs and First Nations inequities in the Canadian child welfare system
Mediators and Moderators of Treatment Outcome Following Online Mindfulness and Cognitive-Behavioral Treatment for Female Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder
abstract: eSense is a digital tool delivering mindfulness-based therapy (MBT) and cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to individuals with female sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD). eSense is feasible, usable, satisfying, and efficacious, and helps overcome barriers to care. We sought to examine potential mediators and moderators of improvements in sexual desire and distress following use of eSense. Women with SIAD (n = 129, mean age 44.8 ± 12.3 in the MBT arm and 41.9 ± 13.1 in the CBT arm) were randomly assigned to arm and completed self-report measures at baseline, mid-treatment, immediately post-treatment, and 6-month follow-up. Potential mediators were changes in depression, posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms (PTSD), and avoidance of sexual activity. We examined treatment expectations after module 1 as a potential moderator, and partner involvement, homework completion, and modules completed as process indicators that may predict magnitude of improvement. Decreases in depressive and PTSD symptoms were associated with improvements in sexual desire and distress in the MBT arm, and reductions in sexual avoidance were associated with improvements in both arms. Higher expectations for treatment were associated with greater improvements in desire and distress for those in the CBT arm only, whereas partner involvement, homework completion, and number of eSense modules completed were associated with improvements in both arms. This study helps identify putative mechanisms by which digital health tools for SIAD, like eSense, may be effective, and to identify participant characteristics as well as treatment engagement factors that might be associated with differential responses to online MBT and CBT.

title: Predictors of Sexual Aggression Intentions Among Sexual Minority Men: Exploring the Utility of Vignette Methodologies
abstract: Sexual violence (SV) is prevalent yet understudied among sexual minority men (SMM), leaving gaps in understanding perpetration risk. Experimental analogues are commonly used to examine SV perpetration among heterosexual samples, yet little to no research has examined whether these methods are relevant to SMM, limiting researchers’ ability to identify unique predictors among this population. This study examined the feasibility of using vignette methodologies with SMM and investigated empirically supported predictors of aggressive sexual intentions. First, among the full sample (N = 604), we assessed the feasibility and validity of using written SV vignettes with SMM (n = 253) by comparing their perceptions of scenario realism, immersion, and sexual arousal to those of heterosexual men (n = 351). SMM rated the vignettes as similarly realistic and engaging, supporting their utility for this population. Second, limiting the analytic sample to SMM, we tested a model in which internalized homophobia predicted sexually aggressive intentions via male rape myth acceptance (MRMA), conditional on self-reported sexual interest and perceived partner interest. These findings highlight the importance of addressing MRMA and situational misperceptions in prevention efforts. Tailored interventions that consider both internalized stigma and contextual risk factors are critical for reducing SV perpetration risk among SMM.

title: Correction to: Resignation and return to work in patients receiving allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation
Arabic Validation of the Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale: Psychometric Properties, Measurement Invariance, and Gender-Specific Network Analysis
abstract: Problematic pornography use (PPU) remains understudied in Arabic-speaking populations, partly due to the limited availability of culturally validated assessment tools. This study translated and validated the Arabic version of the Problematic Pornography Consumption Scale (PPCS) and examined gender-based differences in symptom structure. A total of 959 Egyptian university students who watched pornography at least once per week (65.1% male, 34.9% female) completed the Arabic PPCS, along with standardized measures of depression, anxiety, perceived stress, and problematic internet use. Confirmatory factor analysis supported the original six-factor model (CFI = 0.950, RMSEA = 0.075, SRMR = 0.031), with the scale demonstrating excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = .95) and moderate-to-strong construct validity as indicated by positive correlations with measures of depression (r = .42), anxiety (r = .37), perceived stress (r = .37), and problematic internet use (r = .46; all p < .001). Overall, 22% of participants were identified as at risk for PPU. Measurement invariance across gender indicated the scale functioned similarly for males and females. Network analysis further revealed gender-specific symptom patterns, with tolerance emerging as the most central symptom among males and withdrawal most central among females. These findings provide initial validation of the Arabic PPCS and highlight the importance of culturally informed and gender-sensitive approaches to understanding PPU in Arabic-speaking populations.

title: Compensatory local turn?: municipal international relations and migration governance in Türkiye
abstract: This article examines how metropolitan municipalities and selected district municipalities in Türkiye have mobilised international relations in the context of migration governance. Based on a content analysis of municipalities’ international activities between 2014 and 2023, the study argues that international relations function primarily as an instrumental and compensatory mechanism rather than signalling a fully institutionalised ‘local turn’. While local authorities are increasingly engaging with international networks and projects to address migration-related challenges, these initiatives remain largely project-based and constrained by strong centralisation. The findings contribute to the urban governance literature by highlighting the contextual limits of the ‘local turn’ in migration governance.

title: Graph neural networks for transmission grid topology control: Busbar information asymmetry and heterogeneous representations
Battery degradation and frequency stability considerations in the design of off-grid mining microgrids
A comprehensive review of global advanced metering infrastructure cost-benefit evidence and a data-integration framework for master-metered high-voltage apartment complexes
abstract: Advanced metering infrastructure (AMI) is the core sensing layer of decarbonizing grids, but its value is realized only where interval data reach the grid operator and the tariff setter. This review synthesizes three separate literatures: the functional evolution of metering; cross-national AMI cost-benefit analyses (CBAs) covering Europe, Japan and South Korea; and data governance in master-metered multi-occupancy buildings. Deconstructing CBA formulations shows that only labor substitution accrues directly from meter installation; every other benefit category depends on coefficients that require data reachability. This helps account for the order-of-magnitude dispersion in benefit–cost ratios, which is associated more closely with the evaluation boundary and complementary institutions than with technology cost, and exposes a structural vulnerability in South Korea. Deployment reached 20 million low-voltage customers in 2024 (B/C 1.03), yet the 11.96 million households in 28,253 high-voltage apartment complexes largely sit outside the metering data pipeline: the complex, not the household, is the contracting customer, and household meters are private assets behind the supply point. AMI hardware reaches 53% of these households but only 15.4% (1.84 million) are linked to the utility, leaving 4.5 million households whose interval data reach a private server and go no further. The exclusion became binding in 2026, when residential time-of-use (TOU) tariffs were deferred nationally for want of AMI coverage. Japan’s Specified Metering (IoT-route) system, Australia’s embedded networks and North American master metering show that such arrangements can be made useful without dissolving supply contracts. We propose a conceptual, hypothesis-generating architecture for an apartment-dedicated meter data management system (APT-MDMS) with gateway-based integration, server-side TOU settlement, a consent and privacy architecture, and a five-year, four-segment roadmap. The proposed architecture and roadmap are design hypotheses whose system interfaces, reliability, costs and economic viability require pilot validation.

title: Maximising self-consumption in energy communities: a comparative study of demand flexibility and dynamic sharing strategies
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) have emerged as a vehicle for actively engaging citizens in the energy transition, enabling them to generate, consume, store and share renewable energy. Maximising collective self-consumption is a key objective of ECs, as it allows members to better capture the benefits of shared energy generation, and several approaches have been developed toward this goal. However, most of existing works aim to maximise ECs’ self-consumption by applying demand side management strategies or increasing the benefits with dynamic energy sharing, but not combining them. This study is one of the first to propose a data-driven framework that leverages machine learning, optimisation, battery management and dynamic energy sharing strategies to increase the self-consumption of ECs. The impact of the optimisation and dynamic energy sharing coefficients on ECs’ self-consumption and electricity costs was examined, together with their combination. The application of the proposed framework to an established Renewable Energy Community (REC) in Spain shows that dynamic energy sharing yields better results compared to load optimisation, and their combination shows more promising results. Permitting more frequent updates of dynamic energy-sharing coefficients can improve the allocation of locally generated energy and support higher member-level self-consumption, particularly in communities with heterogeneous and seasonal demand profiles.

title: Multi-head actor-critic proximal policy optimization for coordinated control of EV charging and battery storage in PV-integrated microgrids
Institutional resilience and land-acquisition governance: Participation and conflict-management mechanisms in the Jakarta–Bandung High-Speed Railway project
Can digital-real integration effectively curb urban sprawl? Evidence from China using double/debiased machine learning
abstract: Urban sprawl (URS) has become a major challenge to China’s sustainable development under the backdrop of rapid urbanization. Digital-real integration (DRI) provides a new pathway for urban spatial governance, yet its concrete impacts and mechanisms remain insufficiently tested. Based on panel data from 280 prefecture-level Chinese cities between 2013 and 2023, this study constructs a multidimensional DRI index and employs a partially linear double/debiased machine learning (DML) framework to estimate the effect of DRI on URS. Multiple robustness checks, including complementary instrumental-variable analyses, yield results consistent with the baseline finding. The findings show that a one-unit increase in DRI is associated with a 0.06-unit reduction in the URS index, and this conclusion holds under various robustness tests. The mechanism analysis provides evidence consistent with three potential transmission pathways: industrial structure upgrading, stronger aggregate city-level correspondence between employment opportunities and resident population, and reduced dependence on highway commuting. Further heterogeneity analysis reveals that the restraining effect of DRI is more pronounced in eastern regions, major national urban agglomerations, and cities at more advanced stages of urban development. This study not only provides empirical evidence on how digital technologies reshape urban spatial structures but also offers policy implications for implementing differentiated digital governance strategies and enhancing the effectiveness of spatial planning.

title: Geological CO2 storage and methane recovery in heterogeneous coal seams: Fractal descriptors for parameter upscaling
abstract: CO 2 -enhanced coalbed methane recovery (CO 2 -ECBM) combines geological CO 2 storage with methane recovery as part of the carbon capture and storage (CCS) system. CO 2 injection alters coal pore–fracture systems. Evaluating reservoir responses requires further parameterization of the structural information obtained from laboratory characterization. Fractal descriptors have been used to quantify pore–fracture heterogeneity and relate structural characteristics to reservoir properties, but their interpretation and application in CO 2 -ECBM models remain inconsistent. This review summarizes fractal approaches to characterizing structural changes in coal after CO 2 exposure and their incorporation into adsorption, diffusion, deformation and permeability models. Quantitative analysis shows that fractal dimension values decreased after CO 2 exposure in 69.6% of the compiled observations, although the direction and magnitude varied among studies because coal properties and treatment conditions differed. The results identify fractal parameter relationships supported by data and compare normalized local sensitivities of selected component relations. Distinguishing descriptors of pore size distributions, transport pathways and fracture connectivity across methods and scales help translate laboratory measurements into reservoir parameters. These parameters inform assessments of CO 2 injectivity, storage capacity and methane recovery. Current applications remain limited by inconsistent definitions, uncertain parameter transfer and insufficient validation under reservoir conditions. Future research should integrate in situ experiments, coupled modeling and field observations. The aim is to improve fractal parameter upscaling for CO 2 storage and methane recovery in heterogeneous coal seams.

title: Upcycling automotive shredder residue into sustainable hybrid composite materials: a cost-effective solution for circular economy
abstract: Automotive shredder residue (ASR), the non-metallic fraction generated during end-of-life vehicle processing, remains a recycling challenge due to its complex composition and limited valorisation pathways. This study presents an approach for transforming 100% non-metallic ASR into hybrid composite panels using recovered plastic fractions as a self-bonding matrix and remaining components as reinforcement. Composite panels were fabricated by hot-press moulding using particle-size distributions and evaluated for mechanical, physical, thermal, and environmental properties. Reducing particle size increased flexural strength from 9.8 MPa to 15.4 MPa, while veneer lamination increased it to 43.2 MPa. The composites exhibited low water absorption (2.46% after 24 h), limited thickness swelling (3.7%), thermal stability to 470 °C, UL 94 HB-compliant flame propagation rate (12.45–13.86 mm/min), and negligible heavy-metal leaching. Life cycle assessment showed lower environmental impacts than commercial MDF and melamine boards. Improved flame performance could enable ASR hybrid panels in light structures.

title: Ecological Roles of Bacillus Lipopeptides in Mediating Plant–Microbe Interactions and Rhizosphere Community Dynamics
abstract: Abstract The plant-beneficial bacterium Bacillus velezensis and related Bacillus species are increasingly recognized as important contributors to plant growth and health, yet the ecological functions of their secondary metabolites in situ remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated how lipopeptides produced by Bacillus species influence plant performance and root-associated microbial communities. Using Arabidopsis thaliana as a model host, we show that bacterial lipopeptides produced during root colonization promote plant growth by enhancing the uptake of essential mineral elements, including magnesium, calcium, iron, and zinc. Transcriptomic analyses revealed that lipopeptides upregulated host genes involved in metal transport and homeostasis in roots, while downregulating negative regulators of metal uptake. The lipopeptide production reshaped the composition of root-associated bacterial communities by increasing the relative abundance of putatively beneficial taxa and altering overall rhizosphere community structure. Functional genes indicated that lipopeptide enrichment was associated with microbial pathways related to metal transport, nutrient acquisition, and stress adaptation, suggesting that lipopeptides modulate both plant and microbial traits relevant to nutrient cycling. These results provide new insight into the ecological roles of B. velezensis-derived metabolites in plant-associated microbiomes and highlight lipopeptides as promising targets for harnessing beneficial plant–microbe interactions in sustainable agriculture.

title: Long-Term Biogeochemical Stabilization of Carbonate-Bearing Pb–Zn–Cu Mine Tailings by Amendment-Assisted Phytostabilization
abstract: Abstract Legacy Pb–Zn–Cu mine tailings can remain barren and geochemically reactive for decades. Although amendment-assisted revegetation can establish short-term plant growth, sustained phytostabilization requires metal attenuation and soil-like development over years after amendment-derived nutrients and organic matter decline. We evaluated seven-year biogeochemical stabilization of carbonate-bearing tailings planted with the native legume Dalea purpurea. Biosolids (BS), biochar (BC), and arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) were incorporated into the upper 8 cm, while the underlying 12 cm remained unamended. Tailings pore water was monitored annually, and year-seven cores were analyzed by depth for organic carbon, PLFA-based microbial indicators, aqua-regia-extractable metals, sequential metal fractionation, and X-ray diffraction. Biosolids initially increased EC, DOC, DN, and dissolved Pb, Zn, and Cu, whereas BC- and/or AMF-containing treatments showed greater long-term reductions in dissolved metal concentrations. AMF-inoculated treatments increased organic carbon and microbial biomass indicators below the amended layer, while deeper root penetration was also observed, consistent with profile-scale biological development. Sequential extraction showed metal-specific repartitioning: Pb was primarily carbonate- and Fe/Mn oxide-associated; Zn remained partly carbonate-linked; and Cu shifted toward organic/sulfide-associated and residual pools, consistent with lower relative lability. These findings show that surface-applied amendment and planting strategies can promote coupled biological and geochemical stabilization in initially unamended deeper tailings layers, supporting ecosystem restoration beyond short-term surface revegetation.

title: Surface Chemistry Shapes Nanoplastic Mixture Responses in Developing Amniote Embryos
abstract: Abstract Nanoplastics (NPs) are an emerging environmental concern, yet their developmental impacts on terrestrial amniotes and their mixture effects are only beginning to be understood. Using a chicken embryo model, we compared the developmental and molecular effects of negatively charged (PS-COOH), positively charged (PS-NH2), and their equal-component mixture (50 nm). No significant mortality was observed across 0.1 to 10 ppm, whereas the lowest tested concentration (0.1 ppm) impaired growth and brain development without significantly increasing mortality. An IA-informed reference-response comparison showed that mixture effects were generally attenuated relative to reference responses derived from the experimentally tested single-particle treatments. Brain transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed distinct surface-chemistry-dependent responses: PS-COOH primarily affected extracellular matrix and glycan-related processes, whereas PS-NH2 altered synaptic, immune, and protein-quality-control pathways. The mixture induced the greatest number of DEGs; this broader omics response does not translate into higher phenotypic toxicity. DIABLO identified treatment-associated RNA-protein covariance, while reference-response comparisons indicated predominantly attenuated molecular responses among statistically supported deviations. Our findings demonstrate that coexposure to oppositely functionalized nanoplastics can reshape developmental and molecular responses during embryonic development.

title: Efficient Water Resistance via High-Spin-State Manganese Species in Low-Temperature NH 3 -SCR
abstract: Abstract Development of highly efficient catalysts for low-temperature NH3–SCR remains a significant challenge, especially in the presence of high concentrations of water vapor. Herein, we have engineered a unique MnCeO2-TDA catalyst with high-spin manganese species by using electron-donating thiophene groups, achieving an excellent NO conversion of over 93% at 160 °C and under 60,000 mL·g–1·h–1 conditions in the higher water vapor of 10–20 vol %. Experimental and theoretical calculations demonstrate that, due to, asymmetrically occupied eg orbitals, high-spin Mn3+ triggers a strong Jahn–Teller distortion, which greatly decreases the O2 dissociation energy (from 2.837 to 1.979 eV) and coactivates O2 and H2O to form the *OOH oxidative species. This enhanced redox ability facilitates NO oxidation and the “fast SCR” reaction, leading to excellent deNOx efficiency under higher levels of water vapor at low temperatures. This work offers a new approach to modulating the spin state of active centers to enhance water resistance in flue gas purification.

title: A Unified Quantitative Framework for Assessing Uncertainty in Microbial-Explicit Soil Carbon Models under Diverse Data Availability of Field Observations
abstract: Abstract Microbial-explicit soil carbon models offer mechanistic representations of soil carbon turnover, but their application to the field remains limited, which is commonly attributed to the scarce microbial observations. However, usually there are significant mismatches between model data requirements and the diverse data availability of field observations, which may greatly affect the uncertainty of soil carbon models and have been largely overlooked. Here, we developed a unified framework that systematically quantified how the field observation type, sampling frequency, and measurement uncertainty jointly constrained model parameters and long-term predictions of three representative microbial-explicit soil carbon models. We quantified how well observations of soil carbon stocks, soil respiration, microbial biomass carbon, and functional gene abundance can reduce the parameter and prediction uncertainties across a comprehensive set of field scenarios. High-frequency, low-error soil respiration observations, when combined with soil carbon measurements, dominated uncertainty reduction across carbon pools, while interestingly, microbial observations only provided conditional improvements for microbial and enzyme-related states. More microbial data did not necessarily yield more effective calibration information, and improvements in prediction accuracy required microbial observations with sufficiently small measurement errors. The unified quantitative framework would also help to design a data strategy when developing new soil carbon models to accurately predict soil carbon cycling.

title: Designing SynComs for Resilience beyond Efficiency
Trimester-Specific Associations of Prenatal Heat Exposure with Neonatal Amino Acid and Acylcarnitine Profiles
abstract: Abstract It remains unclear whether prenatal heat exposure is associated with newborn metabolic profiles. Therefore, based on 4714 mother–infant pairs in Shanghai, we aimed to investigate the trimester-specific associations of prenatal heat exposure with neonatal amino acid (AA) and acylcarnitine (AC) profiles. Heat exposure was defined using the 90th percentile of trimester-specific temperature distributions from the ERA5-Land data set. For AAs, glutamate showed consistently positive associations across three trimesters, whereas phenylalanine, tyrosine, leucine, arginine, and citrulline showed consistently negative associations; other AAs exhibited trimester-specific patterns. For ACs, C2, C4, and C16 showed consistently negative associations, while a chain-length-dependent pattern was observed: short-chain ACs were predominantly negatively associated, whereas most medium- and long-chain ACs reversed to positive associations in the second and third trimesters. Network topology analysis revealed stronger metabolite correlation structures in the heat-exposed group across all trimesters, with AA-AC pairs accounting for the largest proportion of differential correlations. Distributed lag nonlinear models suggested susceptible windows at gestational weeks 10–17 and 25–27 for AAs, and weeks 8–14 and 26–34 for ACs. Overall, prenatal heat exposure was significantly associated with multiple neonatal AAs and ACs, with distinct trimester-specific patterns and a denser intermetabolite correlation network in the heat-exposed group.

title: Receptor Binding Drives Toxicokinetic Processes: Insights from Two Amphipod Species Exposed to Insecticides Targeting the Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
abstract: Abstract Insecticides targeting nicotinic acetylcholine receptors (nAChRs) are used because of their high neuroactive efficacy. However, they can also exert substantial toxic pressure on nontarget aquatic invertebrates. A previous study suggested that irreversible receptor binding is the main driver of thiacloprid bioaccumulation. To determine whether the observed elimination resistance applies to other nAChR-binding insecticides and species, this study investigates five compounds from different substance classes that target nAChRs. Using the two amphipod species, Hyalella azteca and Gammarus pulex, toxicokinetic experiments were combined with assessing receptor binding in vivo and in vitro. The three N-cyanoamidines and N-nitroguanidine neonicotinoids (thiacloprid, acetamiprid, and imidacloprid) and the metabolite imidacloprid-olefin showed resistance toward elimination (i.e., over 15 days of depuration in both amphipod species). This observation could be well described by a two-compartment toxicokinetic (TK)-receptor model (>0.89 R2) with integrated irreversible binding. In contrast, the butenolide flupyradifurone was fully eliminated, and the organic biocide spinosad was eliminated significantly but slowly, both fitted well with a one-compartment TK model (>0.71 R2). These findings demonstrate that receptor-binding specificity and affinity are highly compound class dependent. Although no direct link between receptor binding and acute toxicity could be established, elimination resistance indicates a risk for delayed, sublethal effects that should be critically considered in regulatory risk assessment.

Multiscale design of cryogenic thermoelectric coolers for infrared detectors
abstract: Cryogenic thermoelectric cooling of infrared (IR) detectors remains challenging because the performance of multistage coolers is governed by strongly coupled electrical, thermal, and geometrical parameters. Here, we present a multiscale design methodology combining the optimal control method (OCM), which determines the optimal stage configuration, operating current, and thermoelectric leg geometry, with finite-element modeling (FEM), which quantifies parasitic heat influx and refines the module design under realistic operating conditions. The methodology was demonstrated through the design of an eight-stage thermoelectric cooler for a 10 mW infrared detector operating at 150 K. The optimized architecture consists of a six-stage Bi 2 Te 3 -based high-temperature section and a two-stage hybrid Bi 0.5 Sb 1.5 Te 3 /Bi 0.91 Sb 0.09 ultra-low-temperature section. Compared with a conventional Bi 2 Te 3 design, the proposed architecture reduces the required number of thermoelectric unicouples by approximately 12 % (869 vs. 977) and decreases the electrical power consumption by approximately 12 % while maintaining the required cooling performance. FEM simulations further showed that parasitic heat influx increases the electrical power consumption of the ultra-low-temperature stage by approximately 34 %, demonstrating that these losses must be considered during module optimization. The proposed multiscale methodology enables the module architecture, geometry, and operating conditions to be determined before prototype fabrication.

title: A system-level multicell cluster model with manifold-induced flow distribution for performance evaluation of PEMFC stacks
abstract: Air maldistribution in proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) stacks degrades both steady-state performance and transient stability. However, existing models either resolve internal flow distribution without system-level integration or capture balance-of-plant (BOP) operation without spatial resolution. In this study, a one-dimensional PEMFC system model is extended with a multicell cluster stack model and a quasi-steady manifold representation capturing branch-flow maldistribution induced by pressure recovery and pressure drop. Component submodels are experimentally validated, while stack predictions are benchmarked against an experimentally validated high-fidelity model. The framework compares U-type and Z-type stack configurations under BOP-integrated transient operation. Under identical air supply conditions, the reinforcing pressure gradients in the Z-type configuration produce a maximum absolute airflow deviation from the mean of 95.02%, compared with 45.80% in the U-type configuration. At 1.5 A/cm 2 , the steady-state voltage distribution becomes nonmonotonic in both configurations: membrane dehydration in high-flow clusters increases ohmic resistance beyond the benefit of excess oxygen supply, while oxygen starvation degrades low-flow clusters. During load transients, compressor delays interact with flow maldistribution to amplify transient voltage drops, with the maximum absolute deviation of the minimum transient voltage from the mean reaching 9.9% in the Z-type configuration but only 2.0% in the U-type configuration. Nonuniform heat generation, combined with coolant maldistribution arising from the same manifold geometry, causes Z-type cluster temperatures to exceed the coolant outlet setpoint by 3.5 K, whereas the U-type remains within 1.5 K. These results highlight the coupled effects of BOP operation and flow maldistribution on PEMFC performance.

title: Species-specific metal handling reveals the decoupling between environmental contamination and biological accumulation in Amazonian mangroves
Fingerprinting microplastics: A high-resolution framework for aquatic sediment contamination and degradation
abstract: This study delivers a high-resolution analysis of microplastic (MP) contamination across eight strategic sites using an integrated multi-step protocol. The optimized analytical protocol was a sequential, multi-stage process designed for maximal recovery and high-resolution characterization of microplastics. The recovered particles then underwent a rigorous, high-resolution granulometric analysis via a cascade of standardized sieves (2 mm to 63 μm), enabling precise particle size distribution profiling combined to density separation using various saline solutions, enabling the capture of particles down to 1 μm after pre-sieving through a 2-mm mesh, followed by size fractionation using a standardized sieve cascade from 630 to 63 μm; the <63 μm fraction was subsequently recovered on 1-μm membrane filters, allowing characterization down to 1 μm. Results revealed a non-uniform distribution of microplastics (MPs), with site OH14 showing the highest observed microplastic abundance among the sampled stations exhibiting the highest particle count (265 particles) and a dominance of larger fragments and microfilaments indicative of a primary discharge point. Morphological analysis showed a widespread dominance of microfilaments, particularly at OH14 and OH7, pointing to chronic contamination from domestic wastewater, while fragments and films at sites like OH1 indicated significant secondary pollution from macroplastic degradation. Chromatic profiling shows that RI16 is characterized by valuable, vibrant colors, whereas the finest fractions (63 μm–1 μm) at OH7 and OH4 consist primarily of colorless particles. This study indicates that MP pollution is a multi-source issue governed by site-specific factors such as hydrodynamics and proximity to urban zones. This study provides a high-resolution map of microplastic (MP) contamination, highlighting a highly heterogeneous and location-specific pollution profile.
