Interface engineering of Pt-based catalysts toward enhanced methanol oxidation in direct methanol fuel cells
abstract: Direct methanol fuel cells (DMFCs) are promising power sources, but their practical performance remains limited by sluggish methanol oxidation, CO poisoning, Pt-site degradation, and low Pt utilization. This review critically examines Pt-centered interface engineering for the methanol oxidation reaction (MOR) in DMFC anodes. First, MOR pathways, performance descriptors, in situ and operando methods, and the factors governing the transfer of half-cell activity to DMFC output are assessed. Representative catalysts are then compared according to the dominant kinetic or degradation limitation addressed by their local interfaces, covering adsorption regulation, pathway control, oxygen-species cooperation, Pt-site retention or regeneration, and cooperative low-Pt utilization. The analysis assigns the dominant function of multifunctional interfaces, evaluates that function using process-specific evidence, and determines whether it survives working-state evolution and membrane electrode assembly integration. Cross-case comparison shows that material class does not uniquely define function and that similar activity, CO tolerance, or durability may arise from different mechanisms. It further distinguishes suppression of adsorbed CO (CO ads) formation from oxidation of pre-adsorbed CO ads , nominal oxophilicity from verified water activation, and structural retention from functional retention and controlled regeneration. Finally, problem-matched design rules are proposed for efficient, low-Pt, and durable DMFC anodes.

title: Reinforcement learning based dual population evolutionary algorithm for multi objective optimal power flow with wind and photovoltaic uncertainties and contingencies
Bridging the grid-thermal-computational nexus via physics-informed hierarchical multi-agent reinforcement learning for data center co-optimization
Label-efficient global centralized and distributed photovoltaic segmentation via hierarchical CLIP-calibrated active learning
abstract: Accurate global photovoltaic (PV) mapping is essential for renewable energy planning, grid integration, and carbon-neutral transition assessment. AI-based remote sensing segmentation offers an efficient way to update PV inventories, but pixel-wise annotation of PV imagery remains expensive at large scale, especially across distributed rooftop systems and centralized utility-scale plants with different resolutions and geographic backgrounds. A key practical challenge is therefore to achieve high-accuracy PV segmentation with the smallest possible annotation budget under realistic labeling constraints. To address this challenge, we propose a hierarchical CLIP-calibrated active learning (AL) strategy for label-efficient global PV segmentation. Due to the heterogeneous appearance of PV scenes, CLIP is introduced as an external visual-semantic calibrator, and sample acquisition is organized into three stages: semantic coverage in the CLIP feature space, hybrid-uncertainty hard-example mining, and feature-level redundancy removal. Using SegFormer-B3 as the segmentation baseline, we evaluate the method on two worldwide benchmarks covering distributed rooftop PV at 0.1–1.0 m resolution and centralized utility-scale PV at 10–20 m resolution. Under the same annotation budget, our method consistently outperforms classic AL baselines, including Entropy, BALD, and Core-set, across both benchmarks. Practical deployment analysis shows that, for an IoU ≥ 90 % target, our method reduces the required annotation budget by 39.1–78.8% for distributed PV and 15.1–34.8% for centralized PV, corresponding to estimated manual-labeling savings of approximately 260 h/$5.2k and 114 h/$2.28k relative to Random sampling, respectively. These results support scalable, low-cost PV inventory updates for deployment monitoring, grid planning, and renewable energy planning under constrained labeling resources.

title: A systematic review of cross-sectoral life cycle assessments of carbon capture, utilization, and storage systems
Is more aggregated better? Balancing power generation, employment accessibility, and climate mitigation in photovoltaic deployment
abstract: The rapid expansion of photovoltaic (PV) deployment, together with its growing concentration in large renewable-energy bases, has intensified the need to reassess PV land-use value. However, whether greater spatial aggregation consistently improves power, employment, and climate outcomes remains unclear. Here, we integrated multi-source geospatial data from 30,023 PV plants across China to build a site-to-region framework. This framework links PV aggregation to power-generation potential, population-based local accessibility, and net climate-mitigation benefit, and summarizes their joint performance as total composite benefit (TCB). We found a climate-specific non-linear pattern: TCB peaked at high aggregation in humid and sub-humid regions (76.7% and 62.1%, respectively), but declined monotonically with further aggregation in arid regions. Across regions, aggregation delivered larger gains in power-generation potential than in local accessibility or climate mitigation, and this imbalance became stronger as aggregation increased. Current deployment often falls outside the empirically identified high-benefit aggregation ranges, including 64.0% of PV capacity (42.9 GW) in arid high-demand areas and 87.1% (89.17 GW) in sub-humid flat terrains. These findings show that more concentrated PV deployment is not necessarily associated with greater land-use value. Our framework provides empirical benchmarks for evaluating PV aggregation and informing more balanced PV deployment across power-generation potential, local employment accessibility, and climate outcomes.

title: Constructing reliable clean energy facility network under ambiguous distribution information
abstract: In the context of the transition from clean energy to sustainable development, as an emerging low-carbon energy carrier, hydrogen is of crucial importance. The planning of a hydrogenation facility network (HFN) with a reliable hydrogen supply has thus become an important research topic in the field of hydrogen energy provision. This study investigates the planning of the HFN from the perspectives of economic cost and network reliability, under conditions of uncertain hydrogen supply capacity. To address the challenges posed by uncertainty, the renewable energy-powered hydrogen production process is categorized into multiple scenarios. We formulate an ambiguity set using the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and establish ambiguous chance constraints, thereby proposing a novel bi-objective distributionally robust HFN optimization model (DR-HFN). Based on the decision-maker’s preferences in practice, an economic-oriented optimization model and a reliability-oriented optimization model are developed, respectively. Subsequently, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) representation is derived from the proposed model to ensure computational tractability. A customized branch-and-cut (BC) algorithm is further designed to enhance the model’s solvability and scalability. Finally, a practical case study conducted in Guangdong Province, China demonstrates that our proposed method can withstand uncertainties in hydrogen supply capacity with a probability of 90%. Moreover, the comparison with the sample average approximation (SAA) method shows that our method only generates a robustness cost of about 0.087% when addressing distributional uncertainty. This further demonstrates that our method is capable of generating high-quality decision solutions while also exhibiting strong robustness and applicability.

title: Electricity-hydrogen integrated energy system: a review of architecture, performance, strategies and challenges from the physical-informational-social perspective
Towards sustainable catalyst production: A prospective life cycle assessment of resource-efficient Ni-CeO2 scale-up across current and future electricity mixes
abstract: Scaling up catalytic synthesis from laboratory to industrial scale strongly influences its environmental profile, presenting new opportunities to integrate circular practices into catalyst manufacturing. In this study, a prospective Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is carried out to measure the environmental implications associated with the synthesis of Ni-CeO 2 nanoparticles under three electricity scenarios: the current Global mix, a Business-as-Usual (BAU) pathway according to the IEA Stated Policies Scenario (STEPS), and a fully decarbonized mix aligned with the IEA Net Zero proposal. Solvents and electricity demands are identified as the dominant contributors. The environmental benefits of circular solvent management, resource-efficient process optimization, and electricity decarbonization are systematically evaluated. It is shown that scaling up with process optimization, by integrating higher synthesis yields (up to 90%), solvent recovery (67–75%), and a literature-informed industrial-scale electricity demand, leads to reductions in environmental impacts of 70–90% across most categories. Replacement of fossil-derived methanol with bioethanol and biomethanol is assessed as a strategy for improving solvent sustainability, with biomethanol emerging as the more promising solution for solvent substitution, while bio-ethanol surprisingly leads to deteriorated environmental performance, for the specific production pathways and datasets evaluated. Further comparison is applied across regional electricity mixes (European, German, and French), highlighting the influence of electricity-mix carbon intensity on the resulting impacts. The proposed framework demonstrates how prospective LCA can support the transition towards more sustainable and circular catalyst manufacturing during industrial scale-up.

title: Applications, progress and technical challenges of machine learning in full lifetime of proton exchange membrane fuel cells
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells (PEMFCs), as core devices for hydrogen energy utilization, play an increasingly strategic role in transportation electrification, distributed power generation, and large-scale energy storage. However, the inherent strong multi-physics coupling, complex nonlinear degradation, and high sensitivity to operating conditions of PEMFC impose significant challenges on its cost, durability, and efficiency. Machine learning (ML) provides new opportunities to address these challenges and accelerate intelligent PEMFC development. This review examines ML applications across the full lifetime of PEMFCs, covering material design, manufacturing and quality control, system state management and control, and digital twin (DT) development. Beyond summarizing recent progress, it critically compares ML approaches in terms of data requirements, interpretability, computational cost, robustness, generalization, and uncertainty quantification, while highlighting emerging physics-informed ML, hybrid physics-data-driven models, self-adaptive DTs, and deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Three major challenges are identified: (1) data scarcity, heterogeneity, and insufficient standardization; (2) limited physical consistency, interpretability, generalization, and uncertainty quantification; and (3) computational, real-time, and safe-deployment requirements. Overall, integrating data, physical knowledge, and intelligent decision-making can advance ML-enabled PEMFCs from isolated prediction and optimization toward reliable, adaptive, and full-lifetime intelligent operation.

Somewhere between the highway to hell and the stairway to heaven: Future scenarios for circular production and consumption in Brazil
Resource-Oriented Wastewater Treatment through Quorum Quenching─Integration of AnMBR and Donnan Dialysis
abstract: Abstract Aligned with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 6, water treatment is shifting from pollution removal to resource recovery and circularity. An integration of AnMBR and a Donnan dialysis (DD) (AnMBR-DD) was proposed to simultaneously recover methane and ammonium, and quorum quenching (QQ) was further incorporated to mitigate membrane fouling and enhance process efficiency. The COD removal efficiency was stably maintained above 80%, and the methane conversion efficiency reached 51.6%. The effluent NH4+-N concentration was controlled at 3–5 mg/L, with a recovery efficiency of 47.1% in the AnMBR-DD. The QQ effectively alleviated biofouling on the ultrafiltration membrane in the AnMBR and ion exchange membrane in the DD, while improving methane production and ammonia recovery by 20.6% and 6.6%, respectively. These improvements were mainly attributed to QQ-induced reductions in extracellular polymeric substances (EPS), which weakened microbial adhesion and decreased biofilm compactness. Life cycle assessment showed that coupled methane and ammonium recovery in AnMBR-DD-QQ were the decided advantages in alleviating the environmental impact. These results highlight the great potential of AnMBR-DD-QQ as a resource-oriented wastewater treatment strategy.

title: Landscape Fire-Sourced PM2.5 and Cause-Specific Renal Hospitalizations: A Multicountry Two-Stage Time-Series Analysis of 12.5 Million Admissions
abstract: Abstract Landscape fire-sourced PM2.5 (LFS PM2.5) is increasingly recognized as an important air pollutant, but its short-term contribution to renal hospitalizations remains unclear. Here, we assessed the associations between LFS PM2.5 and renal hospitalizations across 1020 locations in Australia, Brazil, Canada, Chile, New Zealand, and Thailand during 2000–2019 using a two-stage time-series design and estimated the attributable hospitalizations. LFS PM2.5 was associated with increased renal hospitalization risk, with the strongest associations observed for acute kidney injury. A 10 μg/m3 increase in cumulative LFS PM2.5 exposure over lag 0–5 was associated with a 1.1% increase in renal hospitalizations (RR = 1.011, 95% CI: 1.007–1.015). Associations were stronger in warmer areas and differed across levels of GDP per capita. Associations were consistently stronger for LFS PM2.5 than for non-LFS PM2.5. We estimated that LFS PM2.5 contributed to 1.38 renal hospitalizations per 100,000 population annually across the study regions. These findings highlight renal disease as an underrecognized health consequence of landscape fire smoke and support strengthened strategies to reduce wildfire smoke exposure under a changing climate.

title: Enantiomer-Dependent Modulation of Lithium Uptake and Accumulation in Plants by Foliar Application of Chiral SeNPs
abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of lithium-based new energy technologies has led to substantial lithium inputs into soil, potentially threatening human health through the consumption of lithium-accumulated agricultural products. Therefore, efficient strategies are urgently needed to mitigate the uptake and accumulation of lithium in plant fruits. Nanotechnology offers promising avenues for enhancing stress resilience and improving the quality of crops grown in contaminated soils. Here, we found that lithium was distributed unevenly among tissues (leaves: 1365, roots: 508, stems: 112, and fruits: 24 mg kg–1) of eggplants grown in lithium-contaminated soil. Notably, foliar spraying of selenium nanoparticles with levorotatory chirality (l-SeNPs) effectively reduced fruit lithium content and promoted its accumulation in the leaves, roots, and stems, in which vacuolar compartmentalization was the primary pathway for tolerance to high lithium content, whereas the dextrorotatory enantiomer showed no such effects. Mechanism investigation elucidated that l-SeNPs can reinforce antioxidant defense systems of eggplant under lithium stress through a microbiome–metabolome–transcriptome bridging cascade, in which l-SeNPs substantially affected rhizosphere bacterial and metabolic networks along with minor changes in the bioavailability of lithium in rhizosphere soil. This study sheds light on the superiority of nanoscale chirality in modulating lithium uptake and accumulation in plants grown in metal-contaminated soil, providing strategies for agromining of lithium.

title: Heterogeneous Component Degradation Controls Molecular Evolution and Reactivity of Volatile Organic Compounds during Distiller’s Grains Pyrolysis
abstract: Abstract Biomass pyrolysis is a crucial method of resource utilization, but resulting volatiles may pose environmental concerns due to their impacts on air quality and secondary pollution. However, the mechanisms governing thermal degradation and volatile evolution remain unclear. Herein, we integrate online thermogravimetry–Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy–gas chromatography/mass spectrometry, Gaussian deconvolution, and two-dimensional correlation spectroscopy to elucidate the degradation characteristics and sequential temperature-dependent volatile evolution of distiller’s grains (DG), a protein-rich agro-industrial residue. DG pyrolysis exhibited distinct multistage degradation characteristics governed by coupled decomposition and synergistic interactions of lignocellulosic and protein-derived components. The major volatiles included alcohols/ethers, phenols/esters, hydrocarbons, and aromatics, with pronounced temperature-dependent variations. Volatile and intermediate-volatility organic compounds accounted for 47–60% and 35–52% of total detected organic volatile emissions released during pyrolysis, respectively. Most DG-derived volatiles exhibited reducing characteristics, with average carbon oxidation states below zero, while broad saturation mass concentration distributions reflected substantial chemical heterogeneity. The temperature-dependent evolution sequence of DG-derived volatiles followed alcohols/phenols → aromatics/hydrocarbons → aldehydes/ketones/acids → esters → CO2/CH4/NH3. A DG mechanistic framework was proposed, demonstrating that heterogeneous component degradation regulated dynamic volatile generation and variation. These findings provide mechanistic insight into DG pyrolysis and contribute to sustainable biomass valorization and environmental impact assessment.

title: Unlocking the Exceptional Activity of CuS in Fenton-Like Reactions via a Novel Hydroxide–Sulfur Interaction
abstract: Abstract Promoters have been explored to improve Fenton-like reactions for wastewater treatment, yet they are often costly and may cause secondary pollution. This study demonstrates that alkali (OH–), as an inexpensive and environmentally friendly chemical, acts as an efficient promoter for copper sulfide (CuS) by inducing polarization of the disulfide bonds in CuS. OH– substantially enhanced the generation of hydroxyl and sulfate radicals in the CuS/peroxymonosulfate (PMS) system, achieving a >100-fold increase in the apparent degradation rate of sulfamethoxazole (SMX). With OH– assistance, a CuS-packed continuous-flow reactor demonstrated long-term stability (≥800 h), sustaining >95% SMX removal, <1% residual PMS, <0.03 mg/L Cu2+ leaching. Final effluent pH remained stable at 6–9, meeting all applicable discharge standards. Furthermore, the OH–/CuS/PMS system significantly reduced the toxicity of actual wastewater. Density functional theory calculations revealed that the interaction between OH– and disulfide bonds in CuS enhanced the electron spin density and improved the 3d orbital energy level of CuS, promoting electron transfer from CuS to PMS. This work presents a cost-effective Fenton-like system that achieves robust pollutant degradation while ensuring exceptionally low metal dissolution and a consistently discharge-compliant effluent pH (6–9), collectively underscoring its viability for sustainable wastewater remediation.

title: A Multidimensional Framework for Integrated Toxicity Assessment and Prioritization of Naphthenic Acids in Marine Medaka ( Oryzias melastigma ): Neurotoxicity and Mechanistic Insights
abstract: Abstract Petroleum pollution poses a major challenge to global environmental health. Petroleum-derived naphthenic acids (NAs) are frequently detected in marine environments, yet their multidimensional toxicity and mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we developed an integrated toxicity framework combining bioassays, toxicity screening, computational simulations, transcriptomics, and bioinformatics to characterize NAs toxicity in marine medaka (Oryzias melastigma). A concentration gradient spanning environmentally detected levels to higher-effect concentrations (0.015–30 mg/L) revealed developmental defects, cardiac suppression, behavioral disruption, and metabolic dysfunction. CRITIC–AHP-based prioritization identified neurotoxicity as the predominant toxicity dimension, with cyclopentylpropionic acid (CPPA) and cyclohexylpropionic acid (CHPA) identified as major contributors. Mechanistically, these compounds were associated with distinct candidate pathways involving CXCR3-CXCL10 neuroinflammatory responses and DPP10-Kv4.2 ion homeostasis disruption. Their divergent toxicity profiles may be associated with differences in hydrophobicity and molecular flexibility. Rescue experiments supported these pathways, restoring swimming velocity by 60.32% and 62.09%, respectively. Furthermore, NAs induced neurobehavioral alterations and transcriptional signatures overlapping with Alzheimer’s disease-associated genes, with 14 and 12 candidate genes identified for CPPA and CHPA. Collectively, this study provides a cross-scale perspective linking physicochemical properties, toxicity pathways, and adverse outcomes of NAs, offering a conceptual approach for toxicity screening and mechanism elucidation of contaminants.

title: Dual Oxidation in the Amino Acid-Mediated Copper-Catalyzed Fenton-like System: Effects of Ligand Structure and pH-Dependent Speciation
abstract: Abstract The Cu(II)/H2O2 system has attracted increasing interest as a Cu-catalyzed advanced oxidation process and serves as a useful biomimetic model for investigating Cu-mediated biomolecule redox interactions. In this system, reactive oxidants can operate in a dual-oxidation mode, where the oxidant flux partitions between coordinated ligands and coexisting bulk-phase substrates. In this study, we systematically investigated this behavior over a wide pH range (3–12), using 17 structurally diverse amino acids (AAs) as model ligands and benzoic acid (BA), which exhibits negligible Cu(II) complexation, as a model bulk-phase substrate. Speciation-based kinetic analysis identified the bis-chelated complex, [Cu(AA)2], as a key catalytic species associated with effective dual oxidation, namely, balanced oxidant allocation between ligand-centered AA oxidation and bulk-phase BA oxidation, at pH 7–10. Using quantitative structure–activity/efficiency relationships, we demonstrate that the partitioning of oxidant flux is governed by two ligand-associated properties: (i) Cu(II)-binding strength, which promotes ligand-centered oxidation, and (ii) oxidative stability (proxied by the highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO)–lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) gap), which favors the oxidant flux to the bulk phase. At higher pH, the possible formation of mixed hydroxo species, [Cu(AA)2(OH)]−, was associated with a shift toward ligand-centered oxidation and attenuated bulk-phase BA oxidation. Integrated machine-learning models combining ligand descriptors with pH-dependent speciation indicators further supported these trends and predicted AA and BA oxidation kinetics across pH 7–11. These results provide a predictive framework for understanding how ligand structure and pH-dependent speciation jointly control oxidant allocation in the Cu(II)/H2O2 system.

Depth-Independent Soil Organic Carbon Persistence across Climate Gradients in Coastal Wetlands
abstract: Abstract Coastal wetland soils constitute a major global blue carbon pool. Yet, how soil organic carbon (SOC) persistence varies with soil depth and responds to climate change remains poorly understood. Here, we assessed depth-related patterns and climatic controls on SOC persistence using radiocarbon (Δ14C) measurements from 82 samples across 41 sites spanning temperate to tropical coastal wetlands. Radiocarbon-inferred SOC persistence did not differ significantly between topsoil (0–10 cm) and subsoil (40–60 cm) across climate zones and wetland types, with mean Δ14C values of −179.0 ± 155.5‰ and −200.9 ± 161.8‰, respectively (p > 0.05). Interactions among climate, vegetation, and soil biogeochemistry explained about 55% of the variation in SOC persistence in both topsoil and subsoil. Both layers exhibited comparable sensitivity to mean annual temperature and precipitation. However, the inferred regulatory pathways differed between soil layers, with stronger direct climatic effects in topsoil and greater indirect mediation through soil physicochemical and mineral-associated processes in subsoil. Across spatial climatic gradients, higher mean annual temperature and precipitation were associated with greater SOC accumulation but lower persistence, suggesting a potential trade-off between SOC quantity and persistence. These findings demonstrate limited vertical differentiation in SOC persistence between the 0–10 cm and 40–60 cm layers and highlight the need to better represent depth-specific regulatory processes in carbon-climate feedback frameworks.

title: Psychoactive Pollutant Impacts Baseline Immune Traits but Not Behavior and Microbiome in a Fish
abstract: Abstract Pharmaceutical pollution is an increasing global threat to freshwater ecosystems. Psychoactive drugs, such as antidepressants, are of particular concern because they affect evolutionarily conserved neuroendocrine pathways in nontarget organisms. As these pathways regulate interconnected biological systems, understanding the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical exposure requires an integrative approach. Here, we investigated the effects of 28-day exposure to control (freshwater), low (4.2 ± 0.3 ng/L), and high (637.5 ± 173.84 ng/L) fluoxetine concentrations on behaviors, baseline immune traits, and skin mucus microbiome composition in the Murray River rainbowfish (Melanotaenia fluviatilis). Fluoxetine exposure did not impact fish behavior, including activity, freezing behavior, shelter use, or microbiome composition. In contrast, immune traits were significantly altered. Both fluoxetine concentrations reduced total white blood cell (WBC) count, while only fish exposed to the low concentration showed reduced lymphocyte counts and elevated neutrophil counts, consistent with a stress-associated WBC redistribution response. Our findings show that different, but interconnected, biological systems can differ in their sensitivity to pollutants and suggest that immune traits may be an early, sensitive indicator of exposure to psychoactive pharmaceuticals. These findings highlight the importance of integrating multiple biological end points to obtain a more comprehensive understanding of the ecological consequences of pharmaceutical contamination.

title: Warming Patterns Shape Divergent Multilevel Physiological Responses and Underlying Metabolic Mechanisms in Aquatic Organisms
abstract: Abstract Although the impacts of global warming on aquatic ecosystems are widely recognized, the biological consequences of distinct warming patterns remain largely unknown. We investigated physiological and metabolic responses of Daphnia magna, Chironomus kiiensis, and zebrafish under constant warming (+1, +3 °C), heatwave, and temperature fluctuation. Dynamic patterns exhibited stronger physiological responses, with mean absolute effect sizes across survival, growth, development, behavior, and stress functional categories following the order heatwave > fluctuation > +3 °C > +1 °C. Response profiles varied among warming patterns: constant +3 °C induced moderate and broad changes across biochemical stress, developmental, and behavioral end points; heatwave accelerated zebrafish hatching and C. kiiensis pupation while increasing deformity, suppressing growth, and elevating mortality; and fluctuation induced pronounced biochemical stress responses, particularly HSP70, together with developmental disruption, while producing weaker survival and growth effects than heatwave. Across taxa, dominant response profiles differed, with broad multiend point disruption in D. magna, stress-dominant responses in C. kiiensis, and developmental sensitivity in zebrafish. Metabolomic analysis further identified warming-pattern-specific metabolic signatures associated with energy metabolism under +3 °C, membrane-related processes under heatwave, and redox-related processes under fluctuation. Together, these findings provide a scientific basis for improving aquatic ecological risk assessment under increasingly variable warming scenarios.

A novel cathode flow field for PEM fuel cells with alternating depth channels: Under-rib cross flow design and performance assessment
abstract: Enhancing under-rib mass transport while reducing pressure-drop penalties remains a key challenge in proton exchange membrane fuel cell (PEMFC) cathode flow-field design. This study proposes an alternating-depth flow field (ADFF), in which neighboring straight channels are periodically arranged with different depths to generate a lateral pressure difference. A three-dimensional steady-state multiphysics model, validated against experimental data obtained with a multi-channel serpentine flow field (MSFF), is employed to compare the ADFF with the MSFF and a straight parallel flow field (SPFF). The numerical results indicate that the ADFF improves oxygen delivery, reduces cathode concentration loss, limits regions of locally high H 2 O concentration, and produces a more uniform current–density distribution. Compared with the MSFF, the ADFF reduces the maximum cathode pressure drop by 85.6 %, while achieving a 3.4 % higher peak power density than the SPFF. Parametric analysis shows that a channel-depth ratio of 1.5 provides the best performance among the investigated cases, while a cathode stoichiometric ratio of 2.5 provides a favorable balance between electrochemical performance and pressure-drop penalty.

Divergent Responses of Fungal Communities to Vegetation Structural Complexity in Degraded Roadside Slopes Across Climatic Gradients
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how climate and vegetation structural complexity jointly shape fungal communities is essential for effective roadside slope restoration. To address this, we examined restoration effects on fungal diversity, community composition, and ecological networks across three climatically distinct regions: dry‐hot valley, subalpine, and subtropical. In climatically stressful regions (i.e., dry‐hot valley and subalpine), plots with complex vegetation (Herb+Shrub, Herb+Shrub+Tree, and natural sites) harbored higher fungal diversity than herbaceous‐only plots. In contrast, subtropical herbaceous plots supported higher fungal diversity, likely due to disturbance‐induced niche heterogeneity. Fungal community composition differed significantly among climatic regions and vegetation types. Ascomycota was consistently dominant across all sites, whereas Mortierellomycota, Basidiomycota, and Rozellomycota exhibited distinct regional distributions. Network analyses revealed larger and more highly connected fungal networks in the subtropical and subalpine regions than in the dry‐hot valley, with topological keystone taxa identified only in the former two regions. Piecewise structural equation modeling further indicated that climate influenced fungal diversity indirectly via soil nutrients, while vegetation diversity exerted a direct effect. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that the effects of vegetation complexity on fungal communities are climate‐dependent, underscoring the need to integrate climatic context, vegetation management, soil nutrient regulation, and fungal ecological functions into roadside slope restoration.

title: Racial Disparities in Severe Maternal Morbidity: The Role of Maternal Comorbidities
abstract: ABSTRACT The U.S. maternal health crisis disproportionately affects Black women, who face nearly twice the risk of severe maternal morbidity (SMM) compared with White women. Using 2016–2022 Texas hospital discharge data and a validated obstetric comorbidity score, the analysis first documents that the prevalence of SMM increased by 18% between 2016 and 2022, whereas maternal comorbidity burden increased by 42% over the same period. To better assess the role of comorbidities, the comorbidity score is disaggregated into underlying health and pregnancy‐specific conditions. Oaxaca–Blinder decompositions indicate that the former accounts for the largest share—49 to 53%—of the Black–White SMM gap, while the latter accounts for an additional third of the disparity. After accounting for these factors, a residual Black–White SMM gap of 17%–20% persists across and within hospitals, including among women treated by the same physician. Overall, the findings underscore the critical need to improve women's health well before childbirth hospitalization and throughout the reproductive life course, while also strengthening prenatal care to prevent and effectively manage conditions that arise during pregnancy.

title: Taking a Note from Music: Conceptual Sampling and the Creative Logic of Theory Development
When machines learn with organizations: AI ‐enabled knowledge creation and entrepreneurship
abstract: Abstract Research Summary To promote entrepreneurship and new business development, firms will increasingly rely on new forms of knowledge creation to manage environments marked by technological change and radical uncertainty. We argue that as generative artificial intelligence (Gen‐AI) becomes embedded in organizational processes, knowledge creation will no longer remain solely a human activity. Instead, it will increasingly emerge from hybrid interactions between human actors and firm‐specific, closed Gen‐AI systems. These systems begin to participate directly in how knowledge is generated, recombined, internalized, shared, and converted into entrepreneurial initiatives such as corporate entrepreneurship, spin‐offs, and new business models. We also reconceptualize organizational knowledge creation as a hybrid human–AI process and propose a reordered knowledge creation cycle that induces multiple knowledge spirals, captures the emergence of new agents, and the generation of diverse types of knowledge, with faster temporal dynamics. Building on this perspective, we offer a research agenda for future scholarship. Managerial Summary We discuss how firm‐specific generative AI systems are likely to fundamentally alter the ways firms generate knowledge, respond to change, and sustain long‐term renewal. We propose that rather than replacing human judgment, closed Gen‐AI changes where knowledge originates as well as how quickly it evolves, and how broadly it circulates across organizational boundaries. This means that the managerial challenge is less about adopting AI and more about designing knowledge systems and structuring knowledge flows. Executives and entrepreneurs alike need to decide how to structure human–AI collaborations, how much autonomy to grant closed Gen‐AI systems, and how to prevent speed from overwhelming sensemaking. Our work underscores that although hybrid knowledge creation promises faster and more diverse learning, it also introduces risks related to opacity, trust, and cognitive lock‐in. Firms that deliberately orchestrate the role of closed Gen‐AI in their learning systems will be better positioned to shape future advantage by promoting innovation and entrepreneurial activities of different types.

title: The Paternity Leave Ripple Effect in the Finance Industry: Shaping Norms and Social Cohesion
abstract: ABSTRACT Paternity leave shifts work‐life policy from accommodating women's caregiving to legitimizing men's involvement in care. We examine how this is experienced in male‐dominated workplaces and interpreted by those around leave‐takers through interviews with fathers who took extended paternity leave in French finance organizations, and other stakeholders at work (colleagues, HR representatives, top managers) and at home (life partners). Following an interpretivist, context‐dependent approach, we find that participants associated paternity leave with changes in social relations, connectedness, and concern for collective well‐being. We theorize that, under certain conditions, these changes may coalesce into relational and collective experiences aligned with social cohesion beyond the workplace. We further theorize two pathways. In a transformative cycle, paternity leave may disrupt descriptive and injunctive gender norms, and experiences aligned with social cohesion occur. In a maintenance cycle, established norms persist, and such experiences largely do not arise. These divergent pathways depend on the favorability of nested contextual conditions: meso‐ (policy design, top management engagement, organizational climate) and micro‐ (manager, peer support), within the macro‐context of a male‐dominated industry. The study extends work‐life policy research beyond individual and organizational outcomes and identifies conditions under which paternity leave may challenge gendered divisions of labor within and beyond organizations.

title: Leaving on a High or Low Note? An Achievement Goal Perspective on Executive Retirement
abstract: ABSTRACT Executive retirement represents a pivotal career transition with significant implications. However, our understanding of the antecedents of executive retirement remains limited. We contend that, different from the retirement of general employees, it is important to position executive retirement within an achievement context and consider factors such as firm performance and achievement goal orientations. Drawing on late adulthood developmental psychology, we propose an achievement goal framework to theorize the relationship between firm performance and executive retirement, and the moderating roles of goal orientations. We theorize that firm performance is associated with two distinct mechanisms: the legacy fulfillment mechanism (salient for executives with high performance) and the selective prioritization mechanism (salient for executives with low performance), which together result in a U‐shaped relationship between firm performance and the likelihood of executive retirement. We further consider executives’ goal orientations as boundary conditions to probe the underlying mechanisms. We found general support for our theory using an archival dataset of 1840 chief executive officers from S&P 1500 firms (Study 1) and a two‐wave survey of 363 executives (Study 2). By integrating developmental psychology theories into the executive retirement literature, our research sheds light on executive retirement decisions through a developmental psychology lens.

title: Exploring heterogeneous treatment effects for GLP-1 receptor agonists in patients with type 2 diabetes
abstract: Abstract Understanding treatment effect heterogeneity (TEH) is essential to improve care for patients living with chronic diseases like type 2 diabetes. Individual responses to treatment can vary substantially, and identifying the factors that drive TEH may enable increased personalization of treatment and follow-up. In this study, we conduct an exploratory analysis of TEH for glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists used to treat type 2 diabetes. Endpoints are defined using hemoglobin A1c measurements, body mass index, and blood pressure. We use causal forests to conduct global tests for TEH, estimate variable importances to rank candidate effect modifiers, and estimate the magnitude of heterogeneity. Data from three clinical trials are analyzed: SUSTAIN 6 (subcutaneous semaglutide versus placebo, n=3297), PIONEER 6 (oral semaglutide versus placebo, n=3183), and LEADER (subcutaneous liraglutide versus placebo, n=9340), pooled to 13,670 patients after exclusions. Baseline hemoglobin A1c ranks highest among candidate effect modifiers across methods, and kidney function ranks next in the relative risk causal forest; we discuss their clinical implications. The magnitude estimates, however, show that the variation these covariates jointly explain is small. As such, large covariate-driven heterogeneity can be ruled out in these trials, and the average treatment effect provides a reasonable summary for most patients.

title: Myeloma ascertainment and the timing of selenium safety signals
Maternal Education in Context: Reassessing the Infant Health Paradox among Latin American Immigrants
abstract: Abstract One aspect of the Hispanic Health Paradox is the longstanding observation that Latin American immigrants in the United States often experience equal or better health outcomes than U.S.-born counterparts despite greater socioeconomic disadvantage. This advantage extends to their infants and is most pronounced among mothers with the least education. Whether such patterns reflect selective migration remains unclear. This study evaluates the role of educational selectivity in explaining nativity disparities in infant health. Using U.S. natality data among immigrants from Mexico, Cuba, El Salvador, Guatemala, the Dominican Republic, Colombia, Honduras, and Venezuela (2012–2023), linked with internationally harmonized educational data, we assess preterm birth disparities using two measures of maternal education: absolute and relative attainment. Immigrants at the bottom of the U.S. education distribution often rank much higher in their origin countries, consistent with positive selection. For most births to Latin American mothers (except Colombian and Venezuelan), measuring education relative to origin-country distributions reverses immigrant advantages. At equivalent relative education ranks, immigrant mothers face comparable or higher risks of preterm birth than U.S.-born Hispanic mothers. These findings offer a new perspective on the Hispanic Health Paradox, highlighting the importance of relative education in understanding the association between maternal education and infant health.

The Fate of Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) in Municipal Solid Waste Incineration: Atmospheric Emissions from a Waste-to-Energy Plant
abstract: Abstract The atmospheric fate of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) represents a very recent field of research. While ISO and CEN standards are yet under development, PFAS have been identified during the past years in atmospheric emissions, ambient air, and deposition. As high-quality field data are currently scarce, the objectives of this study were to (i) characterize atmospheric PFAS emissions of a state-of-the-art waste-to-energy (WtE) plant under representative operational conditions and (ii) evaluate the emission impact in ambient air in the vicinity of the plant. Results suggest a contribution from the WtE plant at the nearest ambient monitoring location, 450 m downwind of the plant, with a measurable contribution and distinct PFAS fingerprint closely matching the emission profiles independently characterized at two grate incinerator lines. Quantified PFAS emissions do not exceed the temporary assessment framework for ambient air in Flanders. Furthermore, optimization of the activated carbon (AC) dosage achieved a 95% reduction in emissions at line 1, with subsequent emission levels approaching those of field blanks. The waste treatment sector represents a critical frontier of environmental management. Building experimental evidence of potential PFAS releases will be key to ensure comprehensive strategies for responsible PFAS management in the years ahead.

title: Toward a Universal Switch for Microbial Granulation: Photogranule Insights to Advance Granular Wastewater Treatment
abstract: Abstract Microbial granulation─the assembly of self-immobilized, spheroidal aggregates─is a transformative approach for high-density, energy-efficient wastewater treatment. By concentrating biomass and enhancing resilience to influent fluctuations, granular systems significantly reduce infrastructure footprints. Current granular technologies primarily leverage upflow continuous reactors or sequencing-batch reactors, where specific external selection pressures are imposed to drive granulation. However, granulation remains neither spontaneous nor reliably predictable, and its fundamental biological drivers are poorly understood. Recent advances in photogranules challenge selection-pressure models. Photogranules form from activated-sludge inocula in hydrostatic and hydrodynamic batches and even in CSTRs where classical selection conditions are weak or absent. Moreover, the recurring emergence of compact spheroidal granules across diverse natural and laboratory systems suggests shared, intrinsic biological drivers rather than purely engineered causes. In this Perspective, we propose that the bacterial second messenger c-di-GMP functions as a conserved, Goldilocks-like molecular switch that integrates diverse environmental cues into a coordinated granulation program. We synthesize transcriptomic, biochemical, and genetic evidence and advance three hypotheses linking c-di-GMP signaling and community physiology to granulation. If validated, targeted modulation of c-di-GMP─by genetic or chemical means─could enable predictable, resilient granulation across a wider range of systems, including the continuous horizontal-flow basins that dominate wastewater infrastructure.

title: Molecular Evolution of Dissolved Organic Nitrogen from Photoaged Nitrogen-Containing Microplastics Reveals Amine Structures as Key Nitrosamine Precursors
abstract: Abstract Although dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) is continuously released and transformed as nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) age, the evolution of this replenished pool and its reactivity during downstream chloramination remains unresolved. Here, we tracked the compositional evolution of DON molecules in polyamide (PA) and polyacrylonitrile (PAN) suspensions under UV irradiation using a nitrogen atom-based molecular classification strategy (N1–N5). After 7 d of irradiation-induced molecular reorganization, N1–N5 molecules accounted for 87% and 79% of the molecular signal intensity in PA-DOM and PAN-DOM, respectively. Eight annotated compounds followed increasing, decreasing, or transient accumulation trajectories, revealing simultaneous molecular accumulation and depletion. Reaction-network analysis further showed that N1–N5 molecules progressively became the dominant reactants, and these trajectories were dominated by oxidation and accompanied by increasingly frequent amine-related transformation links. Structural analysis revealed amide-rich N1–N2 and N-heterocycle-rich N3–N5 molecules, while secondary and tertiary amines occurred across all N1–N5 classes. As this molecular reorganization progressed, N-MP-DON level dropped, but substantially enhanced N-nitrosodimethylamine and N-nitrosodiethylamine formation, and potential precursor identification was strongly associated with amine structures, rather than nitrogen atom number. Overall, our study highlights N-MP-DON as a potential source of nitrosamine precursors, and the need to carefully consider amine-containing additives use in plastic manufacturing.

Spatio-temporal variation and determinants of urban air quality in Chinese cities during 2014-2023: an interpretable machine learning analysis
abstract: China launched its clean-air action plans in 2013, which have played a crucial role in driving one of the world's most significant and rapid improvements in urban air quality. However, the relative roles of financial, governance, and structural determinants remain poorly understood. This study developed a national-scale, interpretable machine-learning framework to model and explain air quality dynamics across 273 prefecture-level cities from 2014 to 2023. We used city-level AQI as the target variable and assembled a multidimensional panel of socioeconomic, financial, technological, energy, and governance indicators. We fitted a TPE-tuned XGBoost model and interpreted it using SHAP (global and local attributions) and ALE (non-linear response curves and two-way interactions). Nationally, more than 85% of cities exhibit substantial AQI declines, but improvements are uneven across regions and provinces. SHAP results identify green finance, population density, government intervention, openness, and digital finance as the most influential determinants, with energy consumption, green technology innovation, foreign direct investment, industrial structure, and urbanization also playing important roles. ALE analysis reveals strong nonlinearities: green and digital finance, as well as government intervention, are pollution-increasing at low and intermediate levels but become markedly pollution-reducing beyond critical thresholds, while density and energy use rapidly become strong positive drivers once modest levels are exceeded. Interactions show that green and digital finance yield significant air-quality benefits only when combined with strong governance and less energy-intensive and industry-intensive structures. City-level decompositions further distinguish improving from deteriorating cities in terms of the evolution of these drivers. The findings highlight that sustained governance, well-targeted green and digital finance, and accelerated structural change are mutually necessary to secure durable gains in urban air quality.

title: Reed-straw configuration density in Suaeda salsa restoration: Context-dependent biological responses under controlled flooding
abstract: Locally sourced reed straw may provide a biodegradable, near-natural aid for re-establishing Suaeda salsa on hydrologically variable salt-marsh surfaces. We screened no mulch and 1-, 2-, and 3-cm anchored, cross-woven configurations across three flooding depths and three daily inundation durations. The split-plot experiment comprised 36 independently operated tanks and 144 separate pots. The implemented configurations differed in standing seedling proportion, plant height, root biomass, and total biomass, and several configuration contrasts changed with hydrological treatment. A quasi-binomial mixed-model sensitivity analysis supported the early seedling result, while per-pot analyses supported the biomass result. No configuration was consistently superior, and none of the 27 hydrology-specific day-9 or day-90 treatment-versus-control contrasts remained significant after Holm adjustment. The descriptive pattern supports carrying the 2- and 3-cm configurations forward for direct comparison in a subsequent validation study; it does not establish an optimum. The experiment is therefore a controlled screen of a composite reed-straw configuration, not a test of spacing geometry alone or a field-ready restoration prescription.

title: Not all sealed soils recover alike: Pedogenic and technogenic controls on post-de-sealing recovery
Uranium retention and possible redox transformation by Sphingomonas metalli-silicate mixtures in simulated mining environments
Selective upcycling chelated copper from wastewater to Cu2-xSe-rich product: integrating selenium bio-reduction into anaerobic granular sludge technology
abstract: The treatment of wastewater containing chelated copper (Cu), such as Cu-EDTA complexes, remains a persistent challenge owing to the high stability of the chelates and the generation of hazardous heavy metal-bearing sludge. This study proposes a selenium-enhanced anaerobic granular sludge (Se-GS) technology for selective Cu recovery as a Cu 2-x Se-rich product. Over 100 days of continuous operation in a single laboratory-scale reactor with synthetic wastewater, the Se-GS reactor achieved a Cu removal efficiency of 98.7%, with dissolved effluent Cu concentrations consistently below 0.5 mg/L, outperforming the unamended control. Sequential extraction, X-ray diffraction and elemental analysis indicated that Cu and Se in the final Se-GS sludge residue may be predominantly present as crystalline Cu 2-x Se, which was extracted to obtain a Cu 2-x Se-rich product with a Cu recovery efficiency of 62.5%. Metagenomic analysis identified Desulfovibrio as a candidate functional genus associated with selenium transformation and a genome-level pathway for Cu 2-x Se biosynthesis was reconstructed. The recovered product exhibited a higher apparent methylene blue (MB) degradation rate under the tested condition than chemically synthesized Cu 2-x Se. The process is a selective Cu-recovery unit within a broader treatment train; residual EDTA, Cd and recovery-related streams require further management. Further validation with real wastewater, replicate reactors, and scale-up systems is warranted to confirm the robustness and scalability of the Se-GS process.

title: How does integrated white mango scale management affect mango production in Ethiopia?
abstract: White mango scale (WMS) infestation poses a serious threat to mango production in Ethiopia, leading to yield losses, reduced fruit quality, and declining farmer income. This study assesses the impacts of adopting integrated WMS management—combining cultural, chemical, and biological control methods—on mango yield, income, and environmental outcomes using data from 770 households. Results from a multinomial endogenous switching regression (MESR) model indicate that education, access to extension services, cooperative membership, credit availability, and farming experience significantly influence adoption decisions. Integrated management practices significantly improve yield and fruit quality, with the highest gains observed under combined strategies. In addition, the environmental assessment, based on farmers' perceived changes, suggests that integrated approaches are associated with improved soil fertility, water quality, biodiversity, and air conditions, while reducing chemical-related waste and pest resistance, thereby supporting a cleaner and more sustainable production system. The study underscores the importance of strengthening access to credit and enhancing extension and training services to promote wider adoption, ultimately improving productivity, farmers’ income from mangoes, and environmental sustainability in the region.

title: A dispatch-aware framework for resource-efficient distributed electrification: A case study of photovoltaic-battery streetlights
Teen depression and anxiety predicted by childhood brain development
Surprise! White dwarf stars come in a rainbow of colours
A single antimatter particle in a cage opens door to ‘revolutionary’ physics
To heal sick cities, scientists and residents must work together
Huge mapping study reveals how your brain tracks what your body is feeling
