title: Cohort Profile: A Scottish population-level study on the outcomes of people released from prison (RELEASE)
Calls to action and voter engagement on Facebook: a comparative study of eight European election campaigns
abstract: This study examines the use of Facebook by political actors across eight European countries – Czech Republic, Germany, Hungary, Kosovo, Norway, Portugal, Spain, United Kingdom – as they attempt to engage voters through calls to action. By analysing what is often referred to as the supply and demand of political communication, the paper conceptualizes three primary types of calls to action: informing, mobilizing, and interacting. Our findings reveal that mobilizing calls are the most prevalent, reflecting the central mission of election campaigns to secure voter turnout. However, such calls do not necessarily result in higher user engagement compared to informative content. Despite the potential for interactive features to enhance dialogic communication, they remain underutilized, with political actors apparently favouring controlled interactivity to maintain message control. The study highlights significant cross-country differences, with variations in the degree of engagement reached by different calls to action as influenced by national political contexts and campaign cultures. The research underscores the importance of considering both the strategic priorities of political actors and the cultural and institutional factors that shape voter engagement on social media.

title: Data visualisation as an ‘emotional repository’
abstract: Understanding the role of emotions in engagements with data visualisations (graphs, charts, maps) is important given their increasing circulation in everyday life and their influence on how people make sense of social and political issues. This paper builds on sociological perspectives on emotions and advances existing research on the interplay between data visualisation and emotions by proposing the concept of ‘emotional repository’ to describe data visualisations. I argue that data visualisations do not simply evoke emotional responses but become sites where emotions attach to, accumulate around, and acquire meaning through specific visual, data, and socio-political contexts. To explore this, the paper draws on empirical research, analysing thirty-four semi-structured interviews and thirteen follow-up interviews with diverse social media users who responded to climate data visualisations published on social media by environmental organisations. The paper makes an original contribution to the limited existing research on data visualisation in society by showing how data visualisations are socially and politically structured through their embedding within broader socio-political contexts. Moreover, it argues that data visualisations have the potential to make distressing topics, such as climate disaster, more palatable and aesthetically enjoyable, thereby influencing how social media users emotionally engage with and respond to the information presented in the data visualisation. The findings suggest that approaches to data visualisation should extend beyond clarity and accuracy to consider the social, political, and emotional contexts that shape how people engage with data.

title: Quantifying lifetime risk of Lyme disease: a population-based modelling study in the United States
Sleep health and uterine leiomyomata incidence and growth: a prospective ultrasound study
abstract: Abstract Poor sleep may negatively impact reproductive outcomes, yet its role in uterine leiomyomata (UL) development has not been studied. We estimated prospectively the association of self-reported sleep health with ultrasound-detected UL incidence and growth in the Study of Environment, Lifestyle, and Fibroids, a prospective cohort of Black individuals aged 23-35 years in Detroit, Michigan. At each of five clinic visits (2010-2020), participants reported sleep duration, frequency of trouble sleeping, and sleep quality, and underwent transvaginal ultrasound to detect incident UL. We used Cox proportional hazards regression models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) and applied inverse probability weights to adjust for time-dependent confounding. Among 1,137 participants, 351 developed UL (10-year cumulative incidence: 30.9%). Short (<6 hours/day, HR=0.30 95% CI: 0.17, 0.55) sleep duration and consistently poorer sleep quality (<4 days/week feeling well-rested, HR=0.78, 95% CI: 0.56, 1.08) were associated with lower UL incidence. Increased frequency of trouble sleeping was positively associated with UL incidence (≥15 days/month, HR=1.96, 95% CI: 0.76, 5.09). Sleep health was not associated with UL growth. In this prospective ultrasound study, sleep measures were inconsistently associated with UL incidence and not associated with UL growth.

title: Husband smoking, smoking cessation, and fecundability among couples with non-smoking wives
abstract: Abstract Among couples with non-smoking wives, the relationship between husband smoking and fecundability remains uncertain. Evidence is limited regarding whether smoking cessation before conception is associated with improved fecundability. We included a total of 4,569,530 reproductive-aged couples with non-smoking wives from the National Free Pre-conception Check-up Project in China from 2015 to 2017. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate fecundability hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 4,569,530 eligible couples, 1,228,222 (26.88%) husbands reported smoking at baseline. Within 1 year, 3,046,804 couples (66.68%) conceived, with a median TTP of 2.76 cycles. Husband smoking was associated with lower fecundability (HR=0.97, 95% CI, 0.97-0.97), demonstrating a dose-response relationship. Among 781,481 couples in which the husband smoked and conception occurred within 1 year, 507,530 (64.94%) reported smoking cessation. Smoking cessation was associated with higher fecundability (HR=1.23, 95% CI, 1.23-1.24), with consistent benefits across prior smoking levels, although the magnitude of improvement was smaller among husbands who smoked more heavily. Associations varied by age and were more pronounced in older couples. These findings support the inclusion of husband smoking cessation in preconception care and highlight its potential role in promoting smoke-free households and broader tobacco control efforts.

title: Driving Simulation Methods for Assessing Post-Injury Driving Performance After Mild Traumatic Brain Injury: A Scoping Review
abstract: Driving is a cognitively demanding task that involves the continuous integration of attention, executive control, visual processing, and motor coordination. Mild traumatic brain injury (mTBI) may disrupt these functions and affect driving performance during recovery. Driving simulation is increasingly used to examine post-mTBI driving performance, yet substantial heterogeneity exists in simulator platforms, task designs, and outcome selection. This scoping review characterized driving simulation methodologies used to assess post-mTBI driving performance and examined patterns of mTBI-related findings across reported outcomes. A systematic search of seven electronic databases identified 12 eligible publications between 2017 and 2026. Publications were synthesized by participant characteristics, time since injury, simulator platform, task demands, and outcomes. Across publications, mTBI-related findings were most frequently reported for vehicle control metrics, particularly lane position variability and speed regulation. mTBI-related differences were most often condition-specific, including differences during curves, hazard events, and manipulated cognitive load or dual-task conditions. Cognitive measures also demonstrated mTBI-related differences and associations to driving performance, particularly those assessing executive functioning and processing speed domains. Differences were observed across all post-injury intervals, including ≥ 15 days, with a small number of related publications reporting performance differences after symptom resolution. However, the predominantly cross-sectional evidence does not establish whether these differences persist over time within the same individuals. Findings suggest that driving simulation can provide a useful controlled method for examining functional driving performance following mTBI across varying road environments and task demands. Future work should prioritize standardizing simulator outcomes and validating simulator performance against on-road, naturalistic-driving, and crash-related outcomes.

title: Exploring pathways between childhood parental abuse and adulthood generalized anxiety disorder: The roles of neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness
abstract: Background Childhood parental abuse is an established risk factor for adulthood generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), but the personality mechanisms explaining this pathway are underinvestigated. Based on developmental psychopathology and triple vulnerability models, this study evaluated whether neuroticism, extraversion, and conscientiousness mediated the 18-year prospective paths from maternal and paternal abuse to adulthood GAD severity. Each abuse source was tested independently. Method Community adults ( N = 3293) ( M age = 45.61 years, standard deviation [ SD ] = 11.41, range = 20–86; 54.95% women; 89.7% non-Hispanic White) participated in three Midlife Development in the United States (MIDUS) study waves. A parallel latent variable mediation analysis estimated all three personality traits as mediators. Covariate-adjusted analyses controlled for age, sex, race, education, and body mass index (BMI). Random-intercept cross-lagged panel models (RI-CLPMs) and residualized-change models differentiated trait-level from within-person effects. Results Greater maternal, but not paternal, abuse significantly predicted higher neuroticism, which, in turn, significantly mediated the path to GAD symptoms ( B = 0.051, p = .008). This effect remained significant after covariate adjustment and in unadjusted and covariate-adjusted RI-CLPMs ( Bs = 0.074 and 0.060, p s < .001), though paternal abuse showed a smaller effect. Change-based mediation was attenuated ( B = 0.007, p = .014). Conscientiousness and extraversion did not mediate any path. Discussion Neuroticism mediated the 18-year path from childhood maternal abuse to GAD symptoms, mainly via trait-level differences, but pre-existing personality differences are still potential confounders. Neuroticism-focused prevention approaches, possibly optimized via transdiagnostic strategies, require assessment.

title: Maternal childhood emotional abuse and prosocial behavior in Chinese preschoolers: Roles of parenting and children's social information processing
Unpacking the Gender Wage Gap: Integrating Gradational Measures of Gender Perceptions
abstract: The wage gap between men and women remains a durable form of gender labor market stratification. In this article, we integrate gradational measures of gender perceptions with standard models of the binary gender wage gap. Specifically, we articulate two pathways through which gradational gender perceptions may assist in explaining the disparity in wages between people who identify as men and women: the “gender atypicality” perspective and the “masculinity premium” perspective. Drawing on original survey data from more than 4,000 workers in the low-wage service sector in the United States, we find that, on average, men and women receive higher wages when they are perceived as more masculine and that differences in perceived masculinity assist in explaining some of the binary gender wage gap. While this main set of findings aligns with the “masculinity premium” perspective, we show that this pattern is far from universal. It holds only among woman-dominated jobs and does not hold for tips. Additionally, women who are perceived as more masculine also report higher levels of gender discrimination and sexual harassment. Together, these findings contribute to our understanding of the gender wage gap, encourage the use of more gradational and perceptual measures of gender, and point to important heterogeneity in the ways that these processes operate.

title: Data-driven design of hybrid energy systems: Insights from a high-resolution nationwide geospatial assessment
abstract: In the United States, roughly 95% of hydrogen is produced via steam methane reforming (SMR) and natural gas is becoming increasingly valuable for other applications such as power generation and export. This study evaluates pathways to diversify supply and lower hydrogen costs through a high-resolution, physics-based, open-source assessment of off-grid hybrid energy systems for electrolytic hydrogen. We resolve plant design, nonlinear electrolyzer performance and degradation, and hydrogen storage across 58,225 sites, executing approximately 173 million simulations that sweep 198 wind-solar-battery configurations, five hydrogen storage options and three electrolyzer CapEx scenarios, to produce geographically resolved design guidance. Key findings: (1) Hybrid and hybrid-battery plants minimize levelized cost of hydrogen (LCOH) at nearly all sites, with optimal designs consistently oversizing generation relative to electrolyzer capacity. (2) Declining electrolyzer costs simplify plant designs by eliminating batteries, this change in plant design leads to lower capacity factors and shorter stack lives. (3) Electrolyzer cost reductions yield larger LCOH reductions without storage than with buried pipe. (4) Optimal storage adds approximately $0.64/kg on average; buried pipe is never the least-cost option but is widely considered deployable today. Together, these results show that off-grid hybrid energy systems can become increasingly competitive with SMR as electrolyzer CapEx costs fall and indicate where that competitiveness emerges first. Future work should assess advanced dispatch to limit degradation and LCOH, optimize for fixed delivery profiles, and expand to additional electrolyzer types and dispatchable generators to map broader hybridization benefits.

title: An LLM-guided multi-objective optimization framework for cluster-aware electric vehicle charging management toward sustainable grid operation
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EVs) is increasing stress on power distribution networks by amplifying peak demand and reducing charging-station utilization under uncoordinated charging. This study proposes a Large Language Model-guided Hyper-Heuristic (LLM-HH) for adaptive EV charging coordination. The framework uses a lightweight LLM-based meta-controller that monitors compact optimization feedback signals, including hypervolume (HV) improvement, population diversity, and stagnation, to orchestrate a portfolio of multi-objective evolutionary algorithms (MOEAs) through constrained solver selection and bounded parameter updates. Under an hourly coordination model, the framework coordinates a portfolio of MOEAs to jointly optimize three competing objectives: reducing on-peak demand, improving charger utilization, and preserving a cluster-level energy-per-session proxy across three behaviorally distinct charging regimes: Quick Top-Up, Home-Based, and Public-Stay. Experiments on a real-world Korean EV charging dataset demonstrate that the optimization-feedback-driven LLM-HH consistently improves Pareto front quality, achieving statistically significant improvements in Pareto-front quality over strong MOEA baselines and adaptive HH comparators, reducing on-peak demand by up to 18%, and incurring negligible runtime overhead ( < 2 % ). The framework also supports practical deployment through auditable, guardrail-constrained control actions grounded in optimization feedback. These results demonstrate that LLM-guided HH can improve the robustness, efficiency, and scalability of coordinated EV charging for more sustainable grid operation.

title: Calibrated uncertainty quantification for prosumer flexibility aggregation in ancillary service markets
abstract: Reliable forecasting of prosumer flexibility is critical for demand response aggregators participating in frequency controlled ancillary service markets, where reliability requirements such as the P90 standard are enforced. Limited behavioural data and dependence on exogenous forecasts introduce uncertainty into flexibility estimates, which can lead to reserve overestimation and financial penalties. This study applies and systematically evaluates established uncertainty quantification approaches based on Monte Carlo dropout (MCD), conformal prediction (CP), and conformalised quantile regression (CQR) to construct prediction intervals for aggregated prosumer flexibility and support uncertainty-aware aggregator bidding. The approaches are evaluated for a behind-the-meter aggregator participating in the Danish manual frequency restoration reserve capacity market. A large-scale synthetic dataset is generated using an industry-grade home energy management system, combined with publicly available load, solar, price, activation, and device-level data. Multiple multivariate CP strategies are evaluated using MCD predictions, alongside CQR using a separately trained quantile regression model. Under nominal synthetic test conditions, conformal methods substantially improve joint coverage compared with uncalibrated MCD baselines. More conservative methods satisfy the 90% lower-tail reliability requirement, while CQR and MCP provide comparatively narrow intervals and higher retained economic value. CQR and MCP retain approximately 69% and 68% of perfect-information profit, respectively, under the stricter penalty interpretation. A controlled robustness analysis further shows that increasing perturbations of load, solar, price, and activation inputs increase overbidding and reduce empirical coverage and economic performance. The results highlight the trade-off between reliability, economic value, and robustness to input uncertainty when applying established uncertainty quantification approaches to aggregator bidding.

title: Entropic risk-aware end-to-end learning for stochastic optimization of renewable-rich integrated energy systems
Constraint-first energy-efficient indoor environmental control with multi-agent device coordination and knowledge-graph memory
A region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions using improved deep clustering
abstract: Power batteries, as core components of new energy systems, exhibit significant regional variability in field reliability under heterogeneous operating conditions. However, accurate prediction of region-specific reliability remains challenging due to the scarcity of comprehensive field failure data across diverse regions and the homogeneity assumptions commonly adopted in existing regional reliability modeling. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel region-aware field reliability prediction method for power batteries under heterogeneous conditions, leveraging an improved deep clustering algorithm. First, environmental factors and a macro-level socioeconomic covariate associated with regional field reliability are systematically analyzed and identified, and a dynamic panel dataset is constructed. Mutual information is employed to quantify their statistical associations with regional field reliability. Second, an improved Transformer-based multi-kernel ensemble spectral clustering (TMESC) algorithm is developed to enable intelligent regional classification driven by heterogeneity in observed regional characteristics. Third, based on the derived regional clusters and available failure data from observed regions, a nonlinear mapping model is developed to quantitatively link field reliability with regional characteristics, facilitating accurate prediction of field reliability in unobserved regions. Experimental results show that, guided by TMESC clustering, the proposed method estimates power battery failure rates and has accurate predictive ability at the regional aggregate scale, improving regional reliability assessment and providing support for data-driven warranty and maintenance strategies.

title: Resource flows in the UK’s foundation industries
abstract: The UK foundation industries supply essential materials but remain difficult to decarbonise because of high-temperature processing and process emissions. This study implements a gate-to-gate resource flow mapping, integrating material and energy inputs and outputs, by-products, and direct emissions, for selected cement, ceramics, chemicals, glass, metals, and paper products in 2019, benchmarked against global averages and product-mix-adjusted energy best practice. These products totalled 33 Mt/yr, used 330 PJ/yr of fuels and purchased electricity, and emitted 27 MtCO 2 /yr (Scope 1): 12.5 Mt from process reactions, 12.3 Mt from fossil fuels, and 2.1 Mt biogenic. Recovered materials (e.g., scrap), not counting by-products (e.g., slag), supplied 14% of material inputs excluding water and oxygen. UK energy intensity was 13% above the global benchmark. The gap to energy best practice is 28% in energy use but only 15% in direct emissions, mainly due to process-reaction emissions. This baseline can inform sectoral decarbonisation priorities and monitoring.

title: Hippocampal Meis2+ Interneurons Remodeling Involved in the Chronic Pb Exposure-Induced Learning and Memory Impairment: Single-Nucleus and Spatial Multiomics Evidence
abstract: Abstract Lead (Pb), recognized as the second greatest global environmental risk factor, is associated with lifelong and irreversible learning and memory impairments resulting from chronic exposure. However, the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We integrated single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial multiomics, neuroelectrophysiological, and morphological techniques to systematically delineate the susceptible neuronal cells and their interaction networks within hippocampal subregions following Pb exposure. The results indicated that Pb exposure led to a significant increase in the proportion of Meis2+ interneurons in the CA1 and CA3 regions of the hippocampus, and dysregulated calcium signaling. This subtype may affect PV+ and SST+ IN subtypes as well as CA3 excitatory neurons via abnormal intercellular NRG and EPHA signaling, contributing to E/I imbalance and impairing learning and memory. Moreover, reduced NRG signaling output from oligodendrocytes and microglia to IN subtypes likely exacerbates the impairment. Our findings highlight Meis2+ interneurons as a core IN subtype that may drive a cascade of “transcriptional changes – calcium signaling dysregulation – impaired neuronal interactions – reduced glial support”, offering potential targets for intervening in environmental Pb neurotoxicity.

title: Correspondence on “Kidney Urate Underexcretion Mediates the Relationship between Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances and their Alternatives and Uric Acid Levels: Evidence from a Case–Control Study and an Animal Study”
abstract: reports that decreased fractional excretion of uric acid (FEUA%) mediates the association between exposure to perand polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) and increased serum uric acid levels.While the authors integrate epidemiological and experimental data, the direction of causality in their findings warrants more careful consideration.A primary concern is reverse causality in epidemiological study.Although it was described as a "case-control study" in the title, this research essentially functions as a "cross-sectional analysis" because serum PFAS concentrations and FEUA% were measured simultaneously using the blood samples at recruitment. 2 A common misconception is to regard a casecontrol study as merely a comparison between "case" and "control" groups.The critical distinction from a cross-sectional study lies in whether the exposure can be ascertained to have occurred prior to the outcome, i.e., whether a temporal origin of the exposure in the past can be clearly identified.Consequently, the temporal relationship between FEUA% and blood PFAS levels remains unclear in the study design.1 Several PFASs have long biological half-lives, 3 and they may reflect exposure in the past.However, PFASs are eliminated primarily through renal excretion, and their serum concentrations are strongly influenced by renal clearance efficiency.It is highly plausible that reduced renal function leads to the accumulation of both PFASs and uric acid in blood, meaning decreased FEUA% may be confounded, rather than a result (Figure 1).This concern is supported by the study's data.The hyperuricemia group had significantly higher serum creatinine levels (88.43 μmol/L) than the control group (79.84 μmol/L), suggesting baseline differences in renal function.Furthermore, the metabolisms of urate differ fundamentally between rodents and humans.In humans, uric acid is the terminal metabolic product of purines because of the evolutionary loss of the uricase enzyme.Conversely, mice possess functional uricase, meaning uric acid is an intermediate metabolite that is further degraded into allantoin.4 This significant species difference complicates the extrapolation of urate-related mechanisms from mice to humans.We suggest that the authors more extensively discuss the potential for reverse causality, the limitations of their study design, and the extrapolability of animal study based on the biochemical differences.

title: From Equality to Equity: The Dual Socioeconomic Inequalities of Mobility-Based Exposure and Exposure Avoidance Options during Urban Floods
abstract: Abstract Urban pluvial flooding creates unequal risks that are not fully captured by residence-based exposure measures. We developed a framework that jointly evaluates mobility-based flood exposure (MFE) and exposure avoidance constraint (EAC), defined as the additional travel distance required to reduce flood susceptibility. Within Beijing’s Fifth Ring Road, we combined AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings with mobile phone signaling data to quantify flood exposure and flood-avoidance routing constraints for 614,510 residents. EAC is measured by constructing Pareto frontiers through Monte Carlo path simulation, while multinomial logit models with interaction terms are used to examine the relationships between socioeconomic status (SES) and the dual inequalities. The results show: (1) residence-based assessment suffers from the Neighborhood Effect Averaging Problem, leading to systematic bias relative to mobility-based measures; (2) low-SES groups experience dual disadvantages, characterized by higher MFE and higher EAC; and (3) the interaction between exposure and avoidance constraint is state-dependent, reinforcing the relative disadvantage of low-SES residents beyond an additive pattern under finite EAC, while limiting further socioeconomic differentiation under infinite EAC. We argue for a shift from an equality-oriented to an equity-oriented perspective, providing actionable insights for disaster risk reduction and the achievement of SDGs 3, 10, and 11.

title: Emissions of Respirable Magnetite from the Coal-Fired Power Sector in China: Spatial Inequalities and Mitigation Pathways
abstract: Abstract Magnetite particles, being ubiquitous and highly abundant in the atmosphere, have raised notable cardiovascular and neurodegenerative health risks globally. However, the limited understanding of their emissions hinders the targeted mitigation. Here, we developed a multifactor emission modeling framework to evaluate magnetite emission from the coal-fired power sector in China, one of the most sizable contributors to airborne magnetite, and identify policy-effective mitigation pathways. Total atmospheric emissions of respirable magnetite are 2,828.7 (2,307.1–3,371.4) t per year, exhibiting distinct spatial inequalities driven by tiered emission standards. Despite contributing only 4% of national coal-fired power, two superemitting provinces, Guizhou and Sichuan, could reduce over 31% of the national magnetite emission by tightening their emission standards, highlighting that targeting hotspots regions represents a highly efficient pathway to substantial mitigation benefits. These findings can facilitate policy-making for achieving targeted magnetite mitigation and provide transferable insight for air pollution control in other countries globally.

title: Paternal Preconception Calcitriol Intervention Rescued DBDPE-Induced Transgenerational Developmental and Visual Toxicity in Zebrafish
abstract: Abstract Growing evidence highlights the impact of preconception paternal environmental exposures on offspring health, yet the specific paternal contributions and transgenerational mechanisms of emerging contaminants remain poorly understood. Thus, we exposed male zebrafish to decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE), a widely used replacement for legacy flame retardants, for 2 months to investigate its intergenerational (F1) and transgenerational (F2) effects. Paternal DBDPE exposure severely impaired sperm quality in F0 zebrafish, and induced transgenerational developmental toxicity with elevated malformations in F2 larvae. Moreover, significant eye malformations occurred even at low doses in F2 groups, revealing the visual system to be highly sensitive to transgenerational DBDPE toxicity. F1 and F2 larvae exhibited marked behavioral disorders, retinal thinning, and phototransduction gene dysregulation, indicating significant visual dysfunction. Notably, transcriptome analysis revealed that steroid biosynthesis (especially calcitriol synthesis) was consistently disrupted across dose levels and generations, with its enrichment factor progressively increasing from F1 to F2; this was accompanied by a pronounced deficiency of calcitriol in paternal F0 testes. Accordingly, paternal calcitriol supplementation during DBDPE exposure effectively restored F0 sperm quality and mitigated visual and developmental toxicity in offspring. These findings suggest that paternal exposure to emerging contaminants may induce intergenerational and transgenerational effects, and that targeted preconception nutritional intervention may reduce these risks.

title: Dynamic Reconstitution of Fe–In Dual-Atom Sites with Bridged Intermediate Adsorption for Selectively Electrochemical Oxygen Reduction to Hydroxyl Radicals
abstract: Abstract The three-electron (3e–) oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) to hydroxyl radicals (HO•) represents an emerging strategy for water purification, yet achieving high selectivity remains challenging due to the scaling relationships between oxygen-containing intermediates. Herein, we report a Fe–In dual-atom catalyst (FeIn-DAC) with unique d-p orbital hybridization to tailor the electronic structure of Fe–In pairs for triggering optimal oxygen-bridged adsorption. Operando XANES and in situ Raman spectroscopy reveal that the initial Fe–N4 motif dynamically reconstitutes into Fe–N3 as the genuine active site upon ORR initiation, exposing more unsaturated sites for Yeager-type bridge-adsorbed *O–O* species. DFT calculations confirm that charge rearrangement within Fe–In pairs avoids excessively strong or weak electronic coupling with oxygen intermediates for steering 3e– ORR to HO•. As expected, the FeIn-DAC electrocatalytic system achieves a high HO• generation rate of 6.02 μmol L–1 min–1 and delivers ∼90% TOC removal for various antibiotic pollutants across wide pH ranges. A pilot flow-through device further verifies its practical applicability for real pharmaceutical wastewater treatment with ∼75%–85% TOC/COD removal during 24 h continuous operation. This study highlights potential-driven dynamic reconstitution of dual-atom catalysts for steering selective multielectron ORR under real working conditions.

title: Efficient Formation of Atmospheric Triplets and Organosulfur from Photochemistry of Non/weakly Light-absorbing Biomass Burning Tracers and S(IV)
abstract: Abstract Biomass burning (BB) events emit S(IV) and biomass-burning organic aerosol (BBOA). While some BBOA constituents generate atmospheric oxidants through photosensitization, a major fraction of BBOA consists of phenolics with negligible or weak absorption of solar radiation. Therefore, these phenolics, together with S(IV), have generally been viewed as atmospheric substrates of other oxidants. Here, we show that their photochemical interactions constitute an efficient source of brown carbon (BrC) and organosulfur products. Under simulated solar irradiation, aqueous S(IV) photochemistry initiates the decay of non/weakly light-absorbing phenolic BB tracers, including phenols, methoxyphenols, and catechols, with methoxyphenols (guaiacol, GUA; and syringol, SYR) exhibiting the most substantial decay. S(IV) photooxidation generates sulfur-centered radicals, which trigger the formation of organosulfur and BrC products, including quinone-like photosensitizers. Scavenging experiments and kinetic modeling demonstrate that triplets (3PS*)-mediated pathways arising from BrC photosensitization dominate the methoxyphenol decay, in turn leading to new BrC formation. Model results reveal that, across varying atmospheric GUA and S(IV) precursor levels, these 3PS* reach 10–15–10–14 M, comparable to those originating from primary photosensitizers in aqueous-phase BBOA. This work identifies a previously overlooked source of photosensitizers and extends the role of non/weakly light-absorbing BB tracers from passive substrates to active contributors to atmospheric oxidative capacity.

title: Adaptation and Resistance of Nitrifiers to Harsh Engineered Conditions during Partial Nitritation
abstract: Abstract Selective suppression of nitrite-oxidizing bacteria (NOB) is essential for stable partial nitritation (PN), yet NOB often persist or recover under engineered suppression conditions. This study investigated the kinetic, microbial, and genomic responses of NOB and ammonia-oxidizing bacteria (AOB) in a PN system subjected to low pH and high free nitrous acid (FNA) sidestream treatment. A sequencing batch reactor was operated for 283 days under varying treatment intensities. Long-term operation selectively enriched a Candidatus nitrotogafabula-related MAG (bin.69), characterized by a relatively high apparent growth rate (∼1.3 d–1) and low substrate affinity (Ks = 2.3 ± 0.4 mg NO2–-N L–1; Ko = 1.1 ± 0.3 mg O2 L–1). Comparative genomic analyses identified stress-tolerance-associated traits related to proton transport, ion homeostasis, protein stabilization, and cellular stress responses. Proteome isoelectric (pI) point analysis further showed a lower genomic pI profile than other known NOB, potentially consistent with persistence under acidic and FNA stress. These findings provide genome-informed insights into NOB persistence under long-term suppression and implications for improving PN stability.

title: Global Cropland Efficiency-Stress Divide: Typological Diagnosis and Reconciling Pathways
abstract: Abstract Cropland underpins food security but faces mounting resource constraints and environmental pressures. Achieving sustainable agriculture hinges on advancing land use efficiency (LUE) and alleviating land ecological stress (LES). However, a typological framework characterizing LUE and LES remains lacking, hindering the distinction between technical efficiency and ecological sustainability in cropland use. Herein, we establish a coupled LUE-LES diagnostic framework by integrating the super-efficiency slack-based measure model with land ecological footprint accounting. This framework classifies regions into efficiency-stress typologies globally for 2011, 2015, 2019, and 2022, and identifies type-specific improvement priorities through slack and ecological footprint-biocapacity diagnostics. Results show that in 2022, LUE is below 1 in 62.5% of regions, while China and Brazil reach 1.90 and 1.81, respectively, but remain efficient-stressed due to high ecological deficits. Despite ecological deficits, Indonesia and Australia exhibit the highest outflow intensity of embodied cropland use, exporting 55.9% and 68.0% of regional production-based land ecological footprint (PLEF), respectively. Two-dimensional diagnostics identify irrigation water and energy as dominant sources of inefficiency and show that PLEF exceeds land biocapacity by approximately 5%–35% in deficit regions. Policy designs for reconciling LUE and LES should guide supply-side efficiency gains, complemented by demand- and trade-oriented measures for durable agricultural sustainability.

title: Monitoring the Environmental Degradation of Biodegradable Mulch Films Using Py-GC-MS and a Multitechnique Analytical Approach
abstract: Abstract Biodegradable mulch films have been developed for use in agriculture to reduce costs incurred during the retrieval of conventional mulch films and to prevent plastic pollution of soil caused by their incomplete removal. However, there are knowledge gaps on their degradation rate and potential environmental impact of any residuals. This study investigated the degradation of three commercially available mulch films, one made of polyethylene and two labeled as “biodegradable”. These products were exposed to four conditions in the open environment. After 24 months in soil, air, and a combination of air pre-exposure for 3 months followed by soil burial, all samples retained their overall film structure and were still recoverable, although different levels of physical and chemical changes indicated ongoing degradation. In seawater, no residual fragments of the biodegradable mulch films remained after 3 months of exposure. Pyrolysis-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry detected leaching of a plasticizer from one of the biodegradable films in all environments and other degradation features. The outcome of this study highlights the potential for environmental accumulation of mulch films labeled as “biodegradable” and the need for the development of international environmental testing standards and associated labeling to guide users on appropriate use and disposal of mulch films.

title: Emission Mitigation and Climate Warming Increase China’s Ozone Responsiveness to Soil NO x Relative to Biogenic VOCs
abstract: Abstract Surface ozone (O3) remains a major air quality challenge in China despite recent reductions in anthropogenic emissions. Here, we use regional photochemical modeling to quantify changes in summertime O3 responses to relative perturbations in biogenic volatile organic compounds (BVOCs) and soil nitrogen oxides (NOx) under historical emission conditions and future mitigation and climate scenarios through 2060. Declining anthropogenic emissions increase ozone production efficiency and produce divergent response patterns: the modeled O3 response magnitude to BVOCs perturbations generally decreases, whereas the response magnitude to soil NOx perturbations increases. Under the 2060 net-zero scenario, the O3 response to an equivalent relative perturbation in soil NOx exceeds that to BVOCs in several regions. Projected climate warming further enhances O3 responsiveness to soil NOx, particularly in agriculturally intensive regions. These results indicate a scenario-dependent shift in the relative O3-response magnitude to natural precursor emissions, rather than a direct change in their source contributions. The increasing responsiveness to soil NOx suggests that agricultural nitrogen management should be evaluated as a potential complement to conventional industrial and transportation emission controls in future ozone mitigation strategies.

title: Surface-Confined Pt–Ov–Mn Atomic Interfaces Promote Deep Benzene Mineralization through Coupled Electron Transfer and Lattice-Oxygen Activation
abstract: Abstract Single-atom catalysts are promising for VOC abatement, but their application is limited by the trade-off between the stability of isolated atoms and the redox activity. Herein, we report a surface-confined Pt–Ov–Mn atomic interface constructed within the outer layer of Mn2O3 via thermal self-reconstruction. Oxygen vacancies trap isolated Pt atoms and electronically connect them with neighboring Mn centers, forming a vacancy-rich interfacial active center. For benzene oxidation, Pt1/Mn2O3 achieved a specific reaction rate of 45.70 μmol gPt–1 s–1 at 140 °C, which is 3.8 and 11.2 times those of the Pt nanocluster and nanoparticle counterparts, respectively. The catalyst also exhibited excellent thermal stability and enhanced tolerance to SO2 poisoning. Mechanistic studies reveal that the Pt–Ov–Mn interface enables electron–lattice-oxygen coupling: interfacial Pt 5d–Mn 3d electronic interaction upshifts the Pt d-band center, strengthening benzene π adsorption and promoting C–H activation and ring opening, while adjacent oxygen vacancies accelerate lattice-oxygen migration and replenishment through a Mars–van Krevelen cycle. This coupled pathway suppresses the accumulation of partially oxidized intermediates and drives deep mineralization to CO2. These findings identify surface-layer atomic interfaces as designable active centers for developing robust SACs toward hazardous VOC control.

title: Establishing an Air Health Index for Predicting the Risk of Acute Myocardial Infarction Onset Associated with Air Pollution and Ambient Temperature
abstract: Abstract Air pollutants and ambient temperature are important cardiovascular disease determinants, and communicating their overall risk is important for cardiovascular patient management. We developed a composite Air Health Index (AHI) by linking high-resolution exposure data with 1,207,625 acute myocardial infarction (AMI) cases across 325 Chinese cities. The AHI for AMI aggregates excess morbidity risks from fine particulate matter, nitrogen dioxide, ozone, and ambient temperature into a normalized scale (0–10+). Compared with existing metrics, the AHI for AMI showed better predictive performance for AMI onset than the Air Quality Index (AQI) and Air Quality Health Index (AQHI). Each interquartile range increase in the AHI for AMI was associated with a 5.97% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.32%–6.63%) increase in AMI incidence, surpassing the AQHI (3.33%, 95% CI: 2.93%–3.72%) and AQI (2.04%, 95% CI: 1.73%–2.35%). The AHI for AMI showed a nearly linear exposure–response relationship with no evident threshold and accounted for 8,534 per 100,000 AMI cases nationally. These associations were consistently validated in an independent external data set, supporting the robustness and generalizability of the index. In conclusion, the AHI for AMI provides an integrative and practical framework for assessing environmental health risks, offering actionable guidance for cardiovascular patient management.

title: Nanozyme-Based Analytical Platforms for Environmental Pollutants: Classification, Catalytic Mechanisms, and Multimodal Strategies
abstract: Abstract The precise trace pollutant analysis within complex environmental matrices demands robust, highly specific, and anti-interference analytical platforms. Nanozymes, possessing tunable enzyme-like catalytic activities, superior thermodynamic stability, and cost effectiveness, have emerged as innovative tools in environmental analytical chemistry. This Review systematically discusses the integration of diverse nanozymes (metal, metal oxide, carbon, hybrid-structured, and multimetallic alloy) across foundational analytical methodologies, including colorimetric, fluorometric, electrochemical, chemiluminescence, and surface-enhanced Raman scattering assays. To overcome the matrix interference present in real-world samples, this Review highlights the pivotal evolution from conventional single-signal detection to advanced multimodal sensing approaches. The incorporation of molecular imprinting, microfluidics, and photothermal technologies effectively mitigates matrix interference, enhances mass transfer, and eliminates false positives through multidimensional cross-validation. Furthermore, atomic-level regulation strategies including defect engineering, asymmetric coordination, and high-entropy synergistic effects are presented to address inherent limitations such as catalytic passivation and nanoparticle aggregation. A unified standardization metric framework is also proposed for rigorous analytical performance evaluation. Finally, a perspective is provided on coupling artificial intelligence and machine learning with the nanozyme-based sensing platform, guiding a pathway from empirical trial-and-error to the rational and data-driven design of next-generation intelligent environmental analytical systems.

title: The New Frontiers in Endocrine Disruption Research and Policy
abstract: Abstract Since the 1991 Wingspread Consensus Statement, the field of endocrine disruption has emerged as a distinct and complex area that continues to challenge conventional approaches to toxicology and risk assessment. Nonetheless, despite substantial scientific advances, including the identification of over 1,000 Endocrine Disrupting Chemicals (EDCs), the description of nonmonotonic dose–response relationships, and the elucidation of multiple mechanisms of action, regulatory progress continues to lag. Recent stagnation in research investment into EDCs reflects a persistent tension between robust scientific evidence and policy implementation for environmental chemicals, which is especially salient for those bearing the unique properties and concerns of endocrine disruptors. In this article, we delineate the lull in EDC research that began in the mid-to-late 2010s and discuss how per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) have refocused public, scientific, and regulatory attention away from EDCs. While PFAS qualify as EDCs, their structural similarity and environmental persistence enable regulatory pathways that circumvent traditional research bottlenecks confronting other endocrine disruptors. This divergence presents both opportunities and potential drawbacks: while PFAS regulation may revitalize the broader EDC field, overemphasis on PFAS could perpetuate longstanding challenges in chemical prioritization, mixture assessment, and cumulative risk evaluation. We highlight state-level initiatives in Maine, Minnesota, and Washington as promising models for adaptive regulation. Moving forward, coordinated action among states, industry, academia, and civil society will be essential to advancing protective EDC policy while maintaining scientific rigor and feasibility.

title: Atmospheric Observations Reveal the Spatial Influence of Inland Shipping Channels and Enhanced Emission Signals from AIS-Unmatched Vessels
abstract: Abstract Inland shipping is an important but poorly constrained source of urban air pollution, particularly in dense waterway networks, where vessel activity records are incomplete. Here, we integrate high-time-resolution differential optical absorption spectroscopy (DOAS), national air-quality observations, meteorological normalization, spatial exposure analysis, automatic identification system (AIS) records, and field photographs to evaluate inland shipping impacts in two representative channel environments in eastern China. SO2 showed stronger spatial heterogeneity than nitrogen-related pollutants and was more closely associated with the nearby shipping channels. After meteorological normalization, inland-waterway configuration explained 44% of the interstation variability in urban SO2, with the strongest association at an influence distance of approximately 4 km. Event-scale analysis revealed frequent short-term pollutant enhancements associated with the vessel passages. However, only 54.4% of plume events at the open-channel station and 44.8% at the lock-controlled site could be matched to AIS-recorded vessels. AIS-unmatched plume events were not negligible and, in the lock-controlled environment, were associated with SO2 signals higher than those of AIS-matched events. These results demonstrate that atmospheric observations provide an independent constraint on underdetected inland shipping emissions and suggest that inventories relying solely on vessel activity records may underestimate or mischaracterize sulfur-related emissions from inland waterways.

title: Eco-fiscal sustainability of plain afforestation: From ecological value creation to value realization
abstract: Afforestation projects can enhance ecosystem services (ESs) but may leave persistent fiscal commitments for land leasing and forest maintenance after project construction. Existing ES and Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) assessments have largely focused on ecological value creation, with limited attention to whether and under what conditions this value can be converted into funding for long-term operation. This study develops an eco-fiscal sustainability framework integrating spatial restructuring, GEP accounting, life-cycle cost analysis, future projection, ecological value realization (EVR), and uncertainty analysis, using the Plain Afforestation Project in Xiji Town, Beijing, as a case study. From 2010 to 2023, afforestation transformed the landscape from cropland dominance to a forest–cropland mosaic, while GEP increased by 26.6% to CNY 839.5 million and regulating services accounted for 92.02% of total GEP. Assuming no further afforestation, total GEP is projected to increase to CNY 916.2–939.8 million by 2080, mainly through forest development within the afforestation area, whereas annual fiscal costs generally decline as construction expenditure ends and maintenance requirements decrease. However, cumulative cost coverage depends strongly on EVR: under the 2030 baseline activation scenario, and given the specified cost pathway and GEP uncertainty, the 10% and 20% EVR scenarios do not achieve cumulative cost coverage by 2080, whereas all 3000 simulations under the 30% scenario reach non-negative cumulative net cash flow before 2080. These findings show that eco-fiscal sustainability depends not only on ecological value creation but, more critically, on the capacity to convert realizable ecological value into stable funding, providing a framework for the long-term management of post-construction peri-urban plain afforestation.

title: Longevity index for small electrical and electronic appliances: Qualitative assessment of reliability and durability
abstract: The growing concern over electronic waste and the need to extend product lifespans have highlighted longevity as a key aspect of sustainable product design. This research presents a longevity index as a practical tool for manufacturers and stakeholders to assess, communicate and improve the longevity of small electrical and electronic equipment (sEEE). The main novelty of the study lies in the integration of reliability and durability into a single operational index specifically developed for sEEE, combining technical, repairability, maintenance and warranty-related indicators through a transparent scoring and weighting system. The proposed methodology combines qualitative and quantitative elements to evaluate product longevity in a structured and comparable manner. The index was developed for application to different products within the sEEE category and implemented through an Excel-based tool that guides data collection and automatically calculates the final score. A controlled case-study application involving two products from the same category and three evaluators was conducted to examine the practical application of the method, its ability to differentiate between comparable products and inter-evaluator variability. A sensitivity analysis was also performed to assess the stability of the product scores and ranking under variations in the factor weights. As a decision-support tool, the longevity index contributes to circular economy objectives by providing structured information to support sustainable product choices.

title: Dietary transitions for urban water sustainability in arid regions: A planetary health case study from Ürümqi, China
abstract: We develop an integrated domestic water-conservation framework combining dynamic water pricing with healthy-diet interventions to jointly manage physical and virtual water use. (Virtual water refers to the total interregional flow, through trade, of water consumed in the production of traded products.) Relative to the baseline diet, healthy, vegetarian and meat-based diets reduced annual per-capita food water footprints (The water footprint quantifies the total water use associated with consumption by an individual, region or country.) by 166.11, 208.42 and 167.97 m 3 , respectively, and industrial water footprints by 14.95, 22.05 and 15.17 m 3 through supply-chain linkages, while direct domestic water use remained largely unchanged. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual per-capita shower water use by 10.58–15.88 m 3 and total domestic water use by 42.32–83.58 m 3 . Acceptance differed between interventions: 41.67% supported water-price regulation, mainly influenced by consumption habits, whereas 53.57% accepted dietary adjustment, with willingness more strongly associated with ethnicity and income. After accounting for acceptance rates, the three dietary scenarios reduced city-wide annual food water footprints by 370, 464 and 374 million m 3 and industrial water footprints by 33, 49 and 34 million m 3 , respectively. Dynamic water pricing reduced annual urban water use by 73–145 million m 3 , including 18–27 million m 3 of shower water. Water pricing therefore primarily affects direct domestic use, whereas dietary adjustment propagates upstream through supply chains, generating broader water-footprint effects. This framework advances domestic water conservation towards coordinated social–ecological governance of physical and virtual water, offering a transferable pathway for water-scarce cities.

title: Carbon emission efficiency of China's manufacturing industry and choice of precise carbon reduction paths——Analysis perspective based on the potential cost framework
abstract: Targeted decarbonization in manufacturing requires more than identifying efficiency losses; it also requires assessing each energy source's technical abatement potential, marginal abatement cost, and implementation priority. Using a balanced panel of 29 manufacturing subsectors in China from 2010 to 2024, this study estimates carbon emission efficiency with slacks-based measure directional distance function (SBM-DDF) models under meta-frontier and group-frontier technologies. It then uses undesirable-output slacks to quantify the abatement potential for coal, oil, and natural gas and combines these estimates with marginal abatement costs derived from parametric linear programming to construct a potential-Boston matrix. The results show that the manufacturing sector's meta-frontier efficiency increased from 0.520 to 0.641, although substantial room for improvement remains. For the medium- and high-emission groups, group-frontier efficiency was markedly higher than meta-frontier efficiency, indicating the need for both within-group catch-up and technological upgrading toward the meta-frontier. The high-emission group had the greatest abatement potential and the lowest average marginal abatement cost, whereas abating emissions associated with natural gas was generally more costly than abating those associated with coal or oil. The potential-Boston matrix classifies the 29 subsectors into four decarbonization pathways: phased advancement (13), comprehensive advancement (2), steady maintenance (12), and priority-focused mitigation (2). The proposed framework uses the meta-frontier to define long-term targets and group frontiers to set near-term catch-up benchmarks, translating efficiency, potential, and cost estimates into industry-energy priorities. Technology retrofits, fuel substitution, carbon pricing, transition finance, and regulatory measures can then be tailored to limit output losses while prioritizing high-potential, low-cost abatement opportunities.

title: Circularity of different plastic product sectors in Germany: Product interaction with surrounding infrastructure
abstract: Circular Economy (CE) potentials are often classified based on individual aspects such as material recyclability, failing to capture the complex interaction between products and surrounding infrastructure stemming from country-, product- and material-specific regulations and market conditions. While the circularity of individual product sectors has been discussed previously, a cross-sector comparison for the German plastics sector is missing. This study quantifies and compares the circularity of different plastic product sectors in Germany using the Material Circularity Indicator (MCI) for 2022 and projected 2030 scenarios. The applied polymer types and waste collection systems are further assessed regarding their contribution to circularity. The MCI results for 2022 range from below 0.20 (automotive, E&E, HLS, others) to almost 0.40 (packaging, agriculture), revealing large differences in circularity and untapped potentials for both using and providing circular materials. Projected 2030 scenarios based on current and planned recycling targets show substantial increases in several sectors. The polymer assessment shows that 43% to 97% of applied polymers are mechanically recyclable, yet apart from packaging, most sectors are limited by waste collection systems with only medium or low CE potential. Circularity is thus constrained less by polymer choice than by the institutional maturity and infrastructural embedding of each sector, and by missing regulations for recyclate reintegration. A successful CE implementation requires both a product and an infrastructure perspective to be considered together. The findings provide sector-specific circularity benchmarks and inform policy recommendations such as recycled-content quotas, quality standards and sector-specific roadmaps, relevant beyond Germany to other EU member states.

title: Prolonged (80-day) exposure to waste drilling fluids alters the structure and trophic networks of marine plankton communities in a microcosm study
abstract: The ecological risks associated with the direct discharge of waste drilling fluids (WDFs) into the ocean must be systematically assessed. Through an 80-day microcosm experiment, we assessed main pollution characteristics and seawater quality after introducing WDF water extracts at three concentrations and examined the prolonged dynamic effects of continuous exposure on natural plankton communities. WDF input altered key water quality parameters, increased Cr and As, and caused Cr and Hg in the HIGH group to exceed GB 3097-1997 Class I seawater standards. Chlorophyll a (Chl a) and dissolved oxygen (DO) levels and the pH decreased, whereas turbidity increased. WDF input also changed phytoplankton and zooplankton species compositions, increased spatial differentiation within communities, and generated dose-dependent effects. Phytoplankton responded more quickly than zooplankton, and toxicity verification experiments confirmed that phytoplankton were more sensitive. RDA indicated that Cr and Hg were the primary variables that explained changes in the community structure of phytoplankton and zooplankton, respectively. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed decreases in the total network and subnetwork topologies and the connectivity and abundance of key taxonomic groups, suggesting general network degradation. Based on the random forest model and Spearman's correlation analyses, cross-trophic interactions dominated the total network responses, followed by the phytoplankton subnetwork. These results indicate that the central mechanism underlying WDF ecological risk is weakening planktonic interactions via direct interspecies interference and impaired phytoplankton supply. These findings provide a systematic foundation and theoretical support for establishing an ecological risk assessment system for WDFs and promoting their eco-friendly use and emission management.

Arsenic spike prediction in a Hungarian drinking water distribution network using interpretable machine learning
abstract: Arsenic is a global contaminant of concern as chronic exposure above 10 μg/L in drinking water results in health issues including cancer, impaired cognitive development, and skin lesions. Arsenic is naturally abundant in Hungarian groundwater, posing challenges for compliance with European Union regulations. Trace amounts of arsenic accumulate in water distribution system pipes and may be mobilized downstream by fluctuations in pressure and water quality. Additionally, ambient arsenic can infiltrate from surrounding groundwater into compromised pipes during low pressure conditions. This research identifies mechanisms of interaction between water quality and pressure parameters, based on samples collected at ten public water faucets in an at-risk system on the Hungarian Great Plain, to reliably predict transient, localized arsenic spikes. Arsenic species were separated using an ion-exchange resin and measured via inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) or inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy with hydride generation (ICP-OES). Machine learning models predicted arsenic concentration using pressure data from nine hydrant-mounted sensors and water quality measurements. Random forest modeling achieved an excellent F1 score of 0.866 on unseen data. Manganese concentration and manganese interactions with iron, temperature, and mean and maximum pressure severity indices were the most important features aside from finished water arsenic concentration (SHAP = 0.229, 0.126, 0.095, 0.061, respectively). pH, redox potential, and temperature interactions with pressure events constituted the majority of the remaining features. Results were robust to exclusion of finished water arsenic concentration and missing data imputation strategy. Findings indicate that complex water quality and pressure interactions mobilize arsenic within the distribution network, yielding important implications for system management.

title: Agroecological and biological crop-protection practices for climate adaptation and food security in Nigeria: context dependence, trade-offs and evidence gaps
abstract: Nigeria requires crop-production strategies that address climatic stress, soil degradation, pest pressure and food insecurity. This review evaluated agroecological and biological crop-protection practices as pathways to climate resilience and food security in Nigeria. A PRISMA-guided systematic evidence review and narrative synthesis were conducted using Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, CAB Abstracts, Google Scholar and African Journals Online. Ninety substantive evidence sources were included, comprising Nigerian primary studies and contextual regional and international evidence. Nigerian primary evidence included field experiments, observational studies, household surveys and economic evaluations, while reviews, meta-analyses and mechanistic studies were used for contextual interpretation. Intercropping and crop-density management affected component-crop yields, soil moisture and resource capture; higher cassava density increased storage-root yield by 16%, whereas higher maize density increased maize yield by 11% but reduced second-cycle cassava yield by 7%. Maize–legume systems improved soil carbon, nitrogen and aggregation. Combined phosphorus and rhizobial inoculation increased soybean yield by 777 kg ha −1 , although the highest-yielding combinations were not always the most profitable. Atoxigenic Aspergillus flavus reduced aflatoxin by 82%–95% at harvest and 80%–100% after storage. Botanical pesticides reduced pest survival and crop damage, but yield responses were inconsistent. Observational evidence associated conservation and climate-smart practices with higher productivity, efficiency and income, whereas household food-security outcomes were less consistent. Most evidence concerned adaptive-capacity indicators rather than performance or recovery under defined climatic shocks. Scaling requires locally tested practices, reliable biological products, extension, finance, regulatory oversight and longer-term evaluation of climatic, ecological, economic and nutritional outcomes.

Experimental evaluation of planar heat pipes with active cooling integration for photovoltaic thermal hot-spot mitigation.
abstract: Photovoltaic module efficiency declines at high operating temperature, while localized hot spots accelerate degradation, and may reduce module lifetime. This study develops and experimentally evaluates planar heat pipes intended for rear surface heat spreading and for feeding a compact active water-cooled sink. Five full-scale prototypes with different internal configurations were fabricated from stainless steel and tested in a fully automated test rig under non-uniform heating conditions. Experiments were conducted at heating-pad setpoints between 50 and 100 °C, inclination angles of 30° to 45°, and under both natural-convection and localized active water-cooling conditions. Under natural convection, the transferred heat was comparable to that of the reference case without planar heat pipes, indicating limited benefit in bulk heat removal. When coupled to the water-cooled sink, heat removal increased by approximately 15-25 percent relative to the non-cooled baseline. The principal benefit of the planar heat pipes was temperature homogenization, which reduced peak surface temperatures by approximately 8 to 32 °C, depending on the prototype configuration and operating conditions, while markedly suppressing thermal hot spots. To illustrate the potential impact on photovoltaic performance, the experimentally observed temperature reductions were evaluated using a simplified temperature-dependent PV model and representative meteorological data for Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. The assessment indicated potential improvements in annual electricity production under the investigated assumptions. The results demonstrate that planar heat pipes are effective thermal spreaders for photovoltaic applications, particularly for reducing temperature gradients and mitigating hot-spot formation.

title: Nanostructured Colored Radiative Cooling for Energy-Efficient Buildings and Thermal Management Applications
How increasing green hydrogen blending affects techno-economic and environmental performance of renewable energy communities across Italian climates
abstract: Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) can support the decarbonization of local energy systems by promoting renewable generation and sector coupling. This study evaluates the effect of increasing the hydrogen blending ratio from 10% to 20% by volume within an already hydrogen-integrated REC framework. Twelve scenarios are analysed across three Italian climatic zones-Reggio Calabria, Rome, and Turin-considering Combined Heat and Power (CHP) and Gas Absorption Heat Pump (GAHP) configurations coupled with photovoltaic generation, hydrogen production and storage, and hydrogen-natural gas blending. Results show that the response to higher hydrogen blending strongly depends on climate, thermal demand, and system architecture. Moving from 10% to 20% H 2 generally improves renewable-energy utilization and economic and environmental performance within the hydrogen-integrated configurations. The lowest Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE), 148.5 €/MWh, is obtained for the GAHP configuration in Reggio Calabria at 20% H 2 , with a Carbon Avoidance Cost (CAC) of 892.8 €/tCO 2 . CHP systems benefit more from high and sustained thermal demand, resulting in stronger thermal-electric coupling in colder climates. A trade-off also emerges: increasing the H 2 blending ratio can reduce the Self-Consumption Ratio (SCR) and Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR), because the additional PV generation required to support electrolysis also increases grid exports, while LCOE, CAC, and renewable-energy utilization improve. Comparisons with the conventional reference case are used to assess the overall PV-hydrogen-CHP/GAHP architecture and are not attributed to hydrogen blending alone. Sensitivity analysis shows that electricity and natural-gas prices and district-heating infrastructure costs dominate economic performance, whereas ±50% variations in hydrogen-component CAPEX have comparatively limited effects.

title: Sonochemical engineering of Ag-Ni loaded ZnIn2S4 nanocomposites for enhanced solar-driven hydrogen evolution
abstract: The development of efficient photocatalytic routes for hydrogen production is of growing interest for sustainable energy conversion and the storage of renewable energy in the form of a chemical energy carrier. In this work, ZnIn 2 S 4 -based photocatalysts were engineered through the loading of commercial Ni nanoparticles (NPs) and the in-situ formation of Ag NPs via a sonochemical process, leading to enhanced photocatalytic performance. Among the synthesized photocatalysts, ZIS/AgNi-10 (10 min of sonication) exhibited the highest hydrogen evolution activity, reaching a value of 1.65 ± 0.04 mmol g -1 h -1 and apparent quantum efficiency (AQE) of 9.4 % at 420 nm. This improvement is attributed to the synergistic effect of Ni and Ag loading, where Ni provides active catalytic sites, while Ag NPs promote plasmon resonance and facilitate charge separation. These effects result in improved charge carrier dynamics and enhanced light absorption, as supported by optical and electrochemical analyses. Although a reduction in specific surface area is observed after sonication, this limitation is offset by the improved electronic and optical properties. Structural and compositional characterization further confirmed the effective integration of both components, inducing modulation of the electronic structure, including bandgap tuning and a shift in the valence band position. Overall, this work presents a simple, green and scalable strategy to optimize ZIS-based photocatalysts toward sustainable hydrogen generation and photon-to-chemical conversion, with relevance to renewable hydrogen technologies.

An integrated framework for evaluating tidal stream generation potential and its power system benefits: evidence from Great Britain
abstract: This paper presents an integrated framework that combines geospatial analysis with power system modelling to evaluate the optimal deployment and system-level value of tidal stream generation in Great Britain (GB). High-resolution geospatial screening – based on tidal maximum current velocity (≥ 2.5 m/s), mean tidal speeds (≥ 1.5 m/s) water depth (35–45 m and 30–50 m), and distance to shore (≤ 50 km) – is coupled with a multi-objective NSGA-II optimisation to identify Pareto-optimal sites for tidal stream development. The results indicate that promising locations are concentrated in a limited number of high-resource coastal regions, notably around the Orkney Islands and Pentland Firth, the Anglesey and North Wales coastline, and the Bristol Channel. These sites are subsequently incorporated into a 17-zone representation of the 2030 GB electricity system using the PyPSA model. Simulation results show that deploying 1.5 GW of tidal stream capacity – on an energy-equivalent basis in place of wind and solar PV – reduces variable renewable curtailment by 0.6 TWh, displaces a comparable volume of gas-fired generation, and lowers total system operating costs by £65 million per year. Furthermore, analysis of electricity market impacts indicates reductions in average generation costs of up to £1.0/MWh in high-cost zones, alongside relatively stable technology-specific market capture prices for tidal stream generation compared to wind and solar. The proposed framework is modular and scalable, making it applicable to other coastal regions and power systems using location-specific datasets and scenarios.
