Plant Oxidative Stress Mediates the Synergistic Transformation of Benzotriazole Ultraviolet Stabilizers in Rhizosphere Soil: Insights from Dual Exposure Pathways
abstract: Abstract Benzotriazole ultraviolet stabilizers (BUVs) are widespread emerging contaminants in soil. However, their transformation in the rhizosphere and the regulatory effects of plant oxidative stress on rhizosphere remediation remain unclear. The objective of this study was to investigate these effects using molecular simulations and rhizosphere and foliar exposure experiments. The removal efficiency of the four BUVs was 15–46% higher in the rhizosphere of Helianthus annuus than under natural soil degradation. The plant rhizosphere promoted BUV desorption from soil and induced hydroxylation as a specific transformation pathway. Direct rhizosphere exposure triggered oxidative stress and accelerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in soil. Rhizosphere ROS contributed approximately 31.2%–42.7% to BUV transformation. Foliar exposure experiments suggested that plant oxidative stress is an important contributor to rhizosphere ROS generation. Under BUV stress, plant oxidative stress regulated the composition of dissolved organic matter (DOM) and the selective enrichment of bacteria, including Acidobacteriota, Actinomycota, and Bacteroidota. Multivariate correlation network analysis suggested that foliar exposure resulted in more complex interactions among rhizosphere microenvironmental characteristics than did direct rhizosphere exposure. This study provides insights into BUV transformation in the rhizosphere and establishes a framework for plant signal-guided rhizosphere remediation strategies.

title: Exploring the Influence of Chemical Exposures on Breast Cancer Disparities: High-Throughput Transcriptomic Analysis of Normal Breast Cells from Diverse Donors
abstract: Abstract Racial disparities in the incidence of, and mortality from, aggressive breast cancers are a pressing public health issue. Many factors have been investigated in these inequities; however, the role of toxicant exposures is not well characterized. We and others have identified substantial inequities in chemical biomarker concentrations by race. The goal of this study was to test the hypothesis that exposure to these chemicals is linked to biological changes relevant to aggressive breast cancers, such as dysregulation of the Hallmarks of Cancer. We used high-throughput transcriptomic profiling of normal primary human breast epithelial cells from diverse donors (n = 6) to test the effects of 8 chemicals (cadmium, lead, arsenic, copper, PFNA, BPA, BPS, and p,p’-DDE) with documented exposure disparities by race/ethnicity across 3 concentrations (100 nM, 1 μM, and 10 μM). Across chemicals, we identified that pathways related to cell cycle regulation and protein secretion were commonly affected. Through bioinformatic estimation of cell-type proportions, we found that metals like lead and cadmium induced cell-type shifts, consistent with the dysregulated cellular plasticity cancer hallmark. Lead- and arsenic-response genes were enriched for genes associated with poor breast cancer survival in the Cancer Genome Atlas. Integrating concentration–response modeling and chemical biomonitoring data, BPA, p,p’-DDE, copper, and lead elicited expression changes at concentrations relevant to the US population. Finally, we identified substantial interindividual heterogeneity in response to chemical classes, with heavy metals producing the largest dose-responsive transcriptional effects. These findings highlight the value of high-throughput transcriptomics as a new approach methodology (NAM) in quantifying how common exposures may impact aggressive breast cancer-associated biological processes.

title: From Molecular Topography to Ozone Pollution: Species Sources and Photochemical Kinetics of Individual Organic Peroxyl Radicals
abstract: Abstract Ground-level ozone (O3) poses significant threats to global public health and climate change. Organic peroxyl radicals (RO2) serve as crucial intermediates in atmospheric O3 formation. Although individual RO2 species exhibit distinct reactivities, the quantification and source attribution of individual RO2 species remain poorly understood. Here, we address the challenge by integrating high-resolution field observations with fundamental theoretical kinetics within a novel hybrid receptor-kinetic modeling framework. The concentration and composition of RO2 species exhibit significant seasonal and diurnal dependencies. In summer, the 19 RO2 pool was characterized by a substantial contribution from biogenic sources (29%), particularly isoprene-derived species (ISOPOBO2). Conversely, the wintertime RO2 composition shifts, dramatically dominated by industrial emissions (41%), notably ethylene-derived species (HOCH2CH2O2). Source apportionment via the RO2+NO pathway further demonstrates that O3 photochemical formation potentials align closely with the kinetics of RO2 production. A data-driven machine learning model effectively captures the contribution of individual RO2 species to O3 formation in summer, but it shows significant deviations from kinetic simulations in winter. The framework establishes a dynamic framework to support daytime O3 mitigation by quantifying the high-time-resolution RO2 radical pool from field VOCs measurements.

title: Relative Humidity Modulates Nitration and Ring Fragmentation during Heterogeneous Oxidation of Catechol by Nitrate Radicals
abstract: Abstract Catechol is an important biomass-burning-derived phenolic compound and a precursor to secondary organic aerosols (SOAs). Although nitrate radicals (NO3) are recognized as major nighttime oxidants, the influence of the aerosol water content on heterogeneous NO3 oxidation of phenolic compounds remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the impact of relative humidity (RH = 0–90%) on the heterogeneous oxidation of catechol thin films by nitrate radicals generated from the reaction of O3 and NO2. Product formation was characterized using Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, UV–visible spectroscopy, electrospray ionization mass spectrometry (ESI-MS), ultrahigh-pressure liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC–MS), and ion chromatography–mass spectrometry (IC–MS). Under dry conditions, oxidation favored nitration and oligomerization pathways, producing mono-, di-, and trinitrocatechols together with catechol dimers and trimers. These products exhibited enhanced absorption in the 300–500 nm region, characteristic of brown carbon chromophores. Increasing RH progressively suppressed the relative nitration capacity of the NO3/N2O5 system while promoting oxidative ring-opening reactions, leading to the formation of dicarboxylic acids, including cis,cis-muconic acid, 2,3-dihydroxymaleic acid, and oxalic acid. Product distributions revealed a transition from functionalization-dominated chemistry at low RH to fragmentation-dominated chemistry at high RH. These results indicate that RH strongly controls nighttime nitrate radical oxidation of biomass-burning phenolics by shifting product formation from light-absorbing nitroaromatic brown carbon toward highly oxygenated fragmentation products. The findings provide new mechanistic insights into the role of aerosol water in governing the chemical aging and optical evolution of biomass-burning aerosols.

title: Electrification, Lightweighting, and Materials Supply: A Dynamic Life Cycle Assessment of the U.S. Light-Duty Vehicle Fleet
abstract: Abstract Electrification and lightweighting are reshaping vehicle designs and materials demand, with uncertain net effects on life cycle greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. Most existing fleet studies treat material choices, materials markets, and vehicle adoption separately, without capturing feedbacks between design, supply chains, and consumer behavior. This study develops an integrated system dynamics–life cycle assessment (SD–LCA) framework to explore these interactions for the U.S. light-duty vehicle fleet from 2000 to 2060. The model extends an established powertrain diffusion framework by endogenizing vehicle body material selection, battery capacity evolution, and materials market responses, linking these dynamics to a bottom-up life cycle assessment of fleet GHG emissions. Scenario analysis shows that increasing aluminum use in lightweight gasoline vehicles improves their utility and market share, largely offsetting use-phase GHG savings and yielding only modest reductions in total fleet emissions. In contrast, faster battery electric vehicle adoption raises cradle-to-gate emissions but more than compensates through lower use-phase emissions, reducing total fleet GHGs. Shifts in vehicle material demand also generate transient imbalances in steel and aluminum markets, temporarily lowering recycled fraction and increasing cradle-to-gate emissions. The SD–LCA framework demonstrates how feedbacks between vehicle design, materials supply, and consumer adoption shape fleet decarbonization pathways.

Synchrotron micro-XRF and micro-XANES characterisation of metal entrapment in anthropogenic tufa
abstract: Anthropogenic tufa deposits forming in hyperalkaline environments near legacy industrial waste sites can act as passive sinks for toxic metals offering potential for nature-based remediation. To unravel the distribution and mechanisms of metal incorporation in tufa we investigated two tufa samples from a stretch of slag-contaminated stream near Consett (N.E. England) using synchrotron-micro-X-ray fluorescence (μ-SXRF) and micro-X-ray absorption near edge structure (μ-XANES). Analyses revealed that metal content were significantly higher in the upstream sample compared to the downstream sample for As, Fe, Mn, Pb and Zn. Element maps revealed metals distributed heterogeneously as diffuse enrichments, linear features and discrete concentrations between calcite growths. Prominent bands of Cu, Fe, Mn, Ti and Zn were also observed between laminates. Statistical analysis of whole images and transects along the direction of tufa growth in the upstream sample gave notable correlations ( p < 0.005) between: Mn and Zn ( R = 0.66); Fe and Zn ( R = 0.64); Fe and Mn ( R = 0.55); and Cu and Fe ( R = 0.61). Linear combination fitting (LCF) of μ-XANES spectra indicated that Pb micro-sized particles might contain phases of galena (PbS), Pb(II)oxides, cerussite (PbCO₃) and/or crocoite (CrPbO 4 ), while sorbed phases of Pb were not favoured in the LCF fit. These LCF results raise questions about transport and transformation of Pb from the weathered slag and the stability of Pb trapped within tufa. The highly alkaline stream conditions (pH 10.3–11.3) favour metal co-precipitation with CaCO 3 whilst incorporating atmospheric carbon. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of tufa as a natural attenuation material for trapping metals in contaminated post-industrial landscapes. Further study is required to help understand how these tufa metal capturing processes could be harnessed.

title: Post-Paris agreement GHG emissions of 208 countries and territories: A 54-year descriptive trajectory classification relevant to SDG 13.2.2 monitoring (1970–2024)
Human rights impact assessment in Sápmi: a methodological framework
abstract: Emerging due diligence laws aim to ensure responsible resource extraction but leave companies with considerable discretion. In this paper, we explore the role of human rights impact assessment (HRIA) as an arena for clarifying corporate accountabilities, and provide a novel framework based on a synthesis of research, international law, and good practice standards. We focus on the example of Indigenous Sámi reindeer herding in Sweden: this is a high-risk context for human rights violations, and the mining industry has a growing interest in the large mineral resources located on traditional Sámi lands. The criteria-based framework defines six preconditions that must be protected to ensure that herding communities can enjoy their collective rights to land and culture, notably the cultural practice of natural grazing-based herding and its seasonal migration. As a case study we examine state-owned mining company LKAB’s proposed Per Geijer project – notably, the project’s application for a concession permit on the traditional lands of Gabna reindeer herding community. The study is based on collaborative research with members of the community, guided by principles from participatory action research and Indigenous methodologies. The analysis demonstrates how LKAB’s project entails a significant risk of violating the Indigenous rights of the members of Gabna. In so doing, we provide one of the few evaluations of the human rights risks of mining on Sámi lands in Sweden. Finally, because of the challenges of using HRIA tools to build cross-cultural understanding, we consider how innovative methods could help us develop rights-based approaches with Indigenous communities.

A systematic methodology for PTO sizing and hydrodynamic optimization of OWC systems in high-energy Atlantic environments
abstract: This study presents a systematic methodology for the hydrodynamic optimization and power take-off sizing of an L-shaped oscillating water column wave energy converter for high-energy Atlantic environments. While standard oscillating water column designs, such as the Mutriku wave power plant (18.5 kW per unit), serve as a global benchmark, this research demonstrates that such configurations lead to significant energy underutilization in more energetic sea states. The proposed methodology combines multi-criteria site assessment, hydrodynamic resonance tuning, and time-domain numerical simulations. It is validated through a case study on Tenerife (Canary Islands, Spain), where an optimal chamber geometry was identified, matching the dominant wave period (T p = 12.5 s). A key contribution of this work is the optimization of the power take-off capacity. Sensitivity analysis revealed that increasing the rated power to 60 kW effectively mitigates clipping losses, increasing the annual energy production by 105.66% to 138.48 MWh/year compared with the 18.5 kW reference. Furthermore, the capture width ratio improved from 12.16% to 22.51%, highlighting the importance of hydrodynamic–pneumatic impedance matching. Comparative results show that the Tenerife site is 60.61% more energetic than the Mutriku wave power plant, achieving 2308 full-load hours and a capacity factor of 26.45%. These findings provide a transferable engineering methodology for designing resource-optimized oscillating water column systems in high-energy coastal environments. • Systematic four-stage framework for OWC design and PTO optimization. • Hydrodynamic resonance maximized through chamber geometry tuning. • PTO sizing mitigates clipping losses in energetic wave environments. • Optimized PTO increases annual energy production. • Framework transferable to high-energy breakwater-integrated OWC systems.

Provincial pathways for decarbonizing China's steel sector through electricity and hydrogen substitution
abstract: ABSTRACT The deep decarbonization of China’s steel sector is critical for achieving national carbon neutrality and global climate goals. Existing studies on China’s steel transition often lack detailed representations of provincial heterogeneity, cross-sectoral interactions, and breakthrough technologies. This study develops an improved steel module within the Global Change Analysis Model-China (GCAM-China) to explore provincial low-carbon transition pathways for China’s steel sector. The model incorporates calibrated steel demand, multiple breakthrough technologies, and province-specific resource endowments and technology costs, enabling a more realistic representation of provincial transition dynamics and explicit interactions among the steel, power, and hydrogen systems. The results show that China’s steel sector is projected to undergo a structural transition toward electric arc furnace (EAF)-based and hydrogen-based steelmaking pathways. Electricity and hydrogen play critical roles in enabling deep decarbonization through the transformation of upstream energy systems. The combined share of EAF-based and hydrogen-based steelmaking exceeds 80% by 2060, replacing coal-intensive routes and reducing CO 2 emissions by more than 90% relative to 2020 levels, with residual emissions of 60–126 MtCO 2 under carbon neutrality scenarios. Provincial transitions show significant heterogeneity, with southern provinces favoring Scrap-EAF deployment, northern provinces favoring natural gas-based direct reduced iron-EAF (NG-DRI-EAF) deployment, southwestern provinces benefiting from electricity–hydrogen synergies, and eastern, southern, and southwestern provinces showing higher potential for molten oxide electrolysis (MOE) deployment. By integrating national transition dynamics with provincial characteristics, this study provides insights for differentiated policy design and supports more targeted deployment of technologies and infrastructure across regions.

An innovative high-temperature subcritical pumped thermal energy storage system using biphenyl-biphenyl oxide mixture
abstract: Recently, high-temperature pumped thermal energy storage (PTES) operating at 400-600 °C has garnered widespread attention, with several projects successfully launched due to its high energy storage density and ability to provide electricity or high-quality steam. Nevertheless, a range of limitations exists, including substantial work input for gas compression, high capital expenditure and operational pressures, huge equipment and irreversible losses. To alleviate these challenges, this study introduces a novel high-temperature subcritical PTES system based on a biphenyl-diphenyl oxide (BDO) mixture. The dual-tank configuration utilizing BDO enables an extreme heat-storage temperature of 395 °C, while the maximum system operating pressure is only approximately 1 MPa. The BDO also serves as the working fluid for both the heat-pump charging cycle and the power-generation discharging cycle of the PTES. This unified-working-fluid design greatly reduces heat transfer losses. The results reveal that a higher inlet temperature of waste heat flue gas improves the system performance. Conversely, an increase in flue gas mass flow rate reduces both the coefficient of performance (COP) and round-trip efficiency ( ). The maximum reaches 641.62%, with a corresponding COP of 22.71. For a 6-hour heat discharge duration, the levelized cost of storage is 0.369 $/kWh and energy storage density is 27.735 kWh/m 3 .

Research on the nonlinear mechanism of environmental regulations on China's industrial green total factor productivity: Evidence from a dynamic panel threshold model
abstract: Environmental regulations (ERs) are effective in balancing industrial economic benefits with ecological protection. The study aimed to explore how ERs combine with R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure to promote industrial green total factor productivity (GTFP) growth in China's industrial sector. Utilizing input-output data from the industrial sector covering 30 provinces and obtained between 2003 and 2021, the Meta-frontier Malmquist-Luenberger (MML) index is employed to measure GTFP. Then, a dynamic panel threshold model is constructed to empirically examine the nonlinear dynamic effect of different types of ERs on GTFP from the perspectives of R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure, with the objective being to reveal the economic conditions under which ERs generate a “strong” Porter effect. The results indicate that: (1) GTFP is significantly enhanced during the observation period, yet it displays pronounced spatial disparities. Technological progress is the main source of GTFP growth. (2) The results of the benchmark model indicate a significant U-shaped relationship between ERs and GTFP. The stimulation effects driven by market-incentive environmental regulation (MIER) and public participation environmental regulation (PPER) are far stronger than those motivated by command-and-control environmental regulation (CCER) and performance-based environmental regulation (PBER). (3) The dynamic relationship between ERs and GTFP depends on R&D expenditure, human capital, industrial structure, and ownership structure. Speciﬁcally, ERs exert a stronger positive effect on GTFP in the region with lower degrees of nationalization and higher levels of R&D expenditure, human capital, and industrialization. MIER has the greatest positive effect. However, in the region with a higher degree of nationalization and lower levels of R&D expenditure, human capital, and industrialization, ERs exert a weaker positive effect or even a significant negative effect on GTFP.

Visible-light-driven removal of bisphenol A using a Bi12SiO20/Bi2O3 S-scheme heterojunction: Performance and charge-transfer mechanism
abstract: Efficient removal of the emerging organic contaminant bisphenol A (BPA) remains an important challenge for sustainable water treatment. Herein, a series of BSO-Bi 2 O 3 heterojunction composites were synthesized via a facile in situ precipitation strategy to enhance visible-light photocatalytic degradation of BPA. Structural characterizations confirmed intimate interfacial contact between two components, facilitating strong electronic coupling across the BSO-Bi 2 O 3 interface. Among all as-prepared samples, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 exhibited the highest photocatalytic performance, achieving nearly 90% BPA removal within 80 min, significantly outperforming pristine Bi 2 O 3 and Bi 12 SiO 20 . The enhanced photocatalytic performance was mainly attributed to extended visible-light absorption, accelerated charge separation, and efficient interfacial charge transfer. Trapping experiments and ESR analyses revealed that superoxide radicals (·O 2 − ) and holes (h + ) were the dominant reactive species involved in the degradation process. Electrochemical measurements combined with density-functional theory (DFT) calculations further revealed favorable interfacial charge redistribution and enhanced charge-transfer kinetics, supporting an S-scheme charge-transfer pathway that preserves charge carriers with strong redox capabilities. Moreover, the composite BSO-5%Bi 2 O 3 maintained excellent recycling stability and structural integrity after repeated use. This work provides an effective strategy for constructing efficient bismuth-based S-scheme photocatalysts for the photocatalytic removal of emerging organic contaminants.

Seaweed-based blue carbon potential of eco-engineered coastal structures
abstract: Natural coastal ecosystems hold substantial capacity for blue carbon storage, but habitat replacement with harbour and shoreline infrastructure has severely diminished their potential to mitigate climate change. Enhancement of topographic complexity on coastal infrastructure through eco-engineering can increase biota abundance, such as the standing stock of long-lived seaweeds, thus positively impacting carbon capture and mitigating the carbon footprint of concrete-based infrastructure. However, ecosystem services of eco-engineered structures remain largely unquantified. Here, we assessed the seaweed biomass on a large-scale, eco-engineered seawall and show that topographically complex panels supported up to 19-fold greater blue carbon storage than flat surfaces. However, estimated panel CO 2 emissions exceeded CO 2 captures by 3- to 64-fold, after two years of seaweed growth. No retrofitted panel was realistically expected to achieve carbon neutrality within its 20-year design life, despite seaweed turnover and sequestration supporting long-term blue carbon potential. Predictive calculations, using six topographic designs, four concrete mixtures, two installation scenarios, and two detritus sequestration rates, suggested that the most efficient topography for seaweed growth, produced from low-carbon concrete and integrated during the construction phase, may achieve carbon neutrality within 15-32 years. Less effective or less sustainable scenarios were expected to require 52-277 years until carbon neutrality. An active transition towards low-carbon, integrated designs is necessary to align biodiversity-focused thinking in green infrastructure design with broader principles of sustainability and climate change mitigation.

title: Key account managers' relational identity and identification forms: When interpersonal meets intergroup within intra- and interorganizational contexts
abstract: Key account management (KAM) is a strategic priority for many business-to-business (B2B) organizations. In KAM, key account managers play a central role, as they serve as the liaison between the supplier company and one or more key account customers. Existing research highlights the importance of identity (i.e., who a key account manager is) and identification (i.e., with whom a key account manager identifies) in understanding key account relationships. This research builds on the concepts of relational identity and identification, both of which define the self through relationships with others rather than solely through individual distinctiveness or group membership. These concepts are particularly relevant for key account managers and their role in nurturing B2B relationships. Specifically, this research examines how key account managers' relational identity and identification (i.e., interpersonal or intergroup), within both intra- and interorganizational contexts, influence the nature of the relationships they develop with their customers. It then formulates four research propositions on how specific forms of relational identity and identification of key account managers can lead to the development of either a strategic or relational partnership. This research has broad implications for collaborative B2B relationships.

Inclusion of low-income consumers in global consumption dynamics: a socioeconomic framework for sustainable international marketing
abstract: Purpose Despite the growing interest in sustainable marketing over recent decades, research in this area remains limited relative to the needs and scope of the field, in supporting low-income consumers situated at the bottom of the pyramid across international markets. There is an inadequate knowledge of how marketers can precisely reflect on international low-income consumers' needs, to adapt market offerings to serve them profitably. Addressing this lack of research, we aim to develop a novel socioeconomic framework of sustainable international marketing to help marketers enhance low-income consumers' inclusion in global consumption dynamics. Design/methodology/approach Following the realist approach, a systematic literature review (1975–2025)was conducted, using Web of Science, on low-income consumers; equity, diversity and inclusion; and sustainable marketing, published in generalized and international marketing and business journals, to determine the implications of the reviewed literature for international marketing and low-income consumers. Findings The literature review suggests that both sustainability concerns and low-income consumers bring opportunities for international marketing. Findings present eight key socioeconomic constructs and fifty-two underlying factors to design a sustainable international marketing framework (Figure 1), reflecting on the values important to low-income consumers in cross-border markets. We have coined a novel matrix (Figure 2) to help international marketers implement our framework. Practical implications Considering the socioeconomic constructs of our framework are supported by extant empirical literature, the framework helps design sustainable international marketing strategies, which consider the needs of low-income consumers and their socioeconomic settings, whilst offering positive business outcomes. Social implications Our framework and matrix help to inform sustainable marketing strategies, which enable marketers to enhance low-income consumers' inclusion in global consumption dynamics, whilst generating profit responsibly in international markets. Originality/value Given the importance of low-income consumers across international markets and the scarcity of effective frameworks in extant research, we present an initial framework and matrix to pragmatically design sustainable international marketing strategies.

title: Actions Speak Louder Than Words: Behavioral Versus Textual Credibility Signals in Tourism Review Platforms
abstract: Online reviews are central to traveler decision-making, yet their credibility is increasingly challenged by manipulated and strategically generated content. This study compares textual signals, or what reviewers say, with behavioral signals, or how reviewers act over time and across businesses. Drawing on more than five million Yelp reviews, the findings show that behavioral patterns, especially temporal activity and reviewer-business structure, provide more reliable indicators of manipulation likelihood than textual features alone. A late-fusion model combining behavioral and textual evidence offers the strongest overall assessment, while category-level results show that manipulation risk is unevenly distributed across tourism contexts. The study advances tourism research by framing review credibility as a multi-signal assessment problem and by highlighting behavioral consistency as a foundation of trust. Practically, platforms should prioritize behavioral monitoring, review-velocity tracking, and reviewer-business pattern analysis while using text-based detection as a complementary governance layer.

title: A Perspective on the Development of Novel In Situ Remediation of Contaminated Sediments Using Black Carbon
abstract: Abstract The field of contaminated sediment remediation was disrupted two decades ago by the emergence of a new way to reduce risk in situ through the amendment of black carbon sorbents─activated carbon and specialized biochars. This required a paradigm shift from a focus on reducing pollutant mass to reducing exposure through bioavailability control. Sorbent amendment technology has advanced from laboratory and pilot field demonstrations to full-scale applications at many sites and has recently been incorporated in USEPA records of decision at Superfund sites. This perspective summarizes critical points in advancing the new technology: 1) accurate problem definition recognizing that sediment pollutant mass reduction does not necessarily lead to risk reduction, 2) breakthroughs in bioavailability science and unraveling the role of native black carbon in sediments, 3) demonstration of pollutant bioavailability reduction with strong sorption, 4) quantitative descriptions of the process, 5) addressing the challenges of mercury, 6) understanding unintended consequences, and 7) development of freely dissolved concentrations as a key bioavailability metric with regulatory and stakeholder engagement. The lessons learned in this journey from early science through technological maturity can help inform other technologies that are in development to address evolving threats to the environment.

title: Environmentally Persistent Free Radicals on Aged Polyamide Microplastics Drive Neurotoxicity in Eisenia fetida via a Glutamate-Centered Cascade
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing microplastics (N-MPs) are widespread in soil and often exhibit distinct environmental behaviors and effects owing to their unique elemental composition and molecular structure. However, their toxicity to soil organisms remains poorly understood. To address this knowledge gap, the toxicity of pristine and aged polyamides (PA) was evaluated in earthworms (Eisenia fetida), a representative soil invertebrate. At 0.01% (w/w), aged PA increased the magnitude of body-weight loss, MDA levels, and AChE activity by 24.4%, 11.6%, and 24.1%, respectively, relative to pristine PA-MPs. Greater accumulation of aged PA-MPs was accompanied by enhanced oxidative damage and neurotoxicity. Integrated multiomics, quantitative real-time PCR, and biomarker analyses revealed that oxidative stress-mediated membrane damage promoted glutamate accumulation, receptor overactivation, Ca2+ overload, synaptic injury, and ultimately neurotoxicity. Pharmacological interventions and transmission electron microscopy of the ventral nerve cord provided functional and morphological support for this cascade. Radical quenching and comparative leachate bioassays further supported the important contribution of environmentally persistent free radicals in aged PA-MPs to neuronal damage. These findings define a mechanistic pathway for aged microplastic-induced neurotoxicity and provide a basis for assessing the ecological risks of aged N-MPs in soils.

Synthesizing Information-Driven Insider Trade Signals
abstract: Abstract We propose a novel approach to synthesize presumably information-driven insider trading signals for the cross section of stocks. We find that the resulting straightforward composite strategy can often forecast returns in a global sample. This predictability is strongest in equal-weighted portfolios, short holding periods, and insider-buying signals, and it improves further with global diversification. Cross-country analysis reveals that varying insider trading restrictions between countries have limited explanatory power for the performance of the composite strategy. Overall, the results are consistent with a short-term informational advantage of insiders, which might be due to the skillful interpretation of non-private news.

title: Craft and Industrialization: Uncovering the Plasticity and Frontier of Craft
abstract: Abstract Craft as an approach to work has been proposed as an alternative to industrial mass production. While industrialization has led to the replacement of craft logic with industrial logic to create uniformity and scale operations, the role of craft in industrialization remains ambiguous. Building on the analysis of engineering work performed at an R&D laboratory in the pulp and paper industry, we explore how and why craft enables industrialization. Our findings reveal how elements of craft manifest in engineering work by helping to transform ideas into useful objects, balancing scientific accuracy with practical usefulness, and fostering a sense of community and identity within the engineering field. These findings point to the plasticity of craft logic , suggesting that elements of craft can be transferred into new contexts and reinterpreted to address new objectives. Considering that these activities took place in an R&D laboratory that drove industrialization, they also reveal the existence of a craft frontier that escapes standardization by providing a context for crafting candidates for future standards. Craft frontier enables the coexistence of craft and industrial logics, where craft can contribute to industrialization by establishing foundations for managerial control without being absorbed into it.

title: Conceptual search: A generative view of entrepreneurial imagination
abstract: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs cannot pursue ventures they never imagine. This article develops a generative view of entrepreneurial imagination as the construction of an evolving candidate set through generation, provisional evaluation, and revision. Conceptual search represents venture concepts as text, transforms them through interpretable operations, and compares their promise. A large language model prototype demonstrates complementary modes: local refinement lifts a concept from sixteenth to third among 30 ventures under a validated evaluator, while global recombination reaches distant possibilities that refinement makes competitive. The framework shows how search architecture determines what enters, survives, and develops, and how AI may broaden imagination within firms while producing correlated imagination across firms. By making imagination programmable, auditable, and experimentally tractable, conceptual search opens a research program on how entrepreneurial possibilities are constructed. Managerial Summary Entrepreneurs can pursue only the ventures they imagine, and valuable ideas routinely go unbuilt because nobody thinks of them. AI makes imagining cheap: it can draft, critique, and rewrite venture concepts in seconds, so developing ideas becomes a process that can be designed, run, and audited. I demonstrate a system that evolves real venture concepts: step‐by‐step refinement lifted a middling concept to third place among 30 real ventures, as ranked by an AI judge shown to predict fundraising, while recombining distant ideas created novel concepts that refinement made competitive. The entrepreneur's job shifts from generating a few ideas to governing many: choosing what to search, keep, and test in the market. One caution: rivals using the same AI will imagine similar ventures; advantage comes from proprietary problems, data, and evidence.

title: Building Eco‐Innovation in SMEs Through Circular Economy Capability: Revisiting the Role of Green Transformational Leadership
abstract: ABSTRACT Resource‐constrained small and medium‐sized enterprises (SMEs) often struggle to translate sustainability ambitions into eco‐innovation because environmental initiatives must also support economic survival. Although green transformational leadership (GTL) is widely recognized as a driver of eco‐innovation, little is known about how it enables SMEs to develop the organizational capabilities needed to achieve both environmental and economic objectives. Drawing on the Resource‐Based View (RBV), this study examines whether circular economy capability (CEC) mediates the relationship between GTL and eco‐innovation and whether innovative climate (IC) strengthens this relationship. A repeated cross‐sectional design was employed among emerging‐economy SMEs (Study 1, n = 335; Study 2, n = 302), with each study adopting a three‐wave, multi‐source survey design with temporal separation between measurements. The hypotheses were tested using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS‐SEM). The findings show that GTL is positively associated with eco‐innovation primarily by developing CEC, with CEC partially mediating the leadership–innovation relationship across both study periods. Although IC has no direct effect on eco‐innovation, it significantly strengthens the positive influence of CEC on eco‐innovation. The replication of these relationships across the two study periods, alongside stronger capability‐related associations in Study 2, indicates the robustness of the proposed relationships across temporally separated samples. By extending the RBV, this study demonstrates that the strategic value of green leadership lies in developing capabilities that reconcile environmental sustainability with operational efficiency and firm competitiveness, offering important implications for SMEs pursuing sustainable innovation under resource constraints.

title: Under Pressure: Building Relational Water Stewardship Capability in Buyer‐Driven Agri‐Food Chains
abstract: ABSTRACT Buyers increasingly demand water stewardship, yet it is hard to operationalize because water risk is place‐based, collective and only partly auditable. We develop Relational Water Stewardship Capability (RWSC), the relational capacity through which buyers, exporters and intermediaries align incentives, produce credible evidence and test water‐saving practice while protecting yield and quality. Evidence comes from an abductive multiple‐case study of the Tunisian date sector: 32 interviews, 15 days of observation and 190 documents. Three mechanisms generate RWSC: reframing water as a threat to supply continuity, cofinanced field trials that yield locally credible evidence and boundary spanning to producer organizations and agronomists. Contrasting cases show RWSC fails where buyer power lacks recognition and investment and where shared objectives meet no capital at producer level. We specify three pathways from dyadic capability to collective resource and find the fiscal one binding. Over a fossil aquifer, the process slows depletion without reversing it.

title: Bankability as a Mechanism for Sustainability Implementation in Public–Private Partnerships
abstract: ABSTRACT Infrastructure public–private partnerships (PPPs) may formally incorporate sustainability commitments while lacking the financial capacity required to support their implementation over long concession horizons. This paper examines project‐level financial architecture as a structural condition shaping that capacity. Using an analytical single‐case study of a Mediterranean port redevelopment PPP, we combine project finance simulation with sensitivity and scenario analyses. The findings analytically illustrate how a project may be economically profitable yet remain below a minimum analytical financeability threshold, thereby creating financial pressure on non‐revenue‐generating sustainability components and increasing their exposure to potential deferral or renegotiation. Sensitivity analyses identify debt tenor and cost of debt as threshold parameters, while scenario analyses indicate that dependence on a dominant revenue stream may create incentives to prioritize commercial activities over non‐revenue‐generating commitments. The study contributes to sustainability strategy research by conceptualizing bankability as an enabling financial condition—rather than a guarantee—of sustainability delivery and by framing commercial drift as a potential structural risk associated with concentrated revenue architectures. The implications for public authorities, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) investors, and development finance institutions are framed as conditional implications requiring comparative and longitudinal testing.

title: Driving Greater SME Engagement With Stakeholder Support for Environmental Sustainability: The Role of Resources, Barriers and Dependency Activation Strategies
abstract: ABSTRACT External stakeholders are critical in enabling SMEs to achieve environmental sustainability. Yet, despite the growing availability of sustainability support, SME engagement remains limited. This article addresses significant gaps in the SME sustainability literature by mapping the support ecosystem and explaining why available sustainability resources are so underutilized. Drawing on resource dependence theory (RDT) and institutional theory (IT), we analyse 47 interviews and two focus groups with UK SMEs and support providers, revealing (i) latent and reverse dependencies, (ii) institutional and structural barriers and (iii) strategic inaction weakening engagement. Our findings advance RDT by shifting attention from dependency formation to the mechanisms that hinder it, offering a novel conceptual lens on how support relationships can be activated. This study combines academic rigour with practical relevance, providing actionable insights for policymakers and intermediaries seeking to strengthen SME–stakeholder interactions and accelerate sustainability adoption and carbon reduction efforts in line with the net‐zero agenda.

title: Strategic Sustainability Evaluation of Industrial Symbiosis Partners for the Textile Industry: A Robust Fuzzy Decision Analytics Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Technological advancements have transformed production processes, revealing the inadequacy of traditional resource management approaches. This necessitates redesigning industrial systems based on collaborative models. Industrial symbiosis (IS) aims to create a sustainable production ecosystem by generating economic and environmental value. However, decision‐making models addressing uncertainties in IS partner selection under advanced fuzzy approaches remain limited. This study supports IS implementation and sustainable resource management in the textile industry by identifying the most suitable symbiotic partner under uncertainty. The evaluation considers cement and ready‐mixed concrete, ceramics, packaging and recycling, agriculture and greenhouse cultivation, chemical and industrial chemicals, and construction sectors. The study proposes the fuzzy skewness impact through distributional evaluation (F‐SITDE) and fuzzy multiple normalization rating analysis (F‐MUNRA) model, an integrated fuzzy multicriteria decision‐making (MCDM) framework for uncertainty handling. F‐SITDE determines criterion weights, while F‐MUNRA evaluates alternatives. The results show the packaging and recycling sector performs best. Comparative analysis confirms robustness. The framework offers a systematic methodology for decision‐making and contributes to SDGs 9, 12, and 13.

title: Climate, Nature, and the Uneven Expansion of Financial Governance
abstract: ABSTRACT Financial authorities have developed extensive climate‐related policies, but nature‐related financial policy remains less widespread. Using data on individual policy instruments across 116 jurisdictions from 2000 to 2025, this paper compares the adoption, policy areas, binding status, and source of climate‐ and nature‐related policies. Nature‐related policies appear in 27 jurisdictions, compared with 60 for climate‐only policies. National nature adoption is positively associated with a larger existing body of climate and environmental financial policies, mainly through the broader environmental component rather than climate‐specific policy. Climate‐only policies are used more frequently in prudential supervision and credit allocation than policies that combine nature with climate or broader environmental concerns. Nature‐related policies have a higher mandatory share over the full period but a lower share than climate‐only policies in 2023–2025. In the European Union, broad EU‐level coverage coexists with limited national issuance. The paper contributes a common framework for comparing climate and nature policies and distinguishes EU‐level coverage from national policy development. The results show that the climate‐nature gap concerns not only adoption, but also where policies are used, how binding they are, and which level of authority issues them.

title: Translation in State Governance. By DongshengRen, LinJiao, and SanjunSun, Cambridge, UK: Cambridge University Press, 2026. 72 pp. US $68.33(hbk). ISBN: 978‐1‐00‐965981‐9; US $23.75 (ebk), ISBN: 2633‐6480
From Policy to Sustainability: The Evolution of Sustainability in Public HRM in Aotearoa/New Zealand in the SDG Era
abstract: This study examines how sustainable human resource management (SHRM) has been incorporated into public sector HRM policy in Aotearoa/New Zealand before and after the introduction of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Drawing on a longitudinal qualitative analysis of HRM policies from 10 local councils between 2010 and 2021, it explores how sustainability concerns across social, economic, and environmental domains were integrated into public HRM. The findings show that sustainability entered public HRM primarily through incremental layering onto existing HRM frameworks rather than transformational change. Following the SDGs, policy attention to equity, diversity, and wellbeing increased; however, broader social justice commitments remained uneven, while environmental sustainability received limited attention. By examining HRM policies as organizational signals, the study contributes to public HRM and SHRM scholarship by showing how sustainability priorities are communicated before implementation and may remain constrained by institutional logics of compliance, efficiency, risk management, and organizational performance.

title: Extended oxygenation control of endogenous contaminants induced by load fluctuations in bio-trickling filters treating decentralized sewage
Eroding Confidence in Gully Location Risk Prediction in Mine Pit Rehabilitation
abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding how rehabilitation measures, such as landform shaping, and surface finishes impact gully erosion risk could assist in designing less erosive rehabilitation. In this study we use high resolution digital elevation models of rehabilitated mine pits to explore risk factors for gully formation. We determine features that pre‐dispose rehabilitated mining pits to gully formation, how topographic features vary across these areas, and generate a binomial regression and a random forest model relating surface features to erosion risk. These models are benchmarked against the ‘topographic threshold’. We found topographic features, like hillslope gradient and curvature, which concentrate and accelerate runoff were overrepresented at gully heads, while at the mine pit level, erosion risk can be predicted by surface area and average pit hillslope gradient, providing a high‐level risk screening tool. The topographic threshold, applied with high resolution accumulation data, outperformed the random forest and logistic regression models in predicting risk from topographic features alone. Despite being based on post‐erosion data, the topographic threshold performs well to predict erosion risk across rehabilitated mining areas. The method balances data requirements with prediction accuracy and is a conservative approach to highlighting risk areas within rehabilitated pits. The random forest and regression approaches underpredicted gully locations, in contrast with the topographic thresholds over prediction, which limits their utility without additional inputs. Operators have opportunities to collect additional data during rehabilitation that could build better predictive models. Informed rehabilitation design offers the opportunity to avoid, where possible, features that occur more commonly in conjunction with erosion.

Price Gouging and the Monopoly Option
abstract: Abstract We investigate a dynamic oligopoly model with two phases: a normal phase where an essential input is available, and a disruption phase where firms must rely on inventories. Disruptions create an overcutting pricing incentive arising from the option to forgo sales and monopolize the market once rivals stock out. This monopoly option causes the price to jump to a supracompetitive level at the advent of the disruption and to remain above the competitive price path throughout. Price caps raise welfare, but reduce inventory investment. Government reserves reduce prices and raise buffer stocks, as do reserve mandates when financially feasible.

Failures of contingent reasoning in screening decisions
abstract: Abstract Screening decisions—choosing a costly action that reveals information about an unknown quality—can be crucial in various situations, such as hiring workers or designing policies. Choosing whether to screen can be difficult because it requires recognizing and trading off the benefits of information with the costs of getting it. We investigate whether people recognize when the benefits of screening dominate its costs and what causes them to choose otherwise. Our online experiment simulates a hiring scenario with an initial trial task. Participants can first reveal candidates’ quality at a small cost and then choose which candidate to hire. Most participants choose the dominated task that does not reveal the candidates’ quality, and this mistake persists even with experience and feedback. We show that this insufficient screening is driven by failures to anticipate inference and plan the full strategy.

title: Speaking With One Voice: Shareholder Collaboration on Activism
abstract: Abstract I study how an activist shareholder organizes a cost-sharing coalition with active shareholders while seeking support from passive shareholders outside the coalition. A larger coalition shifts more of the campaign cost to members, allowing the activist to pursue lower-value proposals. Observing a larger coalition therefore lowers passive shareholders’ posterior expectation of proposal value. The activist chooses the largest coalition that preserves support from pivotal passive shareholders, endogenizing coalition size. Consequently, coalition size need not be a monotone measure of activist influence, and activism frequency depends on passive shareholders’ preferences. Coalition building strengthens the proxy-fight threat and can increase prevote settlements. (JEL G34, G23, D83)

Pricing Geopolitical Risk: Closed-Form Valuation of Futures and Options on the GPR Index
abstract: On July 31, 2026, the European Central Bank (ECB) published the results of its thematic reverse stress test on geopolitical risk, in which 110 directly supervised banks identified scenarios severe enough to deplete CET1 capital by 300 bps. The exercise delivered narratives but not probabilities: without a market price of geopolitical risk, it has no quantitative anchor. This article closes that gap by applying the Grünbichler–Longstaff (1996) square-root, mean-reverting state-variable model directly to the Caldara–Iacoviello Geopolitical Risk (GPR) index, yielding closed-form prices for GPR futures and European options. Exact maximum-likelihood estimation on the monthly series from 1985 to June 2026 delivers a mean-reversion half-life of about two months toward a long-run mean of approximately 104, with the Feller condition satisfied with substantial slack, so the non-central chi-square pricing structure applies without modification. Applied to the ECB exercise, the framework converts the supervisory threshold into a tail-probability statement. Under the physical measure, the 12-month exceedance probability is approximately 12%—the answer a historical-simulation stress test would report. Under the risk-neutral measure it lies between 29% and 79% across the range of the market price of geopolitical risk motivated by analogy to inflation-swap risk premia—a bandwidth that is wide precisely because no traded GPR instrument yet identifies this parameter. Because the modeling techniques are deliberately standard, the article’s contribution is the practical layer: specification tests grounding the process choice in the data, confidence intervals around the physical anchor, a sensitivity analysis over the loss-channel mapping, and an explicit model-risk map organized for supervisory validation. The wedge between the physical probability and the risk-neutral band is the geopolitical risk premium, and a single observed transaction price on a cash-settled GPR contract—exchange-listed in the VSTOXX/VIX mold or OTC in the inflation-swap mold—would collapse the bandwidth to a point.

title: ESG, Mood and Expected Stock Returns
abstract: We examine how investor mood influences the pricing of ESG characteristics. We hypothesize that stocks with higher ESG ratings are less affected by investor mood because firms with stronger sustainability profiles provide more information, reducing mood-driven noise. We find strong support for this prediction: high-ESG stocks exhibit significantly lower mood sensitivity than low-ESG stocks. We also show that the negative relation between ESG ratings and future returns is conditional on mood sensitivity, appearing only among stocks whose returns respond strongly to mood fluctuations. Finally, we provide evidence supporting socially responsible institutional ownership (SRIO) as an important mechanism through which high-ESG stocks are less mood-sensitive, consistent with ESG-oriented institutions being less influenced by sentiment and playing a stabilizing role in ESG pricing. These findings highlight investor mood as a behavioral driver of ESG underperformance and underscore the importance of responsible institutional investors in mitigating sentiment-driven pricing distortions.
journal_name: Journal of Behavioral and Experimental Finance

title: “The Minimum Wage Is the Maximum Wage”: How Goal Replacement Perpetuates Means–Ends Decoupling
abstract: This research examines how organizations contribute to the perpetuation of means–ends decoupling (MED) within issue-based fields organized around societal problems, under conditions of heightened field scrutiny. In such settings, organizations often profess commitment to field goals and visibly comply with institutionally prescribed practices to satisfy monitoring, reporting, and public evaluation requirements. However, many adopted goals remain underachieved, raising questions about how compliance without progress endures and how claims of commitment remain credible under transparency regimes intended to spur substantive goal pursuit. Our data came from 75 interviews with 68 brands, suppliers, and third-party organizations pursuing worker well-being in global fashion supply chains. We unveil auditability-based goal replacement as an organizational-level mechanism through which actors rhetorically foreground compliance as public evidence of commitment while narrowing internal goal pursuit to auditable thresholds that serve their core goals, thereby allowing shortfalls to persist. Self-silencing about this substitution and the instrumentalizing of shortfalls close the configuration into a self-reinforcing loop. The study advances MED scholarship by (i) showing how organizations leverage field conditions and appropriate the existing scrutiny infrastructures to advance their core goals while reproducing the means–ends gap, (ii) problematizing the authenticity of commitment claims, and (iii) explaining how goal-ineffective compliance prevails as a credible substitute for adopted goals. It also extends research on organizational responses to institutional complexity and calls for greater attention to institutional impact—that is, the realized advancement of the societal aim an institution emerged to address.

title: Sustainability in marketing: A systematic analysis and future research agenda

title: Common ownership and consumer welfare
abstract: Abstract Rival firms with shared institutional investors (i.e., common owners) may compete less aggressively, potentially harming consumer welfare. Yet, research on common ownership has primarily focused on firm performance, often overlooking welfare outcomes or revealing contradictory results. This paper adopts a strategic network perspective to examine how common ownership affects firms’ service quality and pricing levels, which directly impact consumer welfare, and how customer and competitor factors that alter the focus of competitive strategy moderate these effects. To test the hypotheses, the authors analyze a rich, multi-market dataset of U.S. airline firms from 1995 to 2025. Findings reveal that competing firms with higher common ownership tend to have lower service quality and set higher prices. However, this effect is attenuated for firms with high customer-asset value and amplified among rivals competing across multiple markets. The findings demonstrate common ownership’s influence on firms’ marketing mix strategies and offer actionable insights for managers, policymakers, and investors.
journal_name: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science

title: The Equity Market Implications of the Retail Investment Boom
abstract: We quantify the equilibrium impact of retail traders on the U.S. equity market within a structural model of asset demand. Estimating investor-specific demand curves, we find that Robinhood traders are fundamentally distinct from all other investors, including other households: their demand is the most elastic and tilts most strongly toward volatile and microcap stocks. Each dollar invested through Robinhood generates more than five dollars in aggregate equity repricing, exceeding hedge funds, other households, and all other investor types. We decompose the cross-sectional variation in stock returns during Robinhood’s growth surge in 2020 into investor-specific components and find that shifts in Robinhood traders’ latent demand drove 11% of small-cap return volatility despite their negligible aggregate wealth share. To explain these demand shifts, we show that Robinhood traders are the only investor group whose latent demand is well explained by attention proxies: their demand exhibits a V-shaped response to past returns and rises sharply with trading volume. Our findings suggest that the growth of retail trading platforms represents a fundamental shift in the composition of equity demand with equilibrium consequences disproportionate to retail investors’ share of aggregate wealth. This paper was accepted by Lukas Schmid, finance. Funding: P. van der Beck acknowledges financial support from the Swiss National Science Foundation. Supplemental Material: The data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.04854 .

title: Corporate Pension Risk-Taking in a Low Interest Rate Environment
abstract: We examine how funding deficit pressures shape the risk-taking of U.S. corporate defined-benefit pension plans and how targeted regulatory relief can mitigate these incentives. Using the 2012 Moving Ahead for Progress in the 21st Century Act reform, which temporarily eased funding pressure by revising discount rate calculations, we show that plans receiving greater relief significantly reduced their equity allocations and shifted toward safer assets. This derisking was most pronounced among active plans and those sponsored by more financially constrained firms. Our findings demonstrate that targeted regulatory relief can curb risk-taking incentives even without altering underlying economic conditions or financial reporting standards and shed light on the likely (and unlikely) frictions driving such behavior. This paper was accepted by Bo Becker, finance. Funding: R. Pinto acknowledges financial support from the Lancaster University Management School Pump Prime Program. Supplemental Material: The online appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2025.02928 .

Brave new cities? Governance configurations for sustainable city logistics
abstract: Purpose Despite extensive research and policy efforts, there is still no consensus over the aspects that must be influenced to mitigate the environmental and social impact of city logistics. Existing approaches have primarily focused on optimizing urban freight operations but have struggled to generate lasting and systemic improvements. Building on recent supply chain management (SCM) calls to conceptualize supply chains as socially embedded systems, this study aims to investigate why cities implementing broadly similar collaborative governance initiatives produce different sustainable city logistics outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative configurational analysis was conducted across twenty French city logistics initiatives. Drawing on Furnari et al.’s (2021) configurational theorizing toolkit, governance conditions were iteratively identified and combined to explain variation in sustainable city logistics outcomes. Findings The analysis identifies five governance configurations. Rather than depending on collaborative governance alone, high-impact outcomes emerge from the interaction among governance structure, stakeholder representation, structural commitment and intervention scale. Research limitations/implications The governance configurations identified are grounded in French city logistics initiatives and should be further strengthened through fieldwork, and then examined in other institutional contexts. Future research should investigate how governance configurations evolve over time and across different socially embedded supply chains. Practical implications Managers and public authorities should focus less on replicating individual governance practices and more on assembling governance configurations that combine broad stakeholder representation, collaborative decision-making, structural commitment and coordinated ecosystem-level interventions. Originality/value The study advances SCM research by reconceptualizing sustainable city logistics as a governance and coordination challenge embedded within socially embedded supply chains. By doing so, it further demonstrates how configurational theorizing explains wicked sustainability problems in SCM by shifting attention from isolated governance mechanisms toward governance configurations as the appropriate unit of analysis.
journal_name: Supply Chain Management: An International Journal

title: Color lightness as a sensory marketing cue: implications for guest decision-making
abstract: Purpose The comfort of sleep-related hotel amenities plays a critical role in shaping guests’ perceptions and booking intentions. Although prior research suggests that color lightness influences perceived comfort, existing studies have primarily focused on manufactured goods. Given the fundamental differences between goods and hospitality services, this study aims to examine how bedding color lightness influences hotel guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions in the service context. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on Accessibility-Diagnosticity Theory, this research uses one pretest and two experiments to examine the effects of bedding color lightness on perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay, as well as the underlying mechanism explaining the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Findings Compared with light-colored bedding, dark-colored bedding significantly enhances perceived comfort, brand image and willingness to pay. Brand image and perceived comfort serially mediate the relationship between color lightness and willingness to pay. Research limitations/implications Color lightness serves as an accessible and diagnostic cue shaping consumer responses. The findings provide practical insights into how hotel businesses can leverage color lightness in bedding design and visual marketing communication to enhance guests’ perceptions and behavioral intentions. Originality/value Prior research in manufacturing contexts suggests a direct association between light colors and perceived comfort. However, this study shows that, in hospitality settings, darker colors can enhance perceived comfort, as experiential comfort is shaped through brand-level perceptions. Such critical insights highlight how the underlying mechanism of color lightness operates differently in service contexts, reflecting the unique characteristics of hospitality settings.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: When robots take the initiative: how robotic service proactivity shapes customer experience of hospitableness
abstract: Purpose Drawing on social response theory, this research aims to examine whether, how and when robotic service proactivity fosters customer experience of hospitableness. Design/methodology/approach A multistudy design consisting of three scenario-based experiments and one field validation survey was used to test the proposed conceptual model. Findings Customers reported a more intense experience of hospitableness when service robots displayed higher levels of proactivity. Automated social presence accounted for this effect, and the effect was amplified when robots possessed a more human-like appearance. Practical implications This research presents actionable insights for optimizing the coordinated management of robotic behaviors and appearances to enhance customer-robot interaction experiences. Originality/value This research extends research on service robots from static design to dynamic behavior, positioning robotic service proactivity as a key driver of customer experience of hospitableness. From the perspective of customer social responses, this study reveals automated social presence as the socio-emotional mechanism. It further establishes humanoid appearance as a moderating factor, demonstrating that proactive behavior yields greater benefits when robot form and behavior are aligned. These findings advance research on service robot form–behavior consistency and offer novel implications for robot design.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: How could fun activities motivate informal field-based learning?
abstract: Purpose As the motivational mechanisms through which workplace practices activate employees’ informal field-based learning (IFBL) remain underexplored, this study aims to address this gap by examining how fun activities (FA) influence IFBL in hotel contexts. Design/methodology/approach Three-wave survey data were collected from 424 frontline and backstage employees in Chinese hotels and analyzed through the AMOS and Macro PROCESS in SPSS. Findings The results showed that the interaction between FA and individual playfulness influenced IFBL through two distinct mediators: harmonious passion (HP) and obsessive passion (OP), depending on employees’ playfulness. FA activated HP only among employees with high playfulness, whereas among those with low playfulness, FA activated only OP. Practical implications Organizations should design FA that genuinely meet employees’ needs, thereby satisfying psychological needs such as autonomy and activating HP to promote IFBL. Importantly, employees should be given greater flexibility in choosing the form and frequency of their participation in FA according to their level of playfulness. Originality/value This research advances understanding of the organizational antecedents of IFBL and explores the motivational mechanisms that stimulate hotel employees’ IFBL by integrating organizational- and individual-level research on fun and play.
journal_name: International Journal of Contemporary Hospitality Management

title: Can Academia Ethically Use Tools of Techno-Colonial Extraction? The “Problem” of GenAI
abstract: Debates on generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in qualitative research focus on methodological utility versus epistemological harm. We reframe the issue from conditions of use to conditions of production , arguing GenAI’s foundation in exploitative digital labor and geopolitical inequality presents a more fundamental ethical challenge for business and society scholars, who risk complicity in these extractive systems. We outline several pathways through which scholars and institutions can engage GenAI more responsibly.

title: From clearance to capital: regulatory timing, financing conditions, and observability limits in medical-device commercialization
abstract: Abstract An authorized medical device may still need outside capital before its sponsor, the firm responsible for it, can manufacture and launch it. The paper asks what public U.S. records can show about whether authorization timing relates to access to that capital, and what a credible test needs. It does not estimate a financing or commercialization effect. The data combine 52,910 successful authorizations for submissions received in 2008–2024, a monthly capital-market measure, and a prototype match of 510(k) applicant names to Form D notices of private securities offerings. Among submissions received through 2022, the longest tenth accounts for 49.4–57.4 percent of days above the pathway median. Receipt-to-decision durations include applicant-response periods and do not measure unexpected or agency-caused delay. The market measure takes similar values in neighboring months. Its nine high periods, runs of two or more high months, last two to nine months; its relevance to individual sponsors is untested. As an observability diagnostic, the Form D prototype shows how name linkage can mislead. Records in the longest-duration quartile less often have a notice within a year (2.1 versus 3.1 percent in the shortest). Their applicant names, however, also appear less often among issuers (8.7 versus 14.4 percent), and among records with a name found, the notice share is not lower. About 11 percent of outcome windows are incomplete, and amendments count as notices. The contribution is to document these measurement requirements and to specify a sponsor-level test with validated identities, decision-date forecasts at receipt, and dated capital events.

title: It is all about digitalization: investigating antecedents and effects of digital transformation
abstract: Abstract Digital transformation is increasingly recognized as a vital driver of competitiveness, yet the precise organizational factors that most strongly influence its success remain ambiguous. This study addresses this gap by examining how strategic, operational, organizational, and cultural factors jointly relate to digital transformation outcomes, and by uncovering the mediating role of innovation success in shaping overall company success. Drawing upon data from 279 organizational key informants in Germany with substantive involvement in digital transformation, this study develops a holistic framework that not only identifies key organizational factors relevant for digital transformation success but also compares their associations with transformation success when considered simultaneously. The findings reveal numerically larger associations for cultural and operational factors, whereas strategic and organizational factors exhibit smaller coefficients, with the organizational-domain association only marginally significant ( p < 0.10). Although bootstrap-based parameter-difference tests do not support a statistically established ranking of the four domains, the results underline the relevance of all four domains while suggesting that cultural and operational conditions may warrant particular attention depending on firms’ specific transformation context. Furthermore, the results reveal a significant indirect association between digital transformation success and company success through innovation success, accounting for around 60% of the total association in the specified model. Hence, organizations seeking to maximize the returns on their digital initiatives should consider cultural and operational conditions alongside the strategic and organizational foundations of digital transformation. Taken together, these insights offer actionable guidance for businesses aiming to allocate their resources strategically, consider cultural and operational conditions as important diagnostic starting points, and harness the full potential of digital transformation through a concerted emphasis on innovation.

title: Going green but seeing red: Tensions in initiating collective market shaping for sustainability
abstract: Empirical research on market shaping for environmental outcomes remains rare in business marketing research, and existing studies are largely biased towards successful cases while overlooking the challenging “front end” of collective market shaping. This study examines how actor-perceived tensions emanating from the business context influence efforts to initiate a collective market-shaping process for improved environmental outcomes. Drawing on a real-time qualitative case study of a European cruise shipbuilding network, we focus on the phase in which a shared market vision and coordinated action have yet to emerge. Our findings show that accumulated tensions hinder the microprocesses required for initiating collective market shaping. These tensions manifest as conflict, scattered activity and inactivity, delaying progress towards collective market shaping. Shifting attention from successful outcomes to early-stage tensions, this study contributes to market-shaping research by uncovering why collective market-shaping efforts for sustainability may fail to take shape in complex industrial networks.

title: How do monetary rewards impact free knowledge contribution? – business implication for Q&A platforms
