The Prediction and Mediating Role of Lifetime and Daily Aggressive Sexual Fantasies: An Experience-Sampling Study
abstract: Aggressive sexual fantasies (ASF) have consistently been associated with different sexual-aggression measures and mediated the effects of other risk factors on sexual aggression. Little, however, is known about the predictors of ASF and whether they should be considered as an independent risk factor for sexual aggression or rather an expression of aggression-related sexual interests. The present study, therefore, assessed lifetime ASF cross-sectionally (N = 422; Mage = 28.14; SD = 9.76) and over a 14-day experience-sampling period (n = 230; Mage = 27.38; SD = 9.08). Of the participants, 87% reported to have experienced ASF at least once in their lives; 11% reported ASF during the experience-sampling period. Psychopathy, violent pornography consumption, sexual interest in sexual sadism, and the interactions between hypersexuality and sexual-abuse experiences, Machiavellianism, and sexual interest in sadism were associated with higher lifetime ASF. Sexual interest in sadism positively predicted ASF during the experience-sampling period, but only in men. Lifetime ASF were the strongest predictor of sexual aggression and mediated the cross-sectional associations between sexual interest in sadism, hypersexuality, and violent pornography consumption and sexual aggression. These findings support the notion that ASF are an important cognitive risk factor for sexual aggression, partially independent from sexual interest, and require stronger attention by research and practice.

title: Consensual Unwanted Sex and Body Dissatisfaction Among Cisgender Heterosexual Women and Queer Women/Gender Expansive Individuals
abstract: People (especially women) often consent to unwanted sexual activity (especially with men). Reasons for consenting to unwanted sex include facilitating desired and avoiding undesired outcomes, and both positive and negative outcomes are common. Much of this research has focused on cisgender women’s experiences consenting to unwanted sex with cisgender men and associated relationship and emotional outcomes. Building on existing work, we examined how consenting to unwanted sex was associated with body-related harms among samples of cisgender heterosexual (cis/het) women (N = 491) and Queer women and gender expansive individuals (N = 529). Using survey data, we examined whether self-objectification explained the relationship between consensual unwanted sex (yes/no) and body dissatisfaction, and whether sexual/gender identity moderated those relationships. We also explored reasons for consenting to unwanted sex and how those reasons were associated with self-objectification and body dissatisfaction. Results found 70% of participants had ever consented to unwanted sex, and that consenting to unwanted sex was more common among Queer women/gender expansive individuals than cis/het women. There was a significant indirect effect of consensual unwanted sex on body dissatisfaction via self-objectification for both cis/het and Queer participants. Moreover, the frequency of different reasons for consenting to unwanted sex were similar for cis/het women and Queer women and gender expansive individuals. Only avoidance reasons were associated with greater self-objectification and body dissatisfaction. Overall, consenting to unwanted sex was associated with body-related harms, and such harms were experienced by both cis/het women and Queer women/gender expansive individuals.

title: Prevalence of Sexual Acts and Materials Provided for Financial Compensation Among Young Adults in the United States
abstract: Providing in-person (e.g., sex) and virtual (e.g., photos) sexual acts for pay or financial compensation (SAMP) is underreported due to stigma and substantial measurement issues. Prior research using a single item may have underestimated the prevalence and associated characteristics. This study sought to determine lifetime SAMP prevalence and associated characteristics of SAMP in a nationally representative sample in young adults (18–34 years old) in the United States. We administered a cross-sectional web-based survey through the National Opinion Research Council (N = 2,935). We used the validated, behaviorally specific, 10-item SAMP index to assess prevalence and circumstances, standardized measures of health and childhood experiences, and demographics. Over one-third (36%) of participants reported providing SAMP. Of those, 22% first provided SAMP as minors and 65.5% reported coercion. Prevalence differed by gender, sexuality, race, education, employment, income, and parenthood. Participants who provided SAMP had higher odds of depression, PTSD, problematic substance use, rape victimization, childhood adversity, discrimination, and lower social support. Findings suggest that SAMP is more common than previously assumed. Significant differences among those reporting SAMP underscore the need for harm reducing public health approaches to address health disparities, systemic social issues, diverse experiences, and SAMP’s spectrum of agency and victimization.

title: Childhood Physical Abuse Perpetrators: Australian National Survey Data on Prevalence and Perpetrator Types
abstract: = 2,623 experiencing childhood physical abuse), we estimated prevalence by perpetrator type and examined age of onset, cessation and duration. The overwhelming majority of physical abuse occurred within family settings. Lower prevalence estimates among younger cohorts suggest physical abuse may be becoming less common in more recent generations. Physical abuse most commonly began before 10 years of age, particularly when both parents were identified as perpetrators. These findings show that a substantial proportion of physical abuse occurs during children's formative years when they are unlikely to have networks outside of their family to turn to. The predominance of familial perpetration highlights the central role of family environments in the occurrence of physical abuse and the critical need for policies and programs that can target physical abuse within the home.

title: Recruiting for SDGs-Oriented Profiles: Unpacking Drivers of Employer Attractiveness in Hybrid Organizations
abstract: Recruitment is critical for equipping public service organizations with the competencies required to advance the sustainable development goals (SDGs). This is particularly salient for public utilities, hybrid organizations mandated to contribute to the SDGs through essential services in water, waste, and energy management. This study examines employer attractiveness for profiles considered critical to SDG implementation in Italian utilities. Drawing on self-determination theory, we combine semi-structured interviews with HR and Employer Branding managers from 16 utilities with two discrete-choice experiments involving STEM and vocational-technical students and professionals. Salary and competence-related opportunities are consistently important across both groups. Remote work does not significantly affect STEM respondents’ choices, whereas workplace proximity is the strongest driver for vocational-technical respondents. Relatedness, operationalized as environmental and community impact, is not a significant differentiating attribute, suggesting that in organizations whose public value mission is already highly visible, social and environmental impact may function as a baseline expectation.

title: Governance of a Party‐State: Corruption, Law, and the Modus Operandi of the Chinese Communist Party. By LingLi, Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 2025. 358 pp. £110.00/$140.00 (hardcover). ISBN: 978‐1‐00‐927500‐2
The benefits of concentrating solar hybrid systems: A unified benchmarking framework
Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for proton exchange membrane fuel cells: From implementation to application
abstract: Proton exchange membrane fuel cells play a vital role in achieving a hydrogen-powered, carbon-neutral society. Although they have been deployed in stationary and transportation applications, their limited durability and reliability still restrict large-scale commercialization. Assessing internal health states is critical to overcoming these challenges by preventing operational faults and minimizing degradation rates. However, hydrogen fuel cells are highly nonlinear, multiscale, and multiphysics systems, hindering the estimation of system health states. This review investigates a nondestructive and in situ characterization technique, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), to characterize the health states of hydrogen fuel cells. The variation in internal health states is directly reflected in the impedance spectrum, which can be assessed through proper interpretation. Nevertheless, developing EIS for hydrogen fuel cells is a nontrivial task. Implementing and applying EIS requires interdisciplinary studies in signal processing, control theory, and machine learning in particular cases. This review systematically discusses the implementation, interpretation, and application of EIS for hydrogen fuel cells. The onboard applicability and short measurement time are key factors in EIS implementation. Model-based and DRT-based interpretation approaches are reviewed for efficiently extracting valuable health states. Based on these methods, the applications of EIS in performance characterization, fault diagnosis, degradation analysis, and prognostics are discussed. Four perspectives regarding general, non-electrical, localized, and multiphysics-integrated EIS, are proposed to highlight and guide EIS-related studies in hydrogen fuel cells. This review provides a comprehensive overview of the deployment and application of EIS in hydrogen fuel cells and offers insights into addressing durability and reliability challenges.

title: Global soybean markets and land-use emissions: Evidence from the China–Brazil soybean trade relationship
Financing models, energy diplomacy, and strategic dependency in nuclear power projects: A comparative analysis of Akkuyu and El Dabaa nuclear power plants
The complexities and failures of Australia’s East Coast Gas Market
abstract: Australia's East Coast Gas Market (ECGM) presents a policy paradox. Despite abundant gas reserves, households, businesses and industry continue to face high energy costs. These outcomes are commonly linked to the ECGM's integration with the international gas and oil markets. However, market structure alone does not explain why more structural forms of regulatory intervention remain politically constrained. This Perspective examines three recurring claims in Australia's gas policy debate: that increasing gas supply will lower domestic prices, that renewable energy is unreliable without continued reliance on gas, and that government intervention can correct problems within the gas market. Existing research has raised questions about each of these propositions. This paper, therefore, focuses on the political work they perform and argues that the claims circulate and reinforce one another by sustaining increased gas supply in response to affordability concerns, positioning gas as necessary for energy reliability, and providing reassurances that market problems can be managed through regulation. In doing so, they help to maintain an export-oriented gas market while narrowing the political space for structural intervention. The analysis highlights how market structure and political framing interact to constrain domestic energy governance and complicate energy transition in fossil-fuel-exporting economies.

title: The impacts of the 2022 energy crisis on heating in German households - An empirical before-and-after examination of energy relevant concepts
Building integrated agriculture as a competitive energy-saving measure: A life-cycle energy assessment
Microplastic-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter Regulates Reactive Bromine Species Formation by Modulating the Photochemistry of Seawater Dissolved Organic Matter
abstract: Abstract Microplastic-derived dissolved organic matter (MP-DOM) is emerging as a non-negligible organic input to marine systems, yet how its interactions with seawater DOM (S-DOM) regulate the photochemical formation of reactive bromine species (RBS) remains unclear. In this study, the RBS formation potential of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC)-derived MP-DOM, S-DOM, and their mixed systems was systematically investigated under simulated solar irradiation. MP-DOM input exerted a nonlinear ratio-dependent regulatory effect on S-DOM-mediated RBS formation. At relatively low MP-DOM proportions (5–20%), the formation rate constant of 4-bromo-3,5-dimethyl-1H-pyrazole (Br-DMPZ), which represents the RBS formation potential, increased relative to S-DOM alone, reaching a maximum enhancement of 47.4% at 20% MP-DOM under seawater halide ion conditions (540 mM Cl– + 0.8 mM Br–). This enhancement was associated with increased quinone-/carbonyl-related redox-active structures, electron exchange capacity, and tannin-like components, which could facilitate photoinduced charge separation, electron transfer, and Br– oxidation. In contrast, higher MP-DOM proportions (40–50%) promoted hydrophobic lipid-like mixed assemblies, enhancing excited-state quenching and suppressing electron transfer and RBS photogeneration. These findings demonstrate that MP-DOM is not an inert byproduct of microplastic aging but rather an important regulatory factor in S-DOM-mediated halogen photochemistry in plastic-impacted marine waters.

title: Suspect and Non-Targeted Analysis of Organophosphate Esters in Plastic Consumer Products via Ion Mobility Spectrometry-Mass Spectrometry
abstract: Abstract Organophosphate esters (OPEs) are widely used as plasticizers and flame retardants in plastic products, posing critical environmental and human health risks. Traditional liquid chromatography-high resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS) approaches face trade-offs between comprehensive coverage and spectral purity. This study established an advanced multidimensional identification framework utilizing LC coupled with cyclic ion mobility spectrometry and quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (LC-cIMS-QTOF). An integrated screening workflow merging targeted analysis, suspect screening, and nontargeted analysis (NTA) was deployed to characterize the OPEs in consumer plastics. A total of 63 OPEs were successfully characterized across seven polymer types, with 10, 22, and 31 compounds identified via targeted, suspect, and NTA workflows, respectively. Notably, 14 OPEs were traced back to the transformation products of phosphite antioxidants, ethoxy-linked OPEs constituted another predominant class with 22 congeners. This comprehensive characterization enriches current knowledge regarding the diversity of OPEs within plastic products, providing critical target lists for future migration and exposure assessments. Methodologically, the benefits of IMS, including providing cleaner mass spectra, discriminating isomers, and improving confidence levels, were demonstrated throughout the OPEs identification workflow. This established multidimensional screening strategy serves as a robust and efficient tool for uncovering OPEs contaminants in both plastic matrices and broader environmental media.

title: Mn(II)-Mediated Abiotic Humification via Synergistic Interactions with Molecular Oxygen
abstract: Abstract Terrestrial organic carbon (OC) dynamics critically influence the global carbon budget. Humification is a key pathway for stabilizing OC by transforming labile compounds into macromolecular polymers. High-valent manganese oxides (e.g., Mn(IV)O2) are well-known as efficient catalysts of abiotic humification, whereas the role of Mn(II) in OC transformation remains poorly understood. Here, dissolved Mn2+ drives oxidative polymerization and nitrogen-enriched humic-like product formation in the presence of common soil precursors─catechol, glycine, and glucose─through a synergistic interaction with molecular oxygen (O2). Mechanistically, Mn2+ mediates sequential single-electron transfers from catechol to O2, forming reactive intermediates that potentially couple with Maillard precursors to yield nitrogen-enriched macromolecules. FT-ICR-MS reveals that CHON species in lignin-like and highly condensed aromatic regions collectively account for 75.6% of total product relative abundance. This process is accompanied by the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), which could further enhance molecular diversity. Across 14 soil and freshwater DOM samples, 13.1–54.7% of assigned product formulas overlap with those in the corresponding DOM samples. Collectively, these shared formulas account for 78% of the total relative abundance of product formulas, indicating molecular-formula-level compositional similarity. These findings provide mechanistic and molecular-level insight into the underexplored role of Mn2+ in abiotic humification.

title: Modeling to Plan the Future Cities We Desire
abstract: W hat transformational changes are needed to create the future cities people desire�ones that are sustainable, resilient, and equitable�and what modeling tools do we need to support action toward this goal?Many decision-support tools for urban infrastructure, from energy to transportation to water systems, are designed for incremental planning and management over the next months or years�and for use by technical experts.This focus is appropriate for ensuring safe and reliable service provision but not longer-term, transformative, community-driven changes, such as phasing out fossil fuels, moving away from autocentric mobility, and achieving universal access to affordable, clean water.Existing tools are often used defensively, taking the present as a point of departure to identify and avoid potential vulnerabilities.However, a model grounded in the status quo embeds current worldviews, priorities, and power structures, potentially reproducing, or even widening, existing inequities. 1 For instance, if demand forecasting is based on existing user patterns, without taking into account households that are already structurally underserved, underinvestment will continue.In this Viewpoint, we explore possibilities for broadening modeling tools and processes�and the goals, levers, and actors they represent�to support collaborative decisions toward more transformative urban futures.We see an opportunity to orient models, and the planning processes that use them, toward desired futures, 2 not just predicted or plausible ones.3 Visions of what is a desired future are necessarily plural and will vary across contexts, values, and worldviews.This multiplicity is part of their power.Widening the framing of the future to explicitly include plural and diverse aspirations, and not just what is most likely to happen, can create space for more transformational possibilities, particularly for groups whose perspectives are currently marginalized in dominant planning processes.For instance, Afro and Indigenous futurisms often exemplify this stance, imagining futures around Black and Indigenous flourishing rather than the extension of present harms.4,5 Critically, starting with desired futures allows us to center a question that predictive framings can elide: what are the goals Viewpoint pubs.acs.

title: Biochar Application Enhances Photochemical Reactivity of Dissolved Organic Matter to Stimulate CO2 Emissions in Paddy Water
abstract: Abstract Dissolved organic matter (DOM) plays a pivotal role in regulating photochemical reactivity and carbon turnover in flooded paddy systems. While biochar (BC) is recognized as a promising strategy for soil carbon preservation, its impact on DOM evolution and photochemical carbon cycle in paddy water remains unknown. Here, we demonstrated that BC amendment continuously enhanced the photogeneration of hydroxyl radicals (•OH) and low-energy excited triplet-state DOM (3DOM*-L) in paddy water, increasing CO2 emissions by an average of 35.5% while playing a minor role in CH4 formation over a 34-day incubation. The enhanced photoactivity was associated with the enrichment of the photoactive molecular pool characterized by highly aromatic compounds and polyphenols with higher aromaticity, unsaturation, and oxygenated degrees. The proposed mechanisms in enriching photoactive DOM of paddy water depended on soil types, i.e., BC facilitated the biotic reprocessing of inert, highly recalcitrant aromatics into metabolites associated with photoactivity in sandy soil, whereas abiotic processes, including BC-induced dissolved black carbon release and mineral-associated organic carbon desorption, likely played more important roles in loam soil. Enhanced anaerobic fermentation further supplied photolabile substrates for amplifying mineralization. Extrapolation estimations suggested that BC-enhanced photochemistry may release an additional 3.56–15.47 Tg CO2 yr–1 globally, potentially offsetting ∼0.7–7.0% of BC’s CO2 mitigation potential. The findings revealed a previously unrecognized photochemical pathway of BC-involved carbon loss across the soil-water continuum, with implications for evaluating the net climate benefit of biochar as a carbon management strategy.

title: Event-Scale Deposition of Atmospheric Microplastics in Snowfall of the Sierra Nevada in North America
abstract: Abstract Atmospheric deposition of microplastics (MPs) at an event-scale resolution can be measured in snowfall events, as snow scavenges atmospheric MPs and the snowpack serves as a repository for MP accumulation. We monitored MP deposition in freshly fallen snow, the snowpack, and dry deposition over the course of 6 months in the Sierra Nevada of North America. Average microplastic concentrations in fresh snow ranged from 11.8 to 37.5 p/L at remote sites, which were significantly less than the 68.3 to 92.9 p/L MP concentrations found at the anthropogenically impacted site. Average bulk deposition rates were estimated to be 267 to 3190 p/m2/day at remote sites, significantly lower than the 3242 to 7480 p/m2/day at the anthropogenically impacted site. HYSPLIT back-trajectory modeling characterized the potential regional transport of MPs from upwind regions that were predominantly agricultural and suburban areas, as well as localized anthropogenic activities that could significantly affect MP deposition rates in snowfall. This study introduces high-throughput FTIR analysis methods with a highlight on fiber spectroscopy, demonstrates the value of estimating MP fluxes at the meteorological event scale, reports MP deposition rates in a critical water resource, and provides a basis for future long-term atmospheric MP monitoring.

title: Recombinase Polymerase Amplification Coupled with Graphene Oxide Nanomaterial-Assisted Purification and Target Signal Selection for Highly Sensitive and Rapid Harmful Algae Detection
abstract: Abstract Harmful algal blooms (HABs) pose serious ecological and health risks, creating an urgent need for rapid, sensitive, and accurate detection of harmful algae. Here, we developed a graphene oxide (GO)- and Mg2+-regulated recombinase polymerase amplification assay (G-M-RPA) for rapid and ultrasensitive detection of Heterosigma akashiwo, Prorocentrum minimum, and Akashiwo sanguinea. Using conserved internal transcribed spacer sequences, we designed species-specific primers labeled with 6-carboxyfluorescein for fluorescence readout. Innovative one-step purification of RPA products was achieved using self-synthesized GO-wrapped magnetic nanocomposites instead of traditional purification kits, reducing purification time from 15 to 2 min (∼86.7%). The fluorescence resonance energy transfer property of the GO nanosheets was applied to quench the fluorescence of excess single-stranded primers, significantly lowering background levels. Mg2+ further enhanced primer–GO interactions, likely through electrostatic screening and Mg2+-mediated interactions. The entire detection process was completed within ∼30 min, achieving a genomic DNA detection limit of 3.3 fg/μL, corresponding to ∼7 cells/mL for H. akashiwo. The assay also showed reliable performance in mixed-DNA and seawater matrices, with favorable reproducibility and short-term stability. Overall, the proposed G-M-RPA strategy provides a rapid, sensitive, and practical platform for multispecies harmful-algae detection, nearshore environmental monitoring, and early warning of HABs.

Issue Editorial Masthead
Soil Heating from Fire Induces Bidirectional Changes in Dissolved Organic Matter Release and Organic Sulfur Speciation
abstract: Abstract Soil heating from fire influences dissolved organic matter (DOM) release but has unknown effects on organic sulfur (S) speciation, with implications for S and metal cycling in aquatic environments. Here, low and high organic carbon soils (4.80 versus 50.4%) were heated at environmentally relevant temperatures and durations (75–300 °C, 0.25–4.0 h) and subject to leaching experiments that quantified DOM and inorganic anion release, and changes in organic S speciation via S X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy. In both soils, heating between 75 and 200 °C increased dissolved organic carbon (DOC) and inorganic sulfate (SO42–) release (by up to 24- and 88-fold, respectively) while decreasing the % highly reduced S in DOM (e.g., thiols), indicating thiol oxidation to SO42–. Soil heating at 300 °C decreased DOC release and increased SO42– release, with step increases in DOM aromaticity and % heterocyclic reduced S species (e.g., thiophenes). Across treatments, DOM aromaticity positively correlated with DOM % heterocyclic reduced S, interpreted to reflect organic S cyclization during heating. The observed bidirectional changes in organic S speciation in DOM due to soil heating, with thiol oxidation at ≤200 °C and S cyclization at 300 °C with SO42– releases, provide mechanistic insights that improve the prediction of fire effects on S, C, and metal cycling in aquatic environments.

title: Correction to “Nitrous Oxide Emissions from Urban Green Spaces Substantially Offset Their Carbon Sequestration Benefits”
Observation-Based Emission Estimates of the Potent Greenhouse Gas HFC-23 for Article 5 and Non-Article 5 Country Groups under the Montreal Protocol
abstract: Abstract The Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol requires parties to destroy, to the extent practicable, HFC-23 generated as a byproduct during the production of controlled hydrochlorofluorocarbons and hydrofluorocarbons. Global total HFC-23 emissions estimated from reported abatement and known sources (bottom-up) agreed with those inferred from atmospheric observations (top-down) before 2015, but have been substantially lower since then. Here, we show that during 2011–2013, bottom-up estimates of global total HFC-23 emissions were right for the wrong reasons: bottom-up estimates for the non-Article 5 (mainly developed) country group were lower than top-down estimates (1.7 ± 0.2 vs 3.1 ± 0.5 Gg yr–1 on average), while those for the Article 5 (mainly developing) country group were higher (11.8 ± 0.4 vs 9.7 ± 1.0 Gg yr–1), resulting in a cancellation at the global scale. We further show that during 2015–2023, while the underestimation of global bottom-up emissions was dominated by the Article 5 country group, the non-Article 5 country group also contributed in 2023 [bottom-up (byproduct emissions reported to UNEP plus other known sources) vs top-down: 0.5 ± 0.2 vs 1.3 ± 0.6 Gg yr–1]. Our results underscore improvement of emission accounting and mitigation for both country groups under the Kigali Amendment.

Deep eutectic solvent processing of seagrass biomass from beach wrack for sustainable polypropylene composites in large format additive manufacturing
abstract: Seagrass-rich beach wrack collected from the Bay of Cádiz (Spain) was valorized as a reinforcement for polypropylene (PP) composites manufactured by large-format additive manufacturing by fused granular fabrication (LFAM-FGF). Two delignification approaches were investigated with NaOH (SG-NaOH) and a deep eutectic solvent (DES) based on lactic acid and choline chloride (SG-DES). While SG-NaOH achieved greater lignin removal, SG-DES yielded a cellulose-rich material with higher crystallinity and a distinctive nanofibrillar morphology. When incorporated into PP at 15 wt%, untreated seagrass (SG-UT) and SG-NaOH resulted in a marked reduction in tensile strength and ductility. In contrast, composites reinforced with SG-DES exhibited a significant increase in Young's modulus while maintaining tensile strength comparable to neat PP and preserving high elongation at break. Thus, despite its lower delignification efficiency, the DES treatment produced the most effective reinforcement among the investigated formulations, highlighting that extensive lignin removal is not necessarily required to achieve high composite performance. In addition, all seagrass-filled formulations showed improved dimensional stability during LFAM-FGF printing, effectively suppressing the warping commonly observed in neat PP, enabling the fabrication of large-scale demonstrator parts which maintained their structural integrity after more than one year of outdoor exposure.

Changes in the fire resilience of black pine in response to Mediterranean climate variability over the past 300 years
abstract: Elucidating the resilience of trees to wildfires remains a critical issue for forest conservation. The potential changes in tree resilience over time in response to the combined changes in fire regime and climate remain unknown. We hypothesised that tree resilience was influenced by mean fire-return intervals (MFI) and by their interactions with atmospheric conditions over the past 300 years, particularly during drought and hot years. This hypothesis was tested by analyzing tree-ring widths following past fires, using growth during fire-free periods as baseline, and atmospheric values (annual and seasonal temperature and precipitation, drought index and CO 2 concentration). The study focused on black pine ( Pinus nigra ) as a model species to investigate long-term ecological responses to fires in natural forests of Corsica, a western Mediterranean island. The study is based on 180 cross-dated black pines from four Corsican mountain sites. 54 fires were recorded between 1719 CE and 2012 CE. Four contrasted periods, defined according to MFI and atmospheric records are used to assess the black pine responses to fire events, MFI period, and climate. The fire resistance and resilience of trees have gradually declined since about 1850, independently of the MFI and increased atmospheric CO₂ levels. Post-fire radial growth recovery lengthened over time, indicating a decline in resistance. Concurrently, tree-ring responded more positively to precipitation and negatively to drought intensity. In isolation, fire does not compromise tree resilience. But the combined effects of drought and wildfires thus threaten black pines by shrinking their resilience mainly since 1971, which underscores the increasing vulnerability of this Mediterranean tree to fire in an increasingly dry climate.

title: Advanced Exergy Analysis of an Innovative Solar-Driven System for Sustainable Hydrothermal Liquefaction: Experimental Validation and Topology Optimization
Numerical evaluation of a complex fenestration system with solar optics and photovoltaic cells for building energy efficiency and daylight autonomy
abstract: Dielectric crossed compound parabolic concentrator-photovoltaic (CCPC-PV) windows represent an attractive building-integrated photovoltaic (BIPV) fenestration solution, capable of harvesting solar energy for electricity generation while admitting daylight into occupied spaces. Nevertheless, conventional whole-building simulation tools cannot natively reproduce the complex optical, thermal, and electrical behaviours of CCPC-PV windows, and holistic building-scale evaluations considering diverse window design scenarios and climatic conditions remain insufficient. This study presents a coupled multi-physics simulation workflow based on the Equivalent Layer Fenestration Model (ELFM). It converts ray-tracing and computational fluid dynamics (CFD) outputs of complex CCPC-PV window geometry into equivalent-layer thermal/optical datasets compatible with EnergyPlus. Parametric simulations are conducted across different concentrator spacing layouts, window-to-wall ratios (WWRs), and climatic conditions. The simulation results reveal that densely arranged CCPC-PV configurations deliver the best overall system performance. At WWR = 64%, the optimal layout achieves net energy savings of 56.86% in London, 67.63% in Barcelona, and 33.93% in Stockholm. Under all simulated conditions, CCPC-PV windows achieve higher useful daylight illuminance (UDI 500-2000 ) than conventional double-glazed windows and mitigate visual discomfort due to over-illumination. This work demonstrates the effectiveness of the coupled simulation framework for evaluating complex BIPV fenestration systems, and quantifies the energy and daylight benefits of CCPC-PV windows across different design and climate contexts.

Thermal energy storage and district heating as flexibility enablers for industrial heat decarbonization
abstract: Electrifying industrial process heat production links industrial decarbonization to power-system constraints, increasing the need for flexibility. We apply an integrated energy system model, coupling industrial heat demands with district heating systems, to quantify how thermal energy storage (TES) and heat exchange with district heating affect cost-optimal decarbonization pathways for a region in Germany. We investigate the investments required in the transition towards a fully decarbonized energy system, including energy storage, heat pumps and renewable electricity generation, from today to 2050 with tightening emission restrictions. Results show that TES lowers total system costs by 6%–12% and reduces wind and solar curtailment, thereby substituting up to 36% of the cost-optimal battery capacity. In industry, low-temperature TES is deployed in early investment periods to even out heat pump operation and reduce the required heat pump capacity. On the other hand, high-temperature TES becomes relevant in later, highly electrified periods to time-shift power-intensive heat production under grid constraints. Coupling industry and district heating reduces the need for low-temperature storage by sharing heat across sectors, and unlocks more efficient process electrification by providing a heat source for high-temperature heat pumps. This leads to heat exchange between industry and district heating shifting from net export from industry in early periods to net import under tight emission constraints.

Motherhood and Constraints during Job Search
abstract: Abstract Why do women’s labour earnings drop upon motherhood? We shed new light on this question by analysing the changes in job search behaviour associated with motherhood. We exploit data on the job applications sent on a popular online platform linked with administrative registers for 350,000 involuntarily unemployed workers in France. After losing their job, mothers have a 11.7% lower probability to find a job than similar women without children and send 12.2% fewer job applications. To explore the underlying mechanisms, we analyse the timing of job applications. Unlike other women, mothers’ rate of applications decreases by about 20.5% in the hours when there is no school. Moreover, the French reform that introduced school on Wednesday in 2014 led mothers to send more applications on Wednesdays. Our results highlight that childcare creates constraints on the timing of job search activities for mothers. We finally provide suggestive evidence that these constraints decrease their return-to-search, and thereby contribute to their lower application and job finding rates.

title: Welfare Expenditure Growth and its Impact on Elderly Suicide Rates
abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate the causal effect of increased elderly welfare expenditure in South Korea on the suicide rate among older adults, using predicted expenditure changes induced by the Basic Pension reform as an instrumental variable. Our findings show that higher welfare spending explains 74.5% of the decline in the suicide rate among individuals aged 65+ between 2013 and 2019, with especially large reductions among men aged 80+. Household‐level evidence indicates that while total income remained stable, consumption increased following the reform, particularly in transportation and leisure. We further show that the reform reduced unmet medical needs and stress and increased participation in community and leisure activities, while leaving depressive symptoms unchanged. Overall, the results are consistent with the interpretation that stronger public income transfer programs reduce income uncertainty and expand opportunities for consumption, leisure, and social participation, thereby contributing to lower elderly suicide rates.

title: On Bank Pricing of Single‐Family Residential Home Loans: Are Australian Households Paying Too Much?
abstract: ABSTRACT This paper examines the persistent divergence between observed mortgage rates and a capital‐market‐implied benchmark in the Australian residential housing finance market. Using quarterly data from 1998 to 2025, we construct a synthetic variable‐rate mortgage benchmark based on fixed‐rate mortgage yields, interest rate swaps, and swaptions to isolate fundamental funding costs and embedded interest rate risk. We estimate an autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) model to decompose the spread between observed and benchmark rates into risk‐based pricing and sluggish pass‐through. The empirical evidence reveals a large and persistent long‐run spread. On average, mortgage rates exceed the synthetic benchmark by approximately 146 basis points, widening to more than 240 basis points during periods of elevated credit risk. This divergence reflects not only risk‐based pricing but also incomplete and delayed pass‐through, consistent with structural market power in Australia's concentrated banking system. As a result, mortgage rates adjust slowly to changes in capital‐market conditions. The persistence of this spread has important economic implications. By raising mortgage rates relative to their capital‐market benchmark, these pricing frictions increase the income required to qualify for homeownership, thereby exacerbating affordability constraints in an already highly leveraged housing market.

title: What Interruptions Say About Your Organizational Culture
abstract: Recent research suggests that interruptions when meeting attendees are speaking are significant moments that affect how employees experience workplace culture and can lead to self-censoring. Taking a different approach to meeting facilitation can help leaders become more aware of when this is occurring so that they can improve participant dynamics, encourage meeting attendees to contribute, and more effectively respond to interruptions.

title: Sustainability Indicators and Product Diversification: An Exploratory Predictive Assessment
abstract: ABSTRACT This study examines whether carbon footprint, eco‐friendly manufacturing and recycling programmes help predict recorded product‐line count, used as a limited indicator of product diversification. Using the records from a sustainability dataset, we apply exploratory predictive modelling with linear regression, random forest and gradient boosting. We evaluate sustainability‐only, context‐only and combined models against a training‐mean benchmark using a held‐out sample and fivefold cross‐validation. Adding sustainability information improves some predictions beyond price, country, year and market trend but offers little consistent advantage over simply predicting the average product‐line count. The study contributes by showing the difference between improving a model and providing useful predictions of product‐range size. Uncertain corporate provenance and undocumented product‐line definitions prevent broader conclusions about sustainability's effects on strategic diversification or stakeholder value.

title: Carbon Risk and Syndicated Loans: A Network Analysis Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT As the transition to a low‐carbon economy accelerates, understanding how climate‐related risks propagate through the financial system has become a central concern for regulators and researchers alike. Transition risk—the risk arising from the shift toward lower‐emission business models—is not directly borne by banks but may indirectly affect financial intermediaries through their lending portfolios. As firms face increasing pressure to comply with climate regulations, their credit risk increases, potentially threatening the stability of the broader financial system. This study examines how carbon emissions are financed by financial institutions in the syndicated loan market and whether a bank's structural position in that market is associated with its exposure to transition risk. Using a sample of 6924 syndicated loans from DealScan for 2018, we constructed a directed weighted network of lenders and borrowers and computed three financed emissions metrics calibrated on equivalent data from Eikon and financial data from Orbis. Network centrality measures—including eigenvector, betweenness, and degree centrality—are then correlated with each metric. The results show that more central financial intermediaries are positively and significantly associated with higher shares of financed emissions across all centrality measures, with correlations of the order of 60%. Replicating the analysis on the 2025 vintage of the network yields consistent results, indicating that this association is a stable structural feature of the syndicated loan market rather than an artifact of a single year. Several robustness checks confirm the main findings. The results are relevant for both lenders and borrowers as well as regulators, given the results' systemic implications.

title: Measuring What Matters: Constructing an ESG Controversy Index Using AI and Institutional ESG Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) controversies increasingly influence investment decisions, corporate accountability, and sustainability regulation. However, existing commercial controversy measures often rely on proprietary methodologies that limit transparency and make it difficult to understand how controversy assessments are generated. This paper aims to develop an ESG Controversy Index (ESGCI) that combines internationally recognised ESG principles with explainable artificial intelligence to provide a systematic approach to measuring firm‐level ESG controversy exposure. The ESGCI is constructed from more than 5000 annual and sustainability reports issued by S&P 500 firms between 2010 and 2023, together with ESG doctrines published by the United Nations, the Principles for Responsible Investment, the Organisation for Economic Co‐operation and Development and the International Labour Organisation. Natural language processing and supervised machine‐learning techniques are used to identify, classify and aggregate ESG controversies within a structured measurement framework. The proposed index is evaluated through a multi‐layer validation strategy incorporating conceptual assessment, document‐level out‐of‐sample testing, external comparison with Refinitiv ESG controversy measures, inter‐rater reliability, incremental validity and complementary robustness analyses. The findings show that the ESGCI captures controversy‐related information recognised by existing commercial measures while providing additional insights through a fully documented measurement process. The reported relationships remain consistent across alternative weighting schemes, lagged specifications and instrumental‐variable estimations, supporting the robustness of the empirical evidence. Rather than replacing existing ESG controversy ratings, the ESGCI offers a complementary approach that improves methodological transparency and facilitates reproducible ESG controversy measurement. By integrating institutional ESG principles with explainable AI and comprehensive validation procedures, this research seeks to contribute to the advancement of ESG measurement and provide a practical foundation for future research, investment analysis and sustainability reporting.

title: Fair Business Models for Climate‐Smart Agriculture: A Design Science Research Approach
abstract: ABSTRACT Organisations in agri‐food value chains face urgent demands to address climate change, environmental degradation and social inequities through climate‐smart agriculture (CSA). However, sustained CSA implementation remains constrained by business models (BMs) that fail to offer fair solutions to stakeholders. Existing business model innovation (BMI) literature lacks conceptualisation of fair BMs and methodology for operationalising fairness in BMs, leading to the research question: How can fair BMs for CSA be defined, designed and developed? Using design science research across five European case studies, the study defines a fair BM as a BM in which the design of the value proposition, creation, delivery and capture enables equitable value distribution, inclusive processes, transparency of information and respectful relationships among stakeholders. The study operationalises fairness across the BMI process with stakeholder engagement and change management, deriving eight design requirements and thirteen stakeholder‐validated prototypes. The study advances BMI literature by offering prescriptive knowledge for operationalising fairness in agri‐food BMI.

Multiheme c -Type Cytochrome-Dependent Arsenate Reduction Enhances Methanogenesis in Methanosarcina acetivorans
abstract: Abstract Microorganism-mediated arsenate (As(V)) reduction plays a critical role in arsenic mobility and microbial adaptation in arsenic-contaminated anoxic environments. Current understanding of microbial As(V) reduction has primarily focused on two pathways: extracellular reduction mediated by membrane-bound As(V) respiratory reductase, and intracellular reduction catalyzed by cytoplasmic As(V) detoxification reductase. Here, we report an extracellular As(V) reduction process that operates independently of both known As(V) reductases and is mediated by methanogenic archaea that are recognized for obligate methanogenesis across diverse anoxic habitats. We demonstrate that a model methanogenic archaeon is capable of concurrently performing intracellular methanogenesis and extracellular As(V) reduction, with the latter process significantly enhancing methanogenic growth. Through a combination of microbial physiological, biochemical, and molecular genetic approaches, we identify multiheme c-type cytochromes (MHCs), which are widely distributed within the order Methanosarcinales and have been previously implicated in extracellular iron reduction, as the key molecular components responsible for extracellular As(V) reduction. Furthermore, employing density functional theory simulations, we propose plausible reduction pathways for As(V) reduction mediated by the heme prosthetic groups of MHCs and confirm their thermodynamic feasibility. This work not only provides new insights into the previously overlooked coupling between arsenic transformation and methanogenesis in anoxic environments on Earth, but also underscores the interconnected nature of iron and As(V) reduction, both of which can be mediated by MHCs.

title: Influence of Urban Form, Weather and Population on Outdoor Airborne Infection Risk: Implications in Greater London for SARS-CoV-2
abstract: Abstract Although airborne infectious disease transmission outdoors is possible, particularly in densely built urban areas with limited ventilation, the role of urban morphology and neighborhood climate heterogeneity in modulating the risk remains poorly quantified. We couple an urban climate model (SUEWS) and a modified Wells-Riley framework to develop a transferable neighborhood-scale approach for mapping outdoor airborne infection risk across morphologically diverse neighborhoods, factoring in urban form, population distribution and meteorologically driven viral infectivity decay. We demonstrate this framework by applying it to SARS-CoV-2 in Greater London. Considering outdoor urban ventilation alone, estimated risk follows a diurnal cycle and peaks at night. Including population distribution, daytime risk in busy commercial centers is up to 7.23 times higher than nighttime. Infectivity decay from ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure reduces risk by 35–45% in less dense areas and up to 99% in high built-density neighborhoods. Despite this mitigation, the highest risks persist in high-rise, high-workplace-density districts (e.g., City of London and Westminster), while lower-rise areas (e.g., Lambeth and Croydon) exhibit reductions exceeding 90%. For SARS-CoV-2, these findings demonstrate strong intraurban heterogeneity in outdoor airborne infection risk in Greater London. More broadly, the transferable framework supports high-resolution mapping to inform targeted, place-based public health interventions.

title: Substantial Emerging Impact of Amine-Based Carbon Capture on Atmospheric Particle Formation under Carbon Neutrality
abstract: Abstract Carbon capture (CC) is indispensable to carbon neutrality, and amine-based absorption using monoethanolamine (MEA) is among the most mature CC technologies. MEA can enhance atmospheric new particle formation (NPF), the primary source of atmospheric particles. However, the atmospheric impacts of MEA escaping from future large-scale CC deployment remain unknown. Here, we develop a three-dimensional model that represents MEA sources, sinks, and H2SO4-MEA nucleation based on quantum chemical and cluster dynamics calculations, to evaluate atmospheric MEA and its impacts from CC deployment at China’s coal-fired power plants under carbon-neutrality scenarios. By 2060, even moderate CC deployment raises atmospheric MEA concentrations to tens of pptv, exceeding dimethylamine (DMA), the canonical urban NPF agent. H2SO4-MEA nucleation consequently overtakes H2SO4-DMA nucleation across extensive CC-deployment regions (∼1 million km2) and is more than 10 times stronger within the CC-intensive core (∼0.2 million km2), raising particle number concentrations by 50–187% and exposing ∼430 million people to levels exceeding the WHO high-exposure benchmark. The associated rise in ultrafine particles is estimated to cause ∼34,800 additional deaths across China in 2060. We reveal that CC deployment may deliver climate benefits while inadvertently worsening particulate pollution and public-health burdens, warranting proactive and early preventive action.

title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
abstract: Abstract Human neurons are postmitotic and long-lived, requiring precise genomic regulation. Normal neuronal function is highly dosage-sensitive, with copy number variants (CNVs) and heterozygous point mutations associated with a host of neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric conditions 1–4 . Here we investigated somatic CNVs arising in single neurons to understand the dynamic processes that shape the normal neuronal genetic landscape. Altogether, we sequenced 2,357 single neurons from human postmortem brain from fetal to postnatal life. Two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches—Tn5-transposase-based amplification (1,526 neurons, 16 individuals) and primary template amplification 5 (831 neurons, 12 individuals)—showed that an average of 25.9% [12.7–46%] of prenatal cortical neurons have highly aberrant genomes, that is, widespread CNVs involving multiple chromosomes. This proportion reduced by about 4.5-fold after birth across the two single-cell whole-genome sequencing approaches (Fisher meta-analysis P = 3.5 × 10 − 6 ). Neurons with widespread CNVs were mainly eliminated perinatally, timed roughly parallel to periods of programmed cell death 6 , whereas neurons with smaller CNV burdens declined slowly in frequency with postnatal age. CNVs in surviving neurons were depleted for dosage-sensitive genes and genes involved in neurodevelopmental disorders (hypergeometric test P < 0.05), suggesting selective elimination of neurons with these CNVs. Analysis of 44,861 nuclei with single-nucleus assay for transposase-accessible chromatin (snATAC) and single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) showed that neurons with high CNV burdens exhibited abnormal synaptic gene expression, suggesting that abnormal synaptic gene regulation contributes to neuronal elimination. Elimination of defective neuronal genomes might represent an important developmental genome quality-control process that may be vulnerable in neurodevelopmental disease, and suggests purifying selection during human neurodevelopment.

title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
Monolithically and in situ integrated PbS infrared imagers
Tumour assembloids recapitulate tumour–CAF–T cell crosstalk in renal cancer
abstract: Abstract Dynamic interactions between tumours and their microenvironment are crucial for cancer progression and therapeutic outcomes 1,2 . However, our understanding of these relationships remains limited by the constrained capacity of current human model systems to manipulate diverse cellular components and to interrogate complex tumour–stroma crosstalk. Here we generated combinatorial, mix-and-match tumour assembloids by conditionally reconstituting multiple components of human renal cell carcinoma, including cancer cells, cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and tumour-infiltrating immune cells. Using genetically engineered renal cell carcinoma assembloids with humanized mouse models, we uncovered mechanisms by which CAFs coordinate interactions between tumour cells and CD8 + T cells to maintain non-cell-autonomous CD8 + T cell stemness and drive responsiveness to anti-PD-1 therapy. These interactions operate through a tumour–CAF–T cell signalling axis in which tumour-derived WNT induces CAF expression of activin A, which enhances CD8 + T cell stemness and sensitivity to PD-1 blockade. In non-responders, we also identified a subset of WNT-unresponsive CAFs that do not produce activin A, which leads to impaired CD8 + T cell stemness and resistance to therapy. Together, these findings establish a tumour–CAF–T cell axis as a key determinant of heterogeneous responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors. Moreover, tumour assembloids provide a versatile platform for mechanistic dissection of the tumour microenvironment and evaluation of personalized immunotherapy strategies.

title: Emotion regulation capacity lacks a shared neural signature
abstract: Abstract Cognitive reappraisal refers to changing how one thinks about a situation to alter its emotional impact. It is central to well-being 1 and engages prefrontal regulatory circuits 2 , prompting the assumption that their activity reflects a person’s capacity to regulate emotions 3–5 . Yet evidence for this assumption remains inconclusive and has not been established at scale. Here we analysed 40 task-based functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) datasets in a preregistered consortium with 2,175 participants and show that three widely used indicators of reappraisal capacity—trait questionnaires, task-based affective ratings and amygdala down-regulation—do not converge on a common core. Moreover, none of the three indicators showed the expected association with canonical prefrontal regulatory circuits. Trait questionnaires showed no detectable neural associations across the brain and task-based affective ratings were instead associated with responses in the amygdala and sensorimotor cortices. At the process level, canonical control circuits were engaged during both emotion generation and reappraisal, challenging their presumed specificity for emotion regulation. These findings caution against using activation in putatively regulatory brain regions to infer how well a person regulates emotions, with implications for neural biomarkers, interventions and psychoeducation that link emotion regulation difficulties to specific regional brain deficits.

title: Molecular underpinnings of rheumatic diseases and emerging therapeutic concepts
Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
abstract: . Here we describe phase 1 of TenK10K, which leverages single-cell RNA sequencing data from more than 5 million cells across 28 immune cell types, along with matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals. This provides power to detect associations for rare and low-frequency genetic variants that have largely been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression. We map the effects of both common and rare variants in a cell-type-specific manner using a recent method that increases power by modelling single cells directly rather than aggregated 'pseudobulk' counts. We identify putative common regulatory variants for 83% of all 21,404 genes tested and cumulative rare-variant signals for 47% of those genes. We explore how genetic effects vary across cell types and states, develop a framework to determine the degree of single-cell expression quantitative trait loci cell-type specificity and show that about half of the effects are observed only in one or a few cell types. By integrating our results with functional annotations and disease information, we further characterize the likely molecular modes of action for many disease-variant associations. Finally, we explore the effects that genetic variants have on gene expression across continuous cell states, and effects that vary cell-state abundance directly.

title: Delayed electron–hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor
abstract: Abstract Kirchhoff demonstrated the reciprocity between absorptivity and emissivity for blackbody radiation in 1860 (ref. 1 ), thereby establishing the general principle that a good absorber must also be a good emitter. This principle underpins the generalized Planck’s law 2 and, when applied to semiconductors—in the form of the van Roosbroeck–Shockley equation 3 —results in substantial limitations to solar energy conversion. Here we demonstrate how this reciprocity can be circumvented in semiconductors, such as bismuth sulfide, showing a pseudo-direct bandgap character—that is, featuring a lower-energy indirect transition paired with a direct transition placed a few k B T above. After determining the pseudo-direct bandgap nature of bismuth sulfide, we reveal how this feature substantially retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination in this material with respect to classic direct semiconductors 4 . The resulting combination of a high absorption coefficient and delayed recombination offers the unprecedented possibility of overcoming limitations associated with Planck’s law, with far-reaching potential for solar energy conversion.

title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
abstract: Abstract Models of early human dispersal rely on climate to predict where populations could settle, with freshwater assumed to govern the timing and geography 1,2 , particularly across the Saharo-Arabian arid belt, where humid windows episodically opened corridors into the desert interior 3 . Yet Pleistocene dispersals into ‘Green Arabia’ were brief and geographically constrained 4,5 , a pattern not explained by water availability alone. Here we show, from an approximately 1,500-km geoarchaeological survey through the Rub’ al Khali of Arabia, the largest sand sea in the world, that the availability of stone for tool manufacture operated as an independent factor on early human settlement. Palaeolake deposits were recorded at 55 of 125 localities investigated, yet no lithic artefacts and no knappable raw materials were found along the transect, with ground-surface visibility exceeding 95%, despite abundant freshwater and contemporary occupation at the desert margins. Spatial modelling of the Peninsula supports the inference that settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and lithic raw materials rather than water alone. Across the Peninsula, 57% of water-accessible terrain lies on formations that lack knappable stone and adding raw-material availability raises discrimination of known site locations from an area under the curve of 0.695 to 0.768. Convergent patterns from Africa, North America and Asia indicate that the constraint is not peculiar to Arabia. Dispersal models that omit raw-material geology may systematically overestimate the habitable range of stone-tool-dependent populations.

title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
A single-molecule spin–photon interface
abstract: Abstract Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence 1,2 . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly 3,4 . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics 5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design 7 and processable materials 8–10 .

title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
abstract: Abstract Strong light fields have unlocked entirely new possibilities to tailor coherent electron trajectories, engineer band structures and shape emergent phases of matter all-optically 1–9 . Unravelling the underlying quantum mechanisms requires a visualization of the lightwave-driven electron motion 10,11 directly in the band structure. Although photoelectron momentum microscopy has imaged photoexcited electrons averaged over many cycles of light 12–19 , subcycle band-structure videography has been limited to small electron momenta 8,20 . Yet, lightwave-driven elementary processes in quantum materials often occur throughout momentum space. Here we introduce attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone and visualize one of the most fundamental but elusive strong-field processes: non-adiabatic Landau–Zener–Majorana tunnelling. The interplay of strong-field-driven acceleration within the Dirac-like band structure of graphene and periodic Landau–Zener–Majorana interband tunnelling manifests in a coherent subcycle displacement and distortion of the carrier distribution at the Brillouin zone edge. The extremely non-thermal electron distributions also allow us to disentangle competing scattering processes and assess their impact on coherent electronic control. Our panoramic view of field-driven electron motion enables a new quality of microscopic understanding of strong-field control of quantum materials.

title: Genetic variants shape single-cell chromatin accessibility and disease risk
abstract: T cells. A graph neural network trained on both eQTL and caQTL layers inferred peak-gene links in unpaired multiome data with up to 17.2% higher accuracy than QTL-agnostic data, uncovering 128 additional transcription factor-target pairs (22% increase). Together, these results show that genetic variants shape chromatin accessibility in a cell-type-specific and cell-state-specific manner, influencing immune function and disease risk.

title: SWI/SNF complexes shape 3D chromatin architecture through CTCF and cohesin
abstract: Abstract The BAF (also known as mammalian SWI/SNF) chromatin remodelling complexes are essential regulators of nucleosome positioning and transcription factor binding 1,2 . Loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in genes encoding components of the BAF complexes are among the most frequent across cancer types 3 . However, a unifying mechanism that explains their widespread disruption remains unclear. Here we disrupted BAF function through pharmacological inhibition and ARID1A deletion across various mammalian cell types and tissues and observed a conserved chromatin response: increased accessibility at CTCF-binding sites. ARID1A LOF alone was sufficient to drive these changes, which demonstrates that canonical BAF (cBAF) disruption is the key driver of CTCF gain. Genomic profiling showed increased CTCF and SMC3 occupancy, which reveals an antagonistic relationship between cBAF and CTCF–cohesin complexes. Furthermore, cBAF loss restructured 3D genome organization, which led to a strengthening of topologically associating domain boundaries and subdivision of large domains into smaller insulated structures. Long-range enhancer–promoter loops were replaced by shorter, promoter-proximal loops anchored at CTCF-enriched sites. To determine how CTCF function is enabled following cBAF loss, we profiled CTCF-interacting cofactors and found that CTCF binds directly to fully assembled PBAF. After cBAF depletion, PBAF was recruited to sites of increased CTCF occupancy, which demonstrates that there is an antagonistic switch between SWI/SNF subcomplexes. In vivo, conditional Arid1a deletion in primary mouse cells resulted in the expansion of a highly proliferative population marked by elevated accessibility at CTCF sites. This phenotype was fully reversed by either Ctcf or Pbrm1 deletion, which establishes that cBAF and the activity of CTCF and PBAF have contrasting roles.

title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
abstract: Abstract Proteome diversity is generated through alternative mRNA splicing 1 . In tumours, mis-spliced transcripts that contain intronic sequences, skipped exons or noncanonical donor/acceptor splice junctions resulting in frameshifts are often translated into neoantigens that drive anti-tumour immunity 2,3 . Here we report that neutrophils from patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), unlike neutrophils from healthy donors or patients with rheumatoid arthritis, contain many aberrantly spliced gene transcripts, the translation of which was predicted to result in novel amino acid sequences that are absent in normal splice variants or any other proteins. Twenty-one peptides derived from these novel amino acid sequences were detected by mass spectrometry on class I major histocompatibility complex molecules in patient samples. Co-culture of T cells from patients with overlapping sets of 15-mer peptides from the novel sequences resulted in the expansion of CD4 + and CD8 + T cells that were rapidly reactivated to secrete interferon-γ. T cell antigen receptor sequencing and re-expression transferred neoantigen reactivity to a reporter T cell. Serum from patients with SLE also contained IgG autoantibodies that recognized epitopes within the novel amino acid sequences. Our findings demonstrate that dysregulated mRNA splicing in SLE neutrophils generates neoantigens that have caused T and B cell activation, clonal expansion, IgG class-switch and autoimmunity.

title: Eukaryotes’ closest relatives are internally simple syntrophic peptidotrophic archaea
abstract: Abstract Eukaryotes are theorized to have an origin associated with the archaeal phylum Promethearchaeota (formerly Asgard archaea) 1–3 . The first cultured representatives revealed valuable insights 4,5 but are still distantly related to eukaryotes, leaving many unknowns regarding eukaryogenesis. Here we report the isolation of two strains, HC1 and SC1, that belong to the archaeal lineage that branches closest to eukaryotes (Heimdallarchaeia); 6–8 these isolates are members of a pure co-culture and a tri-culture with methanogenic partners. Both are obligately anaerobic, syntrophic, peptide-degrading and mesophilic archaea that produce protrusions and vesicles but lack persistent internal membrane structures, like Promethearchaeales 4,5 . All Promethearchaeota isolates demonstrate behaviour focused on cell construction and membrane structures rather than division, in contrast to typical prokaryotes 9 . Strain HC1 possesses genes associated with aerobic lifestyles (such as cytochrome c oxidase (Cox)) but co-cultures cannot grow under (micro)oxic conditions. Meanwhile, the strain demonstrates growth under microoxic conditions when in the presence of aerobes, suggesting that Cox supports oxygen detoxification rather than respiration. Comparative genomics provides evidence that, like HC1, Cox-possessing Heimdallarchaeia studied to date probably do not respire oxygen. The wide conservation of anaerobiosis, cell structure without persistent intracellular membranes and membrane protrusions across Promethearchaeota suggest that the archaeal ancestor of eukaryotes may have had such physiological features. In this cultivation-informed scenario for eukaryogenesis, the archaea–eukaryote transition would involve a steep transition in cell structure and physiological shift from anaerobiosis to (facultative) aerobiosis 10 , with early interactions between the archaeal host and mitochondrial ancestor probably occurring under low-oxygen conditions and at least partially mediated by oxygen detoxification.

title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
Pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 as a therapy against solid and blood cancers
abstract: Abstract The N7-methylguanosine (m 7 G) modification is one of the most prevalent tRNA modifications, mainly catalysed by the METTL1–WDR4 protein complex 1–4 . The m 7 G methyltransferase METTL1 has been linked to oncogenic transformation and the maintenance of several aggressive malignancies; however, the clinical implications of therapeutically targeting a tRNA-modifying enzyme have not been established. Here we present the development and characterization of STM9005, a highly selective and potent first-in-class tRNA methyltransferase inhibitor of METTL1. Treatment of numerous cancer cell models (including leukaemia, melanoma, pancreatic carcinoma, oesophageal cancer and small cell lung carcinoma) with STM9005 blocks cell growth, causes differentiation changes and dysregulates cell cycle progression. These cellular effects were accompanied by a selective decrease in m 7 G on a subset of tRNAs and a reduction in their expression levels, which impacted the translation of oncogenic mRNAs. We show that pharmacological inhibition of METTL1 in vivo impairs tumour growth and significantly prolongs survival in multiple mouse cancer models of different tissue origin. Collectively, our results provide a strong proof of concept that targeting of tRNA methylation is a promising avenue of anti-cancer therapy and illustrate that catalytic inhibition of METTL1 represents a therapeutic strategy against a number of aggressive malignancies.

title: Spatial and sectoral water demand assessment for the African continent
abstract: Abstract Water demand is the volume of water required by a sector to satisfy its needs 1,2 . Across Africa, these demands are frequently unmet 3 , yet their spatial and sectoral distribution remains incompletely characterized, limiting informed water-management decisions 4 . Here, we provide an Africa-wide estimate of water demand for 2020 across six sectors and multiple subsectors at high spatial resolution. Because the analysis integrates heterogeneous datasets and modelling assumptions, the resulting values should be interpreted as harmonized estimates rather than direct observations of realized water use. We estimate total annual water demand at 347 km 3 , comprising 60 km 3 (17%) for municipalities (57–64 km 3 , with ±20% key parameters variations), 225 km 3 (65%) for irrigation (214–233 km 3 , 95% confidence interval, with ±20% variations in irrigation efficiency), 11 km 3 (3%) for livestock, 15 km 3 (4%) for manufacturing, 33 km 3 (10%) for electricity including hydropower and 3 km 3 (1%) for mining (3–4 km 3 , with annual production variations). Estimated demand increased by 26% between 2010 and 2020. The dominant water-demand sector varies across regions and river basins, broadly reflecting established geographical and socioeconomic patterns. In parts of northern and southern Africa, estimated demand exceeds water availability, although results depend on assumptions regarding environmental-flow protection 5 . Elsewhere, water availability exceeds aggregate demand despite limited access to piped drinking water, indicating that physical availability alone does not determine water security. Our analysis therefore provides a spatially and sectorally resolved baseline for identifying water-demand pressures and access constraints rather than establishing a new causal mechanism of water insecurity. Local estimates should be interpreted cautiously given uncertainties in the underlying datasets.

title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
abstract: , the microbial factors driving NEC and the following brain pathology remain unclear. Here we identify Clostridium perfringens pathobionts containing Delta toxin in the gut microbiome of individuals with severe and fatal NEC. Clinically, infected infants show worse outcomes, including aberrant systemic inflammation, severe neurological damage and coagulopathy. We establish a mouse model in which Delta-toxin-positive C. perfringens infection, or Delta toxin exposure alone, recapitulates clinical features of NEC, including intestinal necrosis and acute cerebral injury. Mechanistically, Delta toxin preferentially targets macrophages, potently activating inflammasome signalling and pyroptosis, triggering a rapid inflammatory cascade that compromises blood-brain barrier integrity and drives neuroinflammation. Through a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify the tetraspanin CD9 as the host receptor for Delta toxin. Using systemic, myeloid-specific and intestinal-epithelial-specific Cd9-knockout mice, we show that systemic and myeloid Cd9 ablation protects mice against toxin-induced lethality, blood-brain barrier dysfunction and multiorgan injury, whereas epithelial Cd9 deletion shows partial protection, implicating macrophage targeting as a primary driver of C. perfringens CD9-dependent pathogenesis. Furthermore, a neutralizing anti-Delta toxin monoclonal antibody confers protection against disease progression. These findings suggest that a subset of NEC is a specific-toxin-mediated disorder and validate the Delta toxin-CD9 axis as a therapeutic target for this subset.

title: Alzheimer’s disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation
abstract: . Here we analysed data from 109,479 cases, 74,141 proxy cases, 2,131,799 controls and 499,708 proxy controls from diverse ancestries, identifying 118 loci in a multi-ancestry analysis and 9 additional loci in ancestry-specific analyses, 48 of which are new. We identified new AD risk genes, prioritized potential drug targets, and found that genes upregulated in microglia and downregulated in neurons in cases compared with controls were enriched for AD-associated genetic risk. Moreover, we improved polygenic prediction and estimated a SNP heritability of 16%, nearly threefold higher than previous estimates. Together, our findings show that the common-variant contribution to AD has been substantially underestimated, and reveal new molecular and cellular mechanisms as well as specific targets for future drug development research.

title: MCT1-dependent mitochondrial lactate import sustains cardiac metabolism
abstract: Abstract The heart possesses a dynamic capacity to oxidize a variety of fuels, including glucose and lactate, to meet its energetic demands under diverse dietary, exertion and injury stressors 1 . Oxidation of carbohydrate substrates is thought to converge on the cytosolic generation of pyruvate, which is transported by the mitochondrial pyruvate carrier (MPC) for entry into the tricarboxylic acid cycle 2 . Here we find that glucose-derived carbon is oxidized in mouse myocardium even when the MPC is genetically ablated. Using genetic and pharmacological tools, we demonstrate that lactate monocarboxylate transporter 1 (MCT1, encoded by Slc16a1 ) is required for the oxidation of glucose carbon by MPC-deficient myocardium. We further observe that MCT1, traditionally localized to the plasma membrane, also resides in the inner mitochondrial membrane of mouse and human cardiomyocytes. Together with matrix-localized LDHB, MCT1 enables mitochondrial lactate conversion to pyruvate and NADH, directly fueling the electron transport chain. Loss of MCT1 impairs lactate oxidation, disrupts metabolic flexibility and accelerates the development of heart failure with increased mortality after hyperactivation of the neurohormonal axis or ischemia–reperfusion injury. Thus, the existence of a parallel lactate-based pathway for carbohydrate oxidation can sustain cardiac energetics and maintain myocardial structure and function under diverse stress conditions.

title: This Arabian desert was once a lush paradise. Why did ancient humans avoid it?
Ribbon made of carbon pentagons and heptagons has metallic properties
abstract: Ribbons that are composed exclusively of five- and seven-carbon rings have metal-like electron transport and conductance. The ribbons can be synthesized by linking previously inaccessible chains of paired five-membered rings, providing a route to making highly conducting carbon nanoribbons. The ‘pentaheptite’ ribbons can be made by joining chains of paired five-membered rings side-by-side.

An unexpected function of a cell-cycle enzyme might explain the toxic effects of its inhibitors
abstract: A previously unknown mechanism required for cells to start proliferating has been identified. A combination of mathematical modelling and cell-based experiments shows that the enzyme WEE1 switches off a protein-degradation complex to allow cell proliferation to start, with implications for WEE1 inhibitors currently in trials for cancer treatments.

title: Clues about complex life come from freshly cultivated archaea
abstract: Two archaeal strains that belong to a lineage closely related to the ancestor of eukaryotic cells (complex cells with membrane-bound organelles) have been brought into culture. Their simple internal organization, elaborate surface structures, microbial partnerships and protein-dependent lifestyle provide clues about how eukaryotic cells arose. Two archaeal strains that share a common ancestor with eukaryotic cells have been examined in culture.
